articles.title: Researchers Uncover Prompt Adware Hidden in OpenAI Codex Jailbreak Toolkit
articles.text:
Cybersecurity researchers have disclosed details of an OpenAI Codex jailbreak bundle that's designed to modify an artificial intelligence (AI) agent's trusted instructions to insert advertisements for a third-party AI gateway.
The phenomenon has been codenamed prompt adware by Check Point Research.
Called Haiou (meaning Seagull in Chinese), the jailbreak modifies OpenAI Codex's configuration files to inject advertisements for the jailbreak author's website into subsequent agent responses.
"The advertised service is an opaque, OpenAI-compatible LLM gateway, a middleware between an application and an LLM provider," Check Point Research said in a technical report. "The likely business model is to use the freely distributed jailbreak bundle as an acquisition channel for the paid gateway service."
Adware is a type of software that displays unwanted advertisements, which can appear on users' computers or mobile devices, often in the form of pop-ups or banners. Prompt adware extends this sketchy behavior to AI agents by means of a jailbreak that defeats the model's safety training and content guardrails.
The idea is to persistently modify the agent's global instructions through natural language to influence future responses. This, in turn, causes common greetings or activation words like "Seagull," "hi," "hello," "hey," "yo," and "are you there?" to trigger an advertisement for "zz.aiapi2025[.]top."
Haiou attempts to jailbreak a model by using several prompt injection techniques, such as role-playing and reframing cybersecurity-related requests into a Capture The Flag (CTF) scenario. In addition, it installs security-focused skills devoted to penetration testing, cracking, and reverse engineering.
However, it doesn't stop there. The bundle also injects persistent ads into the global agent instruction file to promote the LLM gateway website. On GitHub, "haiou-codex" is advertised as a "local enhancement configuration package" that adds a "Chinese technical personality and security research workflow to Codex." As of writing, the repository has been forked 77 times and starred 403 times since it was made available on July 10, 2026.
It's worth noting that Codex is not officially available in mainland China, suggesting that the service is likely aimed at individuals or organizations wanting to try out Western AI coding assistants.
What's more, the jailbreak has been bundled within Codex-X, an open-source Chinese visualization tool for configuring Codex through a graphical user interface.
"The behavior is introduced through natural-language instructions and configuration, rather than a traditional executable payload that users and security teams may more readily recognize as software behavior," Pedro Drimel Neto, malware analysis team leader at Check Point, said.
While serving an ad may seem relatively harmless in the larger scheme of things, the findings demonstrate how a bad actor could introduce undesirable behavior through third-party skills or configurations, leading to supply chain attacks.
"As AI agents become part of enterprise environments, the prompts, Skills and third-party components influencing their behavior become part of the trust chain too," Neto said.

articles.title: Quick Share : vos photos Android vont enfin se sauvegarder toutes seules sur votre PC
articles.text:
Google confirme l’arrivée d’une sauvegarde automatique des photos et vidéos Android vers Windows avec Quick Share. La fonction commence son déploiement, mais sa disponibilité et la compatibilité de certains appareils restent à préciser.
Transférer quelques photos sur son ordinateur, c’est pratique. Penser à le refaire régulièrement pour conserver une copie de ses souvenirs, c’est une autre affaire. Quick Share permet déjà d’échanger des fichiers entre Android et Windows, et Google a progressivement fait évoluer son application pour PC. L’outil s’apprête désormais à prendre une partie de cette corvée à sa charge.
Vos photos copiées sur le PC, sans passer par le cloud
La nouveauté apparaît dans les notes officielles de Google Play services 26.43, datées du 2 novembre. Une ligne confirme la sauvegarde automatique des photos et vidéos d’un appareil Android vers Windows avec Quick Share. Google ne détaille toutefois ni la procédure complète ni la liste des appareils compatibles.
Le fonctionnement se dessine grâce aux éléments d’interface découverts par Android Authority dans les versions en développement. La configuration commencerait depuis Quick Share pour Windows, avec le téléphone allumé à proximité et les deux appareils connectés au même compte Google. Une fois l’association effectuée, les photos et vidéos seraient enregistrées automatiquement sur l’ordinateur, sans câble ni abonnement à un stockage cloud.
L’intérêt est assez évident pour ceux qui préfèrent conserver leurs fichiers chez eux : le disque du PC devient la destination de sauvegarde, sans devoir sélectionner puis envoyer régulièrement ses dernières images. Cela ne transforme pas pour autant Quick Share en outil de sauvegarde intégrale du smartphone. L’annonce officielle porte sur les photos et vidéos, pas sur les applications, les messages ou l’ensemble des réglages.
Un déploiement progressif, avec une interrogation du côté de Samsung
Comme le rappelle Android Authority, les mises à jour des services Google Play arrivent progressivement. Disposer de la version concernée ne garantit donc pas que l’option soit immédiatement visible. La disponibilité générale en France n’est pas précisée à ce stade, et l’application Quick Share sur Windows devra également être à jour.
Le cas Samsung mérite aussi d’être surveillé. Les précédentes analyses du code faisaient apparaître une exclusion des téléphones et PC du constructeur. Cette restriction n’est cependant pas mentionnée dans les notes officielles : difficile, pour l’instant, de savoir si elle sera maintenue dans la fonction distribuée aux utilisateurs.
Il faut enfin distinguer cette sauvegarde du partage classique, déjà proposé entre Android et Windows. L’arrivée du nouvel automatisme ne signifie pas que tous les appareils capables de recevoir un fichier pourront immédiatement en profiter.
Et sauvegarder ne veut pas dire faire le ménage : Google n’annonce aucune suppression automatique des originaux sur le téléphone. Pour retrouver de l’espace, il faudra encore décider soi-même de ce que l’on conserve dans sa poche.

articles.title: Real application testing keeps AI-driven security patches safe - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Oracle connects AI-driven testing with a new approach to database security
Frontier AI models that uncover software flaws by the hundreds are forcing database providers into larger, faster patch cycles, and real application testing is becoming the safeguard that keeps those fixes from breaking production systems. The same AI wave is also undermining security rules written into applications.
Oracle Corp. has responded on two fronts, hardening its code against outside attackers while moving agent controls down to the data layer. The first effort began when the company turned an early-access frontier model on its own software, according to Juan Loaiza (pictured), executive vice president of Oracle Database Technologies at Oracle.
“Back in March, we got early access to the Mythos model and we ran it against our code and it started finding all these security vulnerabilities,” Loaiza said. “It’s turning up some very serious security issues. And so we said, ‘Hey, this is a code red moment. The house is on fire.'”
Loaiza spoke with theCUBE Research’s Dave Vellante at Oracle AI World, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed why AI-discovered vulnerabilities, AI-generated code and AI agents require enterprises to treat security as a data problem. (* Disclosure below.)
Real application testing meets bigger, faster patches
Most of Oracle’s response to AI-discovered vulnerabilities is landing in its regular quarterly patches, which have grown much larger as a result, Loaiza explained. A quarterly security update earlier this year addressed more than 1,400 vulnerabilities across the company’s portfolio. Customers must automate patching and stay current, but every large patch raises fears of regression in systems that cannot fail.
“We have something called Real Application Testing where we can capture real workload and run it to make sure that your workload is not affected by these patches,” Loaiza said. “It’s not quite as simple as just apply because the applications that people run are extraordinarily complex. They run entire countries, entire industries.”
Patching handles outside attackers. Internal AI use is a separate threat, because applications have traditionally enforced end-user security, and AI now writes much of that code or goes straight to the data. Oracle’s answer is Deep Data Security, which began shipping in April and passes an authenticated user’s identity as an encrypted token through to the database. The company has since extended those authorization controls across remote databases, lakehouse data and related tables.
“The new world as I see it is all these end-user security rules have to be enforced where AI can’t bypass them, which means all the way down in the data,” Loaiza said. “The AI agent has to get your identity. It’s acting on behalf of you. It can’t leak the data if it can’t see the data.”
Business rules follow the same logic. Application code has always blocked a credit card charge above the customer’s limit, but an AI agent told to enforce that rule may not comply, Loaiza noted. Oracle is providing declarative ways to define such rules, along with SQL Assertions that check whether changes made through SQL are valid.
“There’s credit limits, there’s all sorts of things that are business rules that can’t be violated. And again, if we move those all the way down into the data, then no matter how you access the data, what mechanism you use, how AI is used, it cannot violate those rules,” Loaiza said.

articles.title: Netflix estrena una IA que recomienda qué ver según el estado de ánimo
articles.text:
Elegir una película o serie para ver en Netflix puede convertirse en una tarea que consume varios minutos, especialmente cuando ninguna de las recomendaciones parece despertar interés. Para intentar resolver este problema, la plataforma de streaming está probando AI Discover, una nueva función impulsada por inteligencia artificial que busca sugerir contenido de acuerdo con las emociones, preferencias y situaciones de cada usuario.
La herramienta propone una experiencia diferente a los tradicionales algoritmos de recomendación. En lugar de limitarse a mostrar producciones similares a las que una persona ya vio, busca interpretar qué tipo de entretenimiento necesita en ese momento. Así, alguien que quiera relajarse, compartir una película con su familia o pasar una noche de terror podrá encontrar sugerencias relacionadas con esas situaciones.
Según explicó Netflix en un comunicado, AI Discover se incorporará como una pestaña independiente dentro de su aplicación para televisores. Desde allí, los usuarios podrán explorar diferentes categorías creadas mediante inteligencia artificial y recibir recomendaciones personalizadas sin tener que recorrer manualmente todo el catálogo.
Por ahora, la función se encuentra en una fase de pruebas y está disponible para un grupo reducido de usuarios. La compañía busca evaluar su funcionamiento y determinar si esta experiencia puede mejorar la manera en que las personas descubren películas y series.
Cómo funciona AI Discover, la nueva inteligencia artificial de Netflix
Al ingresar a la pestaña AI Discover, los usuarios encontrarán diferentes categorías que funcionan como puntos de partida para encontrar contenido. Estas opciones están diseñadas para representar estados de ánimo, preferencias o situaciones específicas.
Entre las alternativas disponibles aparece «Algo ligero», pensada para quienes buscan una película entretenida que no requiera demasiada atención. También figura “Noche de cine en familia”, orientada a encontrar producciones para compartir con otras personas.
Otra de las opciones es “Asústame”, dirigida a quienes prefieren las películas y series de terror. Asimismo, la plataforma contempla categorías relacionadas con la duración de las producciones, como aquellas que permiten encontrar películas cortas.
Cada tema incluye un avance de una película o serie que sirve como referencia para mostrar el tipo de contenido que puede aparecer en los resultados. Cuando el usuario selecciona una categoría, la inteligencia artificial genera una lista de recomendaciones basándose en ese criterio.
La experiencia también permite afinar los resultados mediante temas adicionales y situaciones más específicas. De esta manera, Netflix intenta reducir el tiempo que las personas dedican a buscar algo que coincida con lo que quieren ver.
Si las sugerencias no resultan satisfactorias, existe una opción llamada “Algo diferente”, que permite explorar alternativas alejadas de las recomendaciones habituales.
Netflix permitirá ajustar las recomendaciones de su inteligencia artificial
Uno de los aspectos más interesantes de AI Discover es que no se limita a ofrecer sugerencias. También incorpora un mecanismo para que los usuarios puedan indicar si los resultados fueron de su agrado.
La herramienta incluye un botón llamado “Ajusta tus recomendaciones”, desde el cual es posible señalar si una película o serie resultó útil o si, por el contrario, no debería volver a aparecer entre las sugerencias.
Este sistema busca que la inteligencia artificial aprenda progresivamente de las preferencias de cada persona. Así, las recomendaciones podrían volverse más precisas con el uso y evitar producciones que no despiertan interés.
Netflix explicó que AI Discover funciona mediante una nueva capa de inteligencia artificial desarrollada internamente. El sistema procesa en tiempo real la información que proporciona el usuario y utiliza esos datos para generar propuestas de entretenimiento.
Sin embargo, existe una limitación importante: la herramienta no funciona como un chatbot. Es decir, no permite escribir o hablar directamente con una inteligencia artificial para solicitar recomendaciones con condiciones específicas.
Por ejemplo, no es posible pedirle que encuentre películas protagonizadas por un actor determinado, que duren menos de 90 minutos o que pertenezcan a un género concreto. En su lugar, el usuario debe desplazarse entre las categorías disponibles y utilizar las opciones que ofrece la plataforma para acotar los resultados.

articles.title: Souveraineté numérique : le CNRS claque la porte de Microsoft et compte économiser 3,5 millions d’euros par an
articles.text:
Le CNRS quitte Microsoft Exchange pour renforcer sa souveraineté numérique grâce à une solution libre française
Le Centre national de la recherche scientifique (CNRS) a fait une annonce encourageante pour la souveraineté numérique (et ses finances) : elle vient d'abandonner Microsoft Exchange pour une solution libre française.
Depuis plusieurs mois, la fronde à l'égard des GAFAM prend de l'ampleur. Toujours plus d'organismes et de pays quittent les outils de Microsoft, Google et les autres, au profit de services européens et souvent libres. Si certaines tentatives échouent, pour le moment le résultat semble être là. Ce mardi 3 novembre, c'est au tour du Centre national de la recherche scientifique (CNRS) d'annoncer un grand changement dans son organisation.
L'organisme a ainsi décidé de quitter Microsoft Exchange comme solution de messagerie, basculant sur un ensemble d'outils français.
Le CNRS quitte Microsoft Exchange pour ses 35 000 agents
Dès à présent, c'est donc PARTAGE, la plateforme de messagerie collaborative en mode SaaS de RENATER, qui a été retenue. RENATER, pour Réseau National de télécommunications pour la Technologie, l'Enseignement et la Recherche, est un réseau national qui lie différentes infrastructures et services numériques pour la communauté éducation recherche. Le CNRS en est l'un des membres fondateurs.
Pour l'hébergement, plutôt que la messagerie externalisée Exchange, la solution passe ici par les outils libres Zimbra, en France. Les 35 000 agents du CNRS sont concernés par cette migration, tandis que l'organisme souligne que cette décision va au-delà de sa volonté de sortie des GAFAM. En effet, cette migration devrait permettre d'économiser environ 3,5 millions d’euros par an.
	
Ce partenariat avec le CNRS, membre fondateur du GIP RENATER, renforce un modèle que nous défendons depuis longtemps : que les acteurs publics de la recherche puissent disposer d’outils numériques qu’ils maîtrisent pleinement.
Sans surprise, RENATER salue la décision du CNRS : "En quittant les outils externalisés pour adopter une infrastructure 100% française et son accès authentifié., le CNRS renforce sa souveraineté numérique tout en garantissant la sécurité des échanges scientifiques." RENATER souligne également que PARTAGE est déjà utilisée par 90 établissements et 930 000 utilisateurs.

articles.title: 'I can confirm it, Windows 11 has been overall much more responsive': Microsoft boasts Windows 11 is now up to 40% faster for multi-tasking — and many users agree it's speedier
articles.text:
Microsoft boasts Windows 11 is now up to 40% faster for multi-tasking, as latest update packs a big speed boost for 8GB PCs
While a developer shows the OS can run on just 128MB somehow
- Windows 11 got a major performance boost with its latest update, including 40% faster multi-tasking on an 8GB PC based on Microsoft's testing
- That update is still a preview, mind, but the full release is coming next week, with other performance boosts, especially for 8GB PCs
- Meanwhile the developer of Tiny11 has managed to get a totally stripped-down version of Windows 11 running in an improbable 128MB of memory
Microsoft has gone into the details of how it's made Windows 11 faster on 8GB PCs (and all systems for that matter), with these changes arriving in the next update for the OS – all while a third-party has demonstrated the operating system running on a meagre 128MB of RAM (with huge caveats as you might expect).
A blog post from Pavan Davuluri, head of Windows at Microsoft, entitled 'Raising the bar for 8GB Windows 11 PCs' gives us some further metrics as to how much performance has been improved by.
Microsoft has mentioned that Windows 11 is now up to 20% more responsive on 8GB machines before, but now it's added another stat to consider, namely that the OS is 40% faster for multi-tasking (and that kind of workload is where 8GB of RAM can feel a lot more pushed to its limits).
In this case, Microsoft's test involved "opening 20 tabs in Microsoft Edge, a 4K video, large Word, PowerPoint and Excel files, Outlook and File Explorer one after another, keeping everything open as we went." This was 40% faster compared to Windows 11 in January 2026 (before the fix the OS campaign started), as measured on an HP OmniBook 3 laptop with a Snapdragon X Plus (Arm) 8-core CPU and 8GB of memory.
Davuluri explains that Microsoft's approach to upping performance in Windows 11 runs along three distinct paths: "Making better use of the memory in every Windows 11 PC, protecting the interactions that need to feel instant even under load, and ensuring key apps and Windows require less memory."
Of course, the exec points out that this work benefits all Windows 11 PCs, but that this tuning will be particularly beneficial for 8GB devices – clearly having key apps drain less system RAM is going to be great for lower memory loadouts.
Microsoft notes that in terms of memory management improvements, in multi-tasking tests on 8GB systems, it has "reduced committed-memory growth by up to 900MB" in Windows 11 running Edge and Microsoft 365 apps.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
We're also told that thanks to improvements in Windows 11's compression techniques, more active data for apps can be stored in RAM (as opposed to on your drive, where it's slower to be fetched) – to the tune of up to 2GB more. Davuluri employs a useful desk metaphor to illustrate this, which I think is worth a read for the less tech-savvy.
If you want the benefit of all this fresh speediness, Microsoft informs us that this performance tuning is in place in the very latest update for Windows 11, which is the optional update that arrived at the end of October (complete with right-click menu customization).
If you download that, though, bear in mind it's a preview so officially still in testing. I'd advise waiting for the full release of the finished November update, which comes out next week on November 10, so you won't have to be patient for long.
Analysis: necessary streamlining – and it appears to have done the trick
Okay, so Microsoft is touting some very specific performance measurements here and there's bound to have been some cherry-picking going on. In other words, run a ton of different tests and pick the results that show off the very best performance levels (with a peak 'up to' value), but of course this is standard practice for any product marketing.
Still, it's clear that strides have been made, and online feedback backs this up. There are numerous users who are observing that Windows 11 is faster after this most recent update, and indeed since version 26H2 was released.
As one Redditor observes: "I can confirm it, Windows 11 has been overall much more [responsive] on my system, it used to be slow as s**t and now even the context menu opens quite instant."
Most of the negativity that now remains on social media, aside from the obvious trolling, is around why Microsoft didn't have Windows 11 tuned up like this in the first place. And that a 40% improvement in multi-tasking was partly made possible because things were in such a sluggish state to begin with, and I think those are fair points (I've brought them up myself in the past).
Still, it's clear that Microsoft is working hard and successfully optimizing Windows 11 for leaner RAM loadouts, and I obviously won't argue with that. Meanwhile, the developer of Tiny11 – which allows you to create a completely stripped-down Windows installation – has proved that Microsoft's OS can be pared back so it runs on just 128MB of RAM (hat tip to Tom's Hardware).
That beats the developer's old record of 184MB, and it's a seriously impressive feat, but as you might imagine, what's left in Windows after pruning it back so viciously is, well, barely anything. You can boot the desktop, open folders or the Start menu, and run Notepad, but not much else. It is "painfully slow" by the developer's own admission, and not a workable version of Windows 11 so much as an exercise in what can be done.
The reason that projects such as Tiny11 are popular is because many folks are fed up with the bloat in Windows 11, and want to create their own tailored and streamlined version. If Microsoft keeps going with its successful performance tweaking and tuning, with any luck, there'll be a lot less demand for the likes of Tiny11 in the future.
Microsoft is promising more memory efficiency tuning, and advances in memory compression, are coming, as well as a greater use of WinUI 3 for speedier apps and parts of the Windows 11 interface.

articles.title: 29 jurisdicciones votaron contra la instalación de data centers, claves para el desarrollo de la inteligencia artificial en EEUU
articles.text:
Durante años, las grandes tecnológicas construyeron sus centros de datos con pocos obstáculos: terrenos baratos, incentivos fiscales y promesas de empleo que neutralizaban las objeciones locales. El martes 3 de noviembre esa ecuación cambió.
Las elecciones de medio término en Estados Unidos dejaron en claro, según analistas e inversores, que el rechazo a los centros de datos de inteligencia artificial se convirtió en una fuerza electoral con consecuencias directas para una industria que mueve billones de dólares.
El golpe llegó en dos frentes simultáneos. Por un lado, Texas, Georgia, Ohio y Pensilvania eligieron gobernadores demócratas que hicieron del freno a esta infraestructura una promesa de campaña explícita.
Por otro, el Washington Post informó que votantes de al menos 29 jurisdicciones aprobaron prohibiciones o restricciones sobre centros de datos el martes, lo que el diario denominó un reflejo de la “repulsión pública generalizada” hacia estos proyectos.
El fenómeno tenía antecedentes concretos en 2026. Los votantes de 13 estados —Arkansas, California, Florida, Illinois, Kansas, Maine, Míchigan, Nevada, Nuevo Hampshire, Nueva Jersey, Dakota del Norte, Ohio y Wisconsin— se pronunciaron sobre al menos 50 medidas locales relacionadas con centros de datos, según Ballotpedia.
De ellas, 41 se votaron el martes. En los seis casos resueltos antes de esa fecha —en Nuevo Hampshire, California, Míchigan y Wisconsin— la restricción ganó en todos, con márgenes de entre el 66% y el 90%.
Lo que pasó en Texas
Gina Hinojosa se convirtió en la primera gobernadora demócrata de Texas en más de tres décadas al derrotar al republicano Greg Abbott.
Durante su campaña, Hinojosa pidió una moratoria inmediata sobre la construcción de centros de datos, a los que acusó de “elevar las tarifas de servicios públicos y agotar el agua”. Prometió detener las aprobaciones hasta “una sesión legislativa que priorice a los tejanos”.
Texas concentra casi el 30% de la capacidad de centros de datos prevista para entrar en operación en 2028, la mayor participación de cualquier estado, según la firma de investigación SemiAnalysis, que advirtió que la victoria de Hinojosa representa “un enfoque claramente más bajista” para la industria y que “la pregunta ahora es cuánto tiempo durará la pausa”.
Ohio, el estado con más frentes abiertos
En Ohio, la demócrata Amy Acton derrotó al empresario multimillonario Vivek Ramaswamy para convertirse en la próxima gobernadora, cambiando de partido un cargo que hasta entonces era republicano.
Acton propuso una moratoria condicional que obliga a los desarrolladores a cumplir una serie de requisitos antes de obtener permisos de construcción. Según Fortune, el estado concentró la mayor resistencia municipal del país: al menos 14 localidades aprobaron prohibiciones u otras restricciones el martes. Diez de ellas —Hubbard, Sunbury, Pataskala, Urbana, Defiance, Upper Sandusky, Piqua, Granville, Conneaut y Trenton— votaron prohibiciones directas sobre nuevas instalaciones.
En Wilmington, además, los votantes rechazaron cuatro rezonificaciones que habrían permitido la construcción de un campus de centros de datos. Empresas como Meta y Amazon Web Services tienen planificadas inversiones de USD 1.000 millones y USD 2.000 millones respectivamente en ese estado.
Georgia y Pensilvania, dos historias distintas
En Georgia, Keisha Lance Bottoms se convirtió en la primera mujer negra elegida gobernadora del estado, arrebatando a los republicanos el control del ejecutivo estatal tras más de dos décadas.
Bottoms también llamó durante su campaña a frenar la construcción de nuevos centros de datos en Georgia, tercer estado del país en desarrollo de esta infraestructura según la firma Jefferies.
En Pensilvania, el gobernador demócrata Josh Shapiro fue reelecto.
Aunque su victoria era esperada y no implica un cambio inmediato de política, Shapiro endureció su postura contra proyectos especulativos y aquellos que enfrentan rechazo local, según Bloomberg.
El impacto en la industria y en los mercados
Según un análisis de Jefferies, las victorias demócratas en estos cuatro estados dejan expuesta a mayor escrutinio regulatorio aproximadamente la mitad de la capacidad de centros de datos de IA propuesta en todo el país.
En Texas, Gordon Johnson, de la firma GLJ Research, estimó que unos 13 gigavatios de capacidad —suficiente para abastecer a alrededor de 10 millones de hogares en simultáneo— quedan directamente afectados por la victoria de Hinojosa.
Johnson señaló que los proyectos con permisos y financiamiento en regla podrían continuar, pero aquellos sin aprobaciones estatales ambientales sufrirían retrasos de entre 12 y 18 meses. Los que “no tienen ni lo uno ni lo otro probablemente vayan a Luisiana, Oklahoma o a ningún lado”, advirtió en una nota enviada el martes a la noche, recogida por Bloomberg.
Los resultados electorales generaron movimientos en los mercados financieros desde las operaciones previas a la apertura de las bolsas en Nueva York el miércoles. Las acciones de Tesla cayeron más del 6% en el premarket, mientras que las de SpaceX bajaron un 5,6%, perforando los USD 135 por acción —el precio de su oferta pública inicial de junio—, según The New York Times.
Ambas empresas están controladas por Elon Musk, quien destinó casi USD 474 millones al Partido Republicano durante las elecciones de medio término, la mayor contribución individual en un ciclo electoral en la historia de Estados Unidos, con excepción de candidatos que financian sus propias campañas.
Musk reaccionó en su red social X: “Los centros de datos en el espacio resultan bastante atractivos en este momento”, en referencia al objetivo de SpaceX de desplegar clústeres de computación de IA en órbita.
En contraste, Nvidia, Alphabet y Amazon cotizaban al alza en el premarket, ya que los mercados habían comenzado a incorporar el riesgo regulatorio semanas antes, según Bloomberg.
Por qué el rechazo ciudadano llegó hasta las urnas
Según una encuesta de 2025 del Pew Research Center, la mitad de los estadounidenses declara sentir más temor que entusiasmo ante la IA.
Los centros de datos —que demandan enormes cantidades de energía, agua y terreno, y generan ruido y contaminación— concentraron buena parte de ese malestar.
Al menos 45 proyectos fueron interrumpidos en el segundo trimestre de 2026 por oposición local, según Data Center Watch.
Una encuesta de salida de NBC indicó que más del 50% de los votantes consideró que la IA y los centros de datos fueron “un factor crucial o importante” en su decisión de ir a las urnas.
La jefa de política pública de PIMCO, Libby Cantrill, advirtió antes de las elecciones que las carreras por las gobernaciones tendrían un impacto significativo en el futuro de los proyectos.
“Incluso si no se producen moratorias a nivel estatal, esperamos ver mucha más fricción en el proceso de construcción de la IA, con más tiempo necesario para obtener permisos y más concesiones que los desarrolladores deberán hacer”, señaló en declaraciones recogidas por Bloomberg.

articles.title: APT29-Linked Hackers Hijack Web Analytics Script to Deliver iOS and Android Exploits
articles.text:
The Russia-linked threat actor known as APT29 is said to be behind a large-scale watering hole campaign targeting iOS and Android users through compromised websites, fake domains, and a supply chain attack involving a Ukrainian web analytics service called Plerdy SEO Tracker.
"The injected JavaScript code collects browser and device attributes," Sekoia researchers Amaury-Jacques Garçon and Félix Aime said in a technical report shared with The Hacker News. "Then, the delivery infrastructure delivers a platform-specific N-day exploit chain targeting either iOS or Android."
The end goal of the attacks is to serve payloads capable of stealing browser cookies, and in some cases, Wi-Fi passwords or full mobile device data. The activity, codenamed Poisoned Source, was discovered by the French cybersecurity company in mid-October 2026.
A defining aspect of the campaign is the use of three infection vectors -
- Compromise of legitimate websites to inject malicious JavaScript
- Lookalike sites masquerading as high-profile websites in the U.S. ("america250[.]holiday"), Ukraine, Czech Republic, and Bulgaria
- Supply chain compromise of Plerdy SEO Tracker between August 27 and September 3, 2026, by injecting malicious code into "a.plerdy[.]com/public/js/click/main.js"
Some of the compromised websites include a major industry trade association representing U.S. companies operating in the chemical industry, a far-right European political party, and a Bulgarian military-related website. It's suspected that the watering hole campaign may have been designed to target specific individuals rather than a broad effort.
"It remains unclear whether the attackers intended to target visitors to specific websites or sought to compromise as many unpatched mobile devices as possible, indiscriminately exfiltrating data before selectively identifying and exploiting information of interest," Sekoia said.
"However, several of these sites are likely to attract high-value or strategically important visitors in the context of the Russia-Ukraine war. This supply chain attack spread through high-value targets, such as army, special forces, and military equipment (ballistic, UAV) websites."
Regardless of the method employed, all roads lead to the same payload: a JavaScript loader that profiles the visitor's device and web browser, and then serves appropriate next-stage malware. For iOS users, it leads to an exploit kit called DarkSword to harvest cookies and full device data.
On Android, the malware is equipped to exfiltrate Chrome data and Wi-Fi passwords without establishing persistence. No less than three different exploits have been identified -
- Class A, which targets iOS devices running iOS 16.7 and exploits CVE-2025-43529 (the same vulnerability exploited by DarkSword) and CVE-2024-27834 to deliver JavaScript malware for cookie theft.
- Class B, which targets iOS devices running iOS 18.5 and exploits the DarkSword exploit chain comprising CVE-2025-43529, CVE-2026-20700, CVE-2025-14174, CVE-2025-43510, and CVE-2025-43520 to deliver JavaScript malware for full device data exfiltration. This includes SMS messages and iMessages; Apple Mail Envelope Index and Protected Index SQLite databases; voicemail; WhatsApp and Telegram databases; iCloud Keychain, Wi-Fi passwords; contacts; call history; Safari browser history and cookies; photos; and data from Apple Health, Calendar, Notes, and iCloud Drive.
- Class C, which targets Android devices running Chrome versions from 139 through 145 (but explicitly excluding version 143 for reasons that remain presently unknown) and exploits CVE-2026-3910 and CVE-2025-27038 to achieve remote code execution, sandbox escape, privilege escalation, and ultimately deliver AndroSnitch to collect Chrome data and Wi-Fi passwords.
In all three cases, the exfiltrated data is sent to the "ad.starx-net[.]com:8881/telemetry/v12" endpoint. The Android attack chain incorporates a check to determine whether the targeted device is a Samsung Galaxy S25 Ultra by examining its model identifier (i.e., SM-S938B). If the device matches, the exploitation activity is terminated.
AndroSnitch derives its name from its similarities to ANDROSNATCH, a Chrome cookie-stealing payload that Google documented in August 2024 in connection with a suspected APT29 watering hole campaign, which targeted Android users visiting a Mongolian government website by leveraging a Chrome exploit chain involving CVE-2024-5274 and CVE-2024-4671.
"This operation also confirms the continued reuse of CSV [Commercial Surveillance Vendors] mobile exploit frameworks, such as DarkSword, by state-sponsored intrusion sets," Sekoia said. "The adoption of packaged N-day exploit chains lowers the cost and technical threshold required to conduct advanced mobile exploitation."
Coruna and DarkSword Kits Evolve
The development comes weeks after iVerify and Report URI detailed the P7 variant of DarkSword being delivered via half-click attacks that leverage ad-based infrastructure. In one case, the exploit is said to have been propagated through a malicious Instagram ad themed around the World Cup and served from "ad-track[.]live."
The other pathway is part of a criminal campaign dubbed DeadTag, in which attackers acquire expired domains behind old analytics and advertising tags that are still loaded by thousands of websites. The idea is to serve malicious JavaScript to iPhone visitors and silently do the attacker's bidding.
"It checks who's visiting," Report URI said. "Search engines, security scanners, automated browsers and anything else that looks like a bot gets nothing."
The script then interacts with the attacker's server, which then decides the destination to which each visitor has to be redirected. The iPhone exploit paths that take advantage of DeadTag lead to the Coruna exploit kit for older iPhones running iOS version 13 to 17.2.1 and DarkSword P7 for iOS devices running 18.4 to 18.7.
"These are not phishing pages or fake app downloads, both kits attack the browser itself," Report URI's Scott Helme said. "Simply opening the page is enough for your device to be compromised. There's nothing to tap, you don't need to click any link, nothing to install and no warning. If the iPhone is running a vulnerable version of iOS, the kit breaks out of the browser and installs spyware on the device."
Other schemes lead to decoy Google redirects, betting and casino scam sign-up pages, search advertisements for car deals and dentists, and fake surveys and "you've won" prize pages. More than 660 expired and re-registered domains are part of the DeadTag network.
According to an analysis published by Zimperium zLabs, campaigns distributing Coruna and DarkSword exploit kits have continued to evolve, with 608 domains delivering Coruna-family code as of October 2026.
Although Coruna was initially developed by a nation-state actor for highly targeted operations, its subsequent leak following initial disclosure has made the toolkit widely accessible to multiple threat actors for their own campaigns.
In many cases, the lure sites have been found to explicitly instruct visitors to exit their in-app browser or alternative iOS browser and open the link in Safari so as to trigger the exploit chain depending upon the device operating system.
"Targets running iOS 17.2.1 or earlier receive the legacy Coruna framework (exhibiting byte-identical JavaScript payloads across multiple recovered configurations)," security researcher Santiago Rodriguez said. "Conversely, devices running later iOS builds receive a DarkSword-derived execution chain."
"The analyzed distribution footprint spans dating portals, AI-companion platforms, cryptocurrency promotions, media streaming services, and – in several instances – compromised legitimate sites serving the kit via hidden iframes."

articles.title: Black Friday Apple : on a trouvé l’iPhone Duo en stock, à 699€ avec un forfait
articles.text:
Moins de deux semaines après sa sortie, le premier iPhone pliant reste difficile à obtenir : Free se disait en rupture fin octobre et SFR promettait ses modèles 256 Go pour décembre. Bouygues Telecom propose l’iPhone Duo 256 Go à 699 € à la commande puis 54,31 € par mois avec forfait, une somme à peser, car la remise réelle sur le téléphone se limite à 50 €.
Premier smartphone pliant d’Apple, l’iPhone Duo se referme sur un écran de 5,4 pouces et s’ouvre sur une dalle de 7,6 pouces. Bouygues Telecom le propose en 256 Go à 699 € à la commande, puis 36 mensualités de 54,31 €, avec un forfait Confort 130 Go et un engagement de 24 mois. Ce tarif intègre 50 € de remise immédiate sur le prix public de 2 339 €, soit 2 289 € au comptant.
Le forfait affiche 14,99 € par mois avec la remise B.iG, liée à une Bbox, et 19,99 € sans box. L’offre vise donc surtout les abonnés Bbox et les propriétaires d’un iPhone récent à revendre.
L’iPhone Duo 256 Go est à 699 € à la commande puis 54,31 € par mois sur 36 mois chez Bouygues Telecom, avec forfait.
Pourquoi choisir l’iPhone Duo ?
- Deux formats en un : Replié, il se manie comme un iPhone compact. Ouvert, sa dalle de 7,6 pouces est 50 % plus grande que celle de l’iPhone 18 Pro Max.
- Deux applications côte à côte : Chaque moitié de l’écran intérieur reprend à peu près le format de l’écran externe, et vos paires d’applications se sauvegardent.
- La puissance des Pro : Il reprend la puce A20 Pro des iPhone 18 Pro, avec 12 Go de RAM, et Apple annonce 50 % de batterie en 20 minutes environ.
Lire, travailler, regarder : ce que change l’écran de 7,6 pouces
Une fois plié, l’iPhone Duo pèse 254 g pour 11,3 mm d’épaisseur. Déplié, deux applications s’y partagent l’écran à parts égales, à la verticale comme à l’horizontale, et Messages peut rester ouvert pendant que vous consultez un autre contenu. Posé en chevalet sur une table, il active le mode StandBy. Apple annonce 44 heures de lecture vidéo sur l’écran externe, mais 31 heures sur le grand écran.
Ce format parle à ceux qui veulent réunir un iPhone et une petite tablette dans un seul appareil. Il convient moins aux amateurs de photo : pas de téléobjectif, un zoom de qualité optique 2x contre 4x sur les iPhone 18 Pro, ni ProRAW ni ProRes. Face ID laisse sa place à Touch ID, et le téléphone fonctionne uniquement en eSIM. Nous n’avons pas encore publié de test de l’iPhone Duo : ces éléments viennent des annonces d’Apple.
Plus cher qu’un iPhone 18 Pro et qu’un pliant Android
À 256 Go, l’iPhone Duo coûte 860 € de plus que l’iPhone 18 Pro, pour une photo moins polyvalente. Face au Galaxy Z Fold 8, il oppose un écran intérieur plus défini et une certification IP68 contre IP48, mais 12 Go de RAM contre 16 Go sur les versions 512 Go et 1 To du Samsung. Dans notre comparatif des meilleurs smartphones, le Honor Magic V6 reste notre pliant de référence, noté 9/10 et affiché sous les 1 600 €. L’iPhone Duo se justifie donc surtout si vous voulez rester sur iOS.
✅ Les points forts
- Grand écran de 7,6 pouces dans un téléphone de 5,4 pouces une fois plié
- Puce A20 Pro, identique à celle des iPhone 18 Pro
- Certification IP68, face à l’IP48 du Galaxy Z Fold 8
- Forfait de 130 Go utilisable en France métropolitaine, en Europe, dans les DOM et en Suisse
- Jusqu’à 650 € de moins dans l’exemple de reprise de Bouygues
❌ Les limites
- 2 654,16 € au total à crédit, dont 365,16 € d’intérêts
- Forfait à 19,99 € sans Bbox, et non 14,99 €
- Mensualités sur 36 mois pour un engagement de 24 mois
- Fissures de l’écran intérieur signalées par certains propriétaires, cause non établie
Un iPhone récent dans un tiroir ? Estimez sa reprise chez Bouygues et contrôlez la livraison, annoncée à partir du 22 novembre pour le 256 Go.
Cette offre n’est pas une vraie promotion sur le téléphone : la remise immédiate se limite à 50 €, et les 699 € sont un apport. Le crédit Younited porte sur 1 590 €, pour 1 955,16 € dus hors assurance facultative, avec un TAEG fixe de 14,89 % et un taux débiteur fixe de 13,96 %. Attention, un crédit coûte de l’argent et doit être remboursé. L’intérêt tient surtout à la reprise : 650 € de moins avec un iPhone 16 Pro 128 Go estimé 500 €, bonus de 100 € et remise immédiate compris, sous réserve d’un renvoi sous 30 jours.
Si vous êtes client Bbox, avec un mobile récent à revendre, le calcul devient défendable. Si vous pouvez payer comptant, les 2 289 € vous épargnent 365,16 € d’intérêts. Si la charnière vous inquiète, patientez jusqu’à un test approfondi : Apple reconnaît qu’un petit nombre d’appareils présente des fissures le long du pli. La garantie légale de conformité de deux ans s’applique aussi chez l’opérateur.

articles.title: Ce général de la Space Force veut des satellites militaires prêts pour 2029 et dit pourquoi : “un domaine de combat”
articles.text:
Space Force : le Pentagone déclare la Lune champ de bataille et prépare cinq satellites pour 2029
Il fut un temps où un général de la Space Force se faisait demander de ne pas parler d'espace cislunaire. Aujourd'hui, le Pentagone sonde l'industrie pour cinq satellites militaires entre la Terre et la Lune, et ses plus hauts gradés parlent de champ de bataille.
Le 2 novembre 2026, le département de l'Armée de l'air américaine a publié sur le site des marchés publics fédéraux un appel à renseignements pour un système spatial cislunaire, c'est-à-dire déployé dans la région qui s'étend de l'orbite terrestre jusqu'à la Lune. Il prévoit jusqu'à cinq satellites, prêts à partir fin 2029. Aucun contrat n'est encore attribué.
Derrière ce document administratif, une idée s'installe au sommet de l'armée américaine : l'espace entre la Terre et la Lune entre dans le périmètre de la défense, avec un calendrier, des industriels sollicités et des généraux qui parlent de champ de bataille.
Cinq satellites militaires prévus pour amorcer une constellation
L'avis décrit des engins qui serviraient de véhicules d'amorçage à une future constellation. Chacun comprendrait un bus satellite, une charge utile fournie par l'État et son intégration, avec un segment sol et une solution de lancement pour l'ensemble. Le Pentagone envisage jusqu'à cinq contrats d'études à prix ferme, réclame une solution rapide et à faible risque, et se dit “notionnellement” intéressé, une formule prudente qui n'engage à rien.
Selon Air & Space Forces Magazine, les premières études pourraient être financées dès début 2027, avec des satellites prêts au lancement fin 2029 et une exploitation en 2031. Entre l'avis et le début des opérations, il reste donc plus de quatre ans.
Le document ne détaille pas les instruments embarqués. Les responsables citent la surveillance de l'espace, la navigation et les communications, et l'avis demande des moteurs capables de maintenir l'engin à poste et de changer d'orbite. Le général Stephen Purdy, qui pilote ces programmes à la Space Force, réclame aussi des satellites dotés d'intelligence artificielle, capables de gérer seuls leurs pannes, leurs calculs et leurs capteurs.
La militarisation de l'espace dépasse la seule région cislunaire, comme le montre le projet américain de bouclier antimissile spatial voulu par Donald Trump.
Pourquoi l'espace entre la Terre et la Lune inquiète l'armée américaine
Le volume en jeu est colossal. D'après une fiche du laboratoire de recherche de l'armée de l'air, cette région représente 1 728 fois le volume de l'orbite géostationnaire, où évoluent déjà de nombreux satellites de télécommunications et de météorologie.
Y suivre un objet pose un vrai problème. Les trajectoires sont moins prévisibles, les distances immenses, et même les capteurs au sol peinent à repérer ce qui s'y déplace. SpaceNews relève que des objets évoluant dans cette zone pourraient s'approcher de l'orbite terrestre par des trajectoires que les capteurs actuels détectent mal. Les militaires parlent d'angles morts. Ces angles morts s'ajoutent à de nouvelles menaces militaires qui pèsent sur les satellites américains, dont un dispositif russe qui pourrait porter une arme nucléaire.
À la distance de la Lune, un signal radio met déjà plus d'une seconde pour faire l'aller simple. Ce délai aide à comprendre l'insistance des responsables sur l'autonomie des engins, et l'armée américaine teste déjà des technologies de navigation autonome pour se passer du GPS.
Un champ de bataille déclaré avant d'avoir les moyens de l'occuper
	
J'ai le secrétaire à la Guerre et le président des chefs d'état-major interarmées qui affirment publiquement : c'est un domaine de combat.
Cette posture est récente. Purdy décrit un changement radical en un an, porté par le secrétaire à la Guerre Pete Hegseth, le général Dan Caine et un décret de Donald Trump de décembre 2025 sur la supériorité spatiale. Il en attribue en partie la cause aux ambitions lunaires chinoises.
	
Il n'y avait aucune discussion sur le cislunaire, et on m'a dit en gros : ne parlez pas de cislunaire, arrêtez d'y toucher.
Les moyens restent modestes. Air & Space Forces Magazine note que la Space Force n'y a consacré que peu de planification, de crédits et de personnel. Un bureau de coordination cislunaire a ouvert en avril 2026, dirigé par Jaime Stearns, avec la NASA comme principal partenaire. Le laboratoire de recherche de l'armée de l'air prépare de son côté un appel à projets de 30 millions de dollars pour le printemps.
Lune, Chine et traité de l'espace : ce que cela change
Washington et Pékin visent chacune une base près du pôle sud lunaire, riche en glace d'eau. La NASA travaille à un séjour durable sur la Lune, et la Space Force veut y apporter surveillance et communications. Pékin avance aussi : les avancées du programme lunaire habité chinois comptent deux tests cruciaux réussis, et la Chine mène par ailleurs des activités spatiales encore mystérieuses.
	
Le champ de bataille moderne s'étend des fonds marins à l'espace cislunaire.
Le général Caine n'a pas nommé la Chine ce jour-là, précise Space.com. Le droit international encadre pourtant ce terrain. Le traité de l'espace de 1967 interdit de placer des armes nucléaires ou de destruction massive en orbite ou sur la Lune. Il interdit aussi d'y établir des bases militaires, de tester des armes ou de conduire des manœuvres, selon son texte officiel. Il n'interdit pas les satellites militaires, ni expressément les armes classiques en orbite. L'avis du Pentagone ne présente pas ces cinq satellites comme des armes.
Reste à connaître leur charge utile, leur budget et leur calendrier réel. Pour l'instant, le Pentagone sonde l'industrie, et les premières études, si elles sont lancées, démarreraient début 2027.

articles.title: Vibe coding meets governance with APEXlang abstraction - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
As AI takes over coding, Oracle rethinks how applications are built
As vibe coding moves from novelty to everyday practice, enterprises face a new problem: Machine-generated software still has to be maintained, governed and understood by people.
Low-code platforms were built to speed up application development, and AI is now rewriting that mission. Oracle Corp. previewed its answer ahead of its annual conference, and the tipping point for software development has already arrived, according to Mike Hichwa (pictured), senior vice president of software engineering at Oracle.
“In 2025, the majority of code was human-authored, and in 2026 and forever afterwards, the majority of code is going to be machine-generated,” Hichwa said. “We’re probably not going back. What we’ve done to address this change is we invented our own language. We call it APEXlang.”
Hichwa spoke with theCUBE Research’s Dave Vellante at Oracle AI World, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed vibe coding and the need to maintain and govern AI-generated code. (* Disclosure below.)
Vibe coding meets enterprise governance
APEXlang is a highly abstracted application definition language that captures intent rather than implementation. Oracle introduced it with the APEX AI Application Generator and is publishing its grammar, skills and documentation in the public domain so coding agents such as Anthropic PBC’s Claude and OpenAI Group PBC’s Codex can generate it. Oracle is also working with OpenAI to train models to generate the language more efficiently, Hichwa explained.
“What you’re generating actually matters, because once you generate it, and you generate it 100 times or 1,000 times within your enterprise, then you’re going to need to maintain it. You’re going to need to look after it,” Hichwa said. “What people want with their portfolio of applications, they want consistency, they want governance, they want ease of understanding.”
Governance comes from the runtime, too. Generated APEXlang is interpreted by the APEX engine, which Oracle patches and updates monthly, so customers don’t have to revisit what they built. The same design is meant to curb AI slop, since a compact definition is easier to read than sprawling generated code, according to Hichwa.
“What we’re generating is much, much smaller, much more human understandable, so it is less sloppy because it is more abstracted,” Hichwa said. “It’s like a CliffsNotes. It’s not the full book.”

articles.title: Top password manager mSecure tells users to change passwords immediately
articles.text:
Top password manager mSecure tells users to change passwords immediately
Users synced with its cloud service might be at risk
- mSecure disclosed a breach involving an encrypted cloud database containing data from current and former users
- Company urged users to rotate critical passwords, MFA methods, and passkeys despite no evidence vaults were decrypted
- Customer criticism grew after limited initial disclosure left uncertainty about the incident’s scope and impact
Top password manager mSecure has confirmed it suffered a data breach and, “out of an abundance of caution”, and told its customers to simply reset everything, leaving some pretty upset.
On November 3 2026, the company behind mSecure, called mSeven Software, sent an email to its customers, saying it “recently learned of suspicious activity associated with the mSecure password management application”. It soon launched an investigation, mitigated the issue, and brought in third-party cybersecurity experts to assist.
The notice, while rather sparse on details, urged customers to “immediately take steps to protect all confidential information stored within the mSecure password management application. This may include changing passwords, resetting or re-enrolling two factor authentication methods, or removing existing passkeys."
Encrypted database
All this was said without detailing what happened, and customers did not take it well. On Reddit, users were asking if this pertained just to the master password, or to all passwords stored inside the manager. Some people have hundreds of secrets locked away in mSecure, and changing all of them would take hours.
“This notice is wildly insufficient,” one user wrote. “Recommending potentially hundreds of credential changes without identifying the underlying threat, the affected customers, or the security of the application being used to make those changes is inadequate.”
mSecure allegedly responded with a follow-up notice that was also shared on social media. In it, it disclosed more details, and somewhat played down the actual breach:
“Yesterday, mSeven learned that an unauthorized actor acquired an encrypted copy of a database containing information belonging to current and former users of the mSecure password management application,” it said. “Importantly, mSeven has no evidence that the unauthorized actor has accessed the confidential information stored within the database in the mSecure Cloud.”
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Putting it plainly, a threat actor walked away with a copy of the database that was sitting in mSecure Cloud, and all users - current and former - who had synced their password manager with the cloud service are at risk.
But mSeven tried to downplay the severity of the incident. Throughout the announcement, it repeated multiple times that the stolen database was encrypted and that there is no evidence that the threat actors managed to decrypt it. Truth be told, encrypted databases should be safe, but many criminals are still hoarding them, in case anyone makes a breakthrough at any point in time. There’s actually a name to the practice - HNDL (harvest now, decrypt later).
It also responded to user criticism about having to change all passwords now:
“As a standard best practice, mSeven continues to recommend that mSecure customers change their master password, change vital stored passwords, reset two-factor authentication methods, replace passkeys and any other sensitive information. This should be a part of all routine security practices.”
Not the only password manager in trouble
Finally, mSecure said deleting the app won’t help the situation and stressed that the issue only pertains to users that were syncing with the mSecure Cloud.
“mSeven takes the security and privacy of all information stored on the mSecure platform very seriously and has no evidence that mSecure is not currently safe for use,” it said. “Our support team is working as fast as possible to respond to customer questions. We take your trust in us seriously, and appreciate your patience and continued support.”
How this reflects the company’s image remains to be seen. One Reddit user said the company was deleting negative reviews and complaints that were being left on the Google Play Store. But mSecure is hardly the only password manager experiencing an incident such as this one. In June this year LastPass confirmed losing sensitive customer data, while Dashlane said hackers obtained at least a dozen encrypted vaults.

articles.title: L'astuce de Tencent pour contourner l’embargo US sur l'IA vient de voler en éclats
articles.text:
Le géant chinois devait accéder à quelque 100 000 puces d’IA installées en Asie du Sud-Est. Selon le Financial Times, les pressions américaines auraient fait échouer l’accord avec Oracle, tandis que les autorités chinoises invitaient Tencent à privilégier les fabricants locaux.
Le cloud n’aura pas permis à Tencent d’échapper à la rivalité entre Washington et Pékin. D’après les informations publiées ce 4 novembre par le Financial Times et reprises par Reuters, Oracle aurait abandonné un contrat de location de puces estimé à 7 milliards de dollars après des interventions de l’administration Trump.
Louer la puissance de calcul sans importer les puces
L’accord prévoyait cinq ans de location dans plusieurs centres de données d’Oracle en Asie du Sud-Est. Il aurait donné à Tencent l’accès à environ 100 000 processeurs d’IA de pointe et constituait, selon le quotidien britannique, son plus important engagement de ce type à l’étranger.
Le principe était de laisser les serveurs chez Oracle et de les utiliser à distance pour les travaux d’IA de Tencent. Le groupe aurait ainsi pu exploiter des puces indisponibles en Chine en raison des restrictions américaines et chinoises, sans les faire entrer sur son territoire.
Des pressions des deux côtés
Des responsables américains auraient contacté Oracle pour lui faire part de leurs inquiétudes sur cet accord. Le groupe aurait ensuite renoncé au contrat, selon les personnes proches du dossier citées par le FT.
Tencent aurait également reçu la visite de hauts responsables du Guangdong, la province où il est implanté. Leur demande était de soutenir les fabricants chinois de puces. L’entreprise devait donc composer avec un Washington soucieux de limiter son accès aux technologies américaines et des autorités chinoises désireuses de favoriser leur propre industrie.
Si cette annulation de contrat se confirme, Tencent devra trouver une autre façon d’obtenir la puissance de calcul IA recherchée. L’épisode montre aussi les limites du cloud : même lorsque les serveurs sont hébergés en Asie du Sud-Est, leur accès reste exposé aux pressions de Washington.
Sources : Financial Times et Reuters

articles.title: Google invertirá USD 15.000 millones en Malasia para centros de datos, energía y agua
articles.text:
Google invertirá USD 15.000 millones en Malasia entre 2027 y 2028 para construir centros de datos, sumar energía limpia, reforzar el suministro de agua y capacitar trabajadores, según el comunicado la empresa publicado el 4 de noviembre en Kuala Lumpur, en un acto con el primer ministro Anwar Ibrahim.
El plan incluye nuevos campus en los estados de Selangor y Negeri Sembilan. Se suman al primero, ubicado en el parque empresarial Elmina, en Selangor, que ya funciona. La cifra amplía los USD 2.000 millones que la empresa anunció en 2024 para infraestructura digital en el país.
Ruth Porat, presidenta y directora de inversiones de Alphabet y Google, dijo que la inversión busca dar capacidad de cómputo al país y, a la vez, sumar recursos locales de energía y agua a medida que las operaciones crezcan.
Según el comunicado de Google, la construcción aportará en promedio USD 1.100 millones por año al producto interno bruto de Malasia y sostendrá más de 37.000 empleos anuales. Cuando los centros operen, mantendrán más de 9.000 puestos por año, con salarios 45% superiores a la mediana nacional.
Quién paga la electricidad y el agua
Google afirmó que pagará el 100% de la electricidad que consuman sus campus y los costos directos de conexión a la red, de acuerdo con su comunicado oficial. También prevé sumar más de un gigavatio de capacidad de energía limpia, mediante una colaboración con la empresa eléctrica Tenaga Nasional.
Anwar destacó ese punto en su discurso. Dijo que la empresa financia su propia energía sin subsidio público y que la prueba de un inversor responsable es si deja al país anfitrión más fuerte y resiliente. Al ser consultado por las preocupaciones ambientales, respondió que las condiciones del Gobierno fueron impuestas y Google las aceptó, recogió The Sun Malaysia.
En agua, la empresa anunció un embalse fuera del cauce y una planta de tratamiento sobre el río Linggi, en Negeri Sembilan. Anwar precisó que el proyecto entregará 65 millones de litros de agua potable por día, ayudará a controlar inundaciones en la temporada de monzones y pasará a manos del gobierno estatal una vez terminado.
El 2 de noviembre, Google había informado una inversión de USD 160 millones para esa obra, que construirá la empresa Gamuda, según el diario The Sun Malaysia.
Los centros de datos presionan la red eléctrica
Malasia concentra más de la mitad de la capacidad de centros de datos en construcción del sudeste asiático, según la consultora DC Byte citada por AFP. El Fondo Monetario Internacional prevé que su economía crezca 5,2% en 2026, en parte por esa actividad.
El costo en recursos es parte del debate. En julio, el viceprimer ministro dijo ante el Parlamento que, hacia 2035, los centros de datos consumirán un tercio de toda la energía del país. El Gobierno afirmó entonces que solo aprobaría proyectos con suministro suficiente de electricidad y agua.
En capacitación, Google anunció cuatro programas para formar a 800.000 malasios en cinco años. Uno de ellos, los Data Center Institutes, comenzará en 2027 y preparará personal técnico para instalar y operar centros de datos.

articles.title: Critical Rails Flaw Lets Attackers Write Server Files via Crafted ImageMagick Uploads
articles.text:
A critical flaw in Ruby on Rails could allow an unauthenticated attacker to write arbitrary files on an app's server by uploading a crafted file if the app processes uploads using ImageMagick. The Rails project disclosed the flaw in an advisory and fixed it in versions 8.1.4.1 and 8.0.5.2.
The flaw is in Active Storage, the part of Rails that handles file uploads. Some apps store uploaded files using Active Storage's Disk service, which stores them on the server's disk. In those apps, an attacker could also read any file the app can read.
Those files typically include the app's secret_key_base and its credentials for other systems, according to Rails. Reading them may in turn allow remote code execution or lateral movement into those systems.
Rails rates the flaw 9.8 out of 10 on the CVSS scale. It is tracked as GHSA-f3w6-w445-fwh9 and does not yet have a CVE identifier.
ImageMagick selects a format handler, which it calls a coder, based on the file's content. Some coders act on other files named inside the image, not on the image itself. Active Storage imposes no limits on which coders an upload can use, so the server's own ImageMagick policy was the only limit.
The ImageMagick analyzer in Active Storage runs when a file is attached. Attaching the upload is enough to reach the flaw. The app does not have to make a variant (a transformed copy of the image) or a preview, or call analyze.
An uploaded SVG file reached ImageMagick's MSL coder through that analyzer, according to the commit that fixed the flaw. MSL is a scripting coder that reads and writes files named by its script.
Rails said one attack chain was reported to it, but it does "not assume it is the only one that exists." The advisory does not say whether the flaw has been exploited.
The flaw was reported through HackerOne by RyotaK, a researcher at GMO Flatt Security.
Which Rails Apps Are Affected
An app is affected only if all three of these are true:
- It uses ImageMagick for Active Storage image processing. That is the setting config.active_storage.variant_processor = :mini_magick, the default for apps on load_defaults 6.1 or earlier.
- Its ImageMagick security policy does not already block the coders involved. Rails says the policies that Debian and Ubuntu ship do not.
- It accepts file uploads from untrusted users.
To check the first condition, look at config.active_storage.variant_processor. If it is not set, the default depends on load_defaults: :mini_magick before 7.0, and :vips from 7.0 on. The same setting decides which library analyzes uploads, not only which one makes variants.
Every Active Storage version before 8.0.5.2 is affected, as are 8.1 versions before 8.1.4.1. Release series older than 8.0 are no longer supported, and Rails will not release fixed versions for them.
In July, Rails fixed a different critical Active Storage flaw, CVE-2026-66066, which affected apps that use libvips instead of ImageMagick. Apps using ImageMagick were not exposed to that flaw's attack path, but they can be exposed to this one.
The same releases fix a second Active Storage flaw, GHSA-v924-7rp8-4mxh, which Rails rates high with a CVSS score of 8.8. Active Storage passed uploads to ImageMagick and FFmpeg under temporary file names that kept the uploaded file's extension.
Those tools can pick a decoder from the extension when a file's content does not show its format. So an attacker who chose an upload's filename and declared its content type could choose the decoder that processes it.
What to Do
Rails strongly recommends upgrading as soon as possible. The two releases fix 21 security issues in total.
The fixed versions ship an ImageMagick security policy. MiniMagick is the Ruby gem Active Storage uses to call ImageMagick. In its default setup, every ImageMagick command it runs applies the policy, not only commands from Active Storage.
The policy blocks the MSL coder; coders that read or delete files other than the image; coders that fetch remote or local references or display them on a screen; every coder backed by Ghostscript, along with the gs delegate; and @filename indirection.
- Upgrade to Rails 8.1.4.1 or 8.0.5.2. Apps on :mini_magick also need mini_magick 5.1 or later, or they raise an error at boot. Rails 8.0 gets security fixes only until November 7, 2026, under its maintenance policy.
- Confirm that the app loads the new policy, as the Active Storage guide describes, by running bin/rails runner 'puts MiniMagick.identify { |i| i.list "policy" }'.
- Check whether the shipped policy reaches the app at all. It does not reach an app that replaces MiniMagick.cli_env after boot, clears the environment with MiniMagick.cli_prefix, or installs its own MiniMagick::Shell. Such an app must put the rules in ImageMagick's system policy.
- Apps that use GraphicsMagick get no protection from the shipped policy, because GraphicsMagick does not read ImageMagick policies.
- Check the server's own ImageMagick policy. The shipped policy adds to it rather than replacing it. A rule there that allows a coder, including a wildcard such as pattern="*", overrides the shipped policy's block on that coder.
- If the app renders PDF or PostScript files through ImageMagick, re-allow the gs delegate and the coders it uses in the server's policy.xml.
- If you cannot upgrade yet, copy the rules of the shipped policy, activestorage/lib/active_storage/image_magick/policy.xml, into ImageMagick's system policy, such as /etc/ImageMagick-7/policy.xml. At a minimum, block the MSL coder, the Ghostscript coders, and the gs delegate. Rails also published the fix as patches for 8.1 and 8.0.
- Apps on release series older than 8.0 can use that workaround or upgrade to 8.0 or later.
- Rails' workarounds for the second flaw only change how FFmpeg is used. None of them covers ImageMagick.
- If the app stores attachments with the Disk service, change secret_key_base and every other secret the app process can read. That includes the master key, everything config/credentials.yml.enc holds, storage and database credentials, and third-party tokens. Do not keep an exposed secret as a fallback.
The advisory does not explain how to check whether an app has already been targeted.

articles.title: The semantic layer turns lakehouses into AI decision backbones - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Oracle rethinks the lakehouse as AI agents become data consumers
A shared semantic layer is fast becoming the dividing line between lakehouses built for reporting and those built for artificial intelligence.
As AI agents join human analysts in querying corporate data, enterprises need platforms that make sense of information scattered across clouds, formats and rival systems. Oracle Corp. has spent the past year rebuilding its data stack around that shift, part of a broader database modernization push. The company now pitches its Autonomous AI Lakehouse as an open layer that sits across an enterprise’s existing data estate rather than replacing it, according to Nipun Agarwal (pictured), senior vice president of software engineering, Oracle Database, at Oracle.
“Lakehouses were the platform which customers use for running analytics,” Agarwal said. “Now, lakehouses have become the decision backbone for AI.”
Agarwal spoke with theCUBE’s Dave Vellante at Oracle AI World, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed how Oracle’s Autonomous AI Lakehouse combines a shared semantic layer with fast, real-time access to data across platforms to support AI agents. (* Disclosure below.)
Building an open semantic layer across catalogs
Oracle’s approach rests on a catalog that can mount other catalogs, such as Databricks Inc.’s Unity Catalog, along with Postgres and MySQL databases, so data is queried in place rather than copied. The company announced a business semantic layer and broader Apache Iceberg support at the October event, with table and column descriptions the system generates applying to non-Oracle sources as well, according to Agarwal. Crucially, Oracle does not see the offering as competing with other lakehouses, he added.
“We really believe that for any enterprise, they’re gonna have a choice,” he said. “They’re gonna be using multiple data sources. They’ll have multiple lakehouses.”
Oracle’s Lake Cache speeds up queries by moving the most-used Iceberg tables into Exadata’s flash cache. Real-time access is also becoming essential as software agents become the main consumers of the data: Scheduled refreshes of copied data can fall short when agents request it on demand, according to Agarwal.
“With AI that’s no longer the case, because for AI, the consumer is not a human necessarily,” Agarwal said. “The need for real-time access is a lot more with AI.”

articles.title: ‘Search and AI are deeply integrated’ — Google says schools can't have Search without AI, and that should worry the rest of us
articles.text:
‘Search and AI are deeply integrated’ — Google says schools can't have Search without AI, and that should worry the rest of us
AI in Google is non-optional for schools
- Google is offering schools more control over how students use and interact with AI
- There is a caveat though: schools that opt-out of using AI will not have access to Google search
- The company has deeply integrated AI within its search platform
Google recently laid out plans to offer AI Guided Learning as part of its Classroom offerings for schools. But schools that opt out of AI could be blocked from using Google Search entirely, posing big problems for education without AI.
For example, New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani has banned AI use in some schools meaning that they would be effectively cut off from using Google Search. “Google is trying to use its monopoly power to force AI into our public schools,” Mamdani wrote on X.
You wouldn’t think it would be so difficult to have a switch that either shows or hides Google’s AI overview, but the search engine giant announced that “Google Search is now AI Search” at Google I/O in June, and Google vice president for education Chris Phillips has confirmed that “Search and AI are deeply integrated.”
No search without AI
As outlined in Google’s blog post, titled “Designing responsible AI for learning,” school administrators will have the ability to control student access to Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom, and Google Search, alongside updates to how AI Mode and AI Overviews are displayed on school accounts to avoid simply providing the answer to schoolwork.
“Our goal is simple: provide school leaders the control and confidence to use AI products in classrooms as they see fit,” the blog post states. But if a school doesn’t want to use AI at all, they could be cut off from the biggest search engine in the world.
The ultimatum over AI in schools has raised questions about Google’s control over the search market — questions that could bring even more antitrust lawsuits against the company.
Former Federal Trade Commission Chair Lina Khan wrote on X that Google’s control over search shows “the danger of allowing an unregulated monopolist to control an essential service.”
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Even Senator Bernie Sanders chimed in on Google's decision, stating that "Google is threatening schools," and saying that the decision to remove search from schools that opt-out of AI is "extortion."
The future of AI apparently isn’t optional
Those who prefer to take a non-AI approach to life might be in for a shock in the coming years. AI is being plugged into every new service and device, making it near impossible to avoid.
Of course, you can use Google the old-fashioned way by simply ignoring the AI Summary and finding the answers yourself (which many websites would prefer), but the separation between a service and its AI “enhancements” are going to become increasingly blurred.
As angry as people are getting over sprawling AI data centers and the effect the technology is having on the job market, there are trillions of dollars riding on AI’s success - and that matters more to billionaires and corporations than their perception in the eyes of the public.
The dangers of becoming too reliant on AI are already beginning to show, especially when it comes to critical thinking and AI psychosis, so there are worrying questions that need to be asked about AI use in education.
