articles.title: Ce logiciel gratuit veut recréer des jeux vidéo, sites et applications avec l'IA
articles.text:
Étudier le fonctionnement d'un logiciel pour en fabriquer une nouvelle version, sans forcément toucher à son code : c'est la proposition de Craft Anything, un outil gratuit qui associe rétro-ingénierie et agents de programmation IA.
Développé par ArtCraft, à l'origine d'une suite de logiciels créatifs libres, Craft Anything a fait ses débuts publics fin octobre. Disponible sur Windows, macOS et Linux, cet outil écrit en Rust propose d'analyser un site web, une application ou un jeu vidéo, puis de confier sa reconstruction à un agent de programmation. L'objectif n'est pas simplement de générer du code à partir d'une consigne, mais de s'appuyer sur des observations concrètes pour reproduire certaines caractéristiques du programme original.
- Inspection de plusieurs types de contenus
- Observations associées à des preuves
- Comparaison avec demandes de modifications
Observer, reconstruire, comparer : comment fonctionne Craft Anything ?
Craft Anything organise son fonctionnement autour de quatre étapes. La première consiste à étudier le logiciel de référence, à l'aide d'outils capables d'examiner son apparence, ses interactions et, selon les autorisations accordées, sa structure interne. Le projet intègre également un serveur MCP et une interface en ligne de commande pour permettre aux agents IA d'utiliser directement ses outils d'analyse.
Deux modes d'inspection sont proposés. Le premier, baptisé « Clean Room », se limite aux éléments observables de l'extérieur : captures d'écran, textes affichés, disposition des interfaces ou interactions visibles. Le principe revient à demander à un développeur de reproduire une interface à partir de son comportement et de son apparence, sans lui fournir les fichiers d'origine.
Le mode « Deep » va plus loin en autorisant l'inspection des fichiers, du code et de certains éléments internes du programme. Il peut notamment s'appuyer sur Ghidra, un outil de rétro-ingénierie, pour approfondir l'analyse des exécutables.
Une fois les informations collectées, Craft Anything transmet ses observations à un agent de programmation chargé de créer un nouveau projet. L'utilisateur peut préciser le langage ou le moteur souhaité, notamment Unity, Unreal Engine ou Godot pour les jeux vidéo.
Le résultat est ensuite comparé à la référence afin d'identifier les écarts et de proposer des corrections. Pour les sites web, le logiciel effectue notamment des vérifications visuelles sur trois largeurs d'écran, tandis que les applications et les jeux disposent de contrôles encore moins aboutis.
Des résultats encourageants, mais une reconstruction encore expérimentale
Craft Anything est distribué gratuitement sous double licence MIT et Apache 2.0. Le projet reste néanmoins en phase alpha, avec une version 0.3.0 publiée le 2 novembre. Toutes ses capacités ne sont donc pas encore au même niveau de maturité, particulièrement lorsqu'il s'agit de reproduire le comportement d'un programme.
Les premiers essais documentés par les développeurs donnent une idée des possibilités actuelles. Sur un site web, Craft Anything a obtenu 96 % de ressemblance visuelle avec l'original. Une petite application a également été reconstruite en Rust, mais sa vérification s'est limitée à la compilation du programme. Quant à l'essai réalisé sur un jeu vidéo, il a été interrompu avant la phase de contrôle.
Ces résultats internes ne garantissent donc pas une reproduction fidèle dans tous les cas. Une interface visuellement identique peut conserver des fonctions défaillantes, et les contrôles comportementaux des applications et des jeux restent partiellement développés.
Autre limite à connaître : Craft Anything ne génère pas lui-même le code. Il s'appuie sur un agent de programmation externe, principalement Claude Code, dont l'utilisation peut entraîner des frais supplémentaires. D'autres intégrations existent, notamment pour Codex, mais toutes n'ont pas encore été validées en conditions réelles. Anthropic a par ailleurs récemment renforcé les restrictions de Claude Code concernant la reproduction de jeux vidéo existants, ce qui peut limiter certains projets.
L'intérêt de Craft Anything réside ainsi dans sa capacité à réunir l'analyse, la reconstruction et les vérifications au sein d'un même environnement. Une approche intéressante pour expérimenter la rétro-ingénierie assistée par IA, à condition de travailler sur des logiciels que l'on est autorisé à examiner.
Reste à distinguer la copie qui ressemble à l'original de celle qui fonctionne réellement comme lui.
- Inspection de plusieurs types de contenus
- Observations associées à des preuves
- Comparaison avec demandes de modifications

articles.title: L’iPhone 18 s’inspirerait directement des iPhone 18 Pro sur deux points clés, au risque de faire grimper la facture
articles.text:
iPhone 18 : du nouveau pour l’autonomie et les performances, mais un prix bien éloigné de l’iPhone 17
L’iPhone 18 irait piocher dans deux nouveautés issues des iPhone 18 Pro pour se démarquer de l’iPhone 17. Cela aurait cependant un prix, qui ferait toujours plus grincer des dents. Merci la pénurie de mémoire liée à l’IA.
Alors que les iPhone 18 Pro et l’iPhone Duo sont arrivés en septembre, le modèle standard se fait attendre. Prévu pour le printemps 2027 aux côtés des iPhone 18e et Air 2, ses deux principales nouveautés viennent d’ailleurs d’être confirmées par une nouvelle rumeur, entre autonomie prolongée et puissance accrue. Seul hic, la facture serait rehaussée d’une centaine d’euros.
Une hausse de prix en échange d’une autonomie et de performance supérieures à l’iPhone 17
Sur le réseau social Weibo, le leaker Digital Chat Station vient de détailler la fiche technique du prochain modèle standard d’Apple, sensiblement amélioré par rapport à la génération lancée en 2025. Pour commencer, on apprend que l’iPhone 18 embarquerait une batterie plus imposante que celle de l’iPhone 17 (3 692 mAh). Apple appliquerait ainsi la même recette que sur les dernières déclinaisons Pro, qui ont profité d’accumulateurs plus grands.
Pour rappel, les versions dotées d’un tiroir SIM physique ont vu leur capacité grimper à 4 056 mAh (+1,7 %) sur le 18 Pro et 5 391 mAh (+11,8 %) sur le 18 Pro Max. Sachant que le format de l’iPhone 18 est quasi similaire à celui de l’iPhone 18 Pro, il faudrait donc s’attendre à une capacité approchant la barre des 3 800 à 4 000 mAh.
Sous le capot, le smartphone profiterait d’une puce A20. Bien que distincte de la version A20 Pro réservée à ses grands frères, elle bénéficierait elle aussi de la dernière finesse de gravure en 2 nanomètres de TSMC. Ce saut technologique promettrait ainsi un gain notable en termes d’efficacité énergétique et de puissance par rapport à son prédécesseur.
Le reste de l’équipement miserait sur la continuité. On retrouverait une dalle Oled haute résolution de 6,3 pouces rafraîchie jusqu’à 120 Hz, un double module photo arrière de 48 mégapixels ainsi que Face ID logé dans une Dynamic Island de taille inchangée, contrairement à celle des iPhone 18 Pro.
Reste la question qui fâche : le prix. Toujours selon l’informateur, ces améliorations s’accompagneraient d’une nouvelle hausse tarifaire. Il faut dire que cela a déjà été le cas avec les iPhone 18 Pro et 18 Pro Max, qui affichent un prix de départ supérieur avec 150 € d’augmentation chacun par rapport aux iPhone 17 Pro et 17 Pro Max. Une hausse similaire aurait donc toutes ses chances d’arriver, sauf si Apple estime que le rehaussement tarifaire de l’iPhone 17 opéré en septembre 2026 a déjà suffi (de 969 € à 1 119 €).
Une envolée des coûts due en grande partie à la pénurie mondiale de mémoire vive, directement asséchée par la course effrénée aux infrastructures d’intelligence artificielle.

articles.title: Apple admitió que “es posible que no logre resolver todos los fallos de la IA antes de que se produzcan”
articles.text:
Apple advirtió que la inteligencia artificial (IA) puede ejecutar acciones no autorizadas y que quizá no consiga corregir todos los fallos antes de que ocurran, un riesgo que podría provocar daños reputacionales, financieros y legales para la compañía.
La empresa incluyó esa evaluación en su resumen anual remitido a la Comisión de Mercado y Valores de Estados Unidos. La tecnológica reconoció que la IA ya está integrada en sus productos, servicios, operaciones y actividades internas.
Sus iniciativas con esta tecnología, señaló, pueden derivar en acciones no intencionadas de sistemas autónomos o agénticos, es decir, capaces de realizar tareas con cierto grado de autonomía.
“Aunque la compañía está comprometida con el desarrollo y la implementación responsables de la IA, es posible que no logre identificar o resolver todos los posibles problemas y fallos antes de que se produzcan”, sostuvo Apple.
La advertencia abarca tanto las herramientas propias como las desarrolladas por terceros. Según la empresa, estas tecnologías pueden comportarse de forma inesperada o impredecible, actuar sin una orden, exceder los permisos otorgados, desobedecer instrucciones o resistirse a seguirlas.
Por qué Apple dice que es difícil controlar a la inteligencia artificial
Los sistemas pueden ocultar acciones, retener o manipular información y producir resultados inexactos o engañosos. Apple alertó que el carácter no determinista de muchas de estas herramientas dificulta prever, controlar, probar y auditar su comportamiento.
La acumulación de errores puede tener efectos difíciles o imposibles de revertir, como la eliminación de datos o la ejecución de transacciones. La compañía admitió que su capacidad para supervisar y controlar a los agentes de IA y otras tecnologías externas puede ser limitada.
Además, sus políticas y mecanismos de control podrían no avanzar al mismo ritmo que estas herramientas ni impedir o detectar a tiempo un uso indebido.
La empresa anticipó una gran incertidumbre sobre los marcos jurídicos y regulatorios, el escrutinio de legisladores y autoridades, los gastos de adaptación y las preocupaciones éticas de los consumidores.
En el aspecto económico, Apple cerró el ejercicio fiscal 2026, que no coincide con el año calendario, con récords de beneficios y facturación. Sin embargo, sus acciones cayeron 2% tras sus previsiones de margen bruto para la temporada navideña, en un escenario de escasez de chips de memoria.
Cómo ve el CEO de Apple el desarrollo de inteligencia artificial en la compañía
El director ejecutivo de Apple, John Ternus, descartó que los agentes autónomos de IA sustituyan a las aplicaciones tradicionales o transformen por completo el ecosistema de la compañía. El ingeniero afirmó que el diseño de productos seguirá dependiendo de las personas.
“Supongo que eso podría facilitarnos mucho la vida, pero la creación de productos es algo profundamente humano y personal”, dijo Ternus a Wired. Su posición parte de que la tecnología puede asistir en procesos concretos sin desplazar la decisión humana sobre qué dispositivos desarrollar.
Ternus llegó al máximo cargo de Apple a los 51 años, después de 25 años en la empresa dedicados a la ingeniería de hardware. Fue designado a principios de septiembre de 2026 en reemplazo de Tim Cook.
Su primera aparición pública como director ejecutivo fue durante el Apple Keynote 2026, donde presentó el iPhone Duo y el iPhone 18 Pro. Más tarde participó en un evento de lanzamiento de los nuevos MacBook Pro táctil y iPad Mini.
De qué forma Apple ha utilizado inteligencia artificial
La compañía utiliza IA para desarrollar componentes de sus dispositivos, incluida la bisagra del iPhone Duo. Para Ternus, el criterio decisivo no es el método de producción, sino la respuesta de los usuarios: “¿Hemos creado algo que realmente les encante?”.
Asimismo, Apple mantendrá su prioridad en el hardware y la experiencia de uso, incluso después de haber quedado rezagada durante los últimos dos años en la competencia por la inteligencia artificial generativa. La empresa pospuso hasta este verano la actualización de Siri, su asistente de voz.
“Todo el mundo tiene su opinión. A mí me gusta mucho dónde estamos”, afirmó Ternus. El ejecutivo sostuvo que Apple no incorporará IA sin una finalidad concreta y que, si la integración es adecuada, los usuarios no deberían detenerse a pensar si una función fue realizada por inteligencia artificial o por software tradicional.

articles.title: Quantum-resistant cryptography: Oracle says to act now - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Oracle urges database customers to prepare for quantum security risks
Attackers can copy encrypted traffic today and decrypt it once quantum computers mature, making quantum-resistant cryptography a present-day concern.
Oracle Corp. is applying the philosophy behind its security controls beneath AI agents to encryption across database fleets, according to Vipin Samar (pictured), senior vice president of software engineering, database security, at Oracle.
“Even though we don’t have quantum computers which are sufficiently powerful today, when they come, that can create a risk because people can make a copy of your encrypted data today,” Samar said. “Your TLS 1.2 traffic, 1.3 traffic, I can make a copy of it. And then when quantum becomes available, I can figure out the session key and decrypt … your entire sensitive data.”
Samar spoke with theCUBE Research’s Dave Vellante at Oracle AI World, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed security concerns related to quantum-resistant cryptography. (* Disclosure below.)
Quantum-resistant cryptography starts with fleet-level visibility
Oracle’s new Cryptographic Posture Assessment in Oracle Data Safe assesses cryptographic configurations across database fleets, flagging weak spots such as lingering TLS 1.0 and 1.1 support. Agentic AI-driven remediation is in preview, Samar noted.
“It doesn’t help if network encryption is strong, but other parts are actually on the weaker side. And this becomes a challenge, especially when PQC or the quantum computers come along because they can attempt to hack into any of those systems,” Samar said.
Deep Data Security, which enforces row- and column-level access in Oracle AI Database 26ai, uses signed OAuth2 tokens to identify the end user behind an AI agent’s query. Oracle treats AI as one more application accessing the same data.
“We said instead of sprinkling this dust everywhere, why don’t we secure at the source?” Samar said. “When you move something inside the database, you get great security because there are no ways to bypass it.”

articles.title: Xen Hypervisor Flaws Let One Malicious VM Read and Write Any Other VM's Memory
articles.text:
Two flaws in the Xen hypervisor allow a malicious guest virtual machine (VM) to read and write the memory of other VMs on the same host, including dom0.
Dom0 is the VM that, by default, has full permissions and manages the others. Patches are out, and there is no known mitigation, the Xen Project said in an advisory on November 3.
All Xen versions from 4.6 onward are vulnerable, while 4.5 and earlier are not. The flaws are tracked as CVE-2026-102703 and CVE-2026-102704, under Xen advisory XSA-523.
The Xen Project credited AI company Anthropic with finding the flaws using its Claude model. Stephan Lipp of Ada Logics then validated the finding, and the CodeAnt AI Security Research Team later independently reported the same issue.
The flaws are in grant copy, the operation Xen uses to copy data between VMs. Each VM tells Xen which of its memory pages other VMs may use, and Xen checks those permissions.
To save time on a batch of copies within the same memory page, Xen reuses checks it has already made. In some cases, it did not check again when it should have. That mistake is what lets a malicious guest read and write memory it does not own.
XCP-ng, an open-source virtualization platform built around Xen, said in its update notes that "a single compromised guest can break out of its isolation and take over the whole host."
Xen's advisory does not mention any attacks that exploit the flaws or specify what access within the VM an attacker needs.
Qubes OS is a security-focused desktop operating system that keeps software in separate Xen-based compartments called qubes. A bulletin said that every supported release and configuration is affected. Its fix is for Qubes 4.3, the only release it still supports.
Because every Xen version from 4.6 on is vulnerable, other products built on those versions are affected until their makers add the XSA-523 patches. As of November 4, Debian's security tracker listed the xen package in its bookworm, trixie, and forky releases as vulnerable, and in sid as fixed.
Fixes and Restarts by Platform
These are the fixes published so far:
- Xen source: the advisory has patches for xen-unstable to Xen 4.19.x, and for Xen 4.18.x to 4.17.x.
- Xen 4.6 to 4.16: the advisory has no patch for these versions. Xen 4.16's security support ended on December 2, 2024.
- XCP-ng 8.3: xen-4.17.7-4.2.xcpng8.3, released November 3. Hosts must be rebooted. Vates, which backs XCP-ng, rates the impact as Critical.
- Qubes OS 4.3: Xen packages 4.19.6-3 in dom0. Dom0 must be restarted, and Anti Evil Maid users must reseal their secret passphrase because the new Xen binaries change PCR18 and PCR19.
Qubes told users on November 3 to keep installing updates as normal. The fixed packages were then in its security-testing repository, due to move to the stable one over the next two weeks after community testing.
XSA-523 is separate from XSA-500, an earlier grant copy flaw that Xen disclosed on July 28, and it has its own patches.

articles.title: Abonnements IA à prix cassés pour les clients, factures à un million pour les entreprises : le LLMJacking, nouveau business des pirates
articles.text:
Des pirates ont trouvé comment revendre à bas prix l'accès aux modèles d'IA les plus coûteux, sans débourser un centime pour leur utilisation. Leur secret ? Faire payer les entreprises dont ils ont volé les accès. Un trafic qui prend de l'ampleur.
Plus de 500 000 requêtes envoyées à des modèles d'IA en moins de huit heures, pour près d'un million de dollars de consommation. Derrière cette facture astronomique, une entreprise qui n'avait rien demandé, et des pirates qui utilisaient ses identifiants pour alimenter leur propre service d'abonnement à l'IA. L'affaire, documentée par le Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) et Mandiant dans une enquête publiée le 2 novembre, témoigne de l'essor du LLMJacking, une pratique qui consiste à détourner les ressources d'IA des entreprises pour les exploiter ou les revendre. Et les cybercriminels commencent à s'organiser pour en faire un véritable commerce.
Protégez votre entreprise gratuitement pendant 30 jours
Découvrez Bitdefender Ultimate Small Business Security et protégez votre activité contre les cybermenaces. Aucune coordonnée bancaire requise.
Des identifiants volés pour faire tourner les IA aux frais des entreprises
Pour comprendre le fonctionnement de ces attaques, il faut savoir que les entreprises accèdent souvent aux modèles d'IA par l'intermédiaire d'API, dont l'utilisation est facturée selon les ressources consommées, notamment le nombre de tokens traités. En récupérant les identifiants qui autorisent ces connexions, les pirates peuvent donc envoyer leurs propres requêtes tout en laissant les frais à la charge des victimes.
Pour obtenir ces accès, les attaquants exploitent principalement des identifiants cloud compromis, des clés API exposées dans des dépôts GitHub ou des comptes de service mal configurés, mais peuvent également détourner des jetons de session actifs pour contourner l'authentification multifacteur.
Une fois dans les systèmes, ils fouillent les dépôts de code et les gestionnaires de secrets à la recherche de nouveaux accès, élargissent leurs autorisations et activent parfois des services d'IA auxquels les entreprises n'avaient même pas souscrit.
Avant de lancer les requêtes à grande échelle, certains prennent aussi soin de vérifier discrètement leurs trouvailles. Ils envoient des requêtes auxquelles les modèles ne peuvent répondre qu'avec un seul token, suffisamment pour confirmer qu'une clé API fonctionne donc, mais trop peu pour déclencher les alertes fondées sur une consommation anormale. Les identifiants valides peuvent ensuite servir à multiplier les appels aux modèles les plus coûteux, parfois en créant et supprimant continuellement des comptes de service temporaires pour contourner les limitations.
Le LLMJacking, de son petit nom, rappelle ainsi le cryptojacking, qui consiste à détourner la puissance de calcul d'une machine pour miner des cryptomonnaies. Mais là où ce dernier exploite généralement les ressources sur une période prolongée, l'utilisation intensive de modèles d'IA haut de gamme peut faire exploser les dépenses en quelques heures. Plusieurs attaques ont ainsi engendré plus de 100 000 dollars de consommation frauduleuse en une seule journée, dans des entreprises issues notamment des secteurs de la finance, du commerce, des technologies et des transports.
Un marché clandestin en pleine croissance
Les pirates ont surtout compris qu'ils pouvaient tirer davantage de ces accès en les revendant. Des plateformes baptisées LLM Mixers regroupent désormais les identifiants dérobés à différentes entreprises pour proposer des abonnements à des modèles d'IA coûteux, parfois pour une soixantaine de dollars par mois seulement. Lorsqu'un client envoie une requête, celle-ci transite par une infrastructure intermédiaire qui la transmet au modèle concerné à l'aide d'une clé API compromise. Le client reçoit sa réponse, les pirates encaissent son abonnement et l'entreprise victime supporte les frais de consommation.
Ce commerce clandestin commence même à se spécialiser. Dans l'une des affaires examinées, deux groupes criminels travaillaient ensemble : le premier compromettait les infrastructures et récupérait les identifiants, tandis que le second se chargeait de leur exploitation commerciale. Une répartition des tâches qui pourrait accélérer le développement de ce marché et rendre le LLMJacking plus lucratif encore que le cryptojacking traditionnel.

articles.title: Canva reveals major restructuring potentially affecting over a thousand jobs
articles.text:
Canva reveals major restructuring potentially affecting over a thousand jobs
Canva announces sweeping changes
- Canva wants to streamline its workforce so fewer employees are working in silos
- Some workers will be asked to relocate – Sydney hub becomes more important
- The company continues to improve its AI models and is on track for an increase in revenue
Canva has announced plans to relocate, reposition or even cut more than a fifth (22%) of its workforce, equivalent to 1,271 employees, making it "without doubt the hardest moment in our thirteen-year history," per a company-wide message from co-founder and CEO Mel Perkins.
She acknowledged that Canva's organizational structure has become increasingly complicated in recent years due to substantial growth, noting that teams have become divided into "narrow areas of ownership" with too many managers and "more handovers and coordination than necessary."
Canva isn't the first company to note this complexity, with plenty of other tech giants also looking to flatten organizational structures and streamline lines of management.
Canva confirms major workforce reshuffling and layoffs
The change is largely being framed as a company transformation to simplify the workforce structure, rather than purely a cost-cutting exercise.
Under the changes, its Product, Growth and Platform teams will be merged into a single Product organization. Canva also wants to reduce the number of specialist and management roles it has, incorporating those responsibilities into broader positions.
Third and finally, the company also wants to move closer to home. It seems Sydney will become the main location for more of Canva's product development teams, hence the mention of relocation in Perkins' message.
"We know relocating is a big decision for those being asked to consider it, and we're committed to making the process as smooth as possible with comprehensive support," Perkins promised.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
The CEO also dropped the 'office working' bomb – while many tech giants have already enforced return-to-office mandates, Canva has largely supported hybrid working.
From January 2027, hybrid workers will be asked to work from the office two or three days per week, depending on what makes sense for those roles and locations.
Workers set to leave the company as a result of the changes will receive at least six months' salary and twelve months of healthcare coverage, among other benefits. Canva isn't asking for company-issued MacBooks back, either.
Departing 'Canvanauts' can also apply for $10,000 grants under the Canva Collective Fund to start their own business or community project – "we won't take any ownership or equity in what they create," Perkins confirmed.
As for the company itself, it recently confirmed 250 million monthly users and vast model improvements, including a 90% reduction in cost per task with 30x cheaper models that are 5x faster than before.
It also had 120 AI researchers developing in-house models as of September, and is on track to deliver a year-over-year growth in revenue this year.

articles.title: Bluetooth SIG Announces Bluetooth High Data Throughput
articles.text:
Wednesday, November 4th 2026
Bluetooth SIG Announces Bluetooth High Data Throughput
The Bluetooth Special Interest Group (SIG), the trade association that oversees Bluetooth technology, today announced the adoption of Bluetooth High Data Throughput (HDT), the next major milestone in the evolution of Bluetooth technology, introducing faster data transfer, increased capacity, better energy efficiency, and enhanced reliability. By significantly expanding the Bluetooth performance envelope, Bluetooth HDT establishes the foundation for the next generation of wireless experiences and continued innovation across the global Bluetooth ecosystem.
Neville Meijers, CEO of the Bluetooth SIG"As the world's most widely used wireless standard, Bluetooth technology has continually evolved to meet the growing demands of an increasingly connected world," "The Bluetooth SIG member community has once again risen to the challenge. Bluetooth HDT brings a new level of performance to Bluetooth technology, expanding the role it can play across consumer, commercial, and industrial markets and creating a powerful foundation for the next generation of wireless innovation."
Bluetooth HDT introduces a new physical layer (PHY) with robust modulation schemes that allow Bluetooth LE devices to communicate more efficiently and carry significantly more information over the Bluetooth link. Bluetooth HDT increases the maximum supported bit rate to 7.5 Mbps, nearly four times that of the Bluetooth LE 2M PHY.
Advancing Bluetooth performance across four dimensions
Keeping pace with the growing demands of wireless connectivity requires more than speed alone. It requires the capacity to communicate larger volumes of information with greater efficiency and reliability. More than a speed enhancement, Bluetooth High Data Throughput enables Bluetooth devices to transfer more data, use wireless resources more efficiently, and perform more reliably across a broader range of applications and environments. The benefits include:
- Faster data transfer: Bluetooth HDT delivers nearly four times the previous maximum Bluetooth throughput, enabling devices to transfer substantially more information in the same amount of time. As applications become increasingly data-intensive, faster data movement supports more responsive wireless interactions, shorter transfer times, faster synchronization and file movement, and improved user experiences.
- Increased capacity: By improving spectral efficiency, Bluetooth HDT creates more room for devices to exchange more data within available wireless resources and enables enhanced support for increasingly sophisticated and data-intensive applications.
- Better energy efficiency: Bluetooth HDT moves more data in less time, allowing the radio to spend less time actively transmitting and more time in lower-power states, helping devices deliver higher levels of performance while using energy more efficiently.
- Enhanced reliability: Bluetooth HDT improves communication robustness and resilience, helping devices maintain more consistent wireless performance across a broader and more demanding range of operating environments.
Joonsuk Kim, executive vice president and head of S.LSI CP development at Samsung Electronics"The significance of Bluetooth High Data Throughput goes well beyond speed. By advancing data throughput, capacity, energy efficiency, and reliability together, Bluetooth HDT gives developers and product makers a stronger foundation for building more capable products and richer wireless experiences," "Together, these advancements enable more sophisticated applications, new product opportunities, and continued Bluetooth ecosystem growth."
Opening new possibilities for Bluetooth applications
Expected to be released in 2027, the first flagship application for Bluetooth High Data Throughput will be standardized premium wireless audio. With demand for higher-quality wireless listening experiences increasing, Bluetooth HDT provides the capacity, efficiency, and wireless performance needed to deliver standardized lossless and high-resolution audio, while supporting advances in multi-channel surround sound, spatial audio, and other elevated Bluetooth audio experiences.
The same performance improvements that enable richer audio experiences can also benefit a growing range of Bluetooth applications, including:
- Immersive and spatial computing: With extended reality (XR), spatial computing, and other immersive applications continuing to evolve, Bluetooth HDT enables more responsive experiences and increasingly complex device interactions, introducing new possibilities for innovation across this rapidly expanding application space.
- AI-enabled devices: With more data being generated, processed, and exchanged at the edge, Bluetooth HDT provides the foundation to support increasingly intelligent, context-aware, and adaptive AI-enabled experiences.
- Commercial and industrial solutions: Reliance on wireless communication continues to grow across commercial and industrial environments. Bluetooth HDT delivers the capacity and reliability needed to enable more advanced automation, monitoring, and operational systems.
- Everyday connected devices: From wearables and health and fitness devices to smart home products, peripherals, and other connected devices, billions of products rely on Bluetooth technology to make everyday connected experiences possible. Bluetooth HDT enables common data exchanges to happen faster, reducing wait times and helping keep data transfer delays from getting in the way of the connected experience.
Øyvind Strøm, executive vice president of the short-range business unit at Nordic Semiconductor"By making it significantly faster to move large amounts of data, Bluetooth High Data Throughput creates new possibilities for Bluetooth applications," "Imagine a smartwatch that syncs hours' worth of sensor-rich training data to your phone in seconds, smart glasses that deliver richer AI experiences by offloading data for processing, or a smart home product that completes a firmware update with virtually no user-visible downtime. Bluetooth HDT paves the way for more sophisticated, data-intensive Bluetooth applications, and we can't wait to see what our customers and the Bluetooth community build next."
Bluetooth High Data Throughput (HDT) is an optional feature in the recently adopted Bluetooth Core 7.0.

articles.title: Nexus Mods obligará a etiquetar los mods de videojuegos creados con inteligencia artificial
articles.text:
Nexus Mods, el mayor sitio para descargar mods de videojuegos (modificaciones hechas por aficionados que cambian o amplían un juego), obligará a los creadores a declarar si usaron inteligencia artificial y permitirá a los usuarios ocultar ese contenido. La plataforma anunció el 3 de noviembre que no prohibirá los mods hechos con IA.
“Somos pro creatividad humana”, escribió Foledinho, copropietario del sitio, en el anuncio oficial. Según explicó, la IA se usa en todo el proceso de creación, desde el autocompletado de código hasta texturas, voces y recursos completos, y una prohibición total no la sacaría del modding: solo impediría que los autores mencionen su uso.
A partir de ahora, quien suba un mod nuevo deberá indicar si empleó IA. Los mods marcados como “asistidos por inteligencia artificial” deberán incluir una explicación pública de cómo y dónde se usó, y las etiquetas aparecerán justo después de las de contenido para adultos, para que se vean mejor.
La página de ayuda del sitio detalla tres categorías: contenido generado por IA, medios de IA (imágenes promocionales, miniaturas o videos fuera de los archivos del juego) y contenido asistido por IA. Para esta última, el autor debe nombrar las herramientas y señalar qué archivos o código salieron de ellas.
Qué pasará con los usuarios que incumplan las reglas
El sitio abrió un período de gracia de 60 días que comenzó el 3 de noviembre y termina el 2 de enero de 2027. Después de esa fecha, los mods sin etiquetar o que incumplan las reglas pasarán al equipo de confianza y seguridad, que pedirá corregir las omisiones.
Si el autor sigue sin actualizar su mod tras el aviso, el sitio podrá aplicar advertencias, restringir su cuenta o quitar el archivo. La plataforma reconoció que no espera que todos declaren: “Esperamos que estos cambios animen a todos a revelar su uso de IA, pero, para ser sinceros, eso no va a ocurrir”, escribió Foledinho.
Para las etiquetas de “asistido por IA”, el sitio exigirá además pruebas de que el trabajo fue dirigido por una persona, como el historial de versiones del proyecto. Si la descripción o la evidencia resultan insuficientes, los moderadores podrán reemplazar la etiqueta.
Permisos nuevos y un filtro para quien no quiere IA
Los usuarios que prefieran no ver contenido generado por IA podrán activar un control desde las páginas de cada juego y la página de inicio. El sitio mencionó que el siguiente paso será llevar esa opción a la búsqueda y a la forma en que se muestran los mods.
También habrá permisos nuevos para los autores sobre el uso de sus archivos para entrenar IA y sobre las copias o versiones derivadas. Por defecto estarán en “pregúntame”: nadie podrá usar los recursos de un mod para esos fines sin permiso escrito del autor. Los permisos ya existentes no se reiniciarán.
Nexus Mods afirmó que no usará los mods de sus autores para entrenar IA ni los venderá o licenciará a quienes lo hagan. La plataforma reconoció que aún debe resolver detalles sobre licencias, copias y versiones, y que esos cambios llegarán más tarde que la obligación de declarar.
Seguridad: 20.000 archivos en cuarentena en un año
El sitio también citó cifras de seguridad, por el riesgo de que la IA facilite el código malicioso escondido en mods. Entre noviembre de 2025 y octubre de 2026, su equipo revisó a mano y aprobó 3.164 subidas, más de cuatro veces la cifra del año anterior, y puso en cuarentena 20.000 archivos para controles adicionales, 12 veces más.
Sobre las donaciones, el sitio informó que los mods con la etiqueta de contenido generado por IA recibieron este año el 2,13% de todos los puntos de donación, un porcentaje que calificó de “cómodamente bajo”. Por ahora no cambiará las reglas de recompensas, para no dar a los autores un motivo para ocultar el uso de IA.
El anuncio deja sin resolver las miniaturas hechas con IA. El sitio no pondrá restricciones nuevas en los casos dudosos, como una captura real con texto añadido por IA, pero prohíbe cualquier imagen que muestre funciones que el mod no tiene. Las reglas completas se aplicarán desde el 2 de enero de 2027.

articles.title: Sovereign AI at Texas A&M cuts research compute costs - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
University AI’s biggest challenge? Scaling research without losing control
The push for sovereign AI is reaching university research labs, where control over data, models and compute now shapes what science gets done.
Universities sit at an unusual crossroads in the current technological shift, as their work spans open education and tightly controlled federal research. Learning sits at the heart of both missions, making AI a core supporting technology for expanding research and education alike, according to Vince Kellen (pictured, center), chief information officer of the Texas A&M University System.
“AI is a platform for thought. It’s a platform for discovery,” Kellen noted. “AI kind of undergirds all of what we’re going to be doing in the future — certainly what we’re doing in the present now.”
Kellen and Casey Bryan (right), chief information officer of the Texas A&M Engineering Experiment Station, spoke with Krista Case (left) during theCUBE’s coverage of the AI Cybersecurity & Resilience Summit. They discussed how Texas A&M is building a secure, controlled foundation for AI-driven research. (* Disclosure below.)
Building a sovereign AI foundation for research at scale
The foundation of Texas A&M’s approach is IGNITE, short for Innovative Growth in Next Generation AI Technology Ecosystem. It is a state-funded AI and high-performance computing platform led by TEES, as the experiment station is known. Dell Technologies Inc. is building the system with Advanced Micro Devices Inc. graphics processing units inside an Equinix Inc. data center in Dallas. That investment will give research teams the computing power their existing systems lack, Bryan noted.
“Part of our current challenge is that existing resources, while they are performing some of that work, are severely underpowered,” he said. “Research is getting done but could be helped by capacity and scale, which I think IGNITE’s going to bring to the table.”
But the economics matter as much as the capability. Public attention has centered on neoclouds and cloud providers, yet on-premises data centers are growing significantly because of both security controls and cost, according to Kellen. High retail prices for AI computing resources are now limiting the ability of institutions to conduct scientific research.
“There’s no way we could take the science to your classic neocloud provider today and conduct the same thing,” Kellen said. “It’s 5 to 10x the cost.”
Controlling those assets significantly reduces costs and strengthens security, Kellen said. Sovereignty spans four pillars — data, infrastructure, capability and model, and governance — with Equinix supplying physical protection for the compute itself, Bryan added. As a state agency, TEES follows National Institute of Standards and Technology frameworks 800-53 and 800-171, as well as Texas Administrative Code 202, and it wants IGNITE to be ready for Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Level 2.
“There’s a lot of controls we have to inherit, but our researchers shouldn’t have to think about all those,” Bryan said. “It should be absolutely seamless when they go to use the capabilities.”
That principle shaped the IGNITE build. When TEES sat down with Dell’s implementation team to schedule workshops, security came first, and the project’s architecture review board has since affirmed that direction, according to Bryan. For institutions starting their own sovereign AI projects, that sequencing is the lesson.
“The idea was to build that security foundation with which all of the other operational components could be built and referenced back to,” Bryan said. “At its core, start with security early — get it embedded in the process earlier on — and it’s much easier to keep it baked in at the beginning than have to worry about adding that at the end.”

articles.title: Radio With No Radar: Why Agent Runtime Security Fails Without the Layers Beneath It
articles.text:
Nearly every agent security pitch now ends on the same promise: the product stops the bad action in real time. The promise holds for one kind of agent, the kind whose traffic passes through a gateway the enterprise owns. Most agents never touch one.
One recent case shows what that gap looks like in practice. An employee asked an AI assistant to trigger a mass-email automation. The automation hit a recipient-limit policy and failed, so the assistant, which was also connected to the employee's personal mailbox, offered to send the batch from there instead. The employee approved without registering that the assistant was about to route around the sanctioned system. An unknown number of external recipients received email from a personal account rather than the approved channel.
No jailbreak was involved. The assistant did exactly what it was built to do, and the fix was not retraining a model. It was a single runtime rule that blocks any attempt to reach more than fifty external domains and explains to the user what the tool is about to do. Knowing where to apply a rule like that depends on seeing which agents exist, what they are connected to and what normal looks like for each. That visibility is the part most runtime pitches skip.
The runtime is the application, not the pipe
The year's largest agent launches placed agents inside platforms the buyer does not own. Claudeforce runs Claude inside Salesforce's trust boundary, Claude Tag lives inside Slack and Copilot lives inside Microsoft 365. Workday, which says AI now drives more than a quarter of its new annual contract value, runs its agents inside Workday. In each case the agent's tools are the application's features, its knowledge is the application's data and its permissions are the application's permission model.
A gateway can only inspect what passes through it. An agent that runs inside Salesforce, fires from a Flow, reads CRM records and writes case comments sends nothing past an inspection point, and the same is true of a Copilot agent assembling a document from SharePoint or a Slack-native agent reading years of channel history. The OWASP Agentic Skills Top 10 describes this gap as the "unreachable skill" scenario under AST09, No Governance: a capability deployed inside a third-party platform where no external scanner can go.
Security has made a move like this before. Firewalls once inspected packets by source, destination and port, until applications stopped mapping cleanly to ports and malicious traffic began to look identical to legitimate traffic. The inspection point moved up the stack to the application, where the signal lives. Agent runtime needs the same move, with a complication the earlier one never faced: the application layer belongs to someone else. A gateway-only strategy protects the agents an enterprise hosts itself, which are the fewest and the slowest growing.
The inspection point is also a target
In March 2026, attackers compromised LiteLLM, the open-source gateway that routes agent traffic to model providers. The malicious packages were live for about forty minutes, and CloudSEK later put the exposure at more than 2,500 organizations. LiteLLM is the kind of component a security-conscious team adds on purpose to watch AI traffic, which made the inspection point itself the attack vector.
None of this argues against gateways. It argues against treating any single component as the whole strategy. A gateway is more software in the supply chain, with its own release pipeline and dependencies, and it concentrates exactly the traffic an attacker wants. When enforcement is a shared component, its failure is a shared failure.
A millisecond verdict needs a memory
Runtime decisions are made in milliseconds, and the hard cases are the gray ones. A support agent pulling customer data may be doing its job or exfiltrating it. A coding agent reading a repository may be gathering context or performing reconnaissance. A finance agent creating an OAuth connection may be doing integration work or making the first move of a compromise. The action alone does not carry the verdict. The agent's identity and owner, its permissions, its normal behavior, the sensitivity of the data, the destination and the delegation chain behind the request do.
Chains raise the bar. Enforcement that evaluates only the last hop sees an authorized agent performing an action it has permission for, and misses that the authority arrived through a chain nobody approved. Judging the whole chain at runtime means already knowing it, and that knowledge cannot be assembled in a millisecond. Enforcement without that map is an air-traffic controller with a radio but no radar: commands can be issued, but the picture of which plane is headed where does not exist.
What real agent runtime looks like
Three properties follow. Enforcement has to sit where the agents are, across several vantage points such as native platform hooks, API-level controls, the MCP layer, the browser and the endpoint, rather than at a single gateway. Every verdict has to be computed against a live map of identity, permissions, connectivity and activity (IPCA), plus data sensitivity and delegation, which is what turns the gray cases into judgments. And the response menu has to be wider than block.
Mature enforcement is graduated. It allows the known-good, warns where justification is plausible, redacts where the data is the problem and blocks where the chain is hostile. It routes the highest-stakes actions to a human and keeps a kill switch for the provably compromised agent that suspends it, revokes its grants and preserves the trail. Every verdict is logged with its full causal path, because an incident review and a regulator want the same five things: the agent, the chain, the data, the destination and the policy.
Do not buy the end state
Irregular's Dan Lahav calls the mistake the end-state fallacy: assuming the properties of the eventual equilibrium apply to the transition actually underway. In runtime purchasing, it is the belief that inline enforcement will eventually see everything, so the unglamorous layers can be skipped. That end state is not available this year from any vendor at any price. Runtime coverage is partial and platform hooks are arriving unevenly.
What can be bought now, everywhere, is the stack runtime depends on: discovery across every vantage point, posture on every platform, identity and ownership for every agent and context for every decision. Each enforcement point that opens later then snaps into a map that already knows what normal looks like. The full argument for where enforcement belongs is in From AI Runtime to Agent Runtime.
The first ninety days, in order
A sequence that follows the stack bottom-up looks like this.
| Window | The work | How to know it is real | 
|---|---|---|
| Weeks 1 to 2: get the number | Connect what is already running (the identity provider, major platforms, network tools, the email layer) and let discovery work across every vantage point at once. No gateway deployment, no endpoint rollout, no rerouted traffic. | Time to first insight is days, not quarters. The discovered population is several multiples of the list IT keeps. | 
| Weeks 3 to 6: names and configurations | Every discovered agent gets a named human owner or is suspended. Configuration debt is triaged, starting with the platforms hosting the most reachable agents: guest-user exposures, intake features wired to agent triggers, sharing rules from three years ago. Guardrails go on customer-facing and privileged agents first. | A human raises a hand within a day when asked "whose is this?" | 
| Weeks 7 to 12: the queue and the path | Context-aware risk tiering so review starts with the agent that can actually hurt the business, a least-privilege review cadence on the top tier and a sanctioned route for business teams to ship agents with secure defaults. | Any critical rating can be explained as a chain, and builders are offered a path instead of only a block. | 
The enablement path matters because the builders are coming either way. Blocking teaches evasion, while a good path teaches compliance.
Teams can place themselves with a four-level test. Blind means the board's three questions (how many agents exist, what they can reach and who is accountable) have no current answer. Inventoried means the population is discovered, counted and refreshed continuously. Governed means every agent has an owner, posture is managed against baselines and risk is tiered with context. Instrumented means enforcement operates where agents run, with graduated verdicts and a full causal path in every alert. Most enterprises are at the first level, whatever the policy document says, and a vendor selling instrumentation to a blind organization is selling enforcement that can act but cannot judge.
Seven questions that sort vendors
Every vendor deck now says agent security. These questions separate vendors that built for the problem from vendors that renamed a product, because each is easy to answer well only if the architecture underneath exists.
| Ask | What a good answer looks like | 
|---|---|
| Can you find agents that never authenticate through SSO? | Yes, across several independent vantage points, each seeing something the others cannot. | 
| For an agent you rated critical, show me the chain. | A complete, reachable attack path (capability, reachability, asset) that an analyst can verify, not an aggregate score. | 
| Does the same finding produce different severities on different agents? | Yes, demonstrated on a sandboxed agent and a customer-facing one. | 
| When one agent invokes another, can you reconstruct the delegation chain? | Original requester, every hop and the final action. An audit trail that starts at the last agent is not one. | 
| What context feeds an allow, block or redact verdict? | Identity, permissions, delegation and data sensitivity, not the prompt alone. | 
| What happens to my protection if your enforcement component is compromised? | A specific answer that addresses the LiteLLM incident directly. | 
| How long until I see my real agent inventory? | Days. A quarter is a different product. | 
Platforms built around the map rather than the individual agent can answer these directly. One leading example is Reco, whose Reco Graph connects every human and non-human identity, application, permission and agent action into a single live view, so that reach, not configuration, is the unit of analysis. One measured program that applied this approach moved its posture score from 47% to 91% across 21 platforms in 30 days.
Learn more about Reco's agent discovery at reco.ai/platform.
The full ninety-day sequence, the four-level self-assessment and all fifteen vendor questions are in The Agent Security Checklist: Your First 90 Days.
About Reco
Reco is the leader in Agent Security. The Reco Platform secures agents and their operating environments where applications, identities, permissions, and workflows intersect. It discovers an organization's entire third-party ecosystem, prioritizes real risk over alert volume and remediates with precision across every human identity, agent, app and permission in the environment. Built on the Reco Graph, with new integrations delivered in hours through the Reco Factory and pre-built agent and app intelligence from the Reco Library. articles.title: Intel Nova Lake-S CPUs Reportedly Drop to 5.1 GHz Max Above 90°C
articles.text:
Wednesday, November 4th 2026
Intel Nova Lake-S CPUs Reportedly Drop to 5.1 GHz Max Above 90°C
Intel's upcoming Core Ultra 4000 "Nova Lake-S" desktop processors will reportedly cap their maximum core frequency at 5.1 GHz whenever they run above 90°C, according to Intel leaker Jaykihn on X. He says the limit applies to the entire Nova Lake-S desktop lineup, works separately from regular TjMax throttling at 100°C, and can't be raised. He also notes that the information is still preliminary. In practice, it looks like a safety net that sits between normal boost behavior and full thermal throttling. Below 90°C, the chips should presumably boost as usual, and models that don't exceed 5.1 GHz in the first place wouldn't be affected at all. 
Final Nova Lake clocks aren't official yet, though the current Core Ultra 9 285K already boosts up to 5.7 GHz, so a high-end Nova Lake chip that runs hot could lose a sizable chunk of its peak frequency. A 100°C TjMax would also be lower than Arrow Lake's 105°C, which can be manually raised to 115°C on the 285K. That puts more weight on cooling, since the 28-core Core Ultra 9 4970K BFC was reportedly set to pull up to 296 W at PL2 despite its 125 W rating, and staying under 90°C at that kind of power draw will probably take a really capable cooler. Nova Lake-S is currently expected to arrive in Q1 2027, and Intel hasn't confirmed any of this yet.
Sources:
				Jaykihn on X, 				via Videocardz			
	
	
	
		
	
		
3 Comments on Intel Nova Lake-S CPUs Reportedly Drop to 5.1 GHz Max Above 90°C
I think people get over the need for a big cooler pretty quickly if the performance is worth it. If it's hot, power hungry, AND has bad IPC or poor improvement over previous generations, it will not go down well.
Also, I think real-usage power is important. Sure, my CPU will draw over 300W in Cinebench, but it only draws about 115W in gaming loads and performs really well while doing it. So if Nova-Lake draws 296W in CB, but is closer to that 125W in gaming workloads and has low idle power-draw, I don't think the maximum power-draw is that important for most people. Of course the 125W is just a thermal rating number for cooler planning...which hasn't been based on real numbers in years anyway, but that's a whole other topic lol.
If this 90C throttle is real, I do think this would be an interesting note for reviewers though. It would help their cause pushing consumers to really consider the cooler requirements if they plan on running heavy workloads on these things. I think DIY builders usually know this, but people go buy pre-builts and wonder why their performance sucks when the thing has a crappy cooler on an i9 (or ultra-9 or whatever)

articles.title: Los ciberataques siguen afectando a empresas europeas y ahora golpean al banco francés Crédit Mutuel Arkéa
articles.text:
Cuando hablamos de ciberataques a bancos, es fácil imaginar cuentas vaciadas o clientes que no pueden acceder a su dinero. Sin embargo, la seguridad de una entidad financiera abarca mucho más que la aplicación que utilizamos para consultar el saldo. También depende de cómo se autorizan las operaciones, de quién puede ejecutarlas y de qué controles entran en funcionamiento cuando algo no encaja. Es ahí donde el problema adquiere otra dimensión: una intrusión puede comprometer determinados procesos sin que eso signifique necesariamente que todos los ahorros de los clientes estén en peligro.
El último caso que hemos conocido nos lleva hasta Francia, donde uno de sus grupos bancarios ha tenido que reconocer un incidente de seguridad de considerable alcance. Hablamos de Crédit Mutuel Arkéa, una entidad con más de 5,8 millones de socios y clientes que confirmó hoy 4 de noviembre haber sufrido un ciberataque que permitió realizar operaciones fraudulentas. La magnitud potencial es notable: el investigador de blockchain ZachXBT estima que se sustrajeron más de 133 millones de dólares, unos 118 millones de euros. Sin embargo, el banco aseguró a Reuters que sus pérdidas serían inferiores y todavía no ha comunicado una cifra definitiva.
Para entender cómo salió a la luz este caso, tenemos que retroceder hasta el 2 de noviembre. Ese día, ZachXBT alertó de movimientos sospechosos relacionados con una entidad europea cuya identidad todavía no había revelado. El investigador amplió sus estimaciones durante los días siguientes hasta señalar a Crédit Mutuel Arkéa el 4 de noviembre. En una aclaración oficial posterior, el grupo explicó que los atacantes habían accedido a través de la plataforma de uno de sus proveedores, sin pasar por Fortuneo, su banco digital. Desde una cuenta propia de Arkéa ejecutaron transferencias hacia otras entidades bancarias, que posteriormente pudieron facilitar la conversión del dinero a criptomonedas.
Qué sabemos del ataque y del dinero comprometido
Una de las particularidades de este caso es que podemos seguir parte del recorrido del dinero sin conocer todavía el alcance completo del ataque. En un primer momento, ZachXBT identificó retiradas superiores a 106 millones de dólares y posteriormente localizó otros 27 millones. La investigación de Bitquery aporta una segunda perspectiva: sus analistas rastrearon movimientos por 108,8 millones de dólares en USDC, distribuidos entre 15 direcciones de criptomonedas durante unas 21 horas. Sin embargo, la propia firma reconoció que no había podido identificar al titular de las cuentas ni verificar el importe total denunciado.
El seguimiento de estas operaciones también permite comprender una dificultad añadida: rastrear los fondos no significa necesariamente poder recuperarlos. Según Bitquery, las retiradas se realizaron desde cuentas de Kraken, Crypto.com y OKX en USDC, una criptomoneda diseñada para mantener su valor próximo al dólar. Buena parte acabó convertida en ether, un activo que no puede ser bloqueado directamente por una entidad emisora. No obstante, la investigación también ha identificado medidas de contención: Tether congeló aproximadamente 1,14 millones de dólares en USDT y Crypto.com confirmó a CoinDesk que había impedido nuevos movimientos de fondos relacionados con el incidente. Por ahora, se desconoce cuánto dinero podrá recuperarse.
Mientras los investigadores intentan reconstruir lo sucedido, hay otra cuestión que afecta directamente a los clientes: qué ha pasado con sus cuentas. Según Crédit Mutuel Arkéa, sus fondos permanecen protegidos porque los atacantes utilizaron una cuenta del propio grupo y no las de sus clientes. Las consecuencias operativas reconocidas se limitaron a retrasos en determinadas transferencias, y la entidad asegura que prácticamente todas las operaciones habían recuperado su funcionamiento durante la mañana del 4 de noviembre. También ha advertido de posibles intentos de phishing, una práctica mediante la que los delincuentes buscan obtener información confidencial haciéndose pasar por entidades de confianza.
Este episodio llega en una semana en la que otras empresas europeas también han sufrido ataques informáticos. Varios supermercados de Bélgica, Suecia e Irlanda vieron alterados sus sistemas de refrigeración, lo que obligó a retirar alimentos de la venta. Son incidentes distintos, sin una relación demostrada, pero reflejan hasta qué punto las operaciones cotidianas dependen de la tecnología. En el sector financiero, la Unión Europea aplica desde enero de 2025 el reglamento DORA, que establece obligaciones para gestionar los riesgos tecnológicos, incluidos los relacionados con proveedores externos, y reforzar la capacidad de las entidades para responder ante incidentes digitales.

articles.title: Des hackers de la honte ont réglé des chambres de l'Établissement français du sang sur 110 °C
articles.text:
L'Établissement français du sang a confirmé une cyberattaque contre l'un de ses prestataires frigorifiques. Les chambres froides de trois sites, où sont stockées des poches de plasma, ont vu leurs réglages de température modifiés à distance.
Une cyberattaque visant un prestataire de l'Établissement français du sang (EFS) a déréglé, dans la nuit du 1er au 2 novembre, les chambres froides de trois de ses sites. D'après Le Canard enchaîné, qui a révélé l'affaire, des équipements censés garder des échantillons de donneurs à –30 °C ont reçu l'ordre de monter jusqu'à 110 °C. Dans un communiqué publié le 3 novembre, l'EFS confirme l'incident et assure qu'aucun produit sanguin n'a été perdu.
110 °C au compteur pour des chambres froides à –30 °C
L'EFS souligne d'emblée qu'il n'était pas directement visé. C'est l'un de ses prestataires qui a été touché, la société Coolworld, chargée de la maintenance de conteneurs de stockage de l'EFS, notamment en Bourgogne-Franche-Comté. Ses installations de supervision et de pilotage des chambres froides ont été atteintes, ce qui a provoqué des anomalies. Les seuils de température et de dégivrage ont été réglés sur des valeurs extrêmes. Quant aux 110 °C, il s'agit de la consigne envoyée aux machines, c'est-à-dire la température qu'on leur demandait d'atteindre.
Ces chambres froides contenaient des produits sensibles. Selon Le Canard, l'EFS a d'abord parlé d'échantillons conservés pour la veille sanitaire, avant de reconnaître que du plasma congelé destiné à la transfusion était aussi visé.
Le communiqué de l'EFS cite également du plasma réservé au fractionnement, le procédé qui permet d'en fabriquer des médicaments. Les alarmes ont fonctionné, et un technicien de permanence a vu les températures remonter pendant la nuit. Selon les cas, les appareils ont été repris en main ou mis hors service, et leur contenu a alors été déplacé par précaution.
Une cyberattaque au triste goût de déjà-vu
Cette tragique cyberattaque rappelle celles qui touchent la grande distribution depuis plusieurs semaines. Dans la nuit du 11 au 12 octobre, des centaines de supermarchés (Intermarché, Carrefour, Leclerc, Coopérative U…) ont vu leurs congélateurs chauffer au lieu de refroidir. L'ANSSI a désigné les contrôleurs du fabricant danois Danfoss comme cible de cette campagne, même si d'autres marques ont aussi été touchées. Les pirates auraient déclenché un dégivrage permanent avec une consigne de 50 °C. Des tonnes de denrées ont été jetées, et une nouvelle attaque de ce type a été menée ces derniers jours en Europe.
Rien ne permet pour l'instant d'affirmer que ces cyberattaques ont les mêmes auteurs, et l'EFS ne fait pas ce rapprochement publiquement. Le ministère de la Santé affirme qu'il y a « zéro conséquence opératoire ». L'EFS assure de son côté que les prélèvements et la distribution de produits sanguins continuent normalement. Il travaille avec l'ANSSI, l'agence nationale chargée de la cybersécurité, et avec le ministère, en plus d'avoir d'ores et déjà renforcé la surveillance de l'ensemble de ses équipements.

articles.title: Ce robot-tondeuse testé par notre rédaction passe sous les 670 € et vous dispense de câble périphérique
articles.text:
Le robot-tondeuse Mova LiDAX Ultra 1200 est à 665,83 € chez Amazon (-39 %)
Sans fil périphérique ni antenne RTK, le Mova LiDAX Ultra 1200 passe à 665,83 € chez Amazon, soit 39 % sous son prix conseillé, pour les jardins jusqu’à 1 200 m².
Vendu et expédié par Amazon, ce modèle affiche un écart de 433,17 € avec son prix conseillé de 1 099 €. L’économie atteint aussi 83,17 € face aux 749 € indiqués comme plus bas prix des 30 derniers jours. Vérifiez toutefois le délai de livraison avant commande.
Une installation sans câble à disposer dans le jardin
Le LiDAX Ultra 1200 associe un LiDAR 3D à une caméra pour se repérer. Aucun câble périphérique ni antenne RTK n’est nécessaire. La cartographie se réalise depuis l’application, automatiquement lorsque les limites sont suffisamment nettes, ou en guidant le robot pour délimiter précisément la pelouse.
L’application permet ensuite de programmer les tontes, de personnaliser les zones et de régler la hauteur de coupe entre 3 et 10 cm. Le robot suit des trajectoires en U et revient à sa station lorsque sa batterie doit être rechargée.
Une tonte régulière, avec quelques limites à connaître
Nous avons bien testé cette version 1200, qui a obtenu 4 étoiles sur 5. Sa navigation ordonnée et sa coupe homogène constituent ses principaux atouts. Le disque mobile réduit également la bande d’herbe laissée près des bordures, même si des finitions manuelles restent nécessaires.
Notre essai relève toutefois une détection perfectible des petits obstacles et des manœuvres susceptibles de marquer les sols meubles. Enfin, la localisation antivol nécessite un module optionnel : elle n’est pas comprise dans l’équipement de cette version.

articles.title: Smartsheet AI-powered platform bridges gap between planning and results - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Smartsheet AI-powered platform bridges gap between planning and results
Smartsheet Inc. today introduced an artificial intelligence-powered planning and execution platform designed to help enterprises identify when projects are veering off course and take corrective action before delays and cost overruns become serious problems.
Announced at the company’s Engage 2026 conference, the new vsActual platform — pronounced “versus actual” — uses AI agents to continuously monitor work across multiple enterprise systems, compare progress against strategic objectives and recommend adjustments. The company also announced new agentic workflow capabilities, integrations and security controls for its existing work management platform.
The centerpiece of vsActual is what Smartsheet calls Execution Graph, a knowledge graph built from what the company said are two decades of workflow data encompassing millions of projects and nine petabytes of information. The graph maps relationships between tasks, projects, programs and strategic objectives to help AI agents understand how changes in one part of an organization affect others.
The company’s goal is to address a growing disconnect between individual productivity improvements enabled by AI and measurable organizational results, said Pratima Arora, Smartsheet’s chief product and technology officer.
“We were seeing a lot of intelligence and productivity gains getting stuck at an individual level and not translating to a team and organization level,” she said.
VsActual is designed to operate across existing enterprise applications rather than require organizations to consolidate work onto a single platform. It can connect to applications from Oracle Corp., SAP SE, Workday Inc., Atlassian Corp. PLC and ServiceNow Inc. to gather information about budgets, schedules, staffing and project dependencies.
Smartsheet said AI agents can turn strategy documents, spreadsheets and budget proposals into structured plans, model alternative scenarios and monitor execution against those plans. A drift-detection agent (pictured) continuously searches for emerging problems, while other agents generate executive reports and recommend changes as business priorities evolve.
The system can also trace the consequences of disruptions across organizational hierarchies. “If there is a delay in a Jira ticket that has impact five levels up, we can detect it and tell you what is happening,” Arora said.
Historical data advantage
Smartsheet said its historical workflow data provides an advantage over competing planning and work management products. Execution Graph builds on an existing Amazon Web Services Inc. Neptune knowledge graph containing approximately 100 million nodes and incorporates information about workflow patterns, dependencies and collaboration, Arora said.
The company uses multiple foundation models, selecting them based on workload requirements and cost. AWS and Databricks Inc. are its major underlying technology providers. Arora said Smartsheet isn’t training its own large language models.
The announcements also expand Smartsheet’s existing AI capabilities. New Agentic Workflows allow users to schedule recurring activities such as status reports and risk assessments. Specialized creation and data-quality agents can generate project structures, dashboards and reports or identify problems in underlying data.
New integrations include native connections to ServiceNow, Microsoft Corp. Dynamics 365, HubSpot Inc. customer relationship management, Workday Inc. human resources software and Intuit Inc.’s QuickBooks. Conversational integrations with GitHub, Zendesk Inc., Airtable and Monday.com Ltd. are entering early access, with additional AI-assisted integrations planned for early 2027.
Arora emphasized that agentic workflows combine conventional automation with AI rather than relying exclusively on large language models. “This industry overuses LLMs sometimes where it is just simple deterministic action,” she said.
Although some agents can execute scheduled tasks automatically, Arora said human approval remains the default approach for consequential actions. “Our default stance is human in the loop,” she said.
The compay also announced International Organization for Standardization/International Electrotechnical Commission 42001 certification, security event streaming and data classification capabilities intended to strengthen oversight of AI operations.
Smartsheet developed vsActual with about a dozen enterprise design partners. The company publishes pricing on its website.

articles.title: Los centros de datos de IA instalan motores de avión reciclados para generar su propia electricidad
articles.text:
Algunos centros de datos de inteligencia artificial (IA) generan su propia electricidad con motores de aviones retirados, convertidos para funcionar con gas natural. Los operadores buscan evitar las esperas de años para conectarse a la red o para comprar turbinas nuevas, según The New York Times, cuya investigación recogió TechCrunch el 3 de noviembre.
Los motores no están pensados como una planta eléctrica permanente. Su atractivo es la rapidez. “Se trata de conseguir energía lo más rápido posible”, dijo al Times Audun Martinsen, analista de la consultora Rystad Energy. Con unidades de este tipo, “pueden tener un centro de datos funcionando en 24 meses”, afirmó.
Conectar 100 megavatios a la red en el norte de Virginia, en cambio, lleva unos siete años, según la Agencia Internacional de Energía, citada por TechCrunch. Un ejecutivo de Mitsubishi Power, uno de los mayores fabricantes de equipos de generación, dijo a Bloomberg la semana pasada que la mayor parte de la capacidad nueva llegará hacia 2031.
xAI y OpenAI ya usan estas turbinas
La empresa xAI, de Elon Musk, instaló ocho turbinas de este tipo en Mississippi para alimentar su centro de datos Colossus 2, según el Times. Las unidades provienen de ProEnergy, una compañía que reconstruye un motor de General Electric común en aviones Boeing.
OpenAI siguió ese camino en 2025 con turbinas de gas, provistas por GE Vernova y Solar Turbines, en Abilene, Texas, el primer sitio de su proyecto Stargate. Crusoe, la empresa de Denver que construye ese campus, encargó 13 unidades convertidas de ProEnergy en abril de este año, informó TechCrunch.
En septiembre, Crusoe canceló una compra de USD 1.250 millones de 29 turbinas de gas a Boom Supersonic, una startup que desarrolla un avión de pasajeros supersónico y que también vende una versión de ese motor como planta eléctrica. Un portavoz de Crusoe dijo entonces a TechCrunch que la empresa seguirá usando turbinas.
Cómo se convierte un motor de avión en generador
ProEnergy fabrica su turbina PE6000 a partir de núcleos usados del motor CF6-80C2, que combina con piezas nuevas. Cada unidad genera 48 megavatios, según Landon Tessmer, vicepresidente de operaciones comerciales de la empresa, citado por IEEE Spectrum. En octubre de 2025 afirmó que había vendido 21 turbinas para dos proyectos de más de 1 gigavatio en total.
Tessmer explicó que esos proyectos usarán la energía como solución puente durante cinco a siete años, hasta obtener conexión a la red. Después, las máquinas pasan a respaldo, complementan la red o se venden a la compañía eléctrica local. ProEnergy estima que unos 1.000 de estos motores se retirarán en la próxima década.
Las turbinas diseñadas para plantas de gas convencionales tienen plazos de entrega que superan 2029, según Data Center Dynamics. Tessmer sostuvo que una PE6000 puede entregarse en 2027, indicó la empresa que vende el equipo.
Menos eficientes y más contaminantes
No obstante, los motores convertidos tienen costos. Según el Times, son menos eficientes y contaminan más que las turbinas hechas para plantas de gas, y hacen falta más unidades para producir la misma energía. Algunos expertos consultados por el diario creen que esas preocupaciones ganarán peso en uno o dos años.
Las demoras ya cuestan contratos. El mes pasado, Microsoft se retiró como cliente principal del centro de datos de Nscale en Loughton, Inglaterra, después de que la compañía eléctrica local dijera que no podría entregar suficiente energía hasta principios o mediados de la década de 2030.
El gobierno del presidente Donald Trump presiona a los desarrolladores para que generen su propia electricidad. “Fue idea mía”, dijo Trump a periodistas en agosto, según el Times, y añadió que los centros de datos deben construir su energía para no tomarla de la red.

articles.title: China-Aligned Hackers Hijack Sogou Input Method DNS Requests to Deploy DarkVigil Backdoor
articles.text:
A China-aligned threat actor known as SlippyNunchucks has been attributed to a Domain Name System (DNS) hijacking operation abusing insecure HTTP communications in Windows versions of Sogou Input Method as part of a surveillance campaign designed to deploy an implant called DarkVigil (aka FDMTP).
The campaign, observed starting July 1, 2026, is assessed to have targeted organizations and Chinese-speaking individuals in Hong Kong, Thailand, Japan, Vietnam, Oman, and Sri Lanka, according to ESET.
"DarkVigil implants are typically deployed through popular Chinese applications," ESET researcher Anh Ho said in a report shared with The Hacker News. "By abusing these applications, the SlippyNunchucks threat actor has been able to reach Chinese-speaking users across Asia and Europe."
Some of the applications abused by the adversary include Sogou Input Method, QuickFox, QingTalk, MiYunChat, SoftCam, and tawk.to.
Active since at least September 15, 2023, SlippyNunchucks is known for targeting organizations and Chinese-speaking individuals across South and East Asia. These attacks lead to the deployment of a modular .NET framework that includes DarkVigil and a set of over 20 plugins.
Although the use of the backdoor has been previously linked to Mustang Panda, ESET said it found no tactical overlaps between the threat actor and DarkVigil-related activity in its telemetry, prompting it to classify it as a distinct intrusion set.
Earlier this August, Fortinet's FortiGuard Incident Response Team detailed the threat actor's supply chain compromise of the QuickFox VPN and network acceleration tool to deliver DarkVigil.
According to the Slovakian cybersecurity company, the adversary shifted to exploiting Sogou Input Method, a popular Chinese-language input method editor developed by Tencent, as a delivery vector three days after QuickFox released a clean version of its program.
Specifically, the attack involves hijacking the app's branded vocabulary promotion mechanism to serve a malicious configuration, which ultimately paves the way for the deployment of the malware via SGTool.exe, a legitimate Sogou Input Method component that functions as a multi-purpose task dispatcher.
In a clean environment, the executable sends an HTTP request to the "config.pinyin.sogou[.]com/api/brandScd/getBrandScd.php" endpoint to fetch a configuration. But in the attack discovered by ESET, the DNS resolution of the domain is tampered with to resolve it to one of the two staging servers -
- 47.239.250[.]102 (sogou-cdn[.]com)
- 47.237.122[.]175 (dev.soft-png-cdn.com)
The consequence of this DNS hijacking was that HTTP requests to the "getBrandScd.php" endpoint were routed to one of the staging servers, which then responded with a malicious configuration. The configuration, for its part, instructs the binary to download two additional payloads from "sogou-cdn[.]com" and launch the malware via DLL sideloading -
- A legitimate Adobe executable ("biz_helper.exe")
- A rogue DLL ("libcef.dll") containing DarkVigil
DarkVigil is notable for its use of Duplex Message Transport Protocol (DMTP) for command-and-control (C2), allowing the client to execute and orchestrate plugins received from an attacker-controlled server to facilitate persistence or data collection.
Following responsible disclosure, Tencent addressed the vulnerability (CVE-2026-120422) in version 16.10, released on October 29, 2026, by migrating the affected HTTP requests to HTTPS.
SlippyNunchucks is suspected to operate keeping the interests of the Chinese government in mind, with ESET describing it as a nation-state surveillance effort.
"Although SlippyNunchucks targets organizations and individuals across multiple sectors, we discovered significant surveillance activity against an organization operating Chinese-language online betting platforms in Sri Lanka, Hong Kong, and the Philippines," ESET said.
"The targeting of this organization is notable given China's restrictions on gambling, including criminal penalties for operating gambling businesses and organizing Chinese citizens to gamble abroad."
This is not the first time China-nexus threat actors have weaponized the Sogou Input Method as an entry point for malware distribution. In September 2026, Gen Digital said a now-patched vulnerability in the input method editor (CVE-2026-51990) was exploited by UNC3569 to deliver a backdoor dubbed GRAYRABBIT by means of a crafted link.
"The vulnerability chains three separate weaknesses into a single, one-click exploit: unvalidated command-line argument injection in the sgbiz: custom protocol handler, unrestricted URL navigation in a CEF-based WebView, and a severely outdated, unsandboxed Chromium browser engine [susceptible to CVE-2021-38003]," Gen Digital said.
