articles.title: Sarva Suvidhaen: Bihar Startup Is Using AI and IoT to Make Indian Railways Smarter
articles.text:
Sarva Suvidhaen: Bihar Startup Is Using AI and IoT to Make Indian Railways Smarter
Bihar-based startup Sarva Suvidhaen is using AI and IoT to modernise Indian Railways, improve operational efficiency, and build smarter railway systems
India’s railway network is one of the largest and most complex public infrastructure systems in the world. Every day, thousands of trains, millions of passengers, freight transportation, stations, tracks, and field teams operate simultaneously. In such a system, even a small delay can have an impact across multiple levels.
Sometimes, reports from the field do not arrive on time. In some cases, data remains scattered across different systems. At times, officials are unable to obtain real-time information about a situation. In such circumstances, technology is no longer just a means of speeding up work; it becomes an important part of better governance and decision-making.
The Bihar-based startup Sarva Suvidhaen is working in this space. The company is developing solutions for railways and other large infrastructure systems with the help of artificial intelligence (AI), the Internet of Things (IoT), computer vision, and software.
The company was founded by Atul Anand and Srishti. Both have different professional backgrounds, but during the lockdown, they observed a common problem closely. While working from home in Patna, they recognised the need for better data, automation, and real-time monitoring in certain processes of Indian Railways.
This led to the idea of a startup that could use technology to solve ground-level problems in public infrastructure rather than limiting its applications to private companies.
YourStory recently spoke with Atul Anand, CTO (Chief Technology Officer) of Sarva Suvidhaen. He spoke in detail about the company's beginnings, the experience of entrepreneurship in Bihar, the AI and IoT solutions developed for railways, the challenges involved, and future plans.
Atul Anand's story began at a Hindi-medium government school in Bihar. He completed his matriculation through the Bihar Board in 2005. He then pursued his intermediate education at Patna Science College between 2005 and 2007.
He went on to earn a BTech in Computer Science and Engineering from NIT Trichy. After that, he worked in software development roles at companies such as Oracle, BEL, CLS, KPI Partners, IQuanti, and SpotOn.
Srishti began her schooling at the School of Creative Learning. She completed her Class 12 education through the BSEB. She then pursued a BBM from Magadh University and an MBA from Uttarakhand Technical University. She worked at SPVR and Co, Randstad, and Cognizant.
Both had different experiences. Atul had experience in technology and software development, while Srishti had experience in business, management, and operations. This difference later became the company's strength.
Atul explains, “After working in the software development sector for more than 12 years, I felt that the use of technology should not be limited to the needs of companies alone. Our country's large public systems also need it. Srishti encouraged me to think in this direction. We decided to use our technical understanding to work on problems that affect public services and ordinary people.”
The Idea Emerged During the Lockdown
During the lockdown, both were working from home in Patna. During this period, they began looking closely at the everyday processes of Indian Railways. They felt that data, field reporting, and monitoring across such a large network could be made more organised. This was particularly relevant to processes that require information to be collected from different locations and decisions to be made based on it.
Srishti encouraged Atul to use his technical background in this direction. Together, they began exploring ways to connect machine learning (ML), IoT, and software with public infrastructure challenges.
Sarva Suvidhaen focuses on organisations where operations are spread across multiple locations. In such systems, manual reporting and limited data visibility can slow down the decision-making process.
The company operates on a B2B and B2G model. This includes developing software and IoT solutions, along with their deployment, consultancy, and maintenance.
Atul says, “We did not start with a large market study. While living in Patna during the lockdown, we observed some real-world problems. We felt that technologies such as machine learning and IoT could help us understand and solve these problems. I took responsibility for technology, while Srishti worked on the business and operations side. In this way, our respective roles gradually became clear, and Sarva Suvidhaen's work progressed.”
Making Indian Railways Smarter
The startup has developed several solutions to digitise field operations for Indian Railways. One of these is WagonEye, an AI- and computer vision-based platform. It is used to identify potential defects in the body and undergear of freight and passenger train wagons. In a large network such as the railways, identifying potential problems on time can be important for both safety and operations.
In addition, RailOps is a digital operations platform. It enables railway teams to record and monitor field activities.
SwachhDNR is a web and mobile platform. It has been deployed in the Danapur division, which includes Patna Junction, as well as the Sealdah and Jhansi divisions. It is used to track and assess employee performance.
Through these solutions, the company's effort is to make field data available in digital form and connect it with the decision-making process.
Atul explains, “Our focus is not limited to developing software. We want technology to work where the actual problem exists. Conditions in railway field operations are not always the same. Therefore, it is important for AI models and IoT systems to function reliably in real-world environments. Solutions such as WagonEye, RailOps, and SwachhDNR have been developed with this approach in mind. Our goal is to convert data into information that can support better decision-making at both the field and management levels.”
Funding from Startup Bihar and Google Cloud
Sarva Suvidhaen started through bootstrapping. This means the founders did not take funding from any external investors initially. Both used their personal savings and the earnings from their initial projects.
Later, they received Rs 10 lakh in funding from Startup Bihar. They also received incubation support from IIT Patna and STPI. In addition, the company received Rs 1 crore in credits from Google Cloud. These resources were used to build and scale its AI and IoT infrastructure.
According to the company, it has received a total of Rs 32 lakh in government assistance. In addition, it has raised Rs 60 lakh in external equity funding from two investors.
The experience of working with government institutions gave Sarva Suvidhaen an opportunity to understand several important aspects of business. Large government organisations follow established rules and procedures for procurement. Therefore, building trust and establishing a strong track record are essential when introducing new technology. At the same time, pilot projects and real-world field environments are highly useful for improving deep-tech solutions. These experiences helped the company make its solutions more practical and reliable.
Now Focusing on India's Large Infrastructure Systems
Sarva Suvidhaen has also witnessed growth in its business. In the financial year 2024–25, the company's turnover was approximately Rs 48 lakh. It recorded a profit of around Rs 9 lakh. In the financial year 2025–26, its turnover increased to approximately Rs 1.16 crore. The company's profit stood at around Rs 20 lakh.
The company's revenue model is based on one-time development and integration fees, along with monthly or annual subscriptions and maintenance contracts.
The company now wants to expand its presence across all zones of Indian Railways. Alongside this, it plans to take its solutions into sectors such as logistics, healthcare, and smart cities.
At the technology level, the company is preparing to invest more in edge AI, computer vision, and predictive maintenance.
The incubation centre at IIT Patna has also played an important role in this journey. According to the company, funding, technical support, mentorship, and industry connections helped transform its prototypes into solutions that could be used in the field.
Atul says, “We do not see Sarva Suvidhaen merely as a company working for the railways. Our goal is to become a partner in AI, IoT, and automation for critical infrastructure. To achieve this, we need to make our technology capable of working under different conditions. Going forward, we want to explore opportunities in sectors such as logistics, healthcare, and smart cities, alongside railways. Our belief is that the journey can begin in Bihar, but the solutions should reach across India and, eventually, the world.”
Starting in Bihar, Building Solutions for India, and Expanding Across the World
Sarva Suvidhaen's story is still in its early stages. The company will continue to face challenges such as government procurement processes, long sales cycles, and the large-scale deployment of deep-tech solutions.
However, there is another side to this story. It shows how new opportunities for entrepreneurship and technological talent are taking shape in Bihar. A startup that begins in a city like Patna can develop solutions for one of the largest public infrastructure systems in the country.
The startup ecosystem, incubation centres, government assistance, and support from technical institutions can help such ventures progress beyond their initial stages. Sarva Suvidhaen's journey is an example of this changing environment.
For Atul and Srishti, the direction ahead is clear. They want to work on problems whose impact can be seen on the ground and whose solutions can be deployed at scale.
Their message also reflects this approach: “Start your journey in Bihar, find solutions to India's real problems, and build solutions that the world can adopt as well.”
Sarva Suvidhaen began its journey in Bihar, but its ambitions are not limited to the state. The company is now working on developing solutions that can be used in other large infrastructure sectors, in addition to railways. Through its efforts to solve ground-level problems using AI, IoT, and automation, the company also presents an interesting picture of Bihar's evolving startup ecosystem.

articles.title: iPhone 18 : Apple miserait sur une plus grosse batterie... et un prix en hausse
articles.text:
Vendu 969 euros à sa sortie, l’iPhone 17 s’affiche à 1 119 euros depuis la hausse générale appliquée par Apple à son catalogue en septembre. Sur Weibo, l’informateur Digital Chat Station ouvre déjà le dossier de son successeur : l’iPhone 18, attendu au premier semestre 2027, embarquerait une batterie sensiblement agrandie. Le même message évoque, sans avancer de montant, un tarif encore revu à la hausse.
Que vaut la promesse d’une plus grosse batterie ?
L’iPhone 17 embarque 3 692 mAh, une capacité donnée en progression sur son successeur, sans le moindre chiffre publié. La même fiche technique prête à l’iPhone 18 un écran de 6,3 pouces à 120 Hz, une puce A20 gravée en 2 nm et un double capteur photo de 48 mégapixels. Dynamic Island et Face ID resteraient de la partie. La fuite recoupe sur ce point des bruits plus anciens, la puissance de la puce A20 Pro ayant été mise en avant dès la fin du mois d’août.
Lire aussi : iPhone Duo : Apple admet un problème de stock, la situation est plus critique qu’on ne l’imaginait
Les iPhone 18 Pro et Pro Max grimperaient de leur côté à 4 056 et 5 391 mAh dans leurs versions à tiroir SIM. Soit 1,7 % et 11,8 % de mieux que la génération actuelle. Pour le modèle standard, la fuite s’arrête à l’adjectif : plus grande, sans dire de combien. Apple n’a validé aucun de ces éléments, et cette pièce du dossier reste pour l’instant isolée.
Jusqu’où le prix peut-il encore monter ?
La hausse de septembre a fait passer l’iPhone 17 de 969 à 1 119 euros en France, soit 150 euros d’un coup, un an à peine après son lancement. Personne n’y a échappé : l’iPhone 16 est remonté à 1 019 euros, l’iPhone 17e à 869 euros, et l’iPhone Air a pris 100 euros sur ses versions 256 et 512 Go, à 1 329 euros.
L’iPhone 18 répéterait l’opération : la fuite évoque un prix en hausse, sans montant ni justification, et sans préciser si la référence est le tarif d’origine ou celui déjà relevé. La question du prix poursuit pourtant la gamme depuis l’été, entre une hausse qui ne devait rien à la mémoire et la piste d’une offre de location pour amortir la facture. Dès août, l’iPhone 18 Pro était donné si coûteux à fabriquer que la marque devrait rogner ses marges pour en contenir le prix.
Le calendrier prêté à Apple pour le premier semestre 2027 aligne trois appareils, iPhone 18, iPhone 18e et iPhone Air 2, et donne le modèle standard comme le plus vendu du trio à venir.

articles.title: GeForce RTX 5080 24 Go : NVIDIA n’aurait toujours pas fourni les design kits à ses partenaires
articles.text:
Tout porte à croire que la – toujours hypothétique – GeForce RTX 5080 dotée de 24 Go de VRAM ne sortira pas avant, au mieux, février 2027.
En attendant des nouvelles plus excitantes sur le front des cartes graphiques de nouvelle génération, c'est un peu le feuilleton de l'automne. Alors, sortira ou sortira pas cette fameuse GeForce RTX 5080 dotée de 24 Go de VRAM ?
Toujours aucune annonce de la part de NVIDIA
Évoquée pour la première fois seulement quelques semaines après le lancement de la nouvelle gamme GeForce Blackwell, l'hypothétique refonte « SUPER » de ces RTX série 50 est toujours un mystère absolu.
NVIDIA ne communique aucune information officielle à ce sujet et même les informateurs habituellement fiables semblent y perdre leur latin. Après, plusieurs séries d'informations parfaitement plausibles, des nouvelles de report puis d'annulation se sont succédé. Nous en étions restés là cet été, mais la rentrée de septembre et l'arrivée de l'automne ont rebattu les cartes, sans mauvais jeu de mots de notre part.
En effet, l'augmentation régulière du prix de la GeForce RTX 5090 puis sa disparition quasi totale des rayonnages ont été expliquées par différents informateurs : les rares cartes produites sont toutes achetées pour être reconverties et utilisées pour l'intelligence artificielle du fait de leur prix plus attractif – malgré les hausses successives – que les modèles PRO imaginés par NVIDIA pour cet usage.
Dans la foulée, les GeForce RTX 5080 16 Go ont été annoncées comme en fin de production… car une version 24 Go était sur le point de débarquer. Une version qui devait donc faire en quelque sorte d'une pierre deux coups : remettre sur le marché grand public une carte très puissante – certes pas autant que la RTX 5090 – et booster un peu la RTX 5080 16 Go alors que la nouvelle génération de GeForce n'est plus attendue que pour 2028.
Vers une sortie pas avant février 2027 ?
Nous en étions encore là la semaine dernière avec même une éventuelle accélération du calendrier pour NVIDIA : plutôt qu'une disponibilité vague, au cours du premier trimestre 2027, cette GeForce RTX 5080 24 Go avec ses puces VRAM de 3 Go serait lancée en janvier 2027, voire décembre 2026.
Seulement voilà, nos confrères du site VideoCardz ont appris sur BenchLife que les partenaires de NVIDIA n'auraient encore reçu aucun kit de fabrication de cette nouvelle carte graphique. Nous sommes début novembre et cette absence de livraison serait un très mauvais signe : ces kits de fabrication sont absolument indispensables pour les partenaires de NVIDIA qui en ont besoin pour, ensuite, élaborer leurs propres designs.
Problème, le délai entre réception des kits de fabrication et conception des designs des marques était généralement estimé à six semaines. Un délai déjà tendu qui, en plus, datait du temps où les cartes graphiques gaming étaient le centre d'intérêt principal des partenaires de NVIDIA et où les tensions sur le marché n'étaient pas aussi importantes. Aujourd'hui, certains se hasardent plutôt à parler d'un délai de deux mois minimum.
Vous aurez vite fait le calcul, deux mois à compter d'aujourd'hui – et rien ne dit que les kits seront reçus cette semaine ou la suivante –, cela nous mène déjà au début de l'année prochaine. Pour cette raison, BenchLife ne semble plus du tout croire à une sortie courant janvier 2027. Cela n'empêcherait d'ailleurs pas NVIDIA de tout de même présenter la carte au CES 2027 qui se tiendra du 6 au 9 janvier. Simplement, les cartes seront disponibles plus tard.
Source : VideoCardz

articles.title: En pleine nuit, des voleurs s'emparent d'une remorque de batteries Stellantis estimée à 500 000 €
articles.text:
Stellantis victime d’un vol de batteries d'une valeur de 500 000 €, une remorque entière a été dérobée en pleine nuit
Une remorque remplie de cellules de batteries, estimée à 500 000 €, a été volée près de l’usine Stellantis de Hordain (Nord). De quoi donner des sueurs froides à toute la chaîne logistique du géant automobile.
Les composants de voitures électrifiées séduisent les voleurs, et Stellantis vient d’en faire les frais avec une pleine remorque de cellules de batteries subtilisée. Destinées aux véhicules hybrides et électriques du groupe, elles ont tout simplement été dérobées à deux pas de son usine nordiste de Hordain. D’après une source proche du dossier, le butin atteindrait un demi-million d’euros. Cependant, sa revente s’avère bien plus compliquée que prévu.
Un vol de batteries évalué à 500 000 € : la piste du grand banditisme privilégiée
Les faits remontent à une quinzaine de jours, près de Valenciennes. En pleine nuit, des malfaiteurs ont déjoué les dispositifs de sécurité pour repartir avec un poids lourd stationné chez GSF, un prestataire logistique situé juste en face du site industriel de Hordain. Contacté par l’AFP, Stellantis a confirmé ce vol chez son sous-traitant, qui a déposé plainte auprès de la gendarmerie dans la foulée. Selon La Voix du Nord, l’enquête a été confiée à la police judiciaire de Lille, qui privilégie la piste du grand banditisme et une équipe particulièrement bien renseignée.
Des composants sous haute surveillance et difficiles à revendre
À Hordain, où quelque 600 utilitaires Peugeot, Citroën, Opel et Fiat sont assemblés chaque jour, ces modules alimentent des “ateliers très spécialisés”. Stellantis explique qu’on “y ajoute la partie électronique” avant de les glisser “dans un bac d’acier pour en faire une batterie”. Si ces cellules renferment des métaux critiques comme le lithium, le nickel, le manganèse ou le cobalt, écouler la marchandise au marché noir s’annonce complexe en raison d’une traçabilité étroite et de fortes contraintes de manipulation.
La logistique de la Battery Valley face au défi de la sécurité
Si Stellantis ne signale aucune perturbation de production, l’affaire montre que le transport de ces pièces clés reste vulnérable, alors que le constructeur concentre sa production de batteries dans le Nord. À quelques dizaines de kilomètres de là, son ancienne usine de moteurs thermiques de Douvrin a d’ailleurs définitivement fermé le 30 octobre, et une partie des salariés de Stellantis a rejoint la gigafactory de batteries ACC implantée juste à côté. Pour rappel, ce site avait lui-même été ciblé fin 2025 par des vols de matériel électroportatif et de carburant, menant à l’interpellation de trois hommes en métropole lilloise.

articles.title: AMD prevé ingresos de 17.000 millones de dólares en el cuarto trimestre, 66% más que hace un año
articles.text:
AMD proyectó ingresos de unos USD 17.000 millones para el cuarto trimestre de 2026, por encima de los USD 16.230 millones que esperaban los analistas, según datos de LSEG citados por Reuters. La fabricante de chips lo anunció tras registrar ventas récord de USD 13.377 millones en el tercer trimestre, con centros de datos casi duplicados.
Los ingresos subieron 45% frente a los USD 9.246 millones de un año antes. La ganancia por acción ajustada fue de USD 2,09, contra USD 1,95 que anticipaba el mercado, según CNBC. La ganancia neta contable llegó a USD 2.428 millones, 95% más. Las acciones subían 8% en la negociación posterior al cierre.
La directora ejecutiva, Lisa Su, dijo en la llamada con analistas que fue el trimestre “más grande y más rentable” de la historia de la compañía. Los ingresos superaron el extremo alto de la proyección que AMD había dado para ese período.
Para el cuarto trimestre, la empresa estimó un margen de ganancia bruta ajustado de 55%. El punto medio de su rango, con una variación de 3% hacia arriba o hacia abajo, implica un crecimiento de 66% anual y de 27% frente al trimestre anterior.
Cómo los centros de datos fueron claves para AMD
El segmento de centros de datos facturó un récord de USD 8.546 millones, 97% más que los USD 4.341 millones del tercer trimestre de 2025. Representó 64% de los ingresos totales, frente a 47% un año antes. Reuters informó que las estimaciones de analistas eran de USD 8.200 millones.
AMD atribuyó el avance a los procesadores EPYC para servidores y al lanzamiento de las GPU (chips gráficos usados para entrenar y ejecutar IA) Instinct MI450. Su dijo que las ventas de servidores a nubes públicas y a empresas más que se duplicaron, por encima del crecimiento superior a 80% que la compañía había previsto.
En su presentación a inversores, AMD informó que Anthropic, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI y Oracle Cloud Infrastructure ejecutan modelos y cargas de trabajo en los primeros sistemas Helios, armarios de servidores completos que la empresa diseñó para IA. La directiva espera que el segmento de centros de datos crezca cerca de 50% frente al trimestre anterior.
El avance también se notó fuera de AMD. Según CNBC, las acciones de proveedoras de capacidad de cómputo para IA como CoreWeave y Nebius subieron durante la jornada y se mantuvieron al alza tras conocerse los resultados.
Videojuegos en caída y un 2027 con más de 80% de crecimiento
El segmento de consumo no acompañó. Cliente y videojuegos facturó USD 3.700 millones, 8% menos. Los ingresos de videojuegos cayeron 40%, a USD 773 millones, por menores ventas de chips a medida y de gráficos. Los procesadores Ryzen para portátiles impulsaron un alza de 7% en computadoras personales, a USD 2.900 millones. El segmento de sistemas embebidos creció 29%, a USD 1.100 millones.
Para 2027, Su proyectó que los ingresos crecerán más de 80%, por encima del 77% que estimaban los analistas según LSEG. El director financiero, Jean Hu, dijo que los centros de datos superarán 80% de las ventas totales. Su agregó que los ingresos por servidores se duplicarán ese año.
AMD terminó el trimestre con USD 15.800 millones en efectivo e inversiones a corto plazo y una deuda de USD 7.100 millones, que incluye USD 4.750 millones en bonos emitidos en agosto. La empresa prevé cerrar en el cuarto trimestre la compra de World Labs y Taalas, anunciadas durante el tercero.
Lisa Su, la única mujer premiada por Trump con la Medalla Nacional de Ciencia
Lisa Su, CEO de AMD, fue distinguida por Donald Trump con la Medalla Nacional de Ciencia, máximo galardón científico de Estados Unidos, y fue la única mujer reconocida ese día.
El premio destacó su liderazgo en computación de alto rendimiento. También recibieron la medalla Elon Musk, Sergey Brin y Jensen Huang. Su patrimonio neto, ligado a AMD, asciende a 3.400 millones de dólares, según Forbes.

articles.title: Los glaciares de los Pirineos tienen fecha de caducidad: apuntan a desaparecer por completo en 2034
articles.text:
Los glaciares que hay en los Pirineos están viviendo sus horas más bajas. Lo que durante siglos fue un paisaje dominado por masas de hielo perpetuo se está transformando a un ritmo que ya no se mide en siglos, sino en veranos de mucha calor. Así lo apuntan los últimos datos de la campaña 2025-2026, que confirman que estamos asistiendo a la extinción en tiempo real de los últimos glaciares de la península ibérica, un proceso irreversible que podrá culminar en 2034.
Un respiro. Podría parecer que 2026 dio un respiro a las cumbres, puesto que durante la primavera, el Pirineo registró nevadas abundantes que dejaron valores récord a principios de marzo. Sin embargo, el informe publicado a finales de octubre por CryoPyr ha apuntado a que la nieve invernal ya no es un escudo frente a los tórridos veranos que estamos viviendo.
Y no es para menos, puesto que esta temporada se ha cerrado como el tercer año con más pérdidas de hielo desde que comenzaron los registros anuales en el año 2012, solo superado por las campañas 2021-2022 y 2022-2023.
La medida. Para medir este declive, los investigadores han abandonado las viejas estimaciones y ahora utilizan drones que generan modelos 3D de alta resolución. Al superponer estos modelos con los de años anteriores, se ha podido ver que en Ossoue (la vertiente francesa) la pérdida media fue de 3,1 metros de espesor, con zonas que han llegado a perder 4,9 metros.
Pero tenemos otros puntos como Aneto, con una pérdida media de 2,4 metros o Monte Perdido, donde la pérdida ha sido de 2,3 metros, con picos locales de hasta seis metros en su superficie.
Fragmentación. El hielo no solo pierde grosor, sino que se está rompiendo, como se ha visto en el glaciar del Aneto, donde ya una división en su zona oriental en 2025 lo dejó reducido a apenas 30 hectáreas. Ahora, una nueva fragmentación parece condenarlo a que cada vez esté dividido en secciones más pequeñas.
A esto se suma el oscurecimiento, que es un fenómeno que hace que los glaciares pierdan su dinámica y dejen de fluir, puesto que ya no tienen fuerza para expulsar las rocas y los sedimentos. El resultado es que, al final del verano, la superficie del hielo se oscurece y al perder su blancura, absorbe mucha más radiación solar, acelerando aún más su propia fundición.
Fecha límite. Un estudio publicado el año pasado realizó una simulación climática para ver cómo progresará este fenómeno y determinó que el Pirinero quedará libre de hielo hacia el año 2034. Incluso bajo escenarios de emisiones moderados, para 2030 el Aneto habrá perdido el 79% de su hielo. Y si se repiten veranos como el de 2022, el final llegará incluso antes.
¿Afectará al agua? La respuesta es no, puesto que el impacto hidrológico de estos glaciares es hoy en día casi despreciable para el caudal de los ríos de la región. Su pérdida es, ante todo, una inmensa tragedia paisajística, ecológica y simbólica, más que un problema de suministro de agua.

articles.title: Your AI agents are generating data you can’t afford to monitor
articles.text:
I’ve spent more than 20 years in enterprise technology, running data centers for major financial institutions, building products at enterprise software companies, working across cloud infrastructure, DevOps, and observability.
I’ve watched a lot of technology waves roll through the enterprise. And in my experience, the ones that catch organizations flat-footed are never the ones nobody saw coming. They’re the ones everyone saw coming and still didn’t prepare for.
Agentic AI is shaping up to be one of those waves.
Chief Product and Technology Officer at Apica.
The conversation in enterprise IT right now is almost entirely focused on the models, which one to choose, how to govern its outputs, whether the ROI is real.
What’s not getting nearly enough attention is what happens to your IT infrastructure when those agents start running. Specifically, what happens to your telemetry data.
Recent Omdia research surveying more than 300 enterprise IT decision-makers across North America and Western Europe should make any CTO uncomfortable.
The explosion is already happening and most organizations are already behind
Start with what’s happening right now, before agentic AI fully kicks in. More than half of the enterprises surveyed reported that their telemetry data volume more than tripled in the past 12 months, with an average increase of 3.7x. AI and ML workloads already account for approximately 43% of that growth. This isn’t a future projection; the majority of respondents are experiencing exponential data growth today.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
The forward-looking numbers are where it gets genuinely alarming. Enterprises anticipate a 9.5x average increase in telemetry data from agentic AI workloads within the next two years. That’s the average; nearly half of respondents expect growth somewhere between 6x and 100x. Omdia’s senior market research analyst Keir Walker put it plainly: “This is just the beginning of the growth curve. We are at the beginning of the hockey stick.”
When I say most organizations aren’t ready for this, I’m not editorializing. Roughly two-thirds of organizations describe themselves as only “somewhat prepared” or worse for the data volumes agentic AI will generate. Twenty-two percent haven’t even begun to consider the data implications. Meanwhile, 35% already report widespread agentic AI deployment. The gap between deployment ambition and infrastructure readiness is not a small one.
The cost problem is already worse than most people realize
Here’s the number that stopped me when I first saw it: 69% of organizations actively running agentic AI projects report that their observability costs now exceed their compute and infrastructure costs. The technology meant to support AI has become the single largest line item in the AI budget.
Average annual enterprise observability spend is sitting at $3.17 million, growing at 28% year-over-year. Thirty-five percent of enterprises are seeing budget increases above 52%. Nearly one in five is already spending more than $5 million annually just on observability. Eighty-one percent are actively looking for ways to cut those costs.
And the consequences of not managing this aren’t just financial. Fifty-nine percent of organizations have already terminated or delayed at least one agentic AI deployment because monitoring costs were too high. These aren’t experimental projects being shelved. When observability costs become unsustainable, organizations pause the AI agents responsible for cybersecurity monitoring, compliance, and fraud detection. 27% and 26% of respondents cited exactly those exposure areas as direct consequences of paused or cancelled deployments.
Think about what that means in practice. A company decides it can’t afford to monitor an AI agent handling fraud detection, so it gets shut down. That’s not a technology problem. That’s a risk management failure.
The infrastructure assumption that’s now broken
The observability infrastructure most enterprises rely on today was built for a different era: Predictable data volumes, manageable costs, centralized platforms. Agentic AI breaks all three of those assumptions at the same time.
The fundamental issue is architectural. Most observability platforms are built to ingest everything and then sort it out. That model works when data volumes are relatively stable. It doesn’t work when you’re facing a 9.5x surge in telemetry from autonomous AI systems that are constantly reasoning, acting, and generating signals. You can’t just throw more storage and more backend capacity at this problem. The math doesn’t work, and the budget won’t survive it.
What the organizations pulling ahead have figured out is that you need an intelligent layer between your telemetry sources and your observability platforms, one that routes, filters, enriches, and governs data before it ever hits a costly backend. This isn’t a new concept in infrastructure terms, but the urgency around it is new. Omdia’s research found that enterprises with a telemetry pipeline in place are 50% more likely to be prepared for 6x or greater data growth, and those with mature pipeline deployments are 80% more likely to have avoided the operational cost challenges still constraining organizations in earlier stages.
The pipeline isn’t a workaround. It’s the architectural foundation that makes continued observability investment viable at agentic AI scale. As Omdia principal analyst Torsten Volk put it: “Scalability is really the underlying issue for everything, for security, for cost, for rolling out projects. I don’t see any point of diminishing returns or any slow downward trend in data volume growth.”
The window to act is narrower than most think
Ninety-seven percent of organizations have either implemented or are actively considering a telemetry pipeline solution, and 70% are in active evaluation cycles right now. This market is not moving slowly.
One detail from the Omdia research that I think gets overlooked: Nearly one in four respondents say existing vendor relationships are not a significant factor in their purchase decision. That’s a more open competitive environment than most people assume. The capabilities buyers say they want most are multi-destination routing, data reduction and sampling, and content-based routing; all of which point toward pipeline-first architecture rather than expanding incumbent observability platforms.
The data represents a decision point, not a warning. The organizations that solve the infrastructure problem before it becomes a budget crisis are the ones that will scale agentic AI on their terms. The ones that don’t will find themselves choosing between monitoring their AI deployments and affording them.
That’s not a choice any organization should have to make.

articles.title: Logitech G Pro X3 Superstrike Review: $200 for the illusion of a click
articles.text:
Tom's Hardware Verdict
The G Pro X3 Superstrike brings a new chipset and rebalancing to Logitech's revolutionary mouse. But at $200, it's probably not worth it for most gamers.
Reasons to buy
- + Lightweight, easy shape
- + 135 hours of battery life
- + Centered weight feels much better
Reasons to avoid
- - $200
- - Haptics are weaker
- - $200
Why you can trust Tom's Hardware
Our expert reviewers spend hours testing and comparing products and services so you can choose the best for you. Find out more about how we test.
It only launched at the beginning of this year, but Logitech's most innovative, game-changing mouse, the Logitech G Pro X2 Superstrike, has already gotten an upgrade.
The new Logitech G Pro X3 Superstrike looks just like its predecessor (okay... the colors are different), but it's what's inside that counts. The new mouse features Logitech's new NxLOGI chipset, which improves performance and efficiency and supports 8,000 Hz polling over both wired and wireless connections. The mouse also weighs two grams less and has been rebalanced to be more center-weighted rather than front-heavy, like the X2 Superstrike.
The upgrade doesn't come without an upcharge, of course: The new G Pro X3 Superstrike costs $199.99, which is... kind of crazy for a mouse. The X2 Superstrike debuted at $179.99, which was already higher than average, but $200 seems like a line most will not want to cross. The mouse does come in two colorways now — black and "magenta eclipse," a black and pink colorway that matches Logitech's other pink G Pro peripherals.
Design and Comfort of the G Pro X3 Superstrike
The G Pro X3 Superstrike has the exact same shape as the original G Pro X2 Superstrike — which has the exact same shape as the G Pro X Superlight and Superlight 2. The mouse has a pseudo-symmetrical design, with sides that taper at the middle, and a centered hump with a mild slope. It's not a terribly exciting or revolutionary shape, but it's comfortable, easy to handle, and quick to get used to. The mouse measures 4.92 inches (125mm) long by 2.5 inches (63.5mm) wide, and is 1.57 inches (40mm) high at its highest point.
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
The X3 weighs just 2.08 ounces (59g), which makes it 2g lighter than its predecessor (2.15oz / 61g). While that's not a big difference, Logitech has rebalanced the weight in the X3 Superstrike to make it feel more centered — and it does feel more centered, though it still felt slightly front-weighted to me. But still, it feels noticeably different (and better) than the very front-heavy feel of the original X2 Superstrike.
Fancy chipsets and HITS technology aside, the X3 Superstrike is a pretty basic five-button mouse, with two large primary buttons that have slight finger grooves, two large side buttons, and a clickable, notched scroll wheel covered in textured rubber. The mouse has the same smooth matte finish as the X2 Superstrike and the Superlights, which feels fine but is prone to fingerprints. Of course, the mouse still has the Superstrike branding all over it, with crosses on the mouse buttons, "Superstrike" on the right side, and a giant "X3" on the left.
The bottom of the mouse is also pretty simple, with large UHMWPE mouse feet at the top and bottom, plus a strip around the sensor. There's also a power switch and a magnetic mouse puck that you can swap out — either for the included extra puck, which is covered in UHMWPE for even more glide, or for the charging puck that comes with Logitech's PowerPlay 2. Under the mouse puck, there's a slot for storing the mouse's wireless dongle, which is a nice touch — other ultra-lightweight, performance-focused mice don't always have this.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
In the box, the X3 Superstrike comes with a rubberized 6-foot (1.8m) USB-C to USB-A cable, a 2.4GHz wireless USB-A dongle, an extra mouse puck, pre-cut grip tape, and a USB converter. The cable is lightweight and flexible — while it's not covered in paracord, it's fairly usable as a mouse cable with the X3 Superstrike. It's worth pointing out that the X3 Superstrike does support 8,000 Hz polling over both its wireless and wired connections, now (the X2 Superstrike only supported 8,000 Hz polling over wireless).
Specs
| Sensor Model | Hero 2 | 
| Max Sensitivity | 48,000 DPI | 
| Max Speed (IPS) | 930 IPS | 
| Max Acceleration | 90 G | 
| Max Polling Rate | 8,000 Hz | 
| Programmable Buttons | 5 | 
| LED Zones | 0 | 
| Cable | 6ft / 1.8m USB-C to USB-A | 
| Connectivity | 2.4GHz wireless, Bluetooth, USB-C | 
| Measurements (L x W x H) | 4.92 x 2.5 x 1.57 inches / 125 x 63.5 x 40 mm | 
| Weight (excluding cable) | 2.08oz / 59g | 
| MSRP / Price at Time of Review | 199.99 | 
| Release Date | Sept. 2026 | 
Performance of the G Pro X3 Superstrike
The G Pro X3 Superstrike features Logitech's Hero 2 optical sensor, which has a maximum resolution of 48,000 DPI and a maximum speed of 930 IPS, and can handle up to 90 G's of force. If those numbers seem different from the Hero 2 optical sensor in the X2 Superstrike, that's because they are — while both mice have the same sensor, apparently the new NxLOGI chipset in the X3 Superstrike unlocks the true potential of said sensor, and allows for higher resolution, speed, and acceleration. That said, it is a great sensor — accurate, consistent, and able to track on virtually any surface without skipping.
Like the X2 Superstrike, the X3 Superstrike features Logitech's Haptic Inductive Trigger System (HITS), which means there are no switches under the primary buttons — instead, there's a combo of haptic motors and inductive sensors that allow for adjustable actuation and create the illusion of a mouse click. This is the most intriguing part of the Superstrike line, since raising the actuation point genuinely does translate to faster, more responsive clicks.
The haptic click feedback is interesting. I found the feedback to be surprisingly convincing on the X2 Superstrike, even though it's still pretty obvious that it's not a "real" switch. The click feedback on the X3 Superstrike is still... fairly convincing, but it's definitely softer than the feedback on the original. You can still adjust the feedback level (five levels), but feedback just feels firmer on the original — I guess Logitech sacrificed some haptic power for efficiency, or something. The side buttons still have regular switches, and they're a little mushy but otherwise inoffensive. The scroll wheel has a very soft scroll and muted click, but at least it's not loud. In fact, this is probably the quietest mouse I've ever used — even with click strength set to the highest (5), it's barely audible.
In addition to adjustable actuation, the X3 Superstrike also allows for Rapid Trigger, which resets the mouse button's actuation as soon as your finger lifts, allowing for even faster clicks.
Features and Software of the G Pro X3 Superstrike
The G Pro X3 Superstrike is configurable via Logitech G Hub, which is the company's universal peripheral software. You can use G Hub to adjust the mouse's settings — DPI, DPI steps, and polling rate (both wired and wireless) — calibrate the mouse, and remap buttons (though you're probably not remapping a ton of buttons on a five-button mouse). You can also enable BHOP for the scroll wheel, which helps prevent accidental movement when you bump the scroll wheel.
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
And, of course, you can set up the HITS features in the HITS tab. These include adjustable actuation, Rapid Trigger, and click haptics, and each mouse button can be set independently. There's also a bunch of presets from professional competitive gamers, in case you're not sure where to start (you can also add your own custom presets to this list).
Wireless Experience and Battery Life of the G Pro X3 Superstrike
Logitech rates the battery life of the G Pro X3 Superstrike at 135 hours in constant motion, which is actually a pretty big improvement over the X2 Superstrike's 90-hour rating. This is over a 1,000 Hz polling rate, of course, and the number drops to under 40 hours with an 8,000 Hz polling rate (which is still not terrible, I suppose). Thankfully, the X3 Superstrike can get an 8,000 Hz polling rate over both its wired and wireless connections — the X2 Superstrike has an 8,000 Hz wireless polling rate but maxes out at 1,000 Hz when plugged in — so it won't be the battery life that does you in.
Bottom Line
The G Pro X3 Superstrike isn't too different from the X2 Superstrike — but the difference in balance, at least, is absolutely noticeable. This doesn't make me think the X3 Superstrike is revolutionary, though it makes me think that Logitech should have waited and launched the Superstrike line with this mouse. The click haptics are weaker here, but the mouse is better overall. However, is it better enough to justify the $200 price? Probably not.
If you're at the top of your game and you're absolutely certain that the only thing holding you back is the minuscule latency from non-adjustable actuation, sure, get the X3 Superstrike. If you already have the G Pro X2 Superstrike, the upgrade probably isn't worth it — in the time it took you to get used to the click haptics, you probably also got used to the balance, and that's the only noticeable difference. And if you're just looking for a symmetrical, ultra-lightweight mouse, you can always pick up the G Pro X Superlight 2, which can often be found for around $100.
Sarah Jacobsson Purewal is a senior editor at Tom's Hardware covering peripherals, software, and custom builds. You can find more of her work in PCWorld, Macworld, TechHive, CNET, Gizmodo, Tom's Guide, PC Gamer, Men's Health, Men's Fitness, SHAPE, Cosmopolitan, and just about everywhere else.

articles.title: Milliardenraub bei Binance: Wie ein falsches Bewerbungsgespräch Angreifern die Tür öffnete
articles.text:
Milliardenraub bei Binance: Wie ein falsches Bewerbungsgespräch Angreifern die Tür öffnete
Dem wohl bislang größten Währungsklau gingen offenbar Monate der Vorbereitung voraus. Gefälschte Bewerbungsgespräche, Schadsoftware und manipulierte KI-Werkzeuge kamen zur Verwendung. Das erklärte Richard Teng, Co-Chef der Kryptobörse Binance, dem US-Nachrichtensender CNBC. Damit widerspricht Teng der bisherigen Darstellung, nach der allein der kompromittierte Laptop eines DevOps-Ingenieurs – also eines Entwicklers, der für Betrieb und Wartung der Systeme der Plattform zuständig war – als Einfallstor diente. Teng schob die Verantwortung zudem nicht ausdrücklich Nordkorea zu, erkannte aber die entsprechende Einschätzung des FBI an. Das nordkoreanische Regime hatte den Vorwurf Anfang der Woche zurückgewiesen, doch gibt es grobe Zweifel an dem Dementi.
Erster Kontakt im Juni: ein vermeintliches KI-Tool
Laut einer Vorfallbeschreibung von Binance auf X begannen die Vorbereitungen der Angreifer vermutlich schon im Juni. Ein Entwickler wollte damals ein KI-Werkzeug auf seinem Rechner installieren, das er über eine schlichte Internetsuche gefunden hatte. Binance entdeckte den Vorfall, stufte dies als Sicherheitsproblem ein, tauschte das Gerät aus und änderte die Zugangsdaten. Zu diesem Zeitpunkt wussten die Angreifer aber bereits, dass der Mann zum Wallet-Team gehörte – also zu jener Abteilung, die die digitalen Geldbörsen der Börse verwaltet.
Im September luden die Angreifer dann einen Kollegen des Entwicklers über eine bekannte Jobplattform zu einem Bewerbungsgespräch ein. Sie gaben sich als Projektleiter aus, lockten mit einer guten Anstellung und nutzten dabei ihr Wissen aus dem ersten Vorfall. Im Gespräch forderten sie den zweiten Entwickler auch auf, eine Software zu installieren. Diese enthielt Schadcode und diente dann als Einfallstor. Am 20. Oktober missbrauchten die Angreifer zusätzlich ein internes KI-Werkzeug von Binance, um weitere Geräte zu übernehmen. Neun Tage später schlugen sie zu und griffen Krypowährung ab.
6,3 Milliarden Dollar in knapp vier Stunden
Am 29. Oktober stahlen die Angreifer somit innerhalb von knapp vier Stunden 6,3 Milliarden US-Dollar. Rund 2,85 Milliarden US-Dollar davon konnten zumindest eingefroren werden. Die verbleibende Währungsbeute von über drei Milliarden US-Dollar ist dennoch die bislang größte der Geschichte. Sie übertrifft den bisherigen Rekord von 1,4 Milliarden US-Dollar deutlich, der im Februar 2025 bei der Kryptobörse Bybit erbeutet wurde.
Hinter beiden Diebstählen soll die nordkoreanische Gruppe „TraderTraitor“ stecken. Die Angreifer arbeiten direkt mit der Regierung zusammen, dürften von der Beute stets nur einen Teil behalten. Sie hätte damit in weniger als zwei Jahren eine beispiellose Summe für das Regime erbeutet. Nordkorea kauft davon unter anderem Waffentechnik, sagen Beobachter.

articles.title: After Xbox, Sony Starts Asking Owners to Trade In Their PS5
articles.text:
Wednesday, November 4th 2026
After Xbox, Sony Starts Asking Owners to Trade In Their PS5
Sony has started nudging some PlayStation owners in the US to sell their PS5, with a PlayStation app notification shared on ResetEra offering "up to $400" for a standard console. The trade-in itself runs through Back Market, which inspects the hardware and then sends cash straight to the owner's bank account instead of offering store credit. That $400 figure comes with some fine print, though. It is based on quotes for a standard PS5 in Grade 0 condition, which is basically flawless, with two or more controllers included, collected between August 23 and September 22. PS5 Pro owners aren't part of this one. The timing certainly looks pretty convenient, with GTA 6 launching on November 19 and pre-load starting on November 10. 
Coincidentally, Microsoft also started emailing inactive Xbox owners last month, offering up to $375 for a Series X traded in at Best Buy. Sony's offer looks a little better on paper, since Microsoft pays out in Best Buy eGift Cards rather than cash. A couple of users who ran the online trade-in estimate got a little over $400 for a base PS5, so the headline number seems realistic for consoles in good shape. A new PS5 now costs $649.99 after Sony's April price hike, while the $899.99 PS5 Pro is hard to find at list price, and GameStop is reportedly asking $1,399.99 for used units. With retailers already expecting console shortages around the GTA 6 launch, used PS5s will probably sell fast. Owners with an idle console are advised to compare Back Market's quote with local resale prices before shipping it off.

articles.title: Garmin Forerunner 70 com 5 ATM cai 38% com cupom no Mercado Livre • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Garmin Forerunner 70 com 5 ATM cai 38% com cupom no Mercado Livre
Forerunner 70 resiste a até 5 ATM e possui bateria que dura até 28 dias; smartwatch da Garmin recebe desconto de 38% no Pix com cupom no mês da Black Friday
O Garmin Forerunner 70 está saindo por R$ 1.599 no Pix com cupom DESCONTOS no Mercado Livre. O smartwatch com resistência a até 5 ATM, bateria de longa duração e suporte a atividades esportivas, recebe desconto de 38% sobre o preço original de R$ 2.599 durante o Black November 2026.
O Forerunner 70 possui um corpo de 43 mm resistente a até 5 ATM, oferecendo proteção a condições extremas e permitindo seu uso em esportes aquáticos, segundo a fabricante. Os apenas 512 MB de espaço interno são dedicados ao SO e não permitem salvar músicas ou instalar apps localmente.
Seus sensores especializados cobrem diversas atividades físicas diferentes, como caminhada, corrida e ciclismo, e o modo Garmin Couch traça planos de treino personalizados. Ele também possui medidores do sono, saúde da mulher e oxigenação do sangue, e monitora o consumo de calorias, álcool e cafeína.
Este acessório também pode ser de grande ajuda em situações de risco: no caso de uma emergência médica, ele pode disparar mensagens para contatos pré-determinados, informando a localização exata do usuário para serviços de resgate e pessoas próximas, mas apenas se estiver pareado a um celular.
A tela AMOLED de 1,2″ do Forerunner 70 reproduz imagens com cores bem definidas e brilho forte. O vidro Gorilla Glass 3 protege-a contra pancadas e arranhões.
Sua bateria resiste a até 13 dias de uso no modo smartwatch (5 dias com Always-On ligado), até 28 dias no modo de economia, e até 16 horas com navegação ativa e todos os recursos disponíveis (até 23 horas apenas com o GPS ligado), segundo a fabricante.
O Garmin Forerunner 70 (R$ 1.599 no Pix com cupom DESCONTOS) suporta iPhone e Android e possui conectividade Bluetooth e GPS multibanda, que determina a posição exata do usuário em tempo real.
O Black November é o mês em que o varejo oferece diversas ofertas em eletrônicos com condições especiais, antes da chegada da Black Friday 2026, em 27 de novembro.

articles.title: Waymo confirms it's shaking up its Uber relationship in January 2028 | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Waymo will end its exclusivity with Uber in the Austin and Atlanta markets starting in January 2028, co-CEO Tekedra Mawakana told Bloomberg News in a report published Wednesday.
The robotaxi company will offer rides directly through its own smartphone app, like it does in other cities. Uber confirmed to TechCrunch Wednesday that it still plans to host Waymo robotaxis on its app for as long as the two companies agree. Waymo did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Mawakana’s comments come after reporting earlier this year by the Financial Times that Waymo was looking to get out of its deal with Uber, which was set to expire in May 2028. Mawakana told Bloomberg that Waymo initially partnered with Uber because the ride-hail giant offered scale. But the experience for riders has been “a little bit of a crapshoot,” she said, especially because riders never know for sure if they’re going to hail a robotaxi or a human-driven car.
“It’s important for us to have that relationship with the rider. We’ve gotten that feedback from the riders in those markets,” Mawakana said.
Uber — which has many robotaxi and other autonomous vehicle partners — told Bloomberg that it was Waymo’s idea not to add an option in the ride-hail giant’s app to book a robotaxi directly.
This story has been updated with new information from Uber.

articles.title: Nykaa's PAT soars 206% in Q2FY27 as beauty, quick commerce arm deliver strong performance
articles.text:
Nykaa's PAT soars 206% in Q2FY27 as beauty, quick commerce arm deliver strong performance
Nykaa also announced the acquisition of an 82% majority stake in Simply Nam, a cosmetics brand founded in 2020 by celebrity makeup artist Namrata Soni alongside Bozzil, a venture studio led by Hanna Strömgren Khan. The acquisition is expected to help Nykaa widen its premium makeup portfolio.
Omnichannel beauty and fashion retailer Nykaa has reported a profit after tax (PAT) of Rs 101 crore, up 206% in Q2 of FY27 compared with Rs 33 crore a year ago.
Nykaa, which is operated by FSN E-Commerce Ventures, reported Rs. 3,006 crore in revenue from operations, an increase of 28% YoY.
Its beauty vertical continued to drive the bulk of its business, with a gross merchandise value (GMV) at Rs. 4,454 crore. Meanwhile, its fashion revenue increased 42.9% YoY to Rs 287.2 crore.
House of Nykaa clocked an annualised GMV run rate of Rs. 4,000 crore, and Rs. 2,300 crore annualised NSV for Q2 FY2027, which is a 36% YoY NSV growth. On the other hand, Superstore by Nykaa has clocked a gross merchandise value (GMV) of Rs 328 crore, and its registered retailer base grew 27% YoY to over 550,000. Net Sales Value or NSV is the actual realised value of goods after the platform accounts for discounts, cancellations, returned items and taxes.
“Our performance this quarter reflects the strength of the Nykaa ecosystem, with each of our businesses contributing to growth and productivity gains. We continued to improve operational efficiency, particularly across marketing and overheads. Beauty and Fashion are seeing accelerated growth, while House of Nykaa and Wellness offer significant runway for long-term growth. We remain focused on building differentiated businesses that serve our consumers and deliver sustainable growth over the long term," Falguni Nayar, executive chairperson, founder and CEO of Nykaa, said.
Nykaa also announced the acquisition of an 82% majority stake in Simply Nam, a cosmetics brand founded in 2020 by celebrity makeup artist Namrata Soni alongside Bozzil, a venture studio led by Hanna Strömgren Khan. The acquisition is expected to help Nykaa widen its premium makeup portfolio.
Nykaa also highlighted the growth of its quick delivery arm, NYKAA Now, which promises 30-to-60 minute delivery. Launched in 2025, the service is available in 15 cities and the company hopes to expand this number to 25 by end of FY2027. Nykaa noted that the vertical offers over 1,000 marquee brands and twice the beauty and personal care (BPC) catalog depth of conventional quick-commerce platforms. The wider selection is reportedly driving an average order value three times higher than typical quick commerce purchases.
Overall, the company has expanded its beauty retail footprint to 338 stores across 111 cities.

Black Friday 2026 – Le drone DJI Lito X1 Pack Fly More Combo RC 2 à 549,99 € (-17%)
Malgré une famille Mini déjà bien fournie, DJI élargi sa gamme en lançant simultanément les drones Lito 1 et Lito X1, deux nouveaux modèles au gabarit très semblable. Ils constituent une porte d’entrée très accessible aux débutants et bien placée côté tarifs sans renier pour autant les performances avec un capteur LiDAR pour la détection d’obstacles.

Points forts
- Stabilité de vol et prise en main exemplaire.
- Détection d’obstacles omnidirectionnelle avec LiDAR frontal.
- RTH intelligent, capable d’éviter les obstacles et de fonctionner sans GPS.
- Tenue au vent jusqu’à 10,7 m/s.
- Mode D-Log M 10 bits en vidéo.
- Autonomie réelle confortable.

Points faibles

- Pas de LED d’éclairage vers le bas.

- Écart entre l’autonomie annoncée et l’autonomie constatée en vol.
- Batterie incompatible avec celle du Lito 1 ou du Mini 5 Pro.
Le DJI Lito X1 ne révolutionne pas le genre, mais ce n’était pas vraiment l’objectif de DJI. Si vous débutez ou possédez encore un ancien Mini dépourvu de tout capteur anticollision, le Lito X1 offre un rapport qualité/prix qui rivalise sans complexe avec un Mini 4 Pro nettement plus onéreux. Les possesseurs d’un Mini Pro récent, en revanche, n’auront pas de raison objective de migrer. Ce drone possède encore une longueur d’avance du côté de la qualité d’image et de la finesse de sa détection d’obstacles, grâce à son capteur d’un pouce. articles.title: ChatGPT à l'assaut de Google : OpenAI revendique déjà 20 % du volume de recherche
articles.text:
OpenAI a avancé un chiffre inédit lors d’un échange avec la presse en début de semaine : le volume de recherches traitées par ChatGPT atteindrait environ 20 % de celui de Google. L’estimation vient d’Adam Fry, responsable du produit ChatGPT grand public, deux ans environ après l’arrivée de la recherche web dans le chatbot. Bing, lui, resterait cantonné à une part à un seul chiffre.
Que compte exactement OpenAI ?
« Chaque fois que vous posez une question et que la réponse passe par une recherche sur le web, c’est une recherche », résume Adam Fry. La définition compte large : elle englobe toute requête qui déclenche une consultation du web, y compris quand ChatGPT décide seul d’aller y puiser. Le point de comparaison, lui, reste flou : OpenAI ne précise ni la source ni le périmètre du volume de requêtes attribué à Google, ce qui laisse au ratio une marge d’interprétation confortable. La période couverte par sa propre mesure n’a pas davantage été détaillée.
Lire aussi : 500 milliards de dollars envolés : le mode IA de Google se retourne contre lui
Une estimation indépendante publiée en mars situait le même rapport autour de 12 %, en comptant comme recherches 65 % de l’activité de ChatGPT. La répartition des usages venait d’une étude menée par OpenAI avec des chercheurs de Harvard sur 1,5 million de conversations. Ses volumes dataient en outre : l’activité de ChatGPT y était photographiée à l’été 2025, celle de Google via une communication de début 2025. Entre les 12 % d’alors et les 20 % revendiqués aujourd’hui, méthodes et périodes diffèrent trop pour y lire une simple progression.
Google doit-il trembler ?
La même estimation documentait un rapport de force intact sur le trafic : environ 40 % des visites des sites web proviennent de Google, 0,21 % de ChatGPT, un écart de 1 à 190. Google a tout de même reconnu fin octobre une monétisation en retrait, liée à la place prise par l’IA dans son propre moteur de recherche. Le tableau d’ensemble bouge d’ailleurs depuis le printemps, ChatGPT ayant perdu au mois de juin la majorité du marché de l’IA qu’il détenait jusque-là.
La recherche web de ChatGPT s’est ouverte fin 2024, et son éditeur la présente désormais en rivale directe du moteur de Google. La publicité ne rebuterait pas ses utilisateurs, au point qu’Adam Fry estime qu’OpenAI pourrait « en faire plus » ; la personnalisation des réponses figurerait, elle, parmi les fonctions les plus appréciées du service. Même à 20 %, il resterait toutefois à transformer ces requêtes en revenus, le terrain exact sur lequel Google a bâti sa fortune et où ChatGPT fait ses premiers pas.
OpenAI se mesure désormais à Google sur le terrain où celui-ci gagne sa vie, la recherche. Et il le fait au moment où la publicité s’installe dans ChatGPT, annoncée en France pour la fin de l’été. Les annonceurs, eux, savent compter.

articles.title: Windows 95 au poignet : cette montre remplace les aiguilles par des curseurs de souris
articles.text:
Un fond turquoise, des fenêtres grises et une barre de chargement : la Desktop 95 transforme les souvenirs de vieux PC Microsoft en montre analogique. Jusqu’aux aiguilles, remplacées par deux pointeurs de souris.
Il fut un temps où l’on cliquait sur « Démarrer » pour éteindre son ordinateur. Où « trois minutes restantes » pouvait laisser le temps d’aller goûter et de revenir. La marque hongkongaise Benly propose d’emporter un morceau de cette époque au poignet, avec la Desktop 95. Sur son cadran, le programme est déjà lancé : « Loading memories… ».
Les curseurs donnent l’heure, les souvenirs chargent
La version bleue retrouve le turquoise caractéristique des bureaux Windows de l’époque, avec ses fenêtres aux bordures en relief, ses petites icônes et sa barre des tâches. On aurait presque envie de chercher le Démineur pour occuper quelques minutes.
Au centre, une main et une flèche de souris font office d’aiguilles. Elles parcourent ce décor informatique en pointant vers les repères horaires disposés sur le pourtour. Une seconde version adopte un fond clair et réorganise les éléments, pour ceux qui ont suffisamment vu de turquoise dans leur jeunesse.
Le détail le plus amusant reste cette boîte de dialogue « Loading memories… », accompagnée d’une barre de progression. Celle-ci n’avancera jamais, mais inutile de chercher Ctrl + Alt + Suppr ou de cliquer frénétiquement, ça ne fera pas arriver la suite plus vite.
Pour ceux qui préfèrent retrouver une interface rétro sur leur écran, EmuOS permet aussi de relancer des jeux et logiciels d’époque directement dans le navigateur.
- Lance des jeux dans le navigateur
- Interface inspirée de Windows
- Aucun téléchargement requis
Une série de 500 pièces, à 173,95 euros
Sous ce décor, Benly reste fidèle à l’horlogerie classique : un mouvement à quartz suisse, dont le fabricant n’est pas précisé, anime les deux pointeurs. Le boîtier en acier inoxydable 316L mesure 39 × 44,5 mm pour 10 mm d’épaisseur.
La Desktop 95 est proposée en précommande à 173,95 euros pour la version blanche avec bracelet en cuir. Benly décline aussi la montre avec un bracelet en maille milanaise ou à maillons métalliques.
La marque prévoit une série de 500 exemplaires et des expéditions en novembre 2026. Elle annonce aussi la livraison internationale gratuite et la prise en charge des taxes et droits d’importation.
À ce tarif, on s’offre surtout un souvenir de ses premières années devant un PC. Avec une différence appréciable : cette barre de chargement ne nous mettra plus en retard.

articles.title: Steam tarda hasta 12 días hábiles en revisar juegos y varios estudios perdieron su fecha de estreno
articles.text:
Valve, empresa estadounidense de videojuegos y tecnología, reconoció que Steam tarda hasta 12 días hábiles en revisar los juegos nuevos que le envían los estudios, el triple de lo habitual. La empresa lo informó el 3 de noviembre y cambió la lista de requisitos para los desarrolladores. Varios estudios independientes ya perdieron su fecha de estreno por la demora.
Valve explicó que recibió “un aumento significativo” de envíos para revisión de tienda y de páginas en los últimos meses. Su objetivo es responder en tres a cinco días. Según la empresa, buena parte del atraso se debe a que debe revisar de nuevo los mismos juegos.
Para reducir esas repeticiones, Valve pidió que cada juego se ejecute al menos cinco minutos a través de Steam antes de enviarlo. “Aunque no lo crean, a veces revisamos versiones que nunca se jugaron a través de la tienda”, escribió la compañía.
La lista incluye otros controles. Los estudios deben confirmar los componentes que el juego necesita instalar y comprobar que los logros funcionen y que las partidas guardadas en la nube estén bien configuradas. También deben etiquetar las capturas de pantalla y subir al menos cinco de juego real, sin frases publicitarias. Valve agregó que prepara más mejoras para la revisión de versiones y que estos cambios son “un buen punto de partida”.
Estudios con el lanzamiento detenido
PC Gamer, revista que se especializa en videojuegos, contó que los responsables de Food Devils, Wheel Make It y Cubic Earth esperaron hasta 20 días sin respuesta, aunque la plataforma anuncia de tres a cinco. El desarrollador de Cubic Earth, que firma como structmira, mencionó a ese medio que no logró hablar con Valve y que solo le queda esperar.
Su tráiler superó las 60.000 vistas en YouTube y el juego sumaba más de 6.000 listas de deseados. “Ahora nuestra página de la comunidad de Steam se llena de quejas de jugadores y perdimos todo el impulso”, dijo.
Una posible causa que Valve no menciona
Valve no explicó por qué el atraso apareció ahora. La prensa especializada lo vincula con el aumento de juegos creados con IA. El desarrollador 2 Left Thumbs escribió en X que los tiempos se dispararon entre septiembre y octubre, y atribuyó parte del problema a la “basura” que inunda la tienda.
Según Engadget, un usuario de Reddit contó que el 49,9% de los juegos lanzados en Steam en octubre declaró contenido generado con IA. Engadget también recordó que en junio casi el 20% de las demos del Next Fest, el festival de demos de Steam, lo había declarado.
Un empleado de la empresa tecnológica reconoció hace poco que existe un problema de juegos de baja calidad, pero dijo que la empresa no quiere ser quien decida qué herramientas deben usar los desarrolladores, según PC Gamer. Por ahora, la compañía no fijó una fecha para volver al plazo de tres a cinco días y los envíos se revisan en hasta 12 días hábiles.

articles.title: Samsung libera One UI 9 para mais smartphones no Brasil • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Samsung libera One UI 9 para mais smartphones no Brasil
Modelos de entrada e intermediários da fabricante sul-coreana ganham Android 17 com One UI 9.
A Samsung continua com a atualização de seus smartphones para o Android 17 com One UI 9. Desta vez, os modelos Galaxy A07 4G, Galaxy A16 (nas versões 4G e 5G), Galaxy A35, Galaxy M35 e Galaxy M54 receberam a atualização com a nova interface.
O Galaxy A07 5G foi o primeiro desta lista: a Samsung disponibilizou o update para os modelos brasileiros na quarta-feira passada (28/10), de acordo com o changelog da atualização. No dia seguinte (29/10), o Galaxy A16 5G recebeu a novidade.
Os modelos A16 4G, A17 4G, M35 e A35 começaram a receber a atualização ontem (03/11). O changelog do M54 ainda não registra a novidade, mas o aparelho também já conta com a nova versão. Esta será sua última atualização do Android; daqui em diante, o modelo deve receber apenas correções de segurança e, possivelmente, a One UI 9.5.
Para facilitar, esta é a nova leva de aparelhos que está recebendo a One UI 9:
Outros celulares, como as variantes 5G do A07 e A17, além do restante dos modelos elegíveis (incluindo aí todos os tablets anteriores à linha Tab S12 e ao Galaxy S23 FE), devem ser contemplados nos próximos dias e semanas.
A descrição oficial da Samsung diz o seguinte: “A One UI 9 aproxima o Galaxy AI do seu dia a dia com experiências mais úteis e intuitivas. Aproveite novas formas de simplificar tarefas, criar e manter-se conectado com funções de IA que se adaptam à maneira como você usa o seu Galaxy.”
Esta nova versão da One UI é baseada no Android 17, o mais recente liberado pelo Google. Entre as novidades de software estão o Now Brief e o New Nudge mais inteligentes, a partir das informações que o sistema captura no próprio telefone da pessoa.
Outra função recente é o aplicativo My FanCam, capaz de analisar vídeos e produzir cortes focando em pessoas específicas. Ele foi originalmente apresentado junto com a safra 2026 de telefones dobráveis.
Por serem modelos intermediários e de entrada, os modelos atualizados pode não receber todos os novos recursos da One UI 9, ao contrário de modelos das linhas Z e S.

articles.title: Thermal Grizzly launches PhaseSheet PTM Pro with improved thermal conductivity — new thermal pad promises easier installation and better cooling performance
articles.text:
Thermal Grizzly launches PhaseSheet PTM Pro with improved thermal conductivity — new thermal pad promises easier installation and better cooling performance
Easier installation and improved thermal conductivity.
Thermal Grizzly has announced the PhaseSheet PTM Pro, an improved version of its popular phase-changing thermal pad. According to the manufacturer, the new thermal pad offers increased thermal conductivity alongside a redesigned carrier film that makes the PhaseSheet PTM Pro easier to handle and install. While this may seem like a relatively minor change, the new carrier film is designed to peel away more easily from both sides, reducing the risk of tearing the sheet during installation.
Like the original PhaseSheet PTM, the Pro version uses a phase-changing material that alters its physical properties depending on the temperature. At room temperature, the sheet remains solid, much like a conventional thermal pad. However, at temperatures above 45°C, the material transitions into a very low-viscosity liquid that behaves similarly to thermal paste.
This phase-changing behavior helps minimize the pump-out effect commonly associated with traditional thermal paste. Pump-out occurs when thermal paste gradually moves out from between a heatsink and a GPU die or CPU IHS due to repeated thermal expansion and contraction of the contacting surfaces. Over time, this can reduce the amount of thermal paste covering the contact area and potentially degrade cooling performance.
The PhaseSheet PTM Pro is also reusable and electrically non-conductive, meaning it can be safely used on components without an IHS, including mobile CPUs, GPUs, and other internal components such as memory and storage. According to a performance graph shared by Thermal Grizzly, the new PhaseSheet PTM Pro outperforms several popular thermal pastes and thermal pads in controlled testing. Using a 30 x 30mm contact area, 300N of mounting force (48 PSI), and a 240W heat load, the PhaseSheet PTM Pro recorded a temperature difference of 5.83°C, the lowest among all the tested materials. This puts it ahead of the KryoSheet (6.13°C), Duronaut Pro (6.29°C), and the original PhaseSheet PTM (6.36°C).
The PhaseSheet PTM Pro can be purchased through Thermal Grizzly's website for $23.28 per 40 x 40mm sheet. That's considerably more expensive than the original PhaseSheet PTM, which costs $13.92 for a larger 50 x 40mm sheet.

articles.title: People say they want small smartphones—the Enough Phone will put that to the test
articles.text:
The first modern smartphones had 3.5-inch screens, which can be hard to remember in today’s world of gargantuan glass slabs. Sure, people talk about wanting smaller phones, but will they buy one? Enough Phone is betting they will. The company will begin taking preorders for its first device today, which is built around a petite 5.3-inch screen that is apparently the smallest it could find with decent performance metrics.
The company’s cheeky name is reflected in its approach to phone design. A flagship killer this is not, but it’s probably “enough” for most people. It has a mid-range MediaTek processor, a single rear-facing camera, a polycarbonate body, and a fingerprint sensor in the power button.
| Specs at a glance: Enough Phone ($399 for a limited time, $599 MSRP) |  | 
|---|---|
| SoC | MediaTek Dimensity 7500 | 
| Memory | 8GB | 
| Storage | 128GB with microSD | 
| Display | 5.3-inch 1520×720 HD+ LCD | 
| Cameras | Sony IMX766 50 MP, 32 MP selfie | 
| Software | Android 17 or OdysseyOS | 
| Battery | 3500 mAh (removable) | 
| Connectivity | 5G, LTE, Wi-Fi 6, Bluetooth, NFC, SIM+eSIM | 
| Measurements | 133×64×12 mm | 
With that compact screen, the Enough Phone will be dwarfed by almost every existing smartphone. While it’s a bit thicker, the device has almost the same footprint as the iPhone 13 Mini. Thinness takes a hit, as the designers have opted to make the battery user-replaceable. Like the Fairphone, you’ll just have to remove a few screws to get the back cover off.
On the software front, the device will offer a choice. You can get an Enough Phone with a standard Google-certified build of Android 17, which is probably what most people will choose. It also supports OdysseyOS, a streamlined, de-Googled version of Android that behaves like a dumbphone (it doesn’t even have a browser).
Some minor details are still up in the air. The designers aren’t yet sure about waterproofing and durability ratings, and the battery capacity could change. But they hope that spec will go up, not down, if it changes at all. Carrier support is also unclear right now. It will be an unlocked 5G phone, and the company is aiming for “broad global support.” But if you’re on a restrictive carrier like Verizon, you may be out of luck.

articles.title: Physical AI doesn't need a bigger brain. It needs a nervous system
articles.text:
Physical AI doesn't need a bigger brain. It needs a nervous system
What elite performance means for physical AI
This year, the World Cup united elite athletes from around the world in competition at the highest level.
As I watched, I kept returning to one question: What makes these athletes elite? Knowledge, fitness, or desire to win don’t fully explain it. It’s something else. It’s mastery of the task. Execution at the highest level when it matters most is what separates the elite from the rest.
President and CEO at NXP Semiconductors.
I’ve been thinking about that word, “elite”, a lot lately. Physical AI is a hot topic and deservingly so as robots, drones, and autonomous machines in all sorts of shapes are emerging. If we’re going to bring all these intelligent systems into our lives, what does elite look like for them?
Excellence is not thinking harder
If you’re a football fan, you’ve seen Messi play. He handles the ball so effortlessly it looks like cheating. The moves he makes seem to anticipate what the opponent will do. We assume that kind of precision must come from thinking faster. It’s the opposite. The decision is too quick for thought at all, instinct takes over.
Look closer at that idea of “doing without thinking,” and you find it everywhere. Keeping balance, blinking, or navigating a crowded room, all of it with no deliberation and minimal energy. And yet for machines this is the hardest thing of all.
The real world changes the rules on AI
There is an old observation in robotics worth revisiting. The tasks we consider the pinnacle of human intellect like solving equations, parsing logic, or recalling facts are the ones machines can do the most easily. The tasks a toddler masters, like grasping a cup, staying upright, or stepping over obstacles are the ones that have challenged AI engineers for decades.
The lesson in that reversal is simple: Intelligence isn’t only something you scale by making the brain larger.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Most of the intelligence we’ve built so far lives in the cloud. Ask it a question and it can afford a moment to think. The physical world grants no such patience. A drone correcting for a gust of wind, a vehicle reacting to a child stepping off a curb, a robot catching a part before it hits the floor, none of these can wait for a round trip to a distant server. The response must happen where the event happens, in milliseconds, every time.
And the stakes are different in kind, not just degree. A wrong answer in software can be corrected. A wrong move in the physical world cannot. You cannot patch a collision or roll back a fall. When intelligence must act in the physical world, then latency, efficiency, and reliability stop being features and become survival requirements.
A blueprint from biology
Biology has been refining intelligence in the physical world for hundreds of millions of years, and the design it arrived at is telling: Intelligence is distributed. The cerebrum handles reasoning and conscious thought, the cerebellum handles motion control and balance, and the spinal cord handles reflexes.
Consider a stumble. By the time our conscious mind registers it, we’ve already caught ourselves. That correction never reached the part of the brain that reasons; it would have been far too slow. Reasoning, coordination, and reflex are separate, independent, and aligned systems, each placing the right intelligence in the right place with the right performance to get the job done.
That is the principle we should be designing toward. Machines are made more capable through the right kind of intelligence in the right place. That’s what a distributed, neural-axis architecture makes possible.
Take the human body as inspiration, and our own neural axis architecture focuses on three independent but highly coordinated layers. A slower, highly intelligent reasoning layer, an intermediary coordination layer, and an ultra-fast reflex layer at the edge. Each playing its part.
Picture a humanoid robot carrying a package across a warehouse. Its reasoning layer sets the destination; its coordination layer keeps it steady as it walks. Then an item falls from a shelf and strikes its arm. Within milliseconds, the reflex layer must rebalance, adjust its grip, and secure the package. Those reflex-like decisions can only happen at the edge, in real time—putting the right intelligence in the right place is what lets machines operate safely.
Making sense of the physical world
Reacting quickly is necessary, but not sufficient. A machine also must understand the world around it. Weight, momentum, friction, the way an object will topple if pushed off center. Children do not learn any of that from a manual. They internalize real world physics from trial and error and parental corrections. But a robot does not have this luxury, because in the physical world, trial and error can do real harm.
Messi didn’t learn any of that from a manual; he absorbed it over thousands of hours. A robot cannot learn the same way.
This is why the most interesting work in the field is teaching machines to anticipate rather than merely respond. Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models are a bridge between perception and action: connecting what a machine sees, what it is told, and how it moves.
That capability is difficult to create and even harder to optimize to run within the tight power and memory limits of an edge device. Closing that gap, between what is possible in a data center and what is practical in the real world, is one of the defining engineering challenges of this decade.
For the physical AI industry, overcoming this challenge means getting two things right. First, building capable and energy-efficient processors optimized for every layer of robotic intelligence, from the cerebrum and cerebellum to the distributed sensory nervous system. Second, equipping teams with tools and frameworks to make developing autonomous agentic intelligence at the edge as simple and efficient as possible.
Trust is the price of admission
Because the real world has no undo button, Physical AI will never reach its potential without trust.
We will only welcome these systems into our homes, our roads, and our factories if we believe they will behave predictably when it matters and fail gracefully when something goes wrong. That kind of dependability cannot be sprinkled on at the end. It must be designed in from the silicon up, so that when a system encounters something it never anticipated, it still does the safe thing.
And that trust doesn’t come from a bigger brain. It comes from the architecture. The same distributed design that biology settled on long ago. Reasoning, coordination, and reflex, each operating where it belongs, and each trustworthy in its own right. If that design is good enough to keep us alive in an unpredictable world, it’s good enough for the machines we will live alongside.
Physical AI will earn its place beside us when it finally gets a nervous system—a neural axis built for trust at every layer.
