articles.title: Galaxy Tab S10 FE Plus 5G tem melhor oferta de 2026 • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Galaxy Tab S10 FE Plus 5G tem melhor oferta de 2026
Galaxy Tab S10 FE Plus 5G (128 GB) com tela de 13,1" e S Pen na caixa alcança o menor preço do ano durante o Black November, com desconto de 53% no Pix na Amazon
O Galaxy Tab S10 FE Plus 5G de 128 GB está saindo por apenas R$ 2.834 no Pix na Amazon. O tablet da Samsung para trabalho, com tela ampla de 13,1″ e que traz a caneta S Pen no kit, atinge o menor preço de 2026 durante o Black November, com desconto de 53% sobre o preço original de R$ 5.999.
O destaque do Galaxy Tab S10 FE Plus é sua tela LCD de 13,1″ com taxa de 90 Hz. Seu amplo espaço a permite rodar apps com tela dividida e bastante conforto, entre documentos, planilhas e outras soluções. O display oferece fluidez, alto brilho e contraste.
O chip Exynos 1580 e os 8 GB de RAM suportam editores de texto e navegadores, mas não apps mais pesados (a Samsung afirma que ele suporta o Adobe Photoshop, entretanto). Os 128 GB de armazenamento podem ser expandidos com cartões microSD de até 2 TB.
A suíte Galaxy AI oferece ferramentas como o Assistente Matemático para fazer cálculos, o Apagador de Objetos em fotos e o Circule para Pesquisar com gestos de busca inteligente, além de outras funções de IA.
O kit do Tab S10 FE Plus inclui uma capa protetora e a caneta S Pen, que oferece precisão ao desenhar e escrever. A bateria de 10.090 mAh resiste a até 21 horas de vídeo, diz a fabricante, e suporta carregamento rápido de 45 W via USB-C.
A certificação IP68 confere proteção contra ambientes empoeirados e mergulhos acidentais. O kit de câmeras inclui wide traseira de 13 MP e frontal de 12 MP, que capturam documentos e sustentam videoconferências com qualidade. Ambas filmam em 4K.
O Galaxy Tab S10 FE Plus de 128 GB (apenas R$ 2.834 no Pix) foi atualizado para o Android 16 e receberá updates por mais seis anos, segundo a Samsung, e possui conectividade 5G, Wi-Fi 6E e Bluetooth 5.3.
A Black Friday 2026 ocorre no dia 27 de novembro, mas o varejo se antecipou e já está trazendo diversas ofertas em eletrônicos durante o Black November, com descontos e condições especiais.
Acompanhe os Achados do TB no Telegram ou WhatsApp e não fique de fora da festa.
Aviso de ética: ao clicar em um link de afiliado, o preço não muda para você e recebemos uma comissão.

articles.title: Binance says hackers who stole billions in crypto spent months planning heist
articles.text:
The hackers who stole billions of dollars in cryptocurrency from the Binance exchange spent months working on the theft and used both social engineering and novel malware in the process, the company said Tuesday.
The heist, which both the FBI and the TRM Security firm attributed to North Korean actors, initially targeted $6.34 billion in cryptocurrency from Binance wallets. The exchange has since frozen or intercepted $2.85 billion of that sum. Binance said it has set aside funds required to cover the loss and provided this link to a Proof of Reserves page. The $6.34 billion represents the biggest sum ever targeted in a cryptocurrency theft.
Advanced persistent threat
Binance said the people behind the heist began no later than June and continued until last Thursday, when they successfully compromised an engineer’s laptop and withdrew assets from several wallets. Like just about every organization that suffers a public, high-consequence hack, Binance said the threat actor was sophisticated and resourceful.
“Our current investigation indicates that this was a sophisticated, multi-stage campaign,” a report on the company’s investigation to date said. “It was not a single isolated breach or a simple phishing incident. The attackers combined a range of techniques, including social engineering by fake recruitment interviews, malicious software downloads, compromised internal AI tooling, endpoint compromise, and an advanced transaction-authorisation method.”
Binance said that the first incident related to the compromise likely occurred in June, when an engineer downloaded a tampered version of Homebrew. The company linked to this incident reported in May, and its security team detected the compromised laptop, but only after the malware operators obtained information about the roles of the engineer and his related colleagues on the Binance wallet infrastructure team.

articles.title: Sequoia hits rewind, undoing 20 years of expansion | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Sequoia Capital posted a memo to X on Wednesday morning titled “The Sequoia of Tomorrow” that’s full of surprises. The firm has raised roughly $10 billion in new funds, it says. It is also closing its London office, shutting down its Arc accelerator and its Scouts program, merging its early-stage and growth teams into one, flattening its partnership, and killing the Monday partner meeting.
The framing is forward-looking, but the messaging is very much about rewinding to an earlier time when the team was smaller and focused more narrowly on Silicon Valley.
Sequoia says as much itself. The firm describes coming out of a roughly 20-year expansionary phase during which it built multiple businesses in multiple geographies and says an unintended side effect was hierarchy. Nearly everything being undone here was built during that stretch, under a succession of stewards running from Doug Leone to Jim Goetz to Roelof Botha.
One of the most surprising developments is that the firm is killing two programs that put Sequoia closest to young founders. Scouts, which Sequoia launched around 2009 and, anecdotally, half the industry has since copied in some form, gave small checks to founders and operators to invest on the firm’s behalf; it was a way to see deals through people closer to interesting new founders than any partner could be. Jason Calacanis famously pointed Sequoia to Uber through the program. Sam Altman brought Stripe to Sequoia as a scout, too. Other early scouts included Airbnb CEO Brian Chesky and Dropbox founders Arash Ferdowsi and Drew Houston.
Arc, launched in March 2022, was Sequoia’s answer to Y Combinator: a batch accelerator for pre-seed and seed founders, running several cohorts a year for seven weeks, with admitted companies getting $500,000 to $1 million up front.
Both were bets on being early and being everywhere. Now Sequoia says it wants to put more energy behind fewer people and things.
Also gone is the firm’s London office, which Sequoia opened in 2020. Several people will leave the firm as result. “We simply don’t see the need for a local presence,” the memo says, adding that Europe will keep producing “outlier founders” and that Sequoia can support them from the Bay Area. (If founders didn’t already feel pressured to move to the Bay Area or open an office in the region, they will now.)
Luciana Lixandru, hired from Accel in 2020 as Sequoia’s first partner in Europe, says she was offered a move to San Francisco and declined. (“Europe is where my family is, and where I want to build,” she wrote on X.) She says she remains a partner and will keep her board seats while investing personally in European founders.
For European entrepreneurs, the message is going to be particularly difficult to digest, especially as it follows Andreessen Horowitz shuttering its London office last year and Coatue closing its own in 2024. Sequoia didn’t say it won’t fund Europeans, but it’s definitely reinforcing here that the center of gravity is once again in the Bay Area.
The rewind extends to people, too. The memo notes that Carl Eschenbach, the former Workday CEO, is very much back in the fold (he returned as a full-time partner in March). It also says the team has “reinvigorated the GOAT,” Doug Leone.
Though the nomenclature at venture firms is all over the place — including Sequoia — the memo makes clear there are now seven general partners who primarily own and operate Sequoia: Alfred Lin and Pat Grady — who are the firm’s co-stewards — along with Andrew Reed, Shaun Maguire, Konstantine Buhler, Sonya Huang, and David Cahn, who joined the firm in 2023.
There are other changes as a result. Jess Lee, the firm’s first female partner and an early-stage investor who oversaw its Arc program, is no longer shown on Sequoia’s investor page but rather as an operator in the role of its chief product officer. Stephanie Zhan, an investor who had joined Sequoia in 2015, has meanwhile left the firm entirely, announcing last month that she is launching her own new firm.
Sequoia rarely lets anyone go entirely. Founder Don Valentine famously kept turning up at partner meetings for roughly a decade after handing over the firm. Goetz, who stepped back from his management responsibilities in 2017, is still featured on the firm’s site. Botha is the exception. He was voted out as senior steward last fall in a surprise shake-up days after sitting down with this editor — the firm framed it as a handoff to Lin and Grady — and he completely cut ties with Sequoia this summer, around the time he joined SpaceX’s board.
The changes are sure to make waves. Still, none of them are completely out of character. Sequoia iterates routinely, including, at times, reversing out of earlier moves. Most notably, in 2023, it separated from its China and India/Southeast Asia arms, which became HongShan and Peak XV, ending a two-decade run as a global franchise under one name.
The rest of the memo is structural. It says the team has decided to dispense with its “early” and “growth” team approaches and operate as one. It also notes the Monday partner meeting — a ritual at Sequoia and at nearly every firm — is finished on the theory that founders operate around the clock and their investors should, too. (These may be going away more generally. At least, in a sit-down with TechCrunch at Disrupt last month, the entire Benchmark team suggested it now mostly uses Monday meetings to socialize.)
Sequoia acknowledges the moves come at some cost. “It is scary to break something that’s already working just fine,” the memo says, and painful to say goodbye to good people. Now to wait and see if these were the right calls.
Here is Sequoia’s post in full:
We live in a world of accelerating change. The best founders reinvent themselves over and over again. We must do the same.
It’s been a year since our generational transition. We’ve been busy! We’re no longer evolving the Sequoia of yesterday; we are now building the Sequoia of tomorrow.
Here are a few of the changes we’ve made, and what they mean for founders.
Focus We are best at high-conviction, highly selective venture capital investing. This is our focus. We have removed much of the complexity associated with the Sequoia Capital Fund, sunset our batch accelerator (Arc) and Scouts programs, and streamlined both operating and investing teams. Putting more energy behind fewer people and things means better support for the founders we back.
One Team There is no more “Early & Growth”. There is only Sequoia. We are one team, operating under one shared mission. This should make things more seamless for founders as they go from stage to stage.
London We are closing our London office, which means several people will be leaving Sequoia. This is not about the team — they are excellent. We simply don’t see the need for a local presence. We believe that Europe will continue to produce outlier founders and companies, and that we can continue to provide world class support from our home base in the Bay Area.
Partners We are coming out of a ~20 year expansionary phase, during which we built multiple businesses in multiple geos. One unintended side effect was hierarchy; it required real management to run the operating side of our business, and this crept over into the investing team. We’ve made several internal changes that have the effect of flattening the partnership. This allows every partner to flourish, and every founder to receive the full benefit of Team Sequoia — regardless of who your lead partner happens to be.
Firepower We’ve welcomed two rising stars (Liam and Sonali) and one transcendentally talented founder & operator (Dev). We’ve reunited with a legendary leader (Carl) and reinvigorated the GOAT (Doug). We’ve elevated and empowered killer operators: Hem, Natalie, Rishi, Stacey, and Theresa. We’ve raised ~$10Bn in new funds. Talent and capital are two of the key ingredients in building legendary companies. Our talent density and capital base are stronger than ever.
24/7 There is no more Monday partner meeting cycle. Founders operate 24/7, and so do we. Founders shouldn’t have to adhere to our process — we will do our best to adhere to yours.
Reinventing Ourselves
Some of these changes were obvious. Others less so. Many were hard. It is scary to break something that’s already working just fine, and it is painful to say goodbye to great people. We ask founders to do the right thing even when it is hard, and we are committed to doing the same.
Some things remain unchanged. Our mission is to help the daring build legendary companies, from idea to IPO and beyond. Our objective function is not scale, but quality: delivering the best possible returns to LPs, and being the best possible partner to founders.
The Sequoia of Tomorrow
Excellence is a moving target, so we will always be changing. But for now, this is Sequoia.
We have seven General Partners who own and operate our organization, and we are on offense: building our business so that we can support you in building yours. We are true believers, and as we enter a golden age of multiple tectonic shifts in parallel (AI, space, biology, reindustrialization, and perhaps more), we are so fired up for what’s to come. Let’s build something legendary together!
— Alfred, Andrew, David, Konstantine, Pat, Shaun, and Sonya, on behalf of Team Sequoia

articles.title: AMD Expects PC Sales to Decline in 2027 Alongside Industry
articles.text:
Wednesday, November 4th 2026
AMD Expects PC Sales to Decline in 2027 Alongside Industry
During its Q3 2026 quarterly results, AMD CEO Dr. Lisa Su expressed expectations that its client PC business will decline significantly in 2027, possibly by double-digit percentage points. The entire industry is experiencing price hikes due to the tight supply of crucial PC components like GPU memory and system RAM. These rising prices have been driving down sales in the client sector, while the enterprise sector has been thriving with strong EPYC CPU sales and Instinct MI accelerator sales to AI labs, hyperscalers, and neoclouds. While a rising tide lifts all boats in the AI datacenter space, there is an opposite lowering tide in the client PC industry, projecting a general decline in this segment.
AMD's CEO Dr. Lisa SuLooking at the market, PC sell-through slowed late in the quarter as higher memory and component costs weighed on demand. We are managing the business accordingly, aligning sell-in with sell-through to keep customer and channel inventory healthy. In 2027, we are planning for PC market unit shipments to decline by a double-digit percentage. In this environment, we expect to outperform the market as we deliver our Ryzen roadmap and grow our commercial footprint.
We already reported that AMD is preparing to raise prices on its Radeon GPU and GDDR6 memory kits again in November. AMD apparently started charging its board partners more for GDDR6 from October 1. The exact scope of the November hike isn't known yet. The main reason seems to be memory, as GDDR6 prices reportedly went up by around 8 to 10% in the third quarter. Meanwhile, Team Group expects the worst period in memory demand to be between Q4 2026 and Q2 2027, which is just a few months away. All of this is driving down consumer PC sales as parts and complete systems are skyrocketing in price.

articles.title: Sony's new $6,000 hi-res audio Walkman has already been totally overshadowed by a mystery 'new, yet original' release
articles.text:
Sony launches two new elite Walkman devices, then teases a retro-inspired third Walkman-adjacent release (which I'm far more excited about)
Are the 1979 Walkman headphones on the way?
- Two new Sony digital audio players have gone on sale
- Both are expensive, with a range of features
- People are more excited for a teased Walkman headphone launch
Despite beginning as a range of cassette and CD players over four decade ago, Sony's Walkman line is still going strong, though nowadays they've ditched the physical media in favor of digital hi-res music. Two new Walkman devices make that point exceedingly clear.
These are the NW-WM1AM3 and NW-WM1ZM3, which were announced in mid-October ahead of a November on-sale date (in most regions, at least, but in the US they're due in January). Checking Sony's website, the AM3 is due to sell from November 27, or Black Friday, while the ZM3 is already sold out. Clearly the Walkman's return is proving popular.
That sold-out model is the priciest of the two, selling for $5,899 / £4,299 / AU$6,499. The real appeal of the NW-WM1ZM3 is in the build, using materials such as oxygen-free copper for top conduction, gold-plated screws and wiring done by a brand called Kimber Kable which focuses on the cabling in audio products. Otherwise, it sounds pretty similar to the $2999 / £2,099 / AU$3,999 NW-WM1AM3.
Both are digital audio players with 5.5-inch screens, 35-hour listening, Wi-Fi or onboard music listening, use the Sony DSD Remastering Engine to upscale PCM audio, and have dual headphone jacks. They have 256GB on-board storage, as well as the ability to expand that with an SD card.
So they both sound like premium digital audio players for people who value high-quality music. Yet they've been totally overshadowed by another Walkman product which isn't even out yet.
Meet the mystery retro Walkman accessory
On social media, Sony has begun teasing a brand-new Walkman device, due to be unveiled on November 5 (tomorrow, at the time of writing):
People are pretty confident about what this is, largely because you can see the outline, and the color scheme harks back to them. It's looking like these will be a new pair of Walkman headphones, like the classic MDR-3 which came alongside the first-generation TPS-L2 Sony Walkman in 1979.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Wired audio's making a comeback, as is retro audio tech, and clearly Sony's leaning on the nostalgia angle here. Presumably, it's set to unveil some new on-ear headphones, but we'll find out more tomorrow.
The real question to me is whether Sony's about to re-vamp the MDR-3, or if it's about to re-vamp the MDR-3 and release some other Walkman products. We're constantly seeing new cassette players and CD players, because of the aforementioned retro audio tech boom, and it wouldn't be surprising if Sony were to release such options too.
After all, Walkman remains the most recognized name in portable audio playing, so if any brand wanted to capitalize on this new trend, Sony would be the one best placed to do so.
We'll see what Sony unveils tomorrow, but whatever it is, it's already overshadowed the WM1AM3 and WM1ZM3.

articles.title: Zu viele KI-PCs von Nvidia im Warenkorb? Warum Amazon den Account eines KI-Entwicklers sperrte
articles.text:
Konto gesperrt wegen KI-Hardware? Warum Händler bei Bestellungen jetzt genauer hinsehen
Die meisten kennen die Beschränkung auf „handelsübliche Mengen“ aus dem Supermarkt, etwa bei Sonderangeboten oder Lieferengpässen. Aber nicht nur Lebensmittel wie Butter, Speiseöl oder Toilettenpapier können rationiert werden, wie der Fall des KI-Entwicklers Nick Saraev zeigt. In einem Beitrag auf X berichtet er, dass er sieben Nvidia DGX Spark KI-Mini-PCs bei Amazon bestellen wollte – aber dann wurde sein Konto gesperrt.
Speicherkrise treibt Preise in die Höhe
Schon seit Monaten beklagen Elektronikhersteller steigende Preise für einzelne Bauteile. Inzwischen haben viele diese Kosten an ihre Kund:innen weitergegeben. Auch Apple ist von der Krise massiv betroffen. „Wir haben noch nie erlebt, dass die Preise für Komponenten so stark und so schnell gestiegen sind. Bisher haben wir unsere Kund:innen von diesen Preissteigerungen verschont“, erklärte der iPhone-Hersteller im Juni gegenüber Reuters. „Jetzt haben wir allerdings einen Punkt erreicht, an dem wir die Preise für einige Produkte anheben müssen.“ Ähnlich geht es Anbietern wie Samsung oder Dell.
Grund für den Mangel ist der KI-Boom. Viele Chip-Hersteller haben ihre Produktion umgestellt, um neue KI-Rechenzentren auszustatten. Jetzt scheint die Speicherkrise allerdings einen neuen Höhepunkt zu erreichen. „Schon der Kauf bescheidener Rechenkapazitäten bringt einen sofort auf eine Beobachtungsliste“, beklagt Saraev in seinem Social-Media-Beitrag. Nach eigenen Angaben wollte er vier Bestellungen aufgeben, die alle storniert wurden. Seine Screenshots zeigen, dass er insgesamt sieben Nvidia DGX Spark KI-Mini-PCs mit jeweils 128 Gigabyte Arbeitsspeicher und vier Terabyte Speicherplatz bestellen wollte.
Gesperrte Konten und stornierte Lieferungen
Saraev gibt an, Amazon habe auf einen früheren Beitrag über das Problem reagiert. Das Unternehmen bot an, den Fall zu überprüfen – und traf danach die endgültige Entscheidung zur Sperrung seines Kontos. Eine genaue Begründung nannte es nicht. Der E-Mail-Verlauf zeigt aber, dass Amazon auf frühere Versuche verwies, das Konto zu verifizieren. Der KI-Entwickler gibt an, diesen Prozess durchlaufen zu haben. Letztlich behält sich das Unternehmen aber vor, Dienstleistungen zu verweigern, Konten zu kündigen oder nach eigenem Ermessen Bestellungen zu stornieren.
Saraev ist nicht der Einzige, der solche Erfahrungen machen musste. Auch Tim Sweeney, der CEO von Epic Games, berichtete in einem Post auf X, dass Amazon seine regulären Bestellungen storniert habe, nachdem er versucht hatte, zwei Nvidia-GPUs zu kaufen. Diese werden häufig für lokale Inferenz verwendet. Außerdem gab ein Nutzer namens Dracones89 schon im September im Nvidia-Entwicklerforum an, dass Amazon sein Konto aufgrund von „verdächtigen Aktivitäten“ gesperrt habe. Grund dafür sei der Versuch gewesen, zwei Asus GX10 zu kaufen.
Händler reagieren zunehmend alarmiert
Lokale Inferenz gewinnt parallel zu Open-Weight-Modellen an Beliebtheit. Ihre Gewichte sind öffentlich und können von jedem heruntergeladen und lokal genutzt werden. Nutzer:innen profitieren hier von mehr Datenschutz und Unabhängigkeit, da Quellcode, Dokumente und Kund:innendaten den Rechner nicht verlassen. Außerdem funktioniert ein lokal installiertes Modell ohne Internetverbindung und antwortet oft schneller. Bei Closed-Weight-Modellen ist das anders: Wer sie in der App oder im Browser nutzt, schickt jede Anfrage über die Server des Anbieters.
Allerdings nutzen nicht nur vertrauenswürdige KI-Entwickler:innen Open-Weight-Modelle – sondern auch Hacker:innen. Wer große Mengen lokaler Inferenz bestellt, könnte deshalb das Misstrauen der Händler wecken. Laut einem Reddit-Post verlangte beispielsweise die US-amerikanische Kette Micro Center von einer Person die Unterzeichnung einer Erklärung inklusive Lichtbildausweis und Angabe des Aufstellungsorts. Zudem untersagte das Formular ausdrücklich den Export oder Weiterverkauf der Hardware. Die Speicherknappheit könnte demnach nicht der einzige Grund für die abgewiesenen Bestellungen sein.

articles.title: Micron details ambitious DRAM and NAND roadmap — 3D NAND, High-NA EUV, new materials, and custom silicon makes a comeback
articles.text:
Micron details ambitious DRAM and NAND roadmap — 3D NAND, High-NA EUV, new materials, and custom silicon makes a comeback
Custom memory is about to become mainstream.
Last month, Micron disclosed its DRAM and NAND memory roadmaps for the next several years, revealing plans to use wafer bonding, new materials that enable making NAND cells smaller, High-NA EUV lithography, and detailing its moves toward 3D DRAM. Perhaps the most revealing part of Micron's story is that the company plans to expand its portfolio of custom DRAM and NAND products as AI developers increasingly require memory and storage solutions optimized for their unique processor architectures and specific workloads.
" DRAM is nearing atomic limits at this point: although we have confidence in several more planar nodes, we are very focused on making sure that we introduce 3D DRAM at the optimal time from a cost and performance point of view," said Scott DeBoer, president and chief technology and products officer at Micron, at the company's event earlier this month. "[With 3D NAND, we are] really focused on new materials densifying the cell architecture, and continuing to focus on that XYZ scaling going forward."
DRAM: 4F2 cells axed, High-NA EUV lithography, new materials, and 3D DRAM enable future scaling
In a surprising move, Micron decided to abandon plans to produce DRAM with 4F2 memory cells, unlike its rivals at CXMT, Samsung, and SK hynix, citing the lack of a viable scaling path beyond where Micron is today. Instead, Micron's roadmap for the coming years includes wafer bonding, High-NA EUV lithography, new materials, and eventually 3D DRAM. The company plans to begin mass production of its next-generation 1δ memory in the second half of 2027, while subsequent 1ε, ζÅ, and ηÅ technologies are at various stages of development. In parallel, Micron is developing two generations of 3D DRAM that could eventually succeed conventional planar memory.
Micron's current 1γ (1-gamma) DRAM process technology, which is in high-volume manufacturing (HVM), is the company's first DRAM node to use EUV lithography. Previously, Micron had used multipatterning with DUV lithography and remained competitive with Samsung and SK hynix, which relied on EUV for critical layers.
Micron's next-generation 1δ (1-delta) fabrication process is currently in the yield ramp stage and is scheduled to enter mass production in the second half of 2027. The company expects the technology to increase bit density by mid-20% compared to 1γ, while advanced high-k metal gate (HKMG) CMOS, new materials, angstrom-level process control, and equipment intelligence should improve performance, power efficiency, and ultimately yields as well as costs.
Micron plans to manufacture 1δ DRAM in the U.S. and use the technology for next-generation DDR, LPDDR, graphics memory, HBM5, vertical HBM (vHBM), and vertical Edge Inference Memory (vEIM) products. Meanwhile, to make HBM5, vHBM5, and vEIM products, the node will also support additional features like through-silicon vias (TSVs) and other elements to improve thermal performance.
The subsequent 1ε (1-epsilon) process will rely on wafer bonding, which will enable Micron to produce different structures on separate wafers and then bond them together. This approach could increase flexibility in memory design and manufacturing, but Micron has yet to disclose its plans to implement wafer bonding, which structures it will bond, or what improvements in density, performance, and power consumption the technology will provide. The process is currently under development, and there is no announced production schedule.
Micron's ζÅ (zeta-angstrom) production node is currently in early development and will introduce High-NA EUV lithography to memory manufacturing, which will enable further reductions in critical dimensions. The company has not disclosed how many layers will require High-NA lithography, the expected density improvements, or when the technology will enter mass production. However, it is obvious that the node will not be here until at least 2030, years after Samsung and SK hynix adopt High-NA EUV at their DRAM fabs (planned for 2028).
The ηÅ (eta-angstrom) process represents the most distant generation on Micron’s disclosed planar DRAM roadmap and is currently in the pathfinding stage. After Micron inserts High-NA EUV lithography into its DRAM production flow, the company intends to bet on other methods of scaling. Although Micron mentions new materials, it hasn't identified them or explained how they will affect device structures. These could include new photoresists, deposition precursors, dielectric materials, or conductive materials that would enable the company to manufacture smaller transistors and capacitors, and ultimately increase DRAM cell density.
In any case, Micron's roadmap is focused on continuing development of DRAM based on 6F² cells, which differs from the plans of CXMT, Samsung, and SK hynix.
3D1 and 3D2: Transition to 3D DRAM is looming
In parallel with conventional DRAM development, Micron is working on two generations of 3D DRAM, currently called 3D1 and 3D2. Unlike planar DRAM, which primarily relies on smaller memory cells to increase bit density, 3D DRAM would use the vertical dimension to accommodate more memory cells within a given area. Micron intends to introduce the technology when it becomes competitive with conventional DRAM in terms of manufacturing costs and performance. The company has not disclosed architectures, layer counts, or density targets.
In fact, while Micron has outlined its future memory architectures through 2030, its DRAM manufacturing roadmap provides a firm production window only for the 1δ process, which is scheduled to enter high-volume manufacturing in the second half of 2027. The company has not disclosed production dates for subsequent planar DRAM nodes or either generation of 3D DRAM.
Custom HBM and vertical memory architectures
In addition to conventional DRAM, Micron plans to use its future manufacturing technologies for HBM4E, HBM5, HBM5E, and new vertically integrated memory architectures. Starting with HBM4E, the company will offer both standard and custom HBM products, which will be followed by custom HBM5E, vHBM, and vEIM (vertical Edge Inference Memory). All of these will mark the re-emergence of custom memory in mass-produced products.
Custom HBM4E (cHBM4E) will enable Micron's customers to shrink memory I/O width and/or integrate additional logic into the memory's base die to free up valuable die space for compute and optimize performance and power consumption for specific AI accelerators. According to Scott DeBoer, Micron’s president and chief technology and products officer, some of these functions would otherwise reside in the ASIC itself, so moving them closer to memory should improve overall system efficiency.
"When we co-design a base die, and the certain logic elements that are desired to be put in that base die are generally an offload from GPU circuitry anyway onto the base die to put it closer to the memory," said DeBoer. "Moving what makes more sense onto the base die will still be a reality in [the] vertical HBM timeframe as well."
To support these capabilities, Micron intends to use advanced foundry process technologies for the base dies of both standard and custom HBM products, although it has not disclosed specific nodes. For custom designs, the company will select the most cost-effective process that meets customer requirements. For example, Micron expects HBM4E to require more advanced CMOS technologies to meet its performance and power targets.
Further down the road, Micron intends to introduce vertical HBM (vHBM), which will stack memory directly on top of ASICs and CPUs rather than next to them on an interposer. This architecture promises substantially higher bandwidth, thanks to dense vertical connections (as well as significantly lower latencies) thanks to adjacent placement, but it is also set to create considerable challenges related to power delivery and heat dissipation. To address them, Micron plans to use hybrid bonding for advanced interconnects, integrated heat spreaders, and thermally aware designs. Interestingly, the company expects conventional HBM and vHBM to coexist in some designs, where vHBM provides maximum bandwidth, while traditional HBM serves capacity requirements.
Another technology under development is vertical Edge Inference Memory (vEIM), which shares many of its packaging and integration technologies with HBM, but targets applications that require power efficiency more than maximum bandwidth. Micron's 1st Generation vEIM aims to deliver formidable HBM4-like 2 TB/s of bandwidth while consuming less than 1 picojoule per bit of data transfer energy.
Both architectures will require close cooperation with customers to optimize memory, logic, packaging, and thermal characteristics for particular applications, so Micron will need to work with its clients to make vHBM and vEIM successful. Interestingly, Micron's customer-specific development efforts extend beyond HBM and EIM.
For example, the company is collaborating with Meta to optimize LPDDR6 for data center applications, which primarily include reliability, serviceability, and availability. Micron expects LPDDR6 to reduce power consumption by approximately 35% compared to LPDDR5, which will be very important for dense memory deployments. The company also intends to develop DDR6 — which targets 2X DDR5 bandwidth — in cooperation with major customers to better understand and ultimately meet their needs.
Speaking of customer cooperation, DeBoer stresses that Micron now collaborates with customers from the earliest stages of product definition through joint design, development, validation, and volume production. According to the executive, this approach differs substantially from how the company worked with customers previously.
"Across our AI co-invention opportunities we are co-imagining, co-designing, co-developing, co-validating, and then delivering at scale," DeBoer said. "This opportunity is truly unique. It is very different than the way we interacted with customers even three or four years ago."
Advanced CMOS: More than 10X performance improvement
In addition to shrinking DRAM cells and developing vertical memory architectures, Micron is developing advanced CMOS technologies for peripheral circuitry. The company's roadmap includes several generations of DRAM CMOS logic with high-k metal gate transistors, followed by 1st and 2nd Generation 3D CMOS technologies.
Micron expects these advances to increase its CMOS logic performance by more than 10X between 2020 and 2030, which should help the company address the growing bandwidth and power requirements of AI-oriented memory products.
3D NAND: From next-gen 400L 3D NAND to AI-oriented NAND
Although Micron's event was mostly dedicated to the future of DRAM, the company also shared some details about its upcoming NAND innovations, which include 11th Generation 3D NAND with 400 layers, post-G11 3D NAND, and AI-oriented NAND memory that either offers high bandwidth or high IOPS.
Micron's next-generation G11 (N170) 3D NAND technology represents a substantial departure from its current G9 (N160) process. The company plans to increase the number of active memory layers from 276 to more than 400, introduce wafer-on-wafer bonding, and implement an industry-leading memory cell pitch.
These improvements are expected to double the bit density of G11 3D NAND compared with G9 3D NAND, presumably from 21 Gb/mm2 to 42 Gb/mm2 in the case of 3D TLC devices, which should substantially reduce manufacturing costs per bit once the technology reaches mature yields.
In addition to increased storage density, G11 also targets a 50% increase in I/O speed compared with G9, which implies a potential transfer rate of approximately 5,400 MT/s. Furthermore, Micron expects to reduce data transfer energy consumption by more than 25% per bit, an important improvement for high-capacity SSDs and AI storage systems that tend to move huge amounts of data.
One of the most important changes with G11 is the adoption of wafer-on-wafer bonding, which lets Micron manufacture memory arrays and the periphery and I/O circuits on another wafer, then bond them together. Chinese manufacturer YMTC has used this method to maximize storage capacity and performance, so it is not surprising that Micron and other memory manufacturers are adopting the technique as well.
Micron expects to start mass production of G11 3D NAND in the second half of 2027.
Improving 3D NAND past G11: New materials and further XYZ scaling
Micron intends to continue improving 3D NAND beyond 11th Generation through a combination of new materials, denser memory cell architectures, and more energy-efficient devices and data paths. Specifically, Micron is investigating high-mobility materials that could improve the electrical characteristics of future memory devices, as well as ultra-dense cell architectures intended to increase storage density beyond what an increase in active layers provides.
Meanwhile, more energy-efficient circuitry and data paths should help offset the growing power consumption associated with higher NAND capacities and faster interfaces.
"Beyond G11, we have a strong roadmap, not going to go into great detail on it today, but really focused on new materials densifying the cell architecture, and continuing to focus on that XYZ scaling going forward," said DeBoer. "[…] The current industry direction and Micron’s direction is scaling both by adding layers [and] also by shrinking the cell dimensions."
The company has not identified the materials it intends to introduce or explained how they will affect memory cell structures. Nor has it provided quantitative density, performance, or power targets for NAND generations beyond G11.
AI-oriented NAND: Higher IOPS and bandwidth
Although Micron is not ready to share details about its G12 or G13 3D NAND generations, the company disclosed that it is developing two specialized NAND architectures for AI applications.
The first — High-IOPS AI NAND — architecture focuses on maximum random I/O performance and uses SLC-based designs with small blocks to accelerate workloads such as vector searches, graph analytics, and AI context management. Micron envisions products capable of delivering approximately 25 million to 100 million IOPS, depending on their configuration, and expects to bring products based on this approach to market over the next couple of years.
The second — High-Bandwidth AI NAND — architecture prioritizes bandwidth over random I/O performance. Micron is investigating vertically stacked NAND devices connected through TSVs and equipped with a logic base die that resides close to AI accelerators, so from many points of view this concept resembles SanDisk's HBF. However, Micron does not believe that simply placing NAND stacks alongside AI accelerators on an interposer offers sufficient advantages. Instead, the company is exploring alternative integration approaches that bring NAND closer to compute resources, but don't necessarily consume valuable shoreline (the perimeter, or edge) of AI accelerators.
"[The High-Bandwidth AI NAND is] more costly and has to be implemented in partnership with customers in a way to ensure that they are meeting the mark and the cost point to drive the value proposition," DeBoer said. "We are enabling TSV-stacked NAND with a logic base die to bring memory closer to accelerators. We do not think placing it along the shoreline of the GPU has merit. Instead, we want to position it closer to the compute itself to take advantage of this high-performance NAND."
These specialized AI-focused NAND architectures will complement Micron's conventional SSD roadmap, which includes plans for drives with capacities of up to 512 TB in the foreseeable future.
Anton Shilov is a contributing writer at Tom’s Hardware. Over the past couple of decades, he has covered everything from CPUs and GPUs to supercomputers and from modern process technologies and latest fab tools to high-tech industry trends.

articles.title: Edmontonians have lost $20 million to an international phone scam
articles.text:
Edmonton Police Service (EPS) is warning residents about an international fraud network that has cost Edmontonians millions of dollars.
In a Tuesday news release, EPS shared details on its investigation into the scam, which it says had been operating since at least October 2024 and was linked to multiple call centres in Lahore, Pakistan. As part of the scam, fraudsters pretended to be representatives of telecoms like Rogers, Telus and Virgin, and offered free or heavily discounted cellphones to persuade victims to provide personal information and order new devices through their legitimate service providers.
Once victims received the phones, they would receive follow-up calls claiming the wrong devices had been shipped and were instructed to ship them to another address. From there, the fraudsters would collect the devices and resell them. EPS says it’s aware of about 100 reports of this scam in Edmonton, which it says has collectively cost residents around $20 million in losses.
EPS says a 31-year-old Edmonton man was arrested in connection with the scam and that it’s shared the results of its investigation with the appropriate international authorities.
Notably, the EPS isn’t the only Canadian law enforcement dealing with these kinds of scams. Earlier this year, we reported on warnings from several Ontario police agencies about telecom scams.
EPS advises residents to be cautious of unsolicited calls, texts and emails from people claiming to represent telecom companies. Anyone who believes they have been targeted by a crime is advised to contact 780-423-4567 or #377 from a mobile phone. EPS also has a resource page providing more information on signs of a scam.
Source: Edmonton Police Service

articles.title: Panne de batterie en électrique : l’option à 30 € qui vous évite un remorquage salé — Frandroid
articles.text:
Est-ce qu’on assure une voiture électrique comme on le fait avec un véhicule à essence ? Oubliez les idées reçues, rouler en électrique ne demande pas un contrat spécifique. La plupart des assureurs les proposent dans les mêmes formules que les thermiques : tiers, intermédiaire et tous risques. Il faut en revanche regarder de près les volets « batterie » et « assistance » : sans la bonne formule, tomber à court d’énergie peut vite coûter cher. Expliquer à votre assureur que le réseau de bornes vous a fait défaut n’y changera rien.
La prise en charge d’une panne sèche n’a rien d’automatique
Vous roulez, encore et encore, jusqu’à ce que la batterie de votre voiture vide son dernier kilowattheure. Tout s’éteint et c’est l’immobilisation nette.
Si votre réflexe immédiat est de composer le numéro de votre assistance, la réalité contractuelle peut vite vous refroidir. La prise en charge d’une panne sèche (d’électricité, donc) n’a rien d’automatique dans les contrats standards, et ce, même si vous vous trouvez à plus de 50 kilomètres de votre domicile. À vrai dire, ces fameux 50 kilomètres (plus ou moins selon les compagnies) inclus de base dans les formules ne s’appliquent qu’aux pannes techniques, et non pas à un oubli de recharge ou à une mauvaise estimation d’autonomie.
Sans une clause explicite ou une option dédiée, l’immobilisation de votre véhicule peut rester intégralement à votre charge.
    Pour aller plus loin
J’ai roulé 2 500 km en voiture électrique pour la première fois : une traversée de la France presque sans stress
            
Les indispensables de votre contrat : ce qui est couvert (et ce qui ne l’est pas)
Toutes les polices ne se valent pas quand le courant vient à manquer. Si l’assurance au tiers de base se contente de couvrir la responsabilité civile, elle vous laissera totalement démuni face à une batterie désespérément vide.
Pour espérer de l’aide, il faut se tourner vers les garanties d’assistance. Certaines options spécifiques intègrent en effet une prise en charge dédiée à la panne sèche de batterie.
Pour éviter la douche froide au bord de la route, plusieurs garanties adaptées doivent être examinées à la loupe, selon les explications des assurances que nous avons contactées.
–L’assistance panne 0 km devient le sésame absolu. Il s’agit de la garantie incontournable pour les électromobilistes car sans elle, une franchise kilométrique s’applique. Grâce à cette option, vous êtes remorqué sans condition de distance, que la panne survienne sur la route ou en bas de chez vous.
–Le remorquage spécifique. Notez qu’une voiture électrique ne peut être tractée comme un véhicule thermique et nécessitera un dépannage adapté. En cas de batterie à 0 %, l’assurance prend en charge l’acheminement de la voiture jusqu’à la borne de recharge la plus proche ou vers un point de service compatible, selon les modalités de votre police.
–L’électricité reste à votre charge. Attention à la nuance ! Si l’assurance règle le déplacement de la dépanneuse et le transport du véhicule, le coût réel de la recharge de dépannage (les kilowattheures réinjectés dans la batterie) reste à la charge du conducteur.
–Le câble de recharge. Coûteux à remplacer, il doit figurer dans votre contrat : vérifiez qu’il est bien couvert contre les dégradations et le vol.
Tous risques ou option 0 km : l’exemple de Direct Assurance
Pour que cela soit bien clair, chez Direct Assurance par exemple, comme chez les concurrents, l’avarie d’une batterie déchargée ne permettant pas de rejoindre son domicile ou une borne est prise en charge par l’assistance. Avec un remorquage jusqu’au point de recharge le plus proche, dès 0 km du domicile.
Cette prise en charge fait partie de l’option « assistance étendue 0 km », proposée sur les formules « tiers », « tiers maxi » et « tous risques », ou incluse dans la « tous risques maxi. En cas de panne technique, l’assistance incluse dans toutes les formules intervient 24h/24 et 7j/7 à partir de 50 km du domicile (plus ou moins selon les compagnies), et donc dès 0 km avec l’option. Et le câble de recharge fait partie des biens assurés, au même titre que le véhicule.
Cette option pèse peu sur la facture : comptez de 10 à 50 euros par an selon les assureurs, d’après le comparateur Le Lynx. Certains l’incluent même d’office, comme Leocare, qui intègre l’assistance 0 km à toutes ses formules (tiers, tiers plus et tous risques). Avant de payer l’option, vérifiez donc que votre contrat ne la contient pas déjà.
Dès 200 euros par an en tous risques pour une Dacia Spring
Le comparateur Assurland publie des tarifs « à partir de » en tous risques pour les électriques les plus populaires. Ils sont calculés sur un profil très favorable : un homme de 45 ans vivant à Niort, avec un bonus de 50 % et aucun sinistre depuis trois ans, dont la voiture a deux ans, parcourt 7 000 kilomètres par an et dort dans un garage fermé. Comptez environ 200 euros par an pour une Dacia Spring, 230 euros pour une Fiat 500 électrique, 290 euros pour un Peugeot e-2008 et jusqu’à 473 euros pour une Tesla Model Y.
À garanties égales, assurer une électrique ne revient pas forcément moins cher qu’une thermique. Assurland estime même que le prix est « généralement plus élevé » que pour les modèles thermiques, à cause du coût des batteries et des pièces de rechange. Gardez toutefois en tête que l’addition finale reste dictée par le modèle choisi, le profil du conducteur et sa situation géographique, l’usage, ainsi que les options de garantie ajoutées.
Les électriques ont longtemps bénéficié d’une exonération de la taxe spéciale sur les conventions d’assurance (TSCA), qui allégeait leur prime. Ce coup de pouce a pris fin le 31 décembre 2024, comme le rappelle la Macif : seules les voitures immatriculées en 2024 en profitent encore, pendant 24 mois au maximum.
Quid de la panne technique ?
En cas de panne technique de la batterie, lisez bien votre contrat : le remplacement de ce composant coûte entre 10 000 et 20 000 euros selon les modèles. La quasi-totalité des constructeurs garantissent la batterie 8 ans ou 160 000 kilomètres, au premier des deux termes atteint.
    Pour aller plus loin
Quelle est la durée de vie d’une batterie de voiture électrique ?
            
Cette garantie ne remplace pas une assurance. Elle couvre les défauts de la batterie et une perte de capacité anormale, le plus souvent sous 70 % de la capacité d’origine, comme chez Tesla. Les accidents et les incendies relèvent de votre assureur : vérifiez donc que votre contrat auto couvre bien la batterie en cas de choc ou d’incendie.
La formule « tous risques » reste la plus protectrice : elle couvre la majorité des risques, dont les accidents responsables et les dommages sans tiers identifié.
Précisons aussi qu’en cas de panne de batterie, il est possible de remplacer uniquement les cellules défectueuses ou la partie électronique et non pas forcément l’ensemble du pack. De quoi réduire le coût de l’opération à plusieurs centaines (ou milliers) d’euros selon les cas, loin du prix neuf d’une batterie.
Des réparateurs habilités pour la haute tension
Intervenir sur la chaîne de traction d’un véhicule électrique ne s’improvise pas. Les batteries haute tension nécessitent des compétences pointues et des habilitations spécifiques. Avant de souscrire ou de vous lancer sur la route, assurez-vous que votre compagnie d’assurance s’appuie sur un réseau de réparateurs agréés, disposant de techniciens habilités pour ce type d’interventions électriques complexes.
Avant de prendre la route, relisez la partie assistance de votre contrat. Si la panne d’énergie et l’assistance 0 km n’y figurent pas, le remorquage d’une voiture à court de batterie risque de rester à vos frais, alors que l’option coûte quelques dizaines d’euros par an. Profitez-en pour vérifier que le câble de recharge est couvert contre le vol et que la batterie l’est en cas d’accident ou d’incendie.

articles.title: Razorpay gets Sebi nod for Rs 5,000-6,000 Cr IPO; eyes $5B valuation
articles.text:
Razorpay gets Sebi nod for Rs 5,000-6,000 Cr IPO; eyes $5B valuation
The development comes after Razorpay submitted its draft IPO papers with Sebi through the confidential route in June, initiating the process to tap the public markets.
Fintech firm Razorpay has secured approval from markets regulator Sebi for its proposed initial public offering (IPO) of Rs 5,000-6,000 crore, sources familiar with the development said on Wednesday.
The company is targeting a valuation of around $5 billion through the public offering, they added.
The development comes after Razorpay submitted its draft IPO papers with Sebi through the confidential route in June, initiating the process to tap the public markets.
Founded in 2014 by Harshil Mathur and Shashank Kumar, Razorpay offers payment acceptance, banking, payouts, payroll, lending and other financial services through an integrated platform.
The company serves millions of businesses across India, ranging from startups and small and medium enterprises to large corporates.
Razorpay attained unicorn status in 2020 and has since expanded beyond payments into a broader financial services ecosystem for businesses. Its offerings enable merchants to manage collections, payouts, payroll, cash flows and access to capital through a single platform.
The company is backed by investors including Peak XV Partners, GIC, Tiger Global, Ribbit Capital, Lone Pine Capital, Alkeon Capital and TCV.
The confidential filing route allows companies to submit draft offer documents to Sebi for review without immediately disclosing sensitive business information to the public.
Rival fintech firm PhonePe's IPO remains temporarily on hold after the company officially paused the process in March 2026 due to geopolitical tensions in West Asia and volatile market conditions. The company intended to raise over $1 billion at a valuation of $9-10.5 billion.

articles.title: Netflix fait appel à l’IA pour résoudre le plus gros problème de ses abonnés
articles.text:
Netflix vient de dévoiler un nouvel outil destiné à ceux qui passent plus de temps à chercher quoi regarder qu’à visionner des séries ou des films sur la plateforme. Cet outil, se présentant sous la forme d’un onglet baptisé « Découvrir », fournit tout simplement des recommandations de programmes à regarder. Sa particularité ? Il est alimenté par l’intelligence artificielle.
Un outil de recommandation alimenté par l’IA
Les recommandations sont effectuées sur la base de l’historique de visionnage de l’utilisateur, de ses préférences, ainsi que des programmes qui rencontrent un certain succès. L’intelligence artificielle vient affiner ces recommandations, tout en se rappelant des préférences de l’utilisateur.
Point important : l’utilisateur ne communique pas oralement avec l’IA intégrée à cet outil de recommandation. Pour l’instant, il faut dire que l’onglet « Découvrir » se révèle assez basique, avec des recommandations organisées autour de thèmes. Ainsi, l’utilisateur qui a aimé la série The Crown pourra cliquer sur le thème « Intrigues à la cour royale » pour découvrir des programmes similaires. Autre exemple avec le thème « Frissons garantis » qui propose des films et des séries liés à l’horreur. À noter que si l’utilisateur n’est pas satisfait par une recommandation, il pourra le signaler et l’IA s’en souviendra.
Un outil qui devrait être enrichi au fil du temps
Netflix explique que l’onglet « Découvrir » est alimenté par « une nouvelle couche d’intelligence que nous avons développée, qui réagit en temps réel aux informations que les membres nous communiquent et qui continue d’apprendre ». Mais la plateforme de streaming ne précise pas non plus en quoi cet onglet est sensiblement différent de son algorithme de recommandation. Précisons toutefois que l’onglet « Découvrir » sera au fur et à mesure enrichi « d’expériences de découverte », les recommandations par thèmes n’étant qu’une première fonctionnalité.
L’outil de recommandation « Découvrir » sera déployé progressivement aux États-Unis auprès des « abonnés qui utilisent Netflix en anglais sur les téléviseurs compatibles ». Nous ne disposons pas encore de date de disponibilité pour la France. Rappelons enfin que Netflix traverse actuellement une période délicate. La plateforme au N rouge a licencié environ 1 000 de ses salariés à travers le monde, soit 6 % de ses effectifs, tandis que son action a perdu près de la moitié de sa valeur par rapport à son sommet de l’année dernière. Quoi qu’il en soit, elle compte investir massivement dans l’IA, et l’onglet « Découvrir » en est un petit exemple.

Protege tu hogar frente a robos y ocupaciones con las cerraduras inteligentes de Verisure, disponibles como parte del sistema de alarma Verisure. Al margen de permitir abrir la puerta usando las llaves o desde el móvil, alertan ante cualquier intento de manipulación y transmiten la información a la unidad central de la compañía para generar un salto de alarma. Descubre la solución que mejor se ajusta a las necesidades de tu vivienda o negocio.

Cómo se escogen los ganadores de los Premios Xataka
Para elegir a los ganadores de los Premios Xataka Verisure 2026 seguimos la mecánica de ediciones anteriores, que está dividida en tres fases:
- Votación del público: en la primera fase, vosotros, con vuestros votos, elegís los candidatos que consideráis que deben pasar a la final en cada categoría.
- Votación del jurado: el jurado de Xataka y otros expertos en tecnología del sector votarán su favorito de entre los finalistas que habéis elegido.
- Elección de ganadores: los votos del jurado se combinan con los del público para elegir los ganadores, que anunciaremos el 17 de noviembre.
En general, los candidatos seleccionados son productos que han salido a la venta en 2026 o lo harán con fecha confirmada antes de fin de año. También incluimos los que el año pasado se quedaron fuera al anunciarse después de los Premios, que se celebraron el 20 de noviembre de 2025. Creemos que es la mejor solución: por desgracia, no es viable celebrar la gala el 31 de diciembre y siempre hemos querido que los Premios sirvan de apoyo para una época tan de compras y regalos como la que tenemos siempre a final de año.

articles.title: Apple TV 4K : cette application débloque enfin le Dolby Atmos en TrueHD et le DTS:X sans perte
articles.text:
Désormais, grâce à Native Player 2.0, l'Apple TV 4K peut restituer les pistes Dolby Atmos en TrueHD et DTS:X sans perte, avec leurs canaux de hauteur. De quoi contourner certaines limites historiques du boîtier d’Apple.
L’Apple TV 4K est un excellent boîtier multimédia, mais il conserve quelques limites frustrantes pour les amateurs de home cinéma. Parmi elles, l’impossibilité de profiter pleinement des pistes audio haute définition des Blu-ray et UHD Blu-ray lorsqu’on lit leurs fichiers vidéo depuis une bibliothèque personnelle.
Des applications populaires comme Plex ou Infuse savent décoder ces pistes, mais perdent les informations spatiales associées aux canaux de hauteur. Avec la version 2.0 de Native Player, disponible depuis le 27 octobre, ce compromis appartient enfin au passé.
Du Dolby Atmos sans perte, mais sans passthrough
Native Player parvenait déjà à préserver les canaux de hauteur, mais au prix d’une compression audio avec perte. Cette nouvelle version restitue désormais le Dolby Atmos en TrueHD sans perte, jusqu’en 9.1.6 canaux. Le DTS:X est également pris en charge, mais toujours restitué en 7.1.4.
Il ne s’agit toutefois pas d’un véritable passthrough audio. L’application décode et effectue elle-même le rendu spatial sur l’Apple TV, puis transmet les canaux audio décodés à l’amplificateur. Contrairement à un lecteur Blu-ray classique, celui-ci ne reçoit donc pas le flux original pour le décoder.
FlatpanelsHD a justement testé cette version et confirmé le bon fonctionnement du Dolby Atmos en TrueHD. Un progrès d’autant plus notable qu’Apple n’a toujours pas proposé de passthrough natif pour ces formats sur tvOS.
Une alternative intéressante, mais encore perfectible
Native Player 2.0 améliore également la compatibilité vidéo avec le Dolby Vision Profile 7 des UHD Blu-ray et le Profile 10 associé à l’AV1, y compris sur les Apple TV 4K dépourvues de décodage AV1 matériel.
L’application peut lire des fichiers depuis un NAS ou un ordinateur via SMB et WebDAV. Son interface reste toutefois assez sommaire face à celle d’Infuse, tandis que l’intégration de Plex et la prise en charge des fichiers ISO et BDMV sont annoncées prochainement.
Disponible sur l’App Store français, Native Player fonctionne sous tvOS 26 minimum et n’est pour l’instant proposé qu’en anglais. Les titres en Dolby Vision, Dolby Atmos en TrueHD ou DTS:X sont lisibles en aperçu gratuit, la lecture complète passant par un abonnement à 5,99 euros par an ou un achat définitif à 29,99 euros. Un amplificateur ou une barre de son compatible Dolby Atmos reste nécessaire pour profiter des canaux de hauteur.
Native Player ne remplace donc pas encore les lecteurs multimédias les plus complets, mais il corrige l’une des frustrations majeures des utilisateurs d’Apple TV 4K disposant d’une vidéothèque personnelle.

articles.title: Oracle canceló un contrato de USD 7.000 millones con una firma china tras la presión del gobierno de Trump
articles.text:
Oracle canceló el contrato de arrendamiento de chips de inteligencia artificial que había firmado con la china Tencent, valorado en unos USD 7.000 millones, después de que funcionarios del gobierno de Donald Trump le plantearan sus objeciones. Lo informó el 4 de noviembre el Financial Times.
Según el medio, funcionarios estadounidenses se acercaron a la compañía para expresar su preocupación por el acuerdo. Tencent, además, recibió visitas de altos funcionarios de Guangdong, la provincia china donde tiene su sede, que le pidieron respaldar chips fabricados en China, según el mismo informe.
El contrato se conoció el 30 de septiembre, también por Financial Times. Era el mayor arrendamiento en el exterior de Tencent: cinco años de acceso a unos 100.000 chips avanzados repartidos en varios centros de datos de Oracle en el sudeste asiático, con un pago inicial de alrededor del 30%, es decir, unos USD 2.100 millones.
Alquilar chips para esquivar los controles de exportación
Las restricciones de Washington impiden a las empresas chinas comprar de forma directa los procesadores más avanzados para IA. Alquilar capacidad en centros de datos fuera de China no estaba prohibido, según el Financial Times, citado por Tom’s Hardware. La publicación agregó que Bloomberg había informado de una revisión del Departamento de Comercio sobre ese acceso remoto.
Ni Oracle ni Tencent confirmaron el acuerdo ni dijeron qué chips incluía, según Network World. Oracle ofrece procesadores de Nvidia y de AMD, de modo que el tipo de hardware no estaba definido en lo que se conoció.
Tom’s Hardware calculó que el contrato equivalía a unos USD 1,60 por chip y por hora durante los cinco años, alrededor de un 43% menos que los USD 2,35 por hora que la firma SemiAnalysis estimó en agosto para un H100 de Nvidia con contrato de un año. El medio advirtió que, sin conocer los chips, la comparación es solo orientativa.
No era la primera vez que Tencent recurría a esta vía. Benzinga, citando al Financial Times, informó que en diciembre de 2025 la empresa había accedido a chips B200 de Nvidia alquilando capacidad en un centro de datos cercano a Osaka, en Japón.
Nvidia endurece las condiciones a sus clientes de la nube
Un día antes de la cancelación, el Financial Times informó que Nvidia comunicó a sus clientes de computación en la nube que deben vender al menos el 51% de su capacidad a empresas no chinas, según resumió el medio.
Los arrendamientos de otras empresas chinas siguen vigentes. Según Investing.com, ByteDance y Alibaba mantienen grandes contratos con proveedores estadounidenses, y Oracle es uno de los principales proveedores de ByteDance en Asia, con varios centros de datos en Malasia.
La demanda de Tencent por capacidad de cómputo crece: según el Financial Times, su inversión de capital en el segundo trimestre subió 176% interanual, hasta 53.000 millones de renminbi (unos USD 7.900 millones), impulsada por infraestructura de IA y pagos anticipados por recursos de cómputo.
Reuters señaló que las empresas tecnológicas chinas figuran entre los mayores clientes de centros de datos del sudeste asiático, donde desarrolladores chinos de IA alquilan aceleradores que no pueden obtener en su país.

articles.title: Xbox vai sortear Series X escondido em réplica de jacaré • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Xbox vai sortear Series X escondido em réplica de jacaré
Batizado de Series X-BITE, edição única do console foi instalada em uma escultura de 1,5 metro. Versão será sorteada nos EUA.
A Microsoft resolveu levar a personalização de consoles a um nível… selvagem. A empresa criou um Xbox Series X funcional instalado dentro de uma escultura de jacaré com aproximadamente 1,5 metro de comprimento. Ele será sorteado pela Microsoft nos Estados Unidos.
A peça única, batizada Xbox Series X-BITE, foi produzida pelo John Nolan Studio, especializado em efeitos práticos para cinema e TV, e traz ainda um controle personalizado com marcas de mordida.
A ação promocional ocorre a poucas semanas do lançamento do GTA 6, fazendo referência ao animal tão popular na Flórida. O estado inspira a região de Leonida, onde está a cidade de Vice City, em que o jogo se passa. Jacarés já apareceram em diversos materiais publicitários do game e devem fazer parte da fauna durante a gameplay.
O John Nolan Studio é uma reconhecida empresa britânica especializada em efeitos práticos, que já trabalhou em produções como The Witcher e a série de Harry Potter, atualmente em produção pela HBO. O jacaré utilizado no projeto foi construído especificamente para receber o console.
A escultura foi construída para dar a impressão de que o animal engoliu um Xbox Series X. O hardware fica integrado ao corpo do estátua, enquanto o botão com o logotipo luminoso do Xbox aparece através das escamas.
O controle também faz parte da brincadeira. A Microsoft criou um Xbox Wireless Controller com marcas de mordida, colocado entre os dentes da escultura. Os olhos receberam detalhes inspirados na identidade visual da marca, incluindo pupilas no famoso símbolo do Xbox.
Apesar da aparência pouco convencional, o Series X-BITE é um console funcional. A Microsoft, porém, trata o projeto como uma peça de exposição e colecionador. A PlayStation também trabalha em versões especiais relacionadas ao próximo Grand Theft Auto, mas nada tão mirabolante. O console da empresa japonesa já recebeu um controle temático com as cores do jogo.
A Microsoft produziu apenas um modelo desses e abriu um sorteio para definir quem ficará com a peça. A promoção ocorre entre 3 e 10 de novembro de 2026, mas não vale para quem está no Brasil. Assim como a edição de colecionador própria do GTA 6, é limitada a moradores dos Estados Unidos com pelo menos 18 anos.
Se você nos lê da terra do Tio Sam, para participar é necessário seguir a conta oficial do Xbox no X, Instagram ou TikTok, republicar o post da campanha e incluir a hashtag #XbitSweepstakes. O perfil utilizado também precisa permanecer público para que a participação seja verificada.
Depois do sorteio, o vencedor terá 48 horas para responder à Microsoft e reivindicar o prêmio. Caso não haja retorno dentro do prazo, a empresa poderá selecionar outra pessoa.

articles.title: What I learned driving the Slate electric truck prototype
articles.text:
If my 45-minute drive yesterday morning is anything to go by, I think Slate Auto will have quite the hit on its hands. The startup had one of its prototype trucks in town and asked if I wanted to check it out—no jumping on a plane or having to spend yet another night in an interchangeable hotel room, just a drive from southwest DC to Rockville, Maryland. Easy-peasy.
The prototype truck had been well-used, with almost 6,000 miles (9,656 km) showing on the small and minimalist but very legible digital display that also shows your speed and, if you engage reverse, the backup camera. And while the cabin layout was representative of the production version, the surfaces most certainly weren’t—the prototype instead uses a lot of hard and shiny black plastic, with strips of Velcro here and there left over from when the interior had to be camouflaged when the vehicle was out in public.
Getting acquainted with the Slate was refreshingly easy. The Morris Marina-like door handles open with a pleasing mechanical action. The seat and steering column adjust manually but with plenty of reach, something many budget models used to leave out to save on cost.
The key fob slots into the dash to turn it on, and there’s a column shifter to select from drive, neutral, park, and reverse. Set your mirrors first—also by hand—and it’s time to go. Visibility from the two-seat cab is good, and even though the Slate is on the smaller side, it’s as tall as most other crossovers at 68 inches (1.7 m), so you still sit relatively high up, certainly compared to a sedan.
I still remember how to use a manual window winder, and the three dials on the dash for making it hotter, colder, and more or less windy inside approach the platonic ideal for car climate controls. Had we needed navigation, a phone mount on the dash would have done the job, but the area they now call North Bethesda is familiar ground from my past life in science policy, and the roads were mostly where I remember leaving them, so I could just concentrate on the drive.

articles.title: I tried Apple's Siri Recaps. They're surprisingly useful — and a little unsettling | TechCrunch
articles.text:
On Tuesday, Apple rolled out a potentially controversial set of Audio Intelligence features into testing with the first developer beta versions of iOS 27.3 and watchOS 27.3. The betas bring four new AI features that allow Apple Watch Series 12 wearers to detect important sounds, identify songs, catch up on conversations, and take notes.
After just a day with Apple’s Siri Recaps feature on my Apple Watch, I can already see how its value may ultimately outweigh any creepiness factor that comes from the AI-powered audio recording and summarization it provides. However, I also see areas where AI-assisted note-taking can go too far, capturing things that aren’t worth remembering, and where there’s room for improvement.
The first two, sound and song detection, don’t represent potential privacy concerns; they are designed to detect either important sounds — like an alarm or doorbell — or identify a song using Shazam’s technology. The former helps deaf and hard-of-hearing users navigate the world, and the latter is something we’ve already done with our iPhone for nearly two decades now.
It’s the two other features, Live Rewind and Siri Recaps, that have raised concerns. The features record and then transcribe or summarize the conversations happening with and around the Apple Watch’s owner. Live Rewind lets you go back to see what was said in the past 15 seconds, while Siri Recaps summarize audio throughout your day, saving notes of the important things that were said.
Apple has taken care to ensure the privacy of these AI features by processing the audio and running AI models on-device, when possible, and by not identifying speakers, storing raw audio files, and redacting private information, like government ID numbers or personal account information.
Still, some are put off by the idea that we’re now normalizing the idea that technology is always listening.
I find myself sympathizing with both camps. I often lament that we’ve allowed technology to become so pervasive in our daily lives, but I still see the value in what Apple has built.
I haven’t yet had an appropriate time to test Live Rewind, nor do I think this will be a feature I use as often. I’m more likely to say “sorry, what?” or “can you repeat that?” if I missed something that was said, before turning to my Apple Watch for help.
But with Siri Recaps, I immediately saw how this could become a feature I rely on regularly to save important notes for later.
I was able to test the feature in a real-world scenario yesterday, when we were dropping off my teen’s car for repairs and picking up a rental. At both places, employees shared a lot of information about time frames, prices, and policies that were delivered verbally. The information came too fast to stop and write anything down. Yet when I returned to Siri Recaps later in the day, it had captured key details that I may need to refer back to.
For instance, it noted the deductible, the repair time frame, the amount of gas we had in the rental at the start, and other things I wanted to remember.
One complaint is that Siri Recaps had mixed this information with other topics that were later discussed in the home, like an errand we needed to run and what time babysitting was this week, something we were discussing in order to create an appointment on the family calendar with an appropriate alert time frame.
I think these items should have been saved in a separate note titled “family schedule and errands,” rather than in the same note with the car repairs, but under a separate heading.
Because I configured Siri Recaps to run at all times, it also captured non-essential things, like our “plan” to watch the midterms coverage on TV, which is not the kind of thing you’d normally jot down a note about. It also was a stark reminder that the feature was listening in on our everyday conversations. That’s something that could feel invasive in different scenarios, if the subject being discussed was more personal in nature.
This had me considering turning off the Recap feature while at home in the evening, so family dinner table chatter doesn’t become note fodder.
While I appreciated that the Recap picked up a reminder about an errand I needed to run from one of the family conversations, other tidbits it saved — like what we were watching on TV — would only be valuable if you were exporting a Siri Recap note to Apple’s Journal app, because it was something you wanted to record for personal reasons.
I’d like to see these sorts of extraneous details saved as separate notes — or at least as dedicated sections that could be exported or deleted on their own at the end of the day.
I’d also love to be able to swipe left on an individual bullet point to remove it from the Siri Recap entirely, rather than having to enter edit mode, place the cursor, and then start deleting the text I don’t need.
Another option I’d like to have would be a setting that would allow you to automatically export any saved Siri Recap (the ones you click the bookmark icon to save) to Apple’s Notes app, instead of that being an extra step.
These Recaps could go into their own folder in the Notes app for easy reference. I can understand why this option is not the default, given how many different ways people use a general-purpose app like Notes. However, it would be useful for those of us who want to keep Notes as the central starting point for all our jotted-down reminders and to-dos.
Though I wasn’t immediately warmed up to the idea that my Watch was always listening, so to speak, I see the value of this sort of automated note-taking in daily life.

articles.title: AI data centers comprehensively defeated at US midterm elections — 45 measures put on the ballot as Americans overwhelmingly vote against developments
articles.text:
AI data centers comprehensively defeated at US midterm elections — 45 measures put on the ballot as Americans overwhelmingly vote against developments
Americans are saying no to data center developments.
Several counties in the U.S. have put data center concerns on the midterm ballot, and early results show that Americans are overwhelmingly voting against them. According to Data Centers on the Ballot, 33 measures restricting data center development have already won, with six more questions leading. Only one measure in Harwood, North Dakota, which adds an extra review process for industrial projects, including data centers, has failed, while a further five have no posted results. This is a major setback for the Trump administration, which has been pushing for AI development in the U.S., but not a surprising result, as one database has shown that “America hates data centers,” with polls showing that 70% of Americans oppose AI data center build-outs.
Note that the issues put to a vote are varied, ranging from outright permanent data center bans to moratoriums, time-limited actions, limitations based on size or consumption, and more. The mid-term elections also resulted in the recall of the mayor and two council members in Piqua, Ohio, and the mayor of Yukon, Oklahoma, for previously supporting data center bans. A second tracker of some 46 data center measures across 10 states reveals that of 33 measures to limit data centers, every single one is set to be passed. Of a further 13 positive measures to permit data centers and their construction, 11 look set to be defeated.
Despite the overwhelming opposition to AI data centers, it’s unclear if they will affect projects that are already underway. In fact, out of the 300-plus local data center bans enacted across the U.S., only three developments totaling 2.3 gigawatts have been delayed, with 38 gigawatts expected to come online by 2027, and that investment into the infrastructure is still on track to hit $32 trillion by 2050. Nevertheless, these votes could affect future developments, especially as the U.S. Senate accuses Big Tech of misleading the public on the advantages of AI data centers. It’s also the reason why OpenAI and Anthropic are scrambling for small data center projects that range in capacity from 20 to 30 megawatts, especially as their hyperscale gigawatt sites face delays.
President Donald Trump has taken steps to reduce the impact of data centers on the average citizen, like forcing AI data centers to pay an energy dividend to local communities and making tech companies, state governors, and utility companies promise to pay their own way via the “ratepayer protection pledge.” However, it seems that his effort was too little, too late, to change the minds of voters who are afraid of utility price hikes, noise pollution, and other negative effects that data centers have had on communities where they’ve been built.

Jowi Morales is a tech enthusiast with years of experience working in the industry. He’s been writing with several tech publications since 2021, where he’s been interested in tech hardware and consumer electronics.
