articles.title: IFC backs 15 African agritech startups to expand farm financing
articles.text:
After two decades of false starts, the International Finance Corporation has selected 15 agritech companies across the continent, backing them with equity while deploying portfolio guarantees to link them directly to the balance sheets of nearly 200 commercial banks.
For the past two decades, the quest to modernise African agriculture through technology has been littered with failed pilots, undercapitalised startups, and commercial lenders unwilling to venture beyond urban corporate headquarters. Yet, with the continent importing an estimated $90 billion in staple food commodities annually—a reliance that directly fuels currency depreciation and sticky inflation—the pressure to industrialise domestic food production has shifted from a development ambition into a macroeconomic imperative.
Speaking on the sidelines of the Africa Financial Industry Summit (AFIS) in Luanda, Aliou Maiga, Director of the Financial Institutions Group for Africa at the International Finance Corporation (IFC), revealed that the private-sector lending arm of the World Bank Group is rolling out a continental framework designed to solve agricultural finance once and for all.
The strategy marks a departure from the venture-capital model that previously pushed agritech startups to take on balance-sheet lending risk. Instead, the IFC is positioning agritech companies as digital origination and field-management engines, while channelling commercial bank liquidity into rural smallholder value chains backed by IFC risk-sharing guarantees.
“We have been looking for solutions in this space for about 20 years,” Maiga explained to TechCabal on Wednesday. “We explored the possibilities back then, but the technology was not sufficiently developed. We tried again about 10 years ago, but the conditions still weren't right. This time, we have identified 15 agritech companies across Africa, with coverage spanning much of the continent.”
Under this tripartite model, the IFC provides direct equity investment to these 15 vetted agritech firms to help them complete product development and achieve commercial scale. Rather than forcing these startups to raise expensive debt to lend directly to farmers—a practice that has strained balance sheets across the African tech ecosystem—the IFC connects them directly to its continental network of nearly 200 commercial banks and institutional lenders.
Who pays, who lends, who takes the risk?
IFC is changing how agricultural technology companies connect African farmers to finance. Explore how the model shifts lending away from startup balance sheets and towards commercial banks, supported by equity investment and risk-sharing guarantees.
The startup no longer has to be the bank
In one earlier approach, agritech startups borrowed capital and lent directly to farmers. IFC’s proposed framework separates the technology provider from the lender. Switch between the models.
This is a simplified illustration of startup-led agricultural lending, not a claim that every earlier agritech or IFC programme used exactly this structure.
Important: IFC’s nearly 200 financial institutions form a wider potential lending network. The number of banks participating in this specific agritech programme has not been disclosed.
Everyone has a different job
Select a participant to see who provides the capital, who originates farmers, who carries lending exposure and who receives support.
IFC: making the model investable
IFC provides direct equity investment to selected agritech companies, helping them develop products and expand their operations.
Separately, portfolio guarantees can cover an agreed portion of eligible lender losses. They do not necessarily eliminate the bank’s risk or guarantee every loan.
Agritech: finding and supporting farmers
The 15 selected companies are intended to identify farmers, gather agricultural data, help assess risks and coordinate last-mile services through local agents.
Instead of financing the entire loan portfolio themselves, they can focus on technology and operational delivery.
Commercial banks: providing the loans
Participating banks provide credit directly from their balance sheets, using information and origination support supplied by agritech partners.
The bank remains a lender exposed to credit risk. IFC’s guarantee may absorb a defined share of eligible losses under the agreed terms.
Farmers: receiving capital and guidance
Smallholders may gain access to formal credit alongside practical support delivered through local agents and connected devices.
IFC says yields have increased by as much as 50% in some cases. That is an upper-end example, not an average or a forecast for participating farmers.
How a smallholder could access bank financing
Follow a hypothetical farmer through the model, from first contact with a field agent to agricultural support. Tap any step or use the next and back controls.
A field agent reaches the farmer
A community-based agent visits a smallholder and uses a connected device to gather information about the farm and its needs.
The agritech builds a risk picture
Agricultural data, field observations and farmer information help the agritech assess production conditions and support credit origination.
A commercial bank considers the loan
A participating bank can use the origination information to evaluate the farmer and, if approved, provide financing from its own balance sheet.
IFC shares eligible lending risk
The portfolio guarantee is an arrangement between IFC and a participating lender. It can absorb an agreed share of qualifying credit losses.
This is a financing safeguard, not necessarily a separate payment to the farmer or a step that happens after each loan is approved.
The farmer receives continuing support
Field agents can help farmers interpret soil conditions, respond to weather changes, schedule fertiliser use and monitor crop health.
The intended outcome is higher productivity and more sustainable agricultural lending relationships. Results depend on implementation and local conditions.
The IFC model separates three functions that were previously concentrated in some agritech startups: technology and farmer origination, credit funding, and risk sharing. Whether this translates into scalable agricultural lending will depend on bank participation, farmer outcomes and the actual terms of the guarantees.
What is a portfolio guarantee?
A portfolio guarantee is a risk-sharing arrangement covering a defined group of eligible loans. If qualifying borrowers default, the guarantor may absorb an agreed portion of the resulting losses.
For a bank, this can make lending to unfamiliar or underserved sectors more manageable. The bank still needs to assess borrowers, administer loans and comply with the guarantee agreement.
What we don’t know: The story does not disclose the guarantee percentage, investment size, number of participating banks, total credit to be deployed or expected number of farmers reached.
How to read this interactive
Source: TechCabal interview with Aliou Maiga, Director of IFC’s Financial Institutions Group for Africa, at AFIS in Luanda.
15 agritech firms: The number IFC says it has identified for its new framework.
Nearly 200 institutions: IFC’s broader commercial bank and institutional lending network, not confirmed programme participants.
Earlier approach: A generalised illustration of startup-led agricultural lending.
Farmer journey: A hypothetical sequence based on the operating model described in the interview. It is not a documented individual loan.
Risk allocation: Actual guarantee terms and lender obligations may differ between agreements.
The agritech firms originate the farmers, assess agricultural risk, and manage the last-mile operational relationships. The commercial banks then disburse credit directly from their balance sheets, with IFC portfolio guarantees absorbing downside risk until lenders build their own underwriting confidence in the agricultural sector.
The macroeconomic motivation behind this capital engineering is urgent. African countries currently spend roughly $90 billion each year to import basic food staples such as rice, wheat, and sugar—commodities that could readily be cultivated on their own soil.
“Africa imports approximately $90 billion worth of food commodities, including rice, wheat and sugar. Yet, much of what we import could potentially be produced locally,” Maiga said. “The idea behind our work is to help Africa address its food security challenges, create jobs and increase productivity. Producing more food locally also reduces dependence on imports and can help moderate inflation because locally produced food is often cheaper. Ultimately, this has implications for interest rates as well, because inflation is one of the factors that influences interest rates.”
By dampening food inflation, which carries the largest weight in consumer price baskets across Sub-Saharan Africa, domestic agricultural productivity directly eases the monetary pressure that has forced central banks to maintain punishingly high benchmark interest rates.
Achieving this productivity, however, requires confronting the physical realities of the African smallholder. Unlike manufacturing or financial services, which have rapidly automated, African farming remains dominated by dispersed, rural smallholders who suffer from severe information deficits and low technical capability.
Maiga dismissed the notion that software alone can bridge this divide. In agriculture, pure-play digital platforms fail because rural producers cannot be served exclusively through smartphone applications. Instead, the IFC’s portfolio companies rely on a hybrid model that blends mobile technology with physical community agent networks.
“Our approach is to combine technology with agents on the ground, usually recruited from the communities where farmers operate,” Maiga observed. “These agents are physically present and equipped with devices that enable them to identify and address farmers’ day-to-day challenges. Through this approach, we can improve agricultural productivity and yields. In some cases, yields have increased by as much as 50%.”
These field agents use connected handheld devices to conduct soil diagnostics, track weather disruptions, schedule fertiliser application, and monitor crop health, translating agronomic data into actionable guidance for farmers.
Beyond technology and commercial bank balance sheets, Maiga emphasised that the agritech sector cannot scale without regulatory alignment from national and regional governments.
The IFC is actively integrating its agritech framework into broader state initiatives, including a flagship agricultural programme launched with the Nigerian government, as well as formal agreements being negotiated with sub-national administrations across key markets.
These sovereign agreements are designed to establish specific production targets, guarantee access to infrastructure, and remove regulatory bottlenecks across the entire value chain.
Once these state commitments are secured, the IFC coordinates with farmer cooperatives, agritech platforms, and commercial lenders to disburse funds and systematically measure the impact on yields.
For Africa’s agritech sector, which has struggled through successive funding winters and tech downturns, the shift in institutional backing signals a strategic maturation.
By pairing field-level technology with the balance sheets of mainstream commercial banks, the IFC is attempting to convert smallholder agriculture from an uninsurable charity case into an investable, productive commercial engine.

articles.title: Inkitt Builds a One-Shot PR Creator with Resumable Agent Orchestration
articles.text:
Inkitt has built a one-shot pull request (PR) creator that automates small, low-risk software changes, from task intake to a draft PR ready for testing and review. Triggered through Slack, Linear, or an API call from another agent, the workflow runs on remote infrastructure, reducing the need for developers to set up and supervise coding agents locally. Inkitt reported that the system was shipping code daily in a technical article published by Inkitt Tech.
The Agi Letkiewicz Tanner Lead Engineer at Inkitt, described it as
Event-driven orchestrator that coordinates short-lived agent containers rather than relying on a fixed pipeline.
Individual stages handle specification, implementation, verification, CI failure repair, and merge conflict resolution. The orchestrator persists each run in a database, allowing execution to resume from its recorded state.
Inkitt’s one-shot PR creator architecture (Source: Inkitt Blog Post)
The orchestrator separates decision-making from side effects. Its core transition function maps the current run state and incoming event to the next action without directly accessing a database, network, or language model. The orchestrator retains credentials for external systems, while agent containers receive short-lived repository tokens and model credentials. They cannot directly access Slack or Linear credentials, cloud identities, or arbitrary network connections. A separate check inspects the actual Git diff to ensure changes do not touch restricted paths.
Inkitt limits automation to changes within predefined boundaries. The workflow rejects tasks involving database migrations, schema or shared contract changes, CI and container build configuration, authentication, payment code, or package additions and updates. Verification, CI repair, and merge conflict resolution each have a maximum of two attempts. Duplicate webhook deliveries are handled through deduplication and conditional database writes, applying the principle of idempotent operations to workflows that may retry or receive repeated events. For CI completion, the orchestrator queries GitHub to determine whether all relevant jobs have finished instead of treating every job event as completion of the entire workflow.
Tanner wrote, describing the implementation challenges around idempotency, locking, retry budgets, and permissions.
The model was the easy part.
The design shares some safeguards with other coding agents but uses a different orchestration model. GitHub Copilot’s cloud agent also restricts agent permissions and requires human review before merging, while SWE-agent focuses on solving repository issues through a model-driven interface for browsing, editing, and executing code. Inkitt’s account emphasizes persistent workflow state, bounded retries, and centralized control of external actions.
Human approval remains part of Inkitt’s process. The system opens draft PRs, cannot bypass branch protection or merge its own changes, and notifies requesters when CI passes and the changes reach staging. A person must mark a PR ready for review and manage reviewer requests and approval. For larger tasks, Inkitt also maintains a local version that keeps a human involved in the development process.

articles.title: US export restrictions on China threaten SK Hynix's plans to build $45 billion worth of chip plants in New York
articles.text:
What we know so far: The US Commerce Department is holding up export licenses SK Hynix needs to ship American chipmaking equipment to its NAND memory plant in Dalian, China, according to people familiar with the matter. The delay is complicating the South Korean chipmaker's plan to build memory plants in New York. SK Hynix argues that more production in Dalian would help pay for the US project, but Commerce has said it does not plan to license equipment that would expand or upgrade chip plants in China.
Two people told Reuters that Solidigm, SK Hynix's US subsidiary, plans to spend about $45 billion on two NAND fabs in Marcy, New York. That figure could grow to about $100 billion over time. The company needs to increase output in Dalian and make more advanced NAND there to fund the US project and keep up with competitors, the people said.
The dispute turns on what counts as expansion. SK Hynix argues that putting tools into empty floor space in Dalian would not add capacity because it built the cleanroom in 2023. Commerce stated its position on upgrades and expansion in August 2025, and at a meeting last week, Under Secretary Jeffrey Kessler held to it, one person said. Still, the department has not formally denied the license to fill the empty space.
Solidigm executives have met with Commerce officials nearly 10 times since late August. At a late-August meeting, co-CEO Richard Chin and other executives met with Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and Kessler.
The officials seemed excited about a US NAND facility and eager to find a solution, one person said. Since then, the company has written several versions of its license applications, revising them together with the department. A separate license for 2027, covering equipment to maintain the Dalian plant, is also being negotiated.
The Treasury Department is involved, too. It would have to waive outbound investment restrictions before SK Hynix could buy tools for China. Company representatives have met with Treasury officials, who said they would wait to see what Commerce decides.
The talks test how far the Trump administration will bend national security rules meant to keep US technology from helping China's military in order to bring chip investment onshore.
"Ultimately, none of this is going to go forward without a green light from the White House," Leland Miller, a member of the US-China Economic and Security Review Commission, a bipartisan panel created by Congress, told Reuters.
New York officials are watching the calendar. "Hopefully we'll have an answer in the next couple of weeks," said Anthony Picente, county executive for Oneida County, where the plant would be built. He noted that a federal investment tax credit expires at year's end.
Solidigm has also looked at other ways to pay for the project. It explored an initial public offering to fund US production and keep up with rising memory demand. In an October 23 statement, SK Hynix said it had halted that review because of market conditions and share price trends. "Expanding Solidigm's production capacity and strengthening its competitiveness remain important priorities," the statement said.
The company, based in Rancho Cordova, California, has not committed to a site. "As a US-founded and headquartered company, Solidigm regularly evaluates strategic alternatives to best serve its customers and enhance its long-term competitiveness. The company is currently exploring options for building a NAND memory fab at potential locations around the world. No decision regarding any specific course of action has been made," Solidigm said in a statement last week. It has stood by that statement since then.
The Dalian problem goes back to 2020, when SK Hynix agreed to buy Intel's NAND factory there for $9 billion. It took control of the plant and Intel's solid-state drive business shortly before the US imposed broad export controls on American chipmaking equipment going to what it considered advanced fabs in China.
Foreign-owned plants in China were initially exempt. Last year, Commerce revoked those authorizations, calling them a "Biden-era loophole." It replaced them with annual licenses that let suppliers ship certain equipment and technology to the fabs, with quantity limits.

articles.title: La crisis de RAM en computadoras personales enfrenta a Elon Musk y Sam Altman: “La usan solo el 5% del tiempo”
articles.text:
Un comentario sobre la memoria de las computadoras domésticas desató un nuevo cruce público entre Elon Musk y Sam Altman.
El consejero delegado de OpenAI sostuvo que resulta ineficiente que millones de usuarios mantengan memoria DRAM en sus equipos personales cuando, según sus propias estimaciones, ese componente se utiliza apenas el 5% del tiempo.
El dueño de X y SpaceX respondió con un meme que se viralizó en horas y reavivó la rivalidad entre ambos empresarios, en medio de una escasez mundial de memoria que ya impacta en los precios de computadoras, celulares y otros dispositivos electrónicos.
El origen del comentario de Altman
Las declaraciones de Altman se produjeron el 29 de octubre durante una entrevista en el pódcast Cheeky Pint, conducido por John Collison, cofundador de Stripe. La conversación giraba en torno a si los modelos de inteligencia artificial de código abierto, ejecutados de forma local en computadoras personales, podrían reducir la dependencia de los grandes centros de datos.
El directivo de OpenAI cuestionó esa premisa y defendió que la DRAM debería priorizarse en infraestructura centralizada antes que en equipos domésticos, dado el contexto de escasez global del componente. No ofreció datos adicionales que respaldaran el porcentaje que citó durante la charla.
La respuesta de Musk con un meme
Dos días después, el 1 de noviembre, Musk publicó en X un meme basado en la escena inicial de la película Malditos bastardos, en la que un oficial nazi interpretado por Christoph Waltz interroga a una familia que esconde personas. En la versión que circuló, el personaje pregunta: “¿Le estás negando DRAM a la nube?”. Junto a la imagen, el empresario escribió: “¡La gente también merece tener su RAM!”.
La publicación generó una cadena de respuestas de usuarios que compartieron sus propios memes. Uno de los más comentados decía: “Díganle a Sam Altman que uso 64 GB de RAM para jugar RollerCoaster Tycoon. Quiero que sepa que fui yo”. Musk respondió con un emoji de risa.
Intereses comerciales detrás del debate
OpenAI mantiene algunos modelos de código abierto, pero su negocio principal se sostiene sobre sistemas de código cerrado que operan en infraestructura propia, lo que vincula la postura de Altman con los intereses de la compañía que dirige: cuantos menos usuarios ejecuten inteligencia artificial de forma local, mayor es la dependencia de los servicios en la nube que factura OpenAI.
Musk, por su parte, tampoco es ajeno a la disputa por el suministro de chips. El empresario opera los centros de cómputo Colossus, de su empresa xAI, que según declaró en septiembre ya utilizan 550.000 procesadores Nvidia GB200 y GB300, con planes de seguir ampliando esa capacidad. En meses previos, también había calificado de “extorsivos” los precios futuros anunciados por algunos proveedores de memoria.
Una escasez con proyección hasta 2027
El cruce se da en un escenario de encarecimiento sostenido de los componentes de cómputo. La firma de investigación TrendForce proyectó que los precios de contrato de la DRAM convencional subirán entre el 10% y el 15% en el cuarto trimestre de 2026, y advirtió que el giro de los fabricantes hacia la producción para servidores podría restringir aún más el suministro destinado a computadoras personales en 2027.
Ejecutivos de otras compañías del sector coincidieron en ese diagnóstico. El consejero delegado de Intel, Lip-Bu Tan, afirmó que el hardware de inteligencia artificial “se mantendrá en escasez durante los próximos dos a tres años” por restricciones persistentes en la cadena de suministro. En la misma línea, el consejero delegado de Dell, Michael Dell, anticipó que la escasez de memoria se agravará hasta 2027.
El rol de los fabricantes surcoreanos
Los principales fabricantes mundiales de DRAM, Samsung y SK hynix, también advirtieron que la escasez impulsada por la demanda de inteligencia artificial se extenderá hasta 2027 o después, con inventarios que, según trascendió, podrían reducirse a menos de diez días de suministro.
OpenAI anunció en octubre de 2025 acuerdos con ambas compañías, en el marco de su proyecto Stargate, orientados a elevar la producción de memoria avanzada hasta 900.000 arranques de oblea de DRAM por mes.
En ese contexto, Altman se reunió recientemente con cerca de 50 ejecutivos sénior de Samsung en Corea del Sur, en una gestión destinada a asegurar mayor provisión de hardware para ampliar la capacidad de cómputo de OpenAI.

articles.title: Open source project renders your Windows 11 desktop using the NPU rather than the GPU — ‘npu-driver’ can only run at 2 to 3 Hz, targets 30 Hz performance
articles.text:
Open source project renders your Windows 11 desktop using the NPU rather than the GPU — ‘npu-driver’ can only run at 2 to 3 Hz, targets 30 Hz performance
Developer is aiming for 30 Hz performance on Intel Panther Lake NPUs but the current version of this research driver is only achieving 2 to 3 Hz.
A developer group by the name of labscommunity has released a prototype driver for Windows 11 that renders the desktop using an NPU instead of the system’s (i)GPU. The new driver is called npu-driver, and the open-source (Apache 2.0) code is available on GitHub. It has been tested on Intel Panther Lake systems, and while it isn’t hitting its 30 Hz performance target yet, it is clever enough to fall back to GPU on request or on any fault.
The reasoning behind the development of this driver may strike a chord with those observing the 2020s processor landscape. “Every new laptop ships an NPU that sits idle while the GPU composes the desktop, runs the browser and, increasingly, runs local models,” notes the npu-driver readme file. “The question this project asks is narrow and testable: can the NPU take over desktop composition, end-to-end, without the applications or the compositor knowing?”
Thankfully, the answer to the question about whether the NPU can render the Windows 11 desktop - and apps like Notepad and Edge windows - is a yes. The npu-driver functions as intended and as demonstrated. Moreover, it seamlessly switches back to GPU rendering if/when it needs to.
The developer admits that this driver is strictly “a research prototype, not a product” at this stage, and the main issue currently is performance. The GitHub readme notes that the target 30 Hz performance isn’t very close right now, with actual screen refresh speeds of around 2 to 3 Hz. npu-driver is being developed on a Panther Lake laptop, and all these Intel processors feature NPU 5 architecture silicon with performance spanning 45-50 TOPS.
A Reddit post that appears to be penned by one of the labscommunity crew says that this project might render Windows 11 visuals rather slowly, but it can “bring 3D GPU usage down from 3.4% to 0.6%,” thus freeing up the GPU for other tasks, like inference.
Having a(nother) useful task for the system NPU to do is a welcome development, even if it seems of rather niche appeal for now. There are no signs consumer processors will abandon NPU integration, and these accelerators will likely remain alongside other now-essentials like hardware for video (de)coding, DSPs, and so on, even if the Copilot+ PC branding exercise has been abandoned by Microsoft and its partners.

articles.title: Uma aba por cima de todas: conheça a Mini Janela do Firefox • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Uma aba por cima de todas: conheça a Mini Janela do Firefox
Mozilla está testando função Mini Janela no Firefox Nightly. Recurso permite manter qualquer aba flutuando sobre outras janelas.
Você já teve a necessidade de manter uma aba do navegador aberta acima de outras janelas? A Mozilla está testando um recurso no Firefox que atende a essa necessidade. Trata-se da Mini Janela (Mini Window) que, apesar de ainda não ser oficial (mas será em breve), já funciona bem.
Na primeira olhada, a novidade funciona como um modo de picture-in-picture (PiP). Mas as diferenças logo aparecem: o PiP deixa um recurso específico, como um reprodutor de vídeo, flutuando sobre outras janelas; já a Mini Janela do Firefox faz qualquer aba funcionar assim, independentemente do que ela contiver.
Quando a Mini Janela está ativada, a aba mostra apenas a página web. Mas, ao aproximar o cursor do mouse do topo da janela, a barra de endereços e os botões de navegação aparecem.
A nova função pode ser útil de diversas formas. Por exemplo, você pode deixar o YouTube reproduzindo um vídeo na Mini Janela enquanto executa outra atividade no computador, ou usá-la para comparar dados em uma planilha aberta em tela cheia, sem ficar alternando entre telas.
Um detalhe interessante é que a Mini Janela do Firefox também funciona com abas anônimas. Outro: você pode enviar apenas uma seção de uma página para a Mini Janela, como um trecho de um texto ou um gráfico.
Além disso, você pode mover a aba para qualquer ponto da tela, bem como alterar as suas dimensões com um simples arrastar do mouse.
No momento, a Mini Janela está disponível apenas no Firefox Nightly, versão experimental do navegador que pode ser baixada aqui (role a tela para encontrar essa opção). Para testar a novidade, você precisa apenas instalar essa versão ou atualizá-la, caso você já use o Firefox Nightly (é preciso ter a versão 160 ou superior).
O novo recurso vem ativado por padrão. Para usá-lo, abra uma página web, clique com o botão direito do mouse sob sua aba e vá em Mover Aba / Mover para Mini Janela. Para fazer a aba voltar ao seu tamanho normal, clique no ícone que aparece ao lado do “X” de fechar janela.
Se você preferir esperar um pouco, saiba que a Mini Janela deverá fazer parte do Firefox 160 (versão final), cujo lançamento é esperado para 10 de novembro.

articles.title: ASUS Republic of Gamers Announces ROG XG Station 3 With Thunderbolt 5
articles.text:
Wednesday, November 4th 2026
ASUS Republic of Gamers Announces ROG XG Station 3 With Thunderbolt 5
ASUS Republic of Gamers (ROG) today announced the ROG XG Station 3 external graphics card dock, featuring a Thunderbolt 5 connection capable of up to 80 Gbps of bidirectional bandwidth or up to 120 Gbps with Thunderbolt 5 Bandwidth Boost for high-volume video traffic. This level of performance enables incredible visual fidelity at a detailed resolution with ultrafluid frame rates, even for everyday laptops. With a graphics card in the NVIDIA GeForce RTX 50 Series, RTX PRO 6000 Series, AMD Radeon RX 9000 Series, or Intel Arc Series, users can access the absolute best performance in AAA games, vast power for content creation, and all the latest game-boosting features.
Customizable graphics power
Premium graphics cards are as stylish as they are powerful, so ROG opted for an open-frame design for the ROG XG Station 3. This keeps a user's graphics card out in the open as a visual centerpiece while also ensuring that it has entirely unobstructed access to cooling. With a standard graphics card, this arrangement will leave a PCIe power cable visible, but users are not limited to standard options.The ROG XG Station 3 includes a GC-HPWR slot that enables users to install a BTF 2.5 graphics card such as the TUF Gaming GeForce RTX 5080 BTF OC Edition or the ROG Astral GeForce RTX 5090 BTF Edition - both of which are capable of drawing power without a visible cable.
The ROG XG Station 3 complements the style of a user's graphics card with polished metallic surfaces and sleek lines. Plus, full Aura Sync support makes it easy to synchronize its RGB illumination with other Aura-compatible gear.
Incredible convenience
The outputs on the graphics card users install in the ROG XG Station 3 will give them plentiful options for connecting displays on their desk, making the dock a one-stop shop for accessing high-end graphics performance on any display (or displays) of their choice.
The XG Station 3 can also give users a true single-cable experience with many devices. The Thunderbolt 5 port used to connect to a compatible laptop offers up to 140 watts of USB Power Delivery, on top of its 80 Gbps of ultrafast data transfer, enabling it to fully power a wide range of laptops.
In addition to the primary Thunderbolt 5 upstream port, the XG Station 3 also gives users a versatile Thunderbolt 5 downstream port. This port gives users an easy way to connect USB-C monitors, supporting up to three 4K displays via daisy chaining - a feature not typically offered by graphics cards. Additionally, it can provide up to 36 W of USB Power Delivery for mobile devices or peripherals.
The XG Station 3 can also act as a comprehensive I/O hub. Two USB 10 Gbps Type-C ports, located within arm's reach on the front, give users a convenient access point for connecting gaming gear, external storage, and more.
Boost laptop setups with desktop-class GPU performance and more
The performance available with laptops has made leaps and bounds in recent years, even with compact options like the ROG Zephyrus G14. But as game developers continually ramp up the fidelity and realism, gamers continually have reason to seek out more performance. That could mean a new gaming PC - or it could mean the flexibility and easy upgradeability of the ROG XG Station 3, which lets users upgrade the power of compatible laptops to desktop-caliber gaming performance.

articles.title: 'We were highly skeptical about the cost of AI': Revolut reveals it cut AI coding costs by cutting out Claude entirely
articles.text:
'We were highly skeptical about the cost of AI': Revolut reveals it cut AI coding costs by cutting out Claude entirely
Revolut opts for self-hosted over commercial models
- Revolut cut Claude for self-hosted Z.ai models and slashed inference costs by 90%
- 70% improvement in lead time productivity, 60% up for coding time productivity
- The model is reportedly running on 56 Nvidia B200 GPUs with 380GB+ memory
Revolut has become one of a growing list of companies looking to reduce its reliance on Claude, and in doing so, it's reportedly cut inference costs by as much as 90% in less than a year.
But the London-headquartered digital bank hasn't cut AI out altogether, instead it's replaced those costly workloads with self-hosted, open-weight models from China's Z.ai.
By derestricting itself, the company now says its developers can use AI much more freely without worrying about token limits, which in turn has also improved productivity.
Revolut cuts Claude for self-hosted, open-weight Chinese models
Revolut seems pretty au-fait with the world of AI, having previously experimented with Google's Gemini before opting to use Anthropic's Claude, but some heavy users were said to be spending thousands of dollars per month on tokens without generating the equivalent ROI.
"We were highly skeptical about the cost of AI," Revolut Infrastructure Lead David Abitbol said in a conference last month (via The Register). "When we launched it we launched it with strict budget limits."
Speaking separately at GTC Berlin, Abitol also noted that Revolut's self-hosted option resulted in a 70% improvement in lead time productivity, and a 60% improvement in coding time productivity. He also praised Z.ai's GLM models for their data privacy and auditability.
Are self-hosted models cheaper to run?
It seems that GLM-5.1 brought inference costs down to around $0.30 per million input/output tokens, or around one-tenth the cost of similar commercial costs. Now, Revolut can operate its own inference infrastructure to manage its own capacity.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
However, with great flexibility comes great cost. While costs associated with direct model usage have been slashed, self-hosting requires significant outlay in terms of hardware and infrastructure. GPUs, maintenance, electricity and maintenance and some of the key areas that will likely have seen a major increase in expenditure.
The bank now reportedly has 56 Nvidia B200 GPUs, plus the model alone needs around 380GB of GPU memory and that excludes the estimated 6 to 26GB of memory per user for context retention.
Ultimately, it's proof that artificial intelligence is a costly beast and deploying it aimlessly in a hope to save time is a poor strategy. But with more companies ditching commercial AI from the likes of Claude in favor of self-hosting, it begs the question whether using less advanced models for mundane work and even self-hosting over renting could improve the economics in the years that come.
All of this, of course, against a backdrop of cost unpredictability, which seems to be hitting companies harder than high costs alone.
"Open source is now a priority at Revolut, and our economics are favorable," Abitol said. "The billing is flat, we don't have any bill shock at the end of the month, and the frontier is the exception."

articles.title: KI-Agenten planen, nutzen Tools, entscheiden – und Anwender tappen beim Nachvollziehen im Dunkeln
articles.text:
Wie 1.000 Bankangestellte ohne Ausweis: So blind setzen Unternehmen KI-Agenten ein
Die Vorfälle mit KI-Agenten haben sich in diesem Sommer scheinbar nahtlos aneinandergereiht: Zuerst der Ausbruch von KI-Agenten von OpenAI aus ihrer Testumgebung und der erfolgreiche Hack der Website von Hugging Face. Etwa zur gleichen Zeit griff ein anderer OpenAI-Agent auf private Dateien einer Website der australischen Regierung zu. Das Problem beschränkt sich keineswegs auf OpenAI. In den Monaten danach haben auch Anthropic, Google und Meta Vorfälle bekannt gegeben, bei denen ihre Agenten frei gedreht haben. Besorgniserregend ist, dass sich die autonomen Programme in vielen Fällen gerade den Augen der Forscher:innen und Sicherheitsteams entzogen haben, die eigentlich mit ihrer Überwachung beauftragt waren.
EU-Regulierung fordert mehr Überwachung von KI-Agenten – doch den Firmen fehlt etwas
KI-Agenten führen unbefugte Handlungen durch, und die Unternehmen, die sie entwickeln und betreiben, verlassen sich größtenteils auf Glück und nachträgliche Erkenntnisse, um schädliche Auswirkungen zu mindern. Sie müssen mehr tun, um die Sicherheit zu gewährleisten. Deshalb fordern EU-Regulierungsbehörden und US-Behörden zu Recht, dass Entwickler:innen und Betreiber von Agenten diese in Echtzeit überwachen. Diese Vorschriften setzen jedoch voraus, dass Unternehmen sehen können, was ihre Agenten tun und warum – während ihnen in Wirklichkeit ausreichende Transparenz fehlt.
Es ist etwa so: Stell dir eine Bank vor, die 1.000 neue Mitarbeiter:innen einstellt. Sie bekommen Zugriff auf Konten von Kund:innen und sensible Informationen, doch die Mitarbeiter:innenausweise ändern sich täglich. Es ist unklar, ob ein Vorgesetzter oder eine Vorgesetzte ihre Arbeit jemals überprüft oder genehmigt hat, und Änderungen, die diese Mitarbeiter:innen an Genehmigungsprozessen vornehmen, werden nicht protokolliert. Genau in dieser Situation befinden wir uns aktuell mit KI-Agenten – ein völliger Mangel an Transparenz.

articles.title: Silicon Photonics Hits the Big Time - EE Times
articles.text:
This week’s news of the $115 billion Marvell-Lumentum deal signals that silicon photonics has turned the corner from being discussed as a potential solution to the power wall caused by interconnect inefficiency to becoming a hotbed of activity, with an ecosystem ripe for exits that can help the technology scale and beat the limitations of copper in the evolving AI story.
Just two years ago, on the sidelines of the OFC conference in San Diego, I chaired a workshop panel discussing whether AI would be the killer application for silicon photonics. At that time, we wrote, “It was clear from the presentations that we are at a potential turning point for silicon photonics. But there were still challenges in terms of scaling, energy efficiency, packaging, ecosystem, and tools like EDA and third-party IP, as well as materials.”
What we are seeing in the market today suggests that we’ve moved well beyond that point. It’s not just the large Marvell-Lumentum deal, but also the emergence of startups such as Salience Labs, which just raised $125 million in Series B funding to accelerate the deployment of its optical circuit switching (OCS) technology. Its backers include Applied Ventures, AMD Ventures, and Intel Capital.
You can watch our video interview with Salience Labs CEO and co-founder Vaysh Kewada here:
In this interview, we asked Kewada why she believes this is the right moment for optical switching and for Salience Labs, and how the company plans to achieve volume manufacturing and commercial adoption.
She said that, by deliberately building its architecture on foundry processes capable of supporting volume production and aligning with co-packaged optics (CPO) manufacturing strategies early on, the company can mitigate standard supply chain friction. She added that 2027 will be a critical inflection year for volume production and deployment of its OCS technology.
Kewada told EE Times, “We’ve taken the approach of developing out an optical circuit switch that’s optical end-to-end so we’re never transforming the payload or the data into the electrical domain. The second differentiating standpoint is that we’ve chosen to take a fully integrated on-chip approach. And we’ve overcome the loss aspect of integrating optics onto the chip through the development of our own amplifiers that are also integrated on chip.”
In the same week that Salience Labs announced its funding round, another startup competing in the OCS space, Voyant Photonics, announced that it is developing a chip-scale OCS engine for AI data center networks. The company said it plans to deliver it to customers as a compact optical switching building block that can be integrated into next-generation data center switching platforms.
Voyant is not starting from scratch, though. It has already developed a high-density silicon photonics switch matrix to route light for its FMCW LiDAR systems. The architecture uses discrete, solid-state optical paths rather than moving mirrors or continuous analog beam steering. The company said this technology is now being adapted, since in a data center OCS implementation, it’s the same fundamental architecture that can be configured to route optical signals among communication ports.
Voyant plans to provide its OCS technology as an engine that optical networking companies can incorporate into their own platforms.
The land grab for silicon photonics
In a report published last month, titled “The Interconnect Imperative—Why AI Is Forcing the Semiconductor Industry to Go Global”, Woodside Capital Partners wrote, “In the space of fifteen months, Marvell paid $3.54 billion for Celestial AI; Nvidia put $2 billion each into Coherent and Lumentum—and then $3.2 billion more into Corning; Ayar Labs closed a $650 million Series E at a $5.0 billion valuation; and Credo, Molex, GlobalFoundries, Ciena, AMD, and FormFactor each bought their way into a different layer of the stack.”
The authors added, “Our view is that this is a land grab for control points—lasers, optical engines, chiplets, packaging, test, and foundry capacity—and that it will not run forever. Each deal removes a control point from the board and raises the scarcity premium on what remains; but as the gaps fill, urgency will decline. For founders, the window for premium strategic exits is open now. For acquirers, the cost of waiting is compounding.”
This context helps explain Marvell’s interest in bringing Momentum into its already strong connectivity portfolio.
If you look at the silicon photonics landscape (see chart above), the ecosystem offers plenty of opportunities for partnerships, mergers, and acquisitions as companies race to beat that power wall.
As I stated in the Woodside Capital report, the surge in investment activity in silicon photonics, whether through high-ticket funding rounds or outright acquisitions, highlights a shift in which foundry economics are favorable to high-volume manufacturability and scaling. Over the past year, the industry has moved very quickly from viewing integrated silicon photonics as an emerging alternative to copper to recognizing optical interconnects as a viable physical backbone for scaling next-generation AI infrastructure.

AI Data Centers Push Silicon Photonics Toward 300-mm Scale
Photonics: A Foundational Scaling Layer for AI-Era Computing
Photonics Chipmakers Race to Production

Verifying chips is becoming much more difficult in multi-die assemblies. Purna Mohanty, CEO of SignatureIP, talks about the impact of chiplets and shared memory resources, the challenges of version control across multiple flavors of I/O, and the challenges engineering teams face when hardware-accelerated tools are running at different speeds than the actual design.

articles.title: Nintendo recibe un golpe que podría afectar a todos los que compran juegos físicos
articles.text:
El futuro de los juegos físicos de Nintendo podría enfrentarse a un nuevo obstáculo. Macronix, uno de los fabricantes de memorias ROM que se usan en los cartuchos de Nintendo Switch y Nintendo Switch 2, decidió abandonar el negocio. Esto podría provocar una subida de precio en los juegos de consola, aunque algunos temen que se repita lo que ocurrió con PlayStation.
De acuerdo con Eurogamer, Macronix abandonó el negocio de las memorias ROM para concentrarse en otros productos con mayor demanda. La compañía ha sido uno de los socios más importantes de Nintendo, suministrando componentes de memoria para diferentes generaciones de consolas que van desde la Nintendo DS y 3DS hasta la reciente Switch 2.
Según el analista David Gibson, las memorias ROM representaron apenas el 5% de los ingresos de Macronix durante el tercer trimestre de 2026, lo que representó una caída con respecto al año anterior. En una llamada con accionistas, la compañía confirmó que dejará de desarrollar estos productos y destinará sus recursos a las memorias NOR y eMMC. Macronix explicó que tiene capacidad de producción limitada, por lo que prefirió invertir en otros tipos de memoria que generen más dinero que los cartuchos de Nintendo.
¿Qué pasará con los cartuchos de Nintendo Switch y Switch 2?
Si bien la noticia es lamentable, la salida de Macronix no representa un riesgo inmediato para la continuidad del formato físico de Nintendo. El gigante japonés trabaja con otros proveedores que pueden producir este tipo de memorias para las tarjetas de juego, lo que aseguraría la fabricación de cartuchos en el corto y mediano plazo.
El problema es que la pérdida de uno de los socios más importantes podría tener un efecto negativo a largo plazo. Macronix no es la única empresa que ha volteado a ver otros mercados en esta crisis de memoria. El caso más reciente es el de Crucial, que dejó de vender memorias RAM y discos SSD tras casi 30 años en el sector. Micron decidió que era más lucrativo venderle esa memoria a las empresas de IA que a los consumidores.
Nintendo es la única compañía de juegos que sigue apostando al formato físico. Pese a ello, los analistas afirman que las ventas digitales siguen ganando terreno y ya representan más del 60% de los ingresos de software. Algunos creen que la salida de Macronix podría acelerar la adopción de formatos alternativos, como las Game-Key Cards que ofrecen una clave de descarga en lugar del juego completo en el cartucho.
Es difícil pensar que Nintendo adoptaría una postura similar a la de PlayStation, que dejará de producir juegos en disco a partir de 2028. La japonesa todavía registra buenos ingresos por las ventas de juegos de sus franquicias clave, sobre todo en lanzamientos como el reciente remake de The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. Probablemente, en un futuro adopte una postura similar a la de Xbox, que mantiene el formato físico y ofrece una licencia digital única por cada juego en disco.

articles.title: Marvel's Blade : le gros jeu AAA bientôt sauvé par Ubisoft ?
articles.text:
Selon les informations exclusives de Jason Schreier pour Bloomberg, publiées ce mardi 3 novembre 2026, Microsoft étudie plusieurs offres pour céder Arkane Studios avant une échéance fixée au 13 décembre. Parmi les candidats au rachat figure Ubisoft, aux côtés d’au moins deux autres entreprises du jeu vidéo dont les noms n’ont pas filtré. L’option d’un rachat par la direction du studio lyonnais reste également sur la table. Une bonne nouvelle pour les employés et Marvel’s Blade.
Microsoft avait annoncé en juillet vouloir se séparer d’Arkane, dans le cadre d’un plan de 3 200 suppressions de postes chez Xbox. Comme le studio est installé en France, le groupe doit consulter les représentants du personnel avant toute fermeture. Cette consultation devait s’achever le 13 novembre. Fin octobre, Microsoft l’a prolongée d’un mois, jusqu’au 13 décembre, le temps de chercher un partenaire pour accompagner le studio jusqu’à la fin du développement. Selon Le Monde, 217 emplois sont en jeu à Lyon.
Une bouffée d’oxygène pour Marvel’s Blade
Annoncé aux Game Awards en décembre 2023, le projet Marvel’s Blade avait immédiatement enthousiasmé les joueurs. Il associe le savoir-faire des spécialistes de l’immersive sim (les créateurs de Dishonored et Deathloop) à la licence du célèbre chasseur de vampires de la maison des idées.
La grande restructuration lancée par Asha Sharma, CEO de Xbox depuis février, menaçait directement l’avenir du jeu, d’autant que le studio sœur Arkane Austin avait fait les frais d’une fermeture brutale en 2024 après le fiasco Redfall.
D’autres studios visés par ce plan ont déjà trouvé une issue. Double Fine et Compulsion Games ont repris leur indépendance en juillet, en gardant leurs jeux et leurs licences.
D’après Bloomberg, un rachat permettrait sans doute à Arkane de terminer Marvel’s Blade, dont la sortie est attendue d’ici un à deux ans.
Vers un sauvetage in extremis par Ubisoft ?
Pour Ubisoft, s’offrir Arkane Studios représenterait un coup stratégique d’envergure pour renforcer ses structures de développement européennes avec l’un des studios les plus respectés de l’Hexagone. Du côté de Microsoft, céder le studio plutôt que de le fermer (selon Le Monde, Microsoft avait annoncé en juillet aux salariés son intention de fermer le site lyonnais) envoie un signal un brin plus mesuré, tout en confirmant le recentrage drastique opéré par la firme de Redmond.
Microsoft a jusqu’au 13 décembre pour trancher. Aucun accord n’a encore été conclu, le montant des offres n’a pas été dévoilé et Ubisoft n’a pas réagi aux informations de Bloomberg.

articles.title: ForgeCode’s Tushar Mathur wants software development to run like a factory, not a project
articles.text:
ForgeCode’s Tushar Mathur wants software development to run like a factory, not a project
At TechSparks 2026, ForgeCode Founder and CEO Tushar Mathur demonstrated how AI agents can manage software development from specification to deployment, while engineers focus on supervision and decision-making.
Traditionally, scaling software development meant adding engineers, time, and resources. AI is changing that equation by making code cheaper and faster to write. But generating code faster does not necessarily mean delivering software faster. Code still needs to be reviewed, tested, and deployed, creating new bottlenecks for engineering teams.
For engineering leaders, this raises a question: how can software delivery scale without a corresponding increase in headcount?
ForgeCode is addressing this challenge by building what it calls an AI-native software factory. The platform uses AI agents to manage the software development lifecycle, from specifications and implementation to testing and deployment, with humans providing oversight.
At TechSparks 2026, Founder and CEO Tushar Mathur demonstrated how the platform works and explained why the falling cost of writing code is making review, testing, and deployment more important to software delivery.
The shift in bottlenecks
While AI has increased individual productivity, those gains have not necessarily translated into faster software delivery across organizations.
“The first thing that we are seeing is practically all code is autogenerated today,” Mathur said.
Engineering teams can now generate thousands of lines of code quickly, but the processes that follow: code reviews, testing, security checks, and deployment are struggling to keep up.
According to Mathur, the bottleneck has shifted from writing code to managing what happens after it is written.
“Earlier, writing code was the main fundamental bottleneck. But today, the cost of writing code is so low that all these other aspects have become the bottlenecks,” he explained.
As a result, teams risk producing more poorly reviewed, buggy or uncoordinated code because the systems needed to manage the increased output have not kept pace.
The rise of the AI-native software factory
To address this gap between individual productivity and organizational output, Mathur introduced ForgeCode’s approach to an AI-native software factory.
The idea is to move away from a software development lifecycle that depends on people manually coordinating each stage.
Instead, AI agents handle tasks such as triaging, planning, implementation, and verification. Humans step in when decisions, direction, or more detailed feedback are required.
Unlike conventional automation, which links a series of predefined steps, the software factory uses continuous feedback loops.
Inputs from CXOs, product managers, and production monitoring systems can feed directly into the development backlog. Agents then work around the clock to develop features, identify bugs, and improve performance, including when engineering teams are offline.
The aim is to keep software development moving without requiring engineers to manage every individual task.
Six tenets of a modern software factory
Mathur outlined six principles that he believes are essential to building an effective AI-native software factory.
- Autonomous operation: The system should work continuously, with humans supervising performance rather than coordinating individual tasks.
- High scalability: Organizations should be able to scale engineering work quickly, whether they are developing a small feature or rewriting an entire application in a different programming language.
- Cost-effectiveness: The factory delivers multifold returns compared with manual development, measured through two key factors: the cost of building software and the speed at which it can be shipped.
- Measurability: The system should track deployment frequency, bug density, and costs, using this information to assess and improve its performance.
- Self-improvement: The factory should use data and feedback to refine its processes over time and avoid repeating earlier mistakes.
- Business-driven development: Features should be prioritized according to business objectives, such as customer retention or compliance, rather than solely by technical backlog requirements.
Together, these principles are intended to make software development more autonomous while keeping it aligned with business priorities.
Handling trade-offs and non-functional requirements
During the audience Q&A, Mathur was asked how engineering teams should approach trade-offs and complex non-functional requirements such as scalability and database architecture.
He said requirements that can be objectively verified, such as scale targets, can be delegated to the software factory. The system continuously tests outcomes and optimises whenever a check fails. Trade-offs, however, require human judgment. Questions such as how much risk or failure a business is willing to tolerate remain decisions for engineers and business leaders, who step in to guide the agent when needed.
ForgeCode said this is possible because the platform operates on a self-improving feedback loop. Every task, decision, and correction contributes to a knowledge base that informs future work. Engineers remain closely involved in the early stages, but as the system learns a team's engineering practices and business context, it can operate with greater autonomy.
The platform also learns which decisions are critical and require expert oversight, particularly those involving security, reliability, performance, and competing business priorities. In such cases, it pauses and seeks human input before proceeding.
This growing ability to distinguish between routine execution and decisions that require expert judgment is central to how the product works.
Steering the factory floor
ForgeCode's AI-native software factory is designed to turn gains in individual coding productivity into faster software delivery across an organization.
By using agents to manage coordination, code reviews, testing, and other development tasks, the platform aims to reduce the bottlenecks that can slow engineering teams.
For Mathur, the shift is about changing the role of engineers. Rather than managing every stage of development, they would focus on defining requirements, making decisions, reviewing outcomes, and guiding the overall process.
The goal is not simply to generate more code or build larger teams, but to develop software more efficiently through autonomous systems that operate continuously, with human oversight.

articles.title: Livreur, banque ou arnaque ? Orange va vous dire qui vous appelle avant même de décrocher
articles.text:
Face à la multiplication des appels indésirables, beaucoup d’abonnés ont pris l’habitude de ne plus décrocher lorsqu’un numéro inconnu s’affiche. Selon le dernier observatoire de la satisfaction client de l’Arcep, 94 % des consommateurs ont reçu au moins un appel ou un SMS indésirable au cours des trois derniers mois, et 69 % des Français ne répondraient jamais ou rarement à un numéro inconnu, selon les chiffres de cette étude cités par Orange. Ce réflexe de protection peut néanmoins faire manquer des appels utiles, qu’il s’agisse d’un livreur, d’un rendez-vous à confirmer ou d’un rappel du service client. Le démarchage téléphonique non consenti est pourtant désormais interdit en France, mais les arnaques par téléphone continuent, elles, de viser les abonnés.
L’opérateur historique veut répondre à ce problème avec Branded Call, un service lancé ce mercredi 4 novembre après avoir été présenté en mars au Mobile World Congress de Barcelone. Lorsqu’une entreprise inscrite au service appelle un client mobile d’Orange, son nom s’affiche à côté de son numéro, même si celui-ci ne figure pas dans les contacts. Le service est gratuit pour les abonnés et fonctionne sur tous les smartphones, sans souscription ni application à installer, puisque tout se passe dans le cœur du réseau de l’opérateur.
Un nom affiché seulement pour les appels certifiés
Encore faut-il éviter que des escrocs n’en profitent pour se faire passer pour une marque connue. Orange assure que son service empêche l’affichage d’un nom sur des appels malveillants. Il s’appuie pour cela sur le mécanisme d’authentification des numéros (MAN), mis en place par les opérateurs français depuis 2024 pour lutter contre l’usurpation de numéro. Seuls les appels ayant obtenu le plus haut niveau de certification, dit « A », peuvent afficher un nom. L’opérateur précise aussi vérifier en amont l’identité et la réputation de chaque entreprise avant de l’accepter.
Avant son lancement, Branded Call a été testé par onze entreprises, dont les instituts Ipsos et Médiamétrie, qui ont passé plus de 2 millions d’appels pour des sondages, de l’assistance technique ou du recrutement. Le service est désormais commercialisé, sans précision sur les tarifs, auprès des entreprises par Orange Business et par des partenaires comme Odigo et Manifone, d’autres distributeurs devant suivre dans les prochains mois. Orange Business lancera par ailleurs le 16 novembre « Appels de confiance », une offre qui permettra aux entreprises d’afficher une identité vérifiée lors de leurs appels sortants et de mieux protéger leur marque contre l’usurpation.
Bouygues Telecom et Free misent aussi sur le réseau contre le spam
Orange n’est pas le seul opérateur sur ce créneau. Bouygues Telecom avait annoncé en mai un service similaire, lui aussi baptisé Branded Call et développé avec l’américain Hiya, avec un déploiement prévu à partir de juin pour tous ses abonnés. L’opérateur prévoit d’y ajouter en 2027 le motif de l’appel et le logo de l’entreprise. Il a aussi lancé début octobre Anti-Spam, un filtrage des appels indésirables directement sur le réseau, facturé 2 euros par mois et par ligne aux particuliers. Chez Free, les abonnés mobiles peuvent de leur côté rejeter les appels anonymes ou créer des filtres depuis leur espace abonné. Ces outils ont toutefois une approche différente, puisqu’ils cherchent à bloquer les appels suspects, là où Branded Call vise à rendre reconnaissables les appels légitimes.
Chaque service ne fonctionne en outre que pour les abonnés de l’opérateur concerné, et l’efficacité de Branded Call dépendra surtout du nombre d’entreprises qui accepteront de l’adopter. Un appel sans nom affiché restera, pour l’abonné, un numéro inconnu comme un autre.

articles.title: Des pirates détournent un système d’alerte et annoncent une attaque nucléaire
articles.text:
Les 1er et 2 novembre, des utilisateurs ukrainiens puis russes ont reçu sur leur téléphone des alertes annonçant des frappes nucléaires. Les deux pays ont écarté ces messages, sans désigner de responsable.
Air Alert, l’application qui prévient des millions d’Ukrainiens en cas de frappe, a été piratée dimanche soir. Quelques heures plus tard, c’est l'application du ministère russe des Situations d’urgence qui était visée à son tour.
Protégez votre entreprise gratuitement pendant 30 jours
Découvrez Bitdefender Ultimate Small Business Security et protégez votre activité contre les cybermenaces. Aucune coordonnée bancaire requise.
Du push d’Air Alert aux chaînes Max : le trajet des fausses alertes
Côté ukrainien, les utilisateurs d’Air Alert ont reçu des avertissements de risques radiologiques et chimiques, ainsi que d’affrontements dans les rues de Kyiv. L’un des messages, rédigé en russe, disait en substance : "Salut ! Il va y avoir une alerte nucléaire sur toute l’Ukraine. Pas d’inquiétude, l’Oreshnik est en route." L'Oreshnik est un missile balistique hypersonique russe. L'armée de l’air ukrainienne a démenti ces alertes et dénoncé une ingérence hostile. Le Centre de lutte contre la désinformation a demandé de ne pas cliquer sur des liens tiers et de ne pas relayer d’informations non vérifiées. L’application a été temporairement coupée, le temps de rétablir le service.
En Russie, les notifications sont arrivées dans les premières heures de lundi 2 novembre. Elles annonçaient que des ogives nucléaires avaient été lancées vers toutes les régions du pays, transportées par des systèmes P1-SUN. Ce sont des drones intercepteurs de conception ukrainienne, pilotés à distance grâce à une caméra embarquée (on parle de drones FPV). L’entreprise SkyFall les a développés pour abattre des drones de type Shahed et des missiles de croisière. Les utilisateurs devaient stocker trois semaines de nourriture et se réfugier dans des sous-sols. Le ministère a évoqué une attaque massive contre son application.
Les fausses alertes ne se sont pas limitées à l’application. Elles se sont aussi affichées sur des chaînes régionales du ministère sur Max, la messagerie soutenue par l’État russe, à Saint-Pétersbourg, dans la région de Moscou et dans plusieurs autres régions, dont Belgorod, Nijni Novgorod, Sverdlovsk et Tioumen. Un message similaire est apparu sur la chaîne Telegram du quartier général opérationnel de Belgorod. Rappelons que Moscou cherche à orienter sa population vers MAX, une messagerie nationale sans aucun chiffrement des communications. Cette fois, la fausse alerte est passée par un canal officiel de ce service.
Le ministère russe parle d’une vulnérabilité (une faille exploitable par un tiers) dans son application mobile et dit travailler à la corriger. Il assure que la situation est sous contrôle et invite à ne se fier qu’aux sources officielles. Reste la question de l’auteur : l'Armée de l’air ukrainienne n’a nommé personne. Futurism y voit la piste d’un acteur extérieur au conflit, puisque les deux camps sont touchés, tout en admettant que rien n’est exclu.

articles.title: Barcelona ha conseguido bajar los alquileres con la Ley de Vivienda. El problema es lo que está pasando con los pisos disponibles
articles.text:
Un alquiler que baja de precio en Barcelona suena casi a fallo de mercado o a medir haciendo trampas. Pero es lo que sostiene la Generalitat. Según los datos de fianzas del Incasòl, la renta media de los contratos nuevos en la ciudad ha caído un 4,4% desde marzo de 2024, cuando entraron en vigor los topes. Ahora rondaría los 1.140 euros al mes. En los municipios tensionados, donde rige el límite, las rentas han subido un 0,7%. En los que quedan fuera, un 11%.
El balance llega a una semana de la huelga general del 11 de noviembre, convocada en Cataluña. Una huelga que reivindica muchas cosas, pero sobre todo vivienda digna, algo que recogen tanto la Declaración Unviersal de los Derechos Humanos como todas y cada una de las revisiones de nuestra Constitución. Eso sí, el titular oficial cuenta solo una pequeña parte de esta historia. Vayamos al meollo.
Lo que dice el Govern. La comparación es entre el segundo trimestre de 2026 y el primero de 2024, justo antes de los topes. En ese tiempo la inflación ha subido un 6,8%, según Salvador Illa, y los alquileres regulados mucho menos. Si hubiera seguido la tendencia previa, calcula la Generalitat, la renta media en las zonas tensionadas sería de 1.023 euros en lugar de 894: un ahorro de 129 euros al mes por inquilino. Ojo: es una estimación contrafactual, no un dato que hayamos podido observar. En Barcelona, además, el precio bajó en cinco de sus diez distritos.
¿Hay menos contratos? ¿Y si la clave está ahí? El sector lo denuncia, pero el Govern lo niega. Su argumento: en el último trimestre se firmaron 26.449 contratos de alquiler habitual y se extinguieron 23.937, un saldo de 2.512 a favor, y hay más de 850.000 contratos activos, un máximo histórico. Al parecer, con esos topes a los caseros les compensa menos cambiar de inquilino. Y si hay menos rotación, hay más estabilidad.
Claro, esos 26.449 contratos nuevos quedan por debajo de los entre 30.000 y 40.000 que se cerraban cada trimestre antes de la medida, como recogía El País. Con las fianzas del Incasòl, el Ara contabilizó 34.496 contratos nuevos en Cataluña en el primer trimestre de 2024 y 26.962 en el tercer trimestre de 2025.
La magia del 4,4%. Ese descenso es de la mensualidad, no del metro cuadrado. Según Crónica Global, con datos del Ayuntamiento, los pisos que se alquilan en Barcelona miden de media 71,1 metros cuadrados, un 5,2% menos que hace dos años. El precio por metro cuadrado, de hecho, era en el primer trimestre de 2026 un 0,9% superior al de principios de 2024. Dicho en román paladino: se paga algo menos al mes, pero por un piso más pequeño.
Qué dicen los estudios. Uno de los análisis más completos es el de Simone Cigna, investigador de la Universitat Pompeu Fabra, que aprovecha que los topes llegaron a unos municipios antes que a otros. Su conclusión es que el efecto sobre los precios es real: las rentas de los contratos nuevos son entre un 5,6% y un 6,7% más bajas de lo que serían sin el límite.
Y también detecta un coste: entre un 13% y un 16% menos de contratos de larga duración firmados cada trimestre. No estamos hablando de un parque que encoge, sino que crece más despacio: en Barcelona, los contratos de larga duración activos pasaron de unos 206.400 a finales de 2023 a unos 212.400 en septiembre de 2025.
Otra cara la aporta un estudio de Fedea firmado por Fernando Pinto: los anuncios de alquiler cayeron un 22,2% en la provincia de Barcelona entre el primer trimestre de 2024 y el cuarto de 2025, mientras en Madrid subían un 3,9%. Cada anuncio barcelonés recibió de media 462 contactos en sus diez primeros días, frente a los 103 de Madrid. No se puede medir a una sola causa, pero la diferencia entre oferta y demanda es real.
Las fugas. Parte de la oferta se desvió a los contratos de temporada, que quedaron fuera del límite hasta enero de 2026. Según Cigna, en Barcelona pasaron del 2%-5% de los contratos nuevos antes de 2024 al 24% en la segunda mitad de ese año. El Sindicat de Llogateres apunta al mismo vacío. Desde que se reguló, la Generalitat dice que esos contratos han caído un 40% en un año. Queda el cumplimiento: Cigna estima que el 57% de los contratos largos para los que se puede calcular el tope se registró por encima de él, y la Generalitat tiene 45 propuestas de sanción, ninguna definitiva.
El Sindicat de Llogateres también defendía que los topes empujan a sacar pisos del mercado, pero pide ir más lejos y limitar las actualizaciones anuales de las rentas. Es de lógica. Los datos disponibles respaldan que el límite contiene el precio de los contratos nuevos. Que eso facilite o no encontrar un piso ya es otro tema. Mientras tanto, sigue sin cerrarse el acuerdo entre PSC y Comunes sobre las compras especulativas de vivienda, y el Gobierno central ha optado por otra vía para los caseros.
Comprar más vivienda a los fondos de inversión, como ha hecho Euskadi, es otra vía.

articles.title: mSecure password manager hack prompts password reset warnings
articles.text:
mSeven Software is warning current and former mSecure password manager customers to change passwords, reset two-factor authentication, and remove passkeys following a cyberattack in which a hacker reportedly stole an encrypted customer database..
In a security notification sent to customers on November 3 and shared with BleepingComputer, the company said it recently discovered suspicious activity involving its mSecure password management application.
"mSeven Software (“mSeven”) recently learned of suspicious activity associated with the mSecure password management application," reads the mSecure security notification.
"In response, mSeven quickly launched an investigation, took steps to mitigate the issue, and engaged external cybersecurity experts to assist. You are receiving this email because you are a current or former mSecure customer."
The notice did not provide any details as to what systems were compromised, whether customer data was stolen, and how many users were impacted.
However, the company urged all current and former customers to immediately protect confidential information stored in the password manager.
"This may include changing passwords, resetting or re-enrolling two-factor authentication methods, or removing existing passkeys," continued the security notice.
mSecure is a password manager that allows users to store passwords, passkeys, financial information, and other sensitive data in encrypted vaults that can be synchronized across devices.
According to mSeven's security documentation, mSecure uses AES-256 encryption and a zero-knowledge architecture that encrypts data locally on users' devices before transmitting it to the company's servers. The company says it cannot access customers' decrypted vault contents.
These security protections have led to confusion among customers about why they are being advised to change all their stored passwords and authentication if their data was encrypted before being uploaded to the company's servers.
Encrypted password database reportedly stolen
While the original notification had few details, customers have shared responses reportedly received from mSeven's support team indicating that a hacker stole an encrypted database from mSecure Cloud.
In one support forum post, a customer shared a response stating that the stolen database contained information belonging to current and former mSecure users.
According to the response, mSeven discovered the theft and subsequently notified customers.
The response also stated that the company had no evidence that the attacker accessed the confidential information stored within the encrypted database.
"Please note, this issue only pertains to users that were synching with the mSecure Cloud," reads the response shared by the customer.
The company also reportedly said it had implemented additional security measures and had no evidence that the mSecure application was currently unsafe to use.
Other customers reported receiving similar explanations, including confirmation that the incident was limited to users who synchronized their password databases through mSecure Cloud.
However, customers have expressed frustration over the company's lack of transparency about the breach and the potential risks to their stored credentials, particularly as mSeven has not publicly explained how the breach occurred.
While mSeven reportedly has no evidence that attackers accessed the encrypted information, stolen password vaults can still pose significant risks if attackers can crack weak master passwords through offline attacks.
This was shown in the 2022 LastPass breach, when attackers stole backups containing encrypted password vaults.
Researchers later linked the breach to cryptocurrency thefts in which attackers are believed to have cracked weak master passwords to access stored credentials, private keys, and recovery phrases.
BleepingComputer contacted mSeven Software with questions about the incident, the stolen database, and the potential impact on customers, but has not yet received a response.

articles.title: La IA está transformando las profesiones STEM: una encuesta recoge salidas de trabajadores relacionadas con ella
articles.text:
La inteligencia artificial está transformando los trabajos de los profesionales de las STEM (ciencia, tecnología, ingeniería y matemáticas). En Alemania se ha encuestado a 817 profesionales de estas áreas para conocer su percepción de estos cambios. La encuesta ha sido realizada por YouGov para la consultora de personal SThree.
Un 38,4 % afirman que en los últimos doce meses han visto compañeros abandonar la empresa por causas relacionadas con la IA. Este dato no permite saber qué porcentaje de los trabajadores han decidido irse (dimitir) por esta causa.
Los motivos de las salidas y las diferencias por sector
De los que mencionan este hecho, un 52,2 % indican que el trabajo se ha modificado de tal forma que ahora es irreconocible (la pregunta ofrecía varias posibilidades). Otro 46,5 % apunta la falta de oportunidades de desarrollo. Por otro lado, un 36,9 % considera que la carga de trabajo era insoportable.
Los datos varían mucho según el sector. Un 56,8 % de los encuestados en ciencias de la vida mencionan que han visto compañeros abandonar la empresa por causas relacionadas con la IA. En cambio, en informática solo lo hacen un 28,9 %, y en ingeniería un 29,6 %.
Más productividad percibida y peticiones de formación
También hay aspectos positivos. Un 66,8 % de los usuarios de IA consideran que sus equipos son más productivos que hace dos años. Un 38 % dedica el tiempo ahorrado a pensar estratégicamente. Un 29,4 % lo emplea en tareas extra. Por otro lado, un 29 % lo dedica a formarse.
En cuanto a las emociones asociadas a la IA, destacan la estimulación (38 %), la curiosidad (37 %) y el entusiasmo (32,7 %). Por el contrario, menos frecuentes son la presión (11,7 %) o el miedo (9,3 %).
Se trata de percepciones. El trabajo de campo se realizó entre el 10 de julio y el 1 de septiembre de 2026. Los datos de productividad no pueden extrapolarse a los resultados de rendimiento de las empresas en las que trabajan.
En las preguntas abiertas, los profesionales plantean la necesidad de formación especializada. Además, también demandan claridad en los usos de la IA. También piden que la dirección los implique en los primeros momentos de los cambios.
