articles.title: Microsoft is giving away 25 Xbox games worth over $500 with new Windows PCs and handhelds
articles.text:
First look: New Windows 11 PCs and handhelds sold in the US now come with an offer of 25 Xbox games valued at more than $500. How far that library reaches beyond the PC depends on which titles support Xbox Play Anywhere. Between that uneven cross-device support and eligibility rules built around specific hardware and software setups, what the offer is really worth comes down to the machine a buyer chooses.
Microsoft is delivering the X25 bundle through the Microsoft Store app on Windows 11, not through codes or retailer redemptions. The bundle will appear on eligible machines no later than the end of November, and owners can claim all 25 games from there. The promotion runs through December and is limited to buyers in the US. It is part of the run-up to Xbox's 25th anniversary.
Eligibility depends on what is preinstalled on the machine. Under Microsoft's terms, any new Windows PC or handheld that ships with Windows Home qualifies, while new PCs that ship with Windows Pro qualify only if they run on Nvidia RTX Spark silicon. Refurbished machines are excluded, as are PCs bought from unauthorized resellers, online marketplaces, liquidators or auction sites.
In practice, those rules leave out most Pro-licensed business hardware. Microsoft also says it may revoke the promotional benefits if a purchase is returned, canceled or not completed for other reasons, so buyers who plan to claim the games and send the PC back risk losing them.
For anyone who plays on both a console and a PC, the technical detail that matters most is Xbox Play Anywhere. With that support, one purchase covers both the Windows and Xbox console versions of a game. Age of Empires II: Definitive Edition, Gears of War: Reloaded and The Elder Scrolls Online all support it, so claiming them on a new PC also gives access on Xbox hardware.
Several of the bigger titles don't. Call of Duty: WWII, Fallout 76, Halo: Combat Evolved Anniversary and Minecraft Dungeons have separate Windows and Xbox versions. Claiming those through the bundle covers the PC version only.
The 25 games cover most of Xbox's history and the Bethesda and Activision catalogs Microsoft now owns. The id Software games include Doom, Doom II, Quake, Quake II and Wolfenstein: The New Order. Bethesda's role-playing lineup includes The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim Special Edition, The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion Game of the Year Edition, The Elder Scrolls Online and Fallout 76.
The strategy games are Age of Empires II: Definitive Edition, Age of Mythology: Retold, Rise of Nations: Extended Edition, Gears Tactics and Pillars of Eternity II: Deadfire. Original Xbox-era games include Fuzion Frenzy, Crimson Skies: High Road to Revenge and BLINX: The Time Sweeper, along with Halo: Combat Evolved Anniversary.
The rest of the list is Gears of War: Reloaded, Call of Duty: WWII, Minecraft Dungeons, The Outer Worlds, As Dusk Falls, Battletoads and Zoo Tycoon: Ultimate Animal Collection.
Because new handhelds running Windows Home are eligible, portable gaming PCs are among the cheapest ways to get the bundle, and they are expected to be popular gifts this holiday season. They can be used on the road or around the house, and the Play Anywhere titles in the bundle carry over to an Xbox console as well.

articles.title: ChatGPT já equivale a 20% das buscas do Google, mas calma • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
ChatGPT já equivale a 20% das buscas do Google, mas calma
Com 1,2 bilhão de usuários ativos, ChatGPT já é o maior rival do buscador, mas "império do Google" está longe do fim.
Você já fez ou faz perguntas ao ChatGPT que, antes, seriam direcionadas exclusivamente ao Google? A resposta é “sim” para muita gente. Não por acaso, a própria OpenAI assegura que seu serviço de IA já tem um volume de uso que corresponde a 20% das buscas realizadas no Google. Mas esse panorama precisa ser observado com cuidado.
A afirmação foi feita por Adam Fry, líder de produtos do ChatGPT, em entrevista ao Big Technology. De acordo com o executivo, o serviço registrou 1,2 bilhão de usuários ativos semanais considerando os últimos 60 dias, sendo que, nesse período, houve adição de 200 milhões de novos usuários.
Tem mais. Fry aponta que o modo de voz do ChatGPT já tem 250 milhões de usuários ativos semanais e que, além disso, o serviço é usado para criar 1,5 bilhão de imagens por semana.
Ainda de acordo com Fry, o número de consultas que o ChatGPT recebe atualmente equivale a aproximadamente um quinto do volume de buscas que o Google recebe, justamente os 20% mencionados anteriormente.
É uma estatística impressionante, principalmente porque começamos há apenas um ano e meio. É difícil lembrar, mas o ChatGPT, naquela época, não tinha nenhuma informação atualizada. Você fazia uma pergunta e ele respondia com algo como “já passou do meu período de treinamento”, e ninguém fazia ideia do que isso significava.
Adam Fry, líder de produtos para consumidores do ChatGPT
Sim e não. O Google está sob ameaça no sentido de, agora, haver um serviço que realmente consegue concorrer com o seu buscador. Até então, o Bing era a única plataforma que fazia frente às buscas do Google, mas a sua participação de mercado sempre foi pequena.
Por outro lado, há algumas nuances que precisam ser consideradas antes de concluirmos que o “império do Google” chegou ao fim. Começa, como o 9to5Google ressalta, com o fato de a fonte sobre o volume de pesquisas do Google não ter sido revelada.
No cálculo feito pela OpenAI, cada pergunta que aciona uma pesquisa na web é contabilizada como uma ação equivalente a uma busca, mesmo quando ela é feita dentro de uma conversa em andamento. Essa forma de mensuração dá margem para interpretações distintas.
Além disso, não está claro quantos usuários o ChatGPT efetivamente “roubou” do Google. Nesse ponto, precisamos considerar que o Google tem o seu próprio mecanismo de IA, o Gemini, que também pode ter tomado parte do volume de pesquisas de seu buscador — isso não seria uma perda de usuários, mas, digamos, uma transferência.
Para completar, precisamos relembrar que o Google tem o Modo IA ativado em seu buscador há algum tempo. Dependendo de como as métricas são estabelecidas, os volumes de uso de cada um podem ser apresentados juntos ou separadamente.
A única certeza que temos neste momento é a de que o Google, enquanto buscador, nunca teve um concorrente tão forte quanto o ChatGPT. Fry deu a entender que a OpenAI quer mais. Um dos próximos passos consistirá em unificar os modos Chat e Work do serviço, afinal, essa separação é pouco compreendida por muitos usuários.

articles.title: Barracuda ESG Authentication Bypass Flaw Opens Path to Root
articles.text:
Barracuda has released patches for two vulnerabilities that can be chained to gain root access to its Email Security Gateway (ESG) appliances.
The first, tracked as CVE-2026-116606 (CVSS score of 9.3), is an authentication bypass that affects only ESG. The second, CVE-2026-111560 (CVSS score of 8.6), is a command injection issue that also impacts five other Barracuda products.
“An authentication bypass in Barracuda Email Security Gateway versions earlier than 9.4.0.030 allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to invoke a configuration-import function and restore a crafted, compatible backup archive, resulting in unauthorized modification of the appliance’s global configuration,” Mandiant explains in an advisory describing CVE-2026-116606.
The command injection bug sits in the timezone configuration setting, in code shared across several Barracuda products. Mandiant says an attacker logged in with administrator privileges could abuse it to execute OS commands as root.
“If exploited in combination, these vulnerabilities could allow an attacker to bypass authorization controls and obtain root access to the device,” Barracuda says.
In addition to ESG, the command injection flaw affects the Load Balancer Application Delivery Controller (ADC), Message Archiver, WAF Control Center, Web Application Firewall (WAF), and Web Security Gateway (WSG).
According to Barracuda, attackers must be able to reach an appliance’s admin interface to exploit the flaws. The company advises organizations to keep these interfaces reachable only from trusted internal networks.
Barracuda’s advisory marks administrative access as required for both bugs, yet also calls CVE-2026-116606 a pre-authentication issue. Mandiant, which published advisories for both flaws, says the ESG bug can be exploited without authentication.
Customers are advised to update to the newest firmware and confirm that every available patch is installed. Barracuda says any patch not applied automatically should be manually installed, and that devices with automatic patching disabled should have it switched back on.
According to Mandiant, Barracuda reported the command injection on October 15 and the authentication bypass on October 22. Neither advisory says whether the flaws have been exploited in the wild.
ESG appliances were previously targeted by Chinese cyberspies who exploited a zero-day, CVE-2023-2868, starting in October 2022. That campaign led Barracuda to tell customers to replace compromised devices.

articles.title: GTA 6 Will Need Up to 212 GB of Storage, Pre-Load Now Starts November 10
articles.text:
Wednesday, November 4th 2026
GTA 6 Will Need Up to 212 GB of Storage, Pre-Load Now Starts November 10
Rockstar has moved GTA 6's pre-load up by two days. According to an updated Newswire post and support page, digital pre-orders can now start downloading on November 10, instead of the November 12 date announced back in June. The exact timing depends on the console. On PlayStation 5, the pre-load unlocks at midnight local time in the user's respective time zone. Xbox Series X|S gets a single global unlock at 12 a.m. GMT, which works out to 7 PM ET or 4 PM PT on November 9 for players in North America, while the full launch is still set for November 19.
Rockstar also put a number on the file size for the first time, saying the pre-load will need "up to 212 GB of available space depending on your device." That's a touch above the 210 GB figure a dataminer pulled from the PlayStation Store backend last week, but it's safe to say it was an accurate leak. The "depending on your device" bit suggests the PS5 and Xbox builds won't be exactly the same size, though Rockstar didn't share a per-console breakdown. That does mean that on a launch PS5 with roughly 667 GB of usable storage, GTA 6 alone would eat close to a third of the drive.We know that GTA 6 "physical" copies ship with a download code instead of a disc, so physical buyers will be downloading the same files. Those code-in-box editions were slated for November 12, and that date reportedly still stands. A PC version is rumored to be coming in Q1 2027, though Rockstar hasn't announced one yet. Until then, console players looking to jump into Vice City are advised to clear some space before November 10.

articles.title: Warum du deinen ChatGPT-Account niemals teilen solltest – 6 alarmierende Risiken
articles.text:
Account-Sharing bei ChatGPT, Claude und Gemini: Diese 6 Risiken drohen dir
Wer Premium-Features von Chatbots nutzen will, wird zur Kasse gebeten. Für die höchsten Nutzungsraten und umfassendsten Möglichkeiten von ChatGPT, Gemini und Claude musst du dafür sogar teilweise mehrere hundert Euro monatlich ausgeben. Nur wenige User:innen sind wohl bereit, diesen Preis zu bezahlen. Also greifen einige von ihnen, die dennoch nicht auf die Fertigkeiten der Chatbots verzichten können, zu einem Trick.
Sie teilen ihren Zugang mit anderen User:innen. So teilen sich auch die Kosten für die besten Modelle von ChatGPT, Gemini und Claude auf. Was im ersten Moment nach einer tollen Idee klingt, um die Kosten für KI zu reduzieren, kann einige Folgen mit sich bringen. Welche Gefahren durch das Account-Sharing drohen, erfährst du am schnellsten, wenn du das Inhaltsverzeichnis im Artikel nutzt.
Geteilte Logindaten als Sicherheitsrisiko bei ChatGPT und Claude
Wer mit anderen den Account für ChatGPT, Gemini oder Claude teilt, gibt zwangsläufig ein Teil seiner Daten preis. Das beginnt schon damit, dass du E-Mail-Adresse und Passwort anderen Personen verraten musst. Das ist gerade dann ein Problem, wenn du die besagten Daten auch für andere Dienste und Webseiten als Login nutzt. So können alle, die Zugriff auf den KI-Account haben, auch auf andere Konten zugreifen. Sie müssen im Zweifel nicht einmal genau wissen, ob du den Dienst nutzt, sie können den Login einfach mit den Daten ausprobieren.
Selbst wenn du für ChatGPT, Claude und Gemini ein Konto erstellst, das eine separate E-Mail-Adresse samt Passwort bekommt, sind die Probleme nicht restlos beseitigt. Die Adresse kann immer noch von anderen genutzt werden, um dich bei Diensten außerhalb anzumelden. Gerade wenn es sich um dubiose Webseiten wie illegale Filesharing-Dienste handelt, könntest am Ende du Probleme bekommen, statt die Person, die eigentlich Unfug damit getrieben hat.
Account-Sharing gefährdet sensible Daten in Gemini und ChatGPT
Da viele KI-Tools mittlerweile auch Anbindung an externe Dienste bieten, kompromittiert das Account-Sharing nicht nur einen Login. ChatGPT bietet etwa Plugins für Gmail, den Google Kalender, Teams, Slack, Streaming-Dienste wie Apple Music, Portale wie Indeed oder Linkedin oder auch Finanzdienste wie Stripe. Alle verknüpften Accounts können mehr über dich verraten, als dir lieb ist, wenn andere User:innen Informationen von den Tools abfragen.
Das gilt genauso für Zahlungsinformationen, die über die Shopping-Fertigkeiten von ChatGPT und Co. aufgerufen werden können. Die Agentic-Commerce-Tools sind teilweise dazu in der Lage, Einkäufe mit nur wenigen Prompts durchzuführen. Bei ChatGPT heißt diese Fertigkeit „Instant Checkout“ und ist bei kompatiblen Onlineshops verfügbar. Auch hier können andere User:innen entweder die Daten einsehen oder sogar Käufe in deinem Namen abschließen, wenn sie Zugriff auf deinen Account haben.
Prompt-Historie sichtbar für alle Nutzer bei KI-Account-Sharing
Viele Menschen teilen mit Chatbots Informationen, die eigentlich privat bleiben sollten. Das reicht von finanziellen Details über die eigene Gesundheit bis zu KI-Gesprächen über soziale Probleme. Jetzt stell dir vor, dass jemand all diese vermeintlich vertraulichen Chats mit der KI mitlesen kann. Die Person, mit der du den Account teilst, kann das aufgrund der gespeicherten Nachrichten und Chat-Historie problemlos.
Gegenüber dem Wall Street Journal berichteten einige ChatGPT-User:innen, die ihren Account geteilt haben, etwa von den damit einhergehenden Problemen. Student Connor Effrain, der an Morbus Crohn erkrankt ist, teilte sich einen Account mit einer Studienpartnerin. Die KI befragte er regelmäßig darüber, was er bei Magenschmerzen und Verstopfungen tun könnte, um die Auswirkungen der Krankheit zu lindern. Erst später merkte er, dass die Partnerin alles mitlesen und damit ungewollte Einblicke in sein Leben erhaschen konnte. Seitdem hat er einen eigenen Account.
ChatGPT und Claude verlieren Präzision durch geteilte Accounts
Viele Chatbots lernen mit der Zeit, wer mit ihnen schreibt. Je mehr Informationen du der KI fütterst, desto mehr weiß sie über dich und kann diese Informationen in künftige Antworten einbinden. Das macht die Antworten präziser und persönlicher. Das Gegenteil ist der Fall, wenn du dir den Account mit anderen teilst. Dann wissen ChatGPT und Co. nicht mehr ganz genau, mit wem sie es zu tun haben.
Das kann gerade dann ärgerlich sein, wenn du das KI-Tool zum Lernen oder im professionellen Kontext nutzt. Gegenüber dem Wall Street Journal berichtete Olivia Martin, eine Medizinstudentin, dass sie ihren Account mit mindestens sechs anderen User:innen geteilt hat. Sie hat Studienunterlagen und Notizen in die KI hochgeladen, um ChatGPT vorbereitende Fragen für Prüfungen stellen zu lassen. Unter die Fragen mischten sich durch den geteilten Account aber immer häufiger Themenbereiche für Lehramtsstudierende, die sich ebenfalls unter den anderen User:innen befanden.
Xavier Wisniewski, der sein Studium abgeschlossen hatte, berichtet über ähnliche Probleme: „Die KI ist mittlerweile verwirrt davon und denkt, dass ich eine Fusion all meiner Freunde wäre.“ Als er sich für Jobbewerbungen ein Anschreiben formulieren ließ, wurden Erfahrungen, Fertigkeiten und bisherige Arbeitsstellen seiner Account-Mitnutzer:innen für sein Anschreiben verwertet.
Verantwortung für KI-Antworten bei Account-Sharing mit OpenAI und Anthropic
Wenn du einen Chatbot-Account erstellt hast und ihn mit anderen teilst, bist du für sämtliche Inhalte verantwortlich, die darüber erstellt werden. Zwar haben die großen KI-Unternehmen mittlerweile ihre Modelle einigen Restriktionen unterworfen, damit keine schädlichen Inhalte generiert werden.
Doch sollten sich Lücken im System finden und jemand das Ganze über deinen Account ausnutzen, fällt es womöglich auf dich zurück. Das gilt selbst dann, wenn diese Grenzen der KI unabsichtlich überschritten werden. Dementsprechend können auch Personen, denen du uneingeschränkt vertraust, für Probleme mit ihren KI-Generierungen sorgen.
Verstoß gegen Nutzungsbedingungen von OpenAI Google und Anthropic
Zu guter Letzt verstößt das Teilen von Chatbot-Accounts in den meisten Fällen gegen die Richtlinien der verantwortlichen Unternehmen. Natürlich wird das im ersten Moment nur die wenigsten Nutzer:innen abschrecken. Aber du solltest es einmal so sehen: Teilst du dir den Account mit jemandem, sparst du womöglich über mehrere Monate hinweg einen Teil der Abokosten. Fliegt das Sharing aber auf, können OpenAI, Anthropic und Google deinen Account dichtmachen.
Dadurch gehen alle Konversationen, die du mit der KI geführt hast, verloren. Dadurch verlierst du aber nicht nur Daten, sondern im Grunde auch das gesamte Geld, das du bisher in den Account investiert hast. Dementsprechend ist es lohnenswerter, auf einen Einzel-Account zu setzen, statt ein paar Euro sparen zu wollen und ein Risiko einzugehen.
Dieser Artikel wurde ursprünglich am 18.08.2026 veröffentlicht, interessiert jedoch immer noch sehr viele unserer Leser:innen. Deshalb haben wir ihn aktualisiert und hier nochmals zur Verfügung gestellt.

articles.title: Google’s Pixel 11 phones are up to 27 percent off
articles.text:
You can save a heck of lot of money on Google’s Pixel 11 phones through November 8th, whether you want the best-for-the-least Pixel 11, or the slightly pricier Pixel 11 Pro that takes better photos. Even the big Pixel 11 Pro XL with a longer-lasting battery is hundreds off its original price.
Google’s Pixel 11 phones are up to 27 percent off
With prices up to $350 off, it’s a good time to consider upgrading if you’re looking for a great Android phone.
The Pixel 11 Pro deal is the most attractive of the bunch, as the $1,099.99 phone with 256GB storage and 12GB of RAM is down to just $799.99 at Amazon, Best Buy, and at the Google Store, beating its October Prime Day price by $50. It’s $100 less than the base Pixel 11 model sold for at launch, and it’s the phone to get if you want great camera performance, plus extra features like HiLight that, while cool, weren’t really worth paying a premium to access. I’d be very surprised if the price dropped more for Black Friday.
There’s absolutely nothing wrong with opting for the Pixel 11 instead, especially at its attractive $699.99 ($200 off) price that now matches the cost of the iPhone 17E, following Apple’s September price bump. The Pixel 11 is the most affordable phone that supports Google’s software features that are exclusive to this year’s phones, including Magic Capture, Camera Looks, and Proactive Assistance. It has fast 25W wireless charging (up from 15W with the Pixel 10), and has 12GB of RAM, like the Pixel 11 Pro.
I’m still happily rocking my Pixel 9 Pro, but if I were going to upgrade right now, I’d get the Pixel 11 Pro. Yes, I want the better cameras and HiLight. But really, the main reason I’m lured to the Pro is because the trade-in offers are really generous right now. It’s just $10 more to opt for the Pro over the base Pixel 11. My base Pixel 9 Pro with 128GB of storage can fetch $530 in trade-in credit at the Google Store and $525 at Best Buy, which seems great.

articles.title: Texas was the new epicenter of the AI data center buildout. That might be kaput.
articles.text:
Texas was the new epicenter of the AI data center buildout. That might be kaput.
Some of the largest AI infrastructure projects in the world are underway in Texas. A dramatic political shift could slow their construction—and deepen concerns about the economics of the AI boom.
Texas is the fastest-growing data center market in the US and ground zero for Big Tech's largest AI buildouts. But the blue wave that swept the Lone Star State may jeopardize that position.
Democrat James Talarico won the US Senate seat against Ken Paxton. Gina Hinojosa won the race for governor against the Republican incumbent, Greg Abbott. At the state level, Democrats will take control of the Texas House for the first time in 24 years. Talarico and Hinojosa made data centers a central issue, discussing them constantly on the campaign trail.
Even before the polls closed, insiders in the data center industry noticed that the times were changing. At the industry's DCD conference in Ashburn, Virginia, on Tuesday, panelists lamented that Texas had been the easiest place to build for years—until September. That's when Abbott, perhaps seeing the increasingly bipartisan distaste for these facilities, began changing course himself.
Developers said the governor’s office had stopped responding to their emails. On September 21, Abbott directed a key state regulator to halt data center permits. Many panelists at the conference were expecting this to mean that existing projects might be slowed and new ones could be halted altogether.
The governor-elect indeed seems eager to do that. Hinojosa supported tax breaks for data centers in 2023 as a way to boost construction jobs, but during her campaign she began pushing for a full-fledged moratorium.
That would be a problem for the hyperscalers of Big Tech, which have ambitious plans for AI training facilities in the state. The scale of projects already underway in Texas is massive. The Stargate Frontier data center in Shackelford County is projected to serve 1,820 megawatts—about as much as the nation’s largest data center, SpaceX’s Colossus 2 in Tennessee, and more than twice as much as the largest data center currently operating in Texas. Nexus Hubbard, also under construction and intended mostly to serve Anthropic, has a planned size of 6,400 megawatts and is the second-largest data center being built in the US, behind only Meta’s Hyperion project in Louisiana.
The potential for Democrats to order delays to these projects or moratoriums on new ones adds to growing anxiety that the AI buildout could stall. Banks and lenders are already getting pickier about the projects they back. And given the extent to which the data center buildout is underpinning growth in the economy right now, those forces combined could have ripple effects.
Voters around the country, though, were unambiguous in the midterms, sending a similar message on everything from state ballot questions to national offices. Voters supported efforts to protect ratepayers from increases in their electricity bills caused by data centers, and they favored some larger bans on new data centers altogether. If we needed any more convincing that Big Tech has fumbled its effort to sell voters on the idea that AI-powered abundance will make health care better, goods cheaper, and scientific breakthroughs more common, this was it.
A key question is whether the Texas counties with the largest data center presence were part of the reason these Democrats got elected, or if the anti-data-center vote came from elsewhere.
It’s complicated: The counties where much of the data center buildout is happening are around Dallas. Dallas County and others closest to it predictably went blue, but nearby Ellis County, which leads in permitting requests for data centers, went for Greg Abbott and Ken Paxton. Cameron County, near the state’s southern border, is a hot spot for data centers and voted blue in the midterms, which was a shift. But Mitchell County and Scurry County, where a bunch of projects in west Texas are located, went red.
This is a big deal, because no single office in the state decides whether a project goes ahead or is halted. Decisions often reflect an interplay between city governments, county officials, and state offices.
Local officials who have some say over data center development may resist sweeping restrictions from the state. And Democrats pushing for a moratorium might also face pushback from the construction unions that supported some of their campaigns. So while the blue wave spells a death knell for Texas data centers in theory, election winners may find that following through on their opposition once in office is much more complicated than campaigning on it.

articles.title: AliExpress calienta motores para el 11/11: recompensas por comprar, entrega al día siguiente y los mejores descuentos del año
articles.text:
Es la gran cita del año para todas las personas que buscan comprar al mejor precio y poder adelantar las compras de Navidad. El 11/11 ha ganado mucha popularidad en España, superando incluso a otras citas comerciales como el Black Friday o las rebajas de enero. Y dentro de los ecommerce que más han hecho por popularizar el 11/11, o día del soltero, es AliExpress, donde vemos descuentos que superan el 50% en precios ya de por sí bajos. Además, este año AliExpress ha lanzado cosas nuevas como un programa de recompensas para sus clientes, un servicio de entrega al día siguiente en cinco ciudades españolas y una oferta increíble en un robot aspirador, que puede ser tuyo por poco más de 100 euros.
El periodo de calentamiento del 11/11 comienza el 29 de octubre por lo que a partir de esos días ya podrás ir viendo bastantes descuentos en la web de AliExpress. Estas promociones afectan a todas las categorías de producto, desde tecnología a otras como moda, deporte, automoción o juguetes. Por eso te animamos a que visites la web de AliExpress asiduamente, selecciones los productos que te interesan y compruebes si ya tienen aplicados el descuento que te haga la compra más económica.
Novedades más allá de los descuentos: programa Elite
Este año, el 11/11 de AliExpress estrena novedades. Una de ellas es el programa Elite que genera una especie de recompensa a los compradores, ofreciendo ventajas exclusivas en función del historial de compra.
De esta manera, los miembros de Elite tienen acceso directo desde la aplicación de AliExpress a precios exclusivos, sin tener que introducir los famosos códigos promocionales. Además, sólo por ser miembro del programa Elite, existe un 5% adicional (que puede llegar al 8% en el Elite Day el primer día de cada mes) en millones de productos, incluidos los de los canales Choice, Local+ y Marcas+.
Pero esto no acaba aquí. Los miembros del programa Elite también tienen otras ventajas, más allá de los precios rebajados. Algunos de ellos son; proceso de devolución mucho más sencillo, mayor protección relacionada con los plazos de entrega, atención al cliente personalizada 24/7 y acceso prioritario a los agentes.
El lanzamiento de Elite coincide con la campaña del 11.11, que transcurrirá del 1 al 18 de noviembre.
Next Day Delivery
AliExpress lleva años alejada de la fama de tardar mucho en los envíos. De hecho, la mayoría de productos se entregan en la misma semana. Ahora va un paso más allá con Next Day Delivery donde un elevado número de compradores podrá tener en su domicilio al día siguiente una gran variedad de productos.
Si nos fijamos en la mayoría de comercios online, estos tiempos de entrega de tan sólo 24 horas sólo se llevan a cabo en las dos principales ciudades españolas: Madrid y Barcelona. Pero AliExpress ha ido más allá y garantiza los mismos plazos en otras tres ciudades más: Valencia, Sevilla y Murcia.
AliExpress está decidida a reducir los tiempos en envío en toda la península para que la experiencia de compra no sea perfecta únicamente mientras usamos la aplicación o la web, sino también con una entrega más rápida, eficiente y cómoda para todos los consumidores.
Un robot aspirador por poco más de cien euros
Entre todas las grandes ofertas que podremos ver en AliExpress del 1 al 18 de noviembre, quizá una de las más interesantes sea las que aplican a la marca ILIFE, especializada en limpieza del hogar. El producto más recomendable es un robot aspirador, y que también pasa la mopa, que lejos de costar los más de 500 euros de otros modelos de la competencia, este cuesta sólo 118 euros. Para todo lo que tiene y hace, es una auténtica locura un precio tan bajo.
El robot ILIFE A30 además de aspirar y pasar la mopa para dejar la casa limpia, también tiene una estación de autovaciado automático. De esta manera, cuando el robot acabe de limpiar, puede vaciar el depósito y limpiar las mopas y quedar listo para la siguiente tarea, sin apenas intervención humana.
También cuenta con un sistema de navegación láser con una gran precisión, capaz de esquivar cualquier tipo de objeto. En cuanto al aspirado, tiene una potencia de succión de 5.000 Pa y una autonomía que llega hasta los 180 minutos, algo poco habitual en el sector y mucho menos teniendo en cuenta su precio. Por último, también se puede controlar con la aplicación desde el teléfono para programar las veces que queramos que salga a limpiar o la habitación concreta.
Su precio habitual ya es bajísimo, de 140 euros, pero es que ahora, durante la promoción del 11/11, se queda en tan sólo 118 euros.
Todo apunta a que este 11/11 será uno de los más ambiciosos de AliExpress por lo que si estabas esperando al mejor momento para comprar eso que llevas tiempo queriendo, es ahora.

articles.text:
How to validate sites before commitment, protect capacity after deployment, and plan for long-term performance.
Sovereign AI raises the stakes on every infrastructure decision. When data residency, operational control, and compliance requirements limit where workloads can run, there’s far less room for error. A site that looks viable on paper can become a costly problem if cooling, airflow, or resiliency assumptions don’t hold up under real operating conditions.

In one case, a data hall appeared sound in review, but once leakage and a cooling failure were modeled, more than half the cabinets ran too hot. The design itself hadn’t changed, only the assumptions behind it. Inside, you’ll see how teams can uncover issues like these early, before they turn into expensive constraints.

articles.title: How Kenya’s PayServe is building the operating layer for managed real estate - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
Kenyan prop-tech and fintech startup PayServe is raising a US$1 million Series A round as it scales a platform that automates billing, payments and reconciliation for the country’s fast-growing managed estates.
Founded in 2024, PayServe provides revenue assurance for managed real estate, handling billing for rent, service charge and utilities across gated communities, large apartment estates and mixed-use developments.
“Our platform reads consumption straight from our smart water and power meters, collects payments through M-Pesa and direct bank integrations with Absa, Co-op Bank, NCBA, Equity and KCB, and reconciles them automatically,” founder and CEO Steve Butler told Disrupt Africa. “It then posts everything to the client’s accounting system, such as SAP, Zoho or QuickBooks, with KRA eTIMS compliance built in.”
Around that core, the startup offers modules for visitor and access control, maintenance, procurement, unit handover, bookings, and a portal for residents and homeowners. Its customers are property developers, facility and property management companies, owners’ associations and community water schemes.
“Put simply, PayServe is the operating layer of managed real estate,” said Butler, who has spent more than 20 years working across fintech, banking, FMCG, real estate and development. He said PayServe was built in response to a structural shift in the Kenyan property market.
“Kenyan real estate has moved from standalone rentals to large managed developments: gated communities, apartment estates of 1,000 or more units, and mixed-use developments. Each one bills rents, service charge, water, power and security to hundreds of households,” he said.
“Yet most still run on spreadsheets, manual meter readings and M-Pesa statements reconciled by hand. That leads to disputed bills, revenue leakage, especially on service charge and water, late payments, and homeowners and residents who don’t trust the numbers.”
The startup sees its competition falling into three groups – rent-collection apps mostly built for landlords with tens of units, meter vendors who sell hardware but not the billing behind it, and global suites such as Yardi.
“Those global suites are expensive and not built for M-Pesa or eTIMS,” Butler said. “We combine software, metering, payments and accounting in one system built for estate-scale operations in Kenya.”
PayServe has been entirely founder-funded to date, but is now raising a US$1 million Series A.
“We’re raising to scale sales, deepen the product and expand regionally,” Butler said.
The startup has already built a sizeable footprint. It now bills more than 10,000 units across over 50 properties, has deployed 3,000 smart meters, and has processed KES1 billion (US$7.7 million) through the platform since inception.
“Flagship deployments include Northlands Heights, with over 1,000 units and more than 1,000 smart water meters, and Mwalimu Kisaju, with 840 units and 1,600 smart meters, plus JJ Tower, Altura, Volaire, Escada and others,” Butler said.
Other milestones include a live KRA eTIMS integration and direct integrations with Safaricom’s Daraja API and five major banks, with PesaLink next on the list.
“Our pipeline now extends into serviced apartments, mixed-use developments and community water projects,” he said.
PayServe makes money through three revenue streams – a monthly software-as-a-service (SaaS) platform fee per unit, smart water and power meters sold outright or leased, and implementation, integration and support services.
“For developers who don’t want upfront costs, we offer a zero-upfront model,” Butler said. “We deploy and operate the system and recover our costs through a revenue share over an agreed period.”
The journey so far has not been without its challenges.
“Sales cycles are long. Decisions involve developers, management companies and often owners’ committees,” Butler said. “And hardware is hard. Site readiness, plumbing and legacy meters from other vendors all affect timelines.”
Onboarding brings its own problems, with inherited billing records usually needing cleanup before go-live.
“Every client has a different bank, accounting system and tax setup, so each integration is its own project,” he said.
PayServe currently operates in Kenya, with clients in Nairobi, Eldoret and Mombasa, but has its sights set further afield.
“The near-term focus is expanding to regional markets like Uganda, Ethiopia and Congo, where the managed-estate market is growing fast, once the Kenya playbook is proven,” Butler said.

articles.title: La identidad del Cliente de 'VisionQuest', revelada: quién es y cómo afecta al futuro de Marvel
articles.text:
ATENCIÓN: El artículo contiene SPOILERS de VisionQuest 1x07.
Marvel ha revelado oficialmente la identidad del Cliente, el misterioso villano de VisionQuest. El séptimo y penúltimo episodio de la serie acaba de estrenarse en Disney+ y, con él, el título ha respondido al fin a su mayor incertidumbre. Quién se ocultaba bajo la máscara del Cliente, la persona que contrató al Paladín y tantos otros mercenarios para tratar de hacerse con Visión.
Los rumores y teorías sobre quién sería este personaje llevaban semanas circulando por las redes. Se hablaba de Mefisto, de la Bruja Escarlata, de Sharon Carter, de S.W.O.R.D. Pero resulta que ninguna de esas teorías ha dado en la diana. De hecho, es muy probable que ni un solo espectador haya acertado con la identidad real del Cliente de VisionQuest.
En los compases finales del capítulo, la misteriosa figura por fin hace acto de presencia. A lo largo del capítulo se nos descubre que la Dra. Jo Carrington, antes de morir, tuvo un romance con un hombre con la apariencia humana de Ultrón. Es decir, la del actor James Spader.
En la última escena, con Visión en la finca de Phineas Horton, el padre la robótica (y de quien resulta que él toma su apariencia), los mercenarios rodean al protagonista. Y del interior de la casa aparece al fin el Cliente de VisionQuest. Se trata de ese antiguo amante de Jocasta.
Quién es el Cliente de VisionQuest
Por ahora, no sabemos exactamente quién es esta persona. Ni siquiera sabemos su nombre. Solo sabemos que es el humano del que Ultrón tomó su apariencia y que mantuvo una relación con la Dra. Carrington. A buen seguro, en el octavo y último capítulo de la serie se nos desvelarán sus intenciones y, seguramente, más detalles sobre su pasado.
"Es curioso, la gente dice que es por una cuestión de presupuesto, pero no es así, es por James Spader. Me encanta James Spader. ¿A quién no le encanta James Spader? Solo quiero ver a James y quiero ver a Bettany", comentaba hace unas semanas el showrunner de la serie, Terry Matalas, sobre el por qué de usar la apariencia humana de Ultrón y de Visión en lugar de sus versiones robóticas. Ahora, estas palabras han tomado un nuevo significado.
Date de alta en Disney+ ahora y ahorra gracias a la suscripción anual, con la que podrás disfrutar de todo su catálogo de series y películas. Acceso a los últimos estrenos, al catálogo de Star y ESPN* y a los mejores documentales de National Geographic.
*ESPN solo está disponible en Latinoamérica. Ahorro respecto a 12 meses de suscripción mensual.
"Trabajar con James Spader es una auténtica delicia. Es como disfrutar de la mejor comida que te hayas tomado en tu vida, es sencillamente delicioso. Es muy divertido, muy irreverente, y tiene ese aire que intimida bastante. Pero en el fondo es realmente atento, amable y cariñoso. Solo hay que esforzarse un poco para llegar a conocerlo, y ahora es uno de mis mejores amigos y espero que lo siga siendo el resto de mi vida. Lo adoro", nos contaba precisamente Paul Bettany en una entrevista concedida a Hipertextual.
El último episodio de VisionQuest se estrena en Disney+ el miércoles 11 de noviembre en España, la noche del martes 10 en EE. UU. y América Latina.

articles.title: Startup news and updates: daily roundup (November 4, 2026)
articles.text:
Startup news and updates: daily roundup (November 4, 2026)
YourStory presents the daily news roundup from the Indian startup ecosystem and beyond. Here’s the roundup for Wednesday, November 4, 2026.
From Canva job cuts affecting over 1,200 employees to EloElo Group raising $80 million, YourStory brings you today’s headlines with the latest developments across sectors.
Latest news
Canva job cuts affect over 1,200 employees as it restructures for AI era
Canva is undertaking a major workforce restructuring affecting 1,271 employees, or 22% of its workforce, as it reorganises its business to adapt to rapid technological change.
The changes include redundancies, role changes and relocation requests, although the company has not disclosed how many employees will leave.
Chief executive officer Melanie Perkins said the restructuring followed the company’s first slowdown in growth in a decade and reflected the need to rethink how it operates and organises its teams.
Funding news
EloElo Group raises $80M in Series C led by Hornbill Capital and NBCUniversal
EloElo Group, a consumer AI and entertainment company that operates micro-drama platform Story TV, has raised $80 million in a Series C round of funding led by Hornbill Capital and NBCUniversal.
This funding round also saw participation from MIT Investment Co. and existing investors Play Ventures, Kalaari Capital, Waterbridge Ventures, Griffin Gaming Partners and others.
Peppermint Robotics bags Rs 100 Cr in pre-Series B funding round
Peppermint Robotics, which makes autonomous cleaning robots, has raised Rs 100 crore (about $10.5 million) in a pre-Series B round led by pi Ventures and Crane Venture Partners. Asiana Fund also participated in the round.
The round involved fresh capital and secondary share transactions. The money arrives on the back of rapid growth by Peppermint.
The Pune- and Austin-based startup said it doubled its revenue last year and grew nearly sixfold between FY24 and FY26. It last raised Rs 34 crore ($4 million) in a Series A round in April 2025. Peppermint has a presence in nine countries, with the US being its biggest market.
Enrission India Capital joins Ottonomy’s Rs 40.6 Cr post-seed funding round
Japan-based investor Enrission India Capital has participated in Ottonomy’s Rs 40.6 crore ($4.2 million) post-seed funding round. Ottonomy develops AI-powered autonomous delivery robots capable of operating indoors and outdoors. Its flagship product, Ottobot, uses proprietary Contextual AI to automate the movement of medicines, equipment and supplies across hospitals and industrial facilities.
The technology aims to reduce routine logistics workloads amid growing labour shortages, allowing skilled employees to focus on higher-value tasks. The investment will support Ottonomy’s global expansion across healthcare and industrial automation. Enrission India Capital said the investment reflects its focus on deep-tech companies addressing practical business challenges.
OneStack raises Rs 12.5 Cr as cooperative banks go live directly on NPCI’s UPI network
Fintech infrastructure company OneStack has raised Rs 12.5 crore from new investor Shepherd’s Hill and existing backers Pentathlon Ventures and AVNM Ventures. The funding will support expansion across cooperative banks and NBFCs, alongside product development in payments, core banking and regulatory compliance.
OneStack has enabled cooperative banks to operate directly on NPCI’s UPI network as both issuers and acquirers under their own bank handles. This allows banks to issue UPI IDs, onboard merchants, manage transaction data and retain payment-related revenue.
The company has raised over Rs 45 crore across four rounds and currently serves more than 200 banks. Its expansion plans include leveraging partnerships covering over 250 cooperative banks and its onboarding as a technology provider on Sahakar Sarathi.
Other news
Decentro launches static and dynamic QR Soundboxes for merchant payment confirmations
Decentro has launched two Soundbox devices to provide instant spoken payment confirmations to merchants. The range includes a Static QR Soundbox and a Dynamic QR Soundbox with a display, keypad and NFC. The static model supports 4G, 2G and optional Wi-Fi, with alerts in English, Hindi and regional languages.
The dynamic model generates transaction-specific QR codes and supports contactless card payments through RuPay, Visa and Mastercard, with card functionality expected to go live in around two months. Both devices are available for purchase or rental through banks, fintechs and other platforms. Decentro currently has over 5,000 offline UPI QR codes deployed and targets one million Soundboxes by the end of 2028.
Four UK universities in India open postgraduate recruitment to employers through placement week
Four UK universities with campuses in India will offer employers early access to more than 250 postgraduate students graduating in 2027 through an invitation-only UK Universities Placement Week scheduled for late November 2026. Convened by Emeritus, the initiative brings together the University of Bristol Mumbai Enterprise Campus, University of York Mumbai, University of Liverpool Bengaluru and University of Aberdeen Mumbai.
The students represent disciplines including finance, technology, artificial intelligence, management and creative industries. Their profiles include fresh graduates and professionals with an average of 2.4 to 3 years of prior work experience across banking, IT, consulting, finance, marketing, analytics and media. Students also gain practical experience through live projects and industry tools, including AI applications in finance, business analysis and operations.
(This article will be updated with the latest news throughout the day.)

articles.title: ChatGPT atteint déjà 20 % du volume de recherche de Google, selon OpenAI
articles.text:
OpenAI est formel : ChatGPT traite désormais l'équivalent de 20 % des requêtes de Google. Un chiffre impressionnant qui mérite toutefois d'être tempéré.
Pas de repos pour les braves ! OpenAI vient d'ouvrir ses portes à Bouygues Telecom et permet désormais aux utilisateurs de se renseigner sur les offres de l'opérateur au sein de ChatGPT. Dans le même temps, la firme a annoncé la fermeture prochaine de l'application de bureau ChatGPT Classic. Le prochain gros chantier ? Concurrencer Google sur son terrain de prédilection.
ChatGPT à l'assaut de Google avec 20 % de son volume de recherche
Adam Fry, responsable produit grand public chez OpenAI, a lâché une véritable bombe lors d'un récent évènement presse : le volume de requêtes sur ChatGPT représenterait aujourd'hui « un cinquième » de celui de Google. Le chiffre impressionne d'autant plus que la recherche n'est accessible via le chatbot que depuis 2 ans. À titre de comparaison, Bing, dont le lancement date tout de même de 2009, plafonnait autour de 3 % de parts de marché en 2023.
Face à ce qu'il perçoit comme une menace extrêmement sérieuse, Google a pris les devants : le géant de Mountain View distribue de moins en moins de clics aux sites tiers et mise de plus en plus sur les outils génératifs, le mode IA et AI Overviews en tête. Mais ces efforts coûtent cher et le retour sur investissement est, pour l'instant, plutôt faible : en répondant directement aux questions de l'utilisateur, l'IA limite, en effet, le recours au moteur de recherche et l'exposition aux liens sponsorisés.
- Chat dans différentes langues, dont le français
- Générer, traduire et obtenir un résumé de texte
- Générer, optimiser et corriger du code
Un chiffre à prendre avec des pincettes
Prenons le temps de lire entre les lignes. Pour OpenAI, une recherche, c'est avant tout une question qui envoie ChatGPT fouiller le web. Comme l'explique Adam Fry, « chaque fois que vous posez une question et que vous effectuez une recherche sur le Web, il s'agit d'une recherche. ». Du côté de Google, en revanche, la méthodologie utilisée pour calculer le volume de recherche n'a pas été précisée. Difficile, dans ces conditions, de faire une comparaison pertinente.
Au delà de cette course aux volumes, l'enjeu est, on le devine, majoritairement économique. En pleine préparation de son entrée en Bourse, OpenAI cherche plus que jamais à améliorer sa rentabilité. La firme mise d'ailleurs depuis peu sur la pub pour booster son chiffre d'affaires. Contre toute attente, ces annonces ne semblent pas avoir fait fuir les utilisateurs : « les publicités nous ont peut-être montré que nous pourrions aller encore plus loin, en réalité », explique Adam Fry.
Cette stratégie sera-t-elle suffisante pour damer le pion à Google ? Rien n'est moins sûr : avec son avance confortable et des années d'expérience, le géant a encore de la marge.

articles.title: US charges two Canadians accused of hacking US universities
articles.text:
A federal grand jury indicted two Canadians suspected of hacking multiple US universities and using the compromised systems to mine for cryptocurrency.
35-year-old Ryan James Roach and 41-year-old Mathiew James Stubbings now face a maximum penalty of 10 years in prison and a $250,000 fine each if found guilty of conspiracy to obtain information from a protected computer and to cause damage to a protected computer, obtaining information from a protected computer, and intentionally damaging a protected computer.
According to court documents, the two accomplices used virtual private servers in multiple countries (registered under fake names) between June 2016 and December 2019 to infect systems on the networks of multiple unnamed educational institutions in New York, Tennessee, North Carolina, and Massachusetts with malware.
"These servers transmitted malware and mining software to victim computers and stored stolen login credentials," the Department of Justice (DOJ) said.
Once inside the victims' networks, Roach and Stubbings allegedly stole data and login credentials, deployed crypto-mining malware, and, in some cases, used compromised systems for vulnerability research after gaining access to supercomputers on the victims' networks.
"Roach and Stubbings targeted educational institutions in the United States that had supercomputers and researched security vulnerabilities in the victim computer networks, using a variety of methods to gain access, including using a server and compromised computers from another victim to conceal their identities," the DOJ added,
"Once inside a network, Roach and Stubbings used sophisticated techniques and tools to conduct reconnaissance and expand their access within the network."
According to prosecutors, the two defendants also damaged at least 10 computers over one year, causing losses of at least $5,000.
Roach was extradited from Canada to the United States on October 28 and was arraigned before a detention hearing on November 3. Stubbings will also be arraigned after his extradition from Canada.
Multiple US universities have been breached over the last year, including Ivy League schools Harvard University, Princeton University, and the University of Pennsylvania. All disclosed data breaches in November 2025, confirming that attackers accessed donors' information and other sensitive data.

articles.title: Switch Al-Maghrib on building domestic payment plumbing
articles.text:
While venture capital chased consumer apps, the real battle for Africa’s digital economy moved behind the scenes. In an in-depth conversation, the Managing Director of Morocco’s Switch Al-Maghrib, Hanae Ben Driss, argues that national fragmentation is a prerequisite for sovereignty, explains why wallets trump cards for cross-border scale, and reveals plans for an association of African national switches.
Across the African continent, venture capital decks and tech keynotes have long championed the front-end revolution: sleek mobile banking interfaces, consumer lending apps, and digital storefronts.
Yet behind this veneer of consumer convenience lies a persistent, frustrating structural reality. A traveller flying from Lagos to Luanda finds their international payment cards repeatedly declined when paying for basic transit visas; transferring funds between two neighbouring North and West African jurisdictions remains an expensive, multi-day ordeal involving intermediary offshore clearing banks; and domestic retail commerce remains stubbornly tethered to physical banknotes.
For the architects of the continent’s underlying financial plumbing, the obsession with consumer-facing software has obscured the foundational work required to move money.
Few operators understand this friction better than the leadership of Switch Al-Maghrib, Morocco’s national payment switch.
Operating quietly within the engine room of North African finance for nearly three decades, the institution sits at the nexus of commercial banks, non-bank financial institutions, and the central bank.
“Our position at Switch Al-Maghrib is interesting because we usually work behind the scenes,” Hanae Ben Driss, the Managing Director of Switch Al-Maghrib, Morocco’s national payment switch, explains. “We are part of the less visible but very important components of the value chain. We are infrastructure providers, and we are not client-facing or involved in business-to-consumer activities. However, our work is essential to making the entire ecosystem function.”
With nearly three decades in the industry, the Switch Al-Maghrib chief offers an unconventional perspective on what development institutions routinely lament as Africa’s payment “fragmentation”: the existence of separate national payment rails is not a policy failure but the vital first step towards continental sovereignty.
Speaking on the sidelines of continental industry deliberations, Hanae Ben Driss offered a fundamental reframing of the debate: what global observers dismiss as inefficient market fragmentation is, in reality, the necessary first chapter of African financial sovereignty.
The case for domestic sovereignty
In development circles and policy conferences, Africa’s distinct national switches and regulatory silos are frequently viewed as obstacles to the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA). Switch Al-Maghrib’s leadership challenges that framing directly.
“You used the word fragmentation, but I may change your perspective on that,” she says. “Fragmentation can actually be the first step towards building things locally, which we subsequently need to make interoperable. If you do not have local infrastructure in the first place, there is nothing to make it interoperable.”
The argument for local infrastructure is rooted in political and financial self-determination. Without national ownership of core switches, countries remain exposed to external shocks and the strategic whims of offshore multinational schemes.
“Every country needs to have sovereign control over its critical infrastructure,” she insists. “These are the foundations upon which we are building the digital economy and payment systems. We should not simply be dependent on an international actor whose objectives may not necessarily align with national priorities. For me, sovereignty is not negotiable.”
Crucially, sovereignty does not require every African state to code every system from scratch or manufacture proprietary hardware. “Sovereignty does not necessarily mean that every country must independently develop every component of its infrastructure,” she notes. “What matters is that each country retains control over the evolution and management of its systems.”
She is equally clear that Africa cannot simply carbon-copy the European Union’s model of top-down integration.
“Africa is not Europe or the United States. We do not have the same political framework for achieving that kind of integration,” she notes. “We can take a different approach. We can build these infrastructures country by country and subsequently agree on how to connect them. That is another way of building an interconnected system.”
Morocco pioneered this model more than two decades ago. Long before the current fintech boom, Moroccan commercial banks joined forces to build a unified domestic interbank switch, which Ben Driss said went live around 2005.
“One of the earliest initiatives was to ensure that domestic transactions could be processed locally,” she recalls. “What this means is that when a domestic transaction takes place, where both the cardholder and the merchant are located in Morocco, the transaction no longer needs to go through international schemes outside Morocco. Even when the payment card carries the logo of an international brand, the domestic transaction can be processed locally. That was an important first step towards achieving greater sovereignty.”
An association of African national switches
While domestic sovereignty has taken root in markets like Morocco, Nigeria, Ghana, Rwanda, and Angola, cross-border interoperability remains painfully slow. Multilateral platforms like the Pan-African Payment and Settlement System (PAPSS) and PAPSSCARD have established a high-level regulatory framework, but Switch Al-Maghrib believes technical operators must now take the initiative.
To accelerate that reality, Switch Al-Maghrib said it is working to forge direct operational ties with its peers across the continent, with an eye toward creating a formal continental coalition.
“We are already in contact with our counterparts in different African countries, particularly national switches,” she reveals. “We have relationships with the national switches in Nigeria, Ghana, Rwanda and other markets across the continent. We are progressively building relationships with these institutions, and there is a shared vision of establishing an association of African national switches.”
The aim of the association is practical, not bureaucratic: to establish technical interoperability between domestic rails without waiting decades for political treaties to harmonise.
“The objective is to create a framework through which we can collaborate and focus on connecting payment infrastructures,” she says. “This does not necessarily mean establishing a continental political or regulatory framework similar to the European Union. Rather, it means creating an effective mechanism for connecting our payment systems.”
Having a unified institutional voice has also become urgent as global technology races ahead. With the rise of artificial intelligence and agentic commerce—where autonomous software agents execute transactions on users’ behalf—isolated African markets risk becoming irrelevant if they remain fragmented.
“Even Europe is struggling to establish sufficient technological independence to compete with the United States and China, which are driving developments in artificial intelligence,” she warns.
“For Africa, therefore, it is important that we come together… Otherwise, it will become increasingly difficult to develop viable solutions at the national level, let alone across the continent.”
Why wallets beat cards for cross-border scale
When exploring how to connect national switches, the disparity between card networks and mobile wallets becomes immediately apparent.
Traditional payment cards remain constrained by the rigid rules, clearing hubs, and interchange fees of multinational networks like Visa and Mastercard.
“Even if we decide tomorrow to connect our international clearing national switch, we cannot simply make every Visa or Mastercard cross-border payment across continents remain so difficult despite decades of conferences and commitments, the boss of Switch Al-Maghrib and strategies.”
Digital mobile wallets, however, present a far more agile route for intra-African commerce.
“Wallets present a different opportunity,” she explains. “If we decide to connect the Nigerian wallet ecosystem with the Moroccan wallet ecosystem, we have greater autonomy to establish that connection because we are not necessarily dealing with an international card scheme. That gives us an opportunity to develop our own interconnected payment arrangements.”
By linking digital wallets directly across national borders, African switches can enable instant, account-to-account payments that bypass international clearing rails altogether.
“Technology is only 20% of the equation”
When asked why cross-border payments across continents remain so difficult despite decades of conferences and commitments, the boss of Switch Al-Maghrib dismisses the idea of a technical barrier.
“I would definitely not say it is technological,” she asserts. “Technology represents only about 20 per cent of the equation in initiatives of this nature.”
Nor does she view political resistance as the primary bottleneck. Instead, the real challenge lies in the complex, resource-intensive work of regulatory execution while managing domestic structural hurdles.
“Every country has its own domestic priorities and challenges,” she explains. “Whether you are talking about Morocco, Nigeria or Angola, the situation is similar. The measurement of financial inclusion and cash is still very dominant. Countries are dealing with these domestic challenges while also trying to find the time and resources to establish cross-border connections.”
Rather than waiting for central banks to design technical frameworks, she argues that switch operators must be proactive.
“Regulators are not necessarily technology experts, and that is understandable,” she says. “When you are dealing with technological infrastructure, regulation alone is not sufficient. I believe we should not simply wait for regulators to take the initiative… we, as infrastructure providers, manage the technological systems and should take the initiative to make proposals to regulators. We have the flexibility and agility to move faster.”
Beyond vanity bank accounts
This pragmatic approach extends to how financial inclusion is measured. While policymakers frequently point to the number of newly opened bank accounts as evidence of progress, she argues that account metrics are superficial.
“For me, financial inclusion goes beyond the number of bank accounts,” she says. “It is about having access to a digital financial record through which institutions can access your risk profile when you need a loan. Whether that record comes from a traditional bank account, a payment account, or a digital wallet does not necessarily matter.”
True inclusion, she argues, is about economic resilience and poverty alleviation. “I strongly believe that financial inclusion helps combat poverty. When people have a financial track record, they can access loans and credit under more favourable conditions.
“Can we establish whether you have savings? Do you regularly pay your bills? Do you have a consistent financial record? These are the indicators that help an institution determine whether you are reliable enough to access credit. The objective of financial inclusion is to make people’s lives better and make them less vulnerable.”
The biggest barrier to creating that digital record remains the dominance of cash in the informal economy, where traders routinely demand physical notes over digital transfers.
She points out that this reluctance is deeply tied to fiscal trust and the social contract: “It is also connected to taxation. If I accept a digital transfer, I become visible within the financial system. My revenues can be tracked, and I may have to declare my income and pay taxes. But what am I getting in return for paying those taxes? Am I receiving quality education, healthcare and other public services? These issues are interconnected. We cannot look at payments in isolation.”
Because cash provides immediate certainty and fee-free liquidity, digital alternatives must offer compelling benefits in safety and merchant convenience to compete.
“We cannot simply expect merchants to change their behaviour,” she notes. “It is our responsibility, as payment infrastructure providers, to innovate and make digital payments more attractive.”
To build that trust, Switch Al-Maghrib said it has integrated artificial intelligence directly into its national routing engine to provide real-time, ecosystem-wide fraud scoring, democratising high-end cyber defence for every connected institution.
“One of the advantages of having this capability at the national switch level is that we can share the cost across the ecosystem,” she explains.
“Rather than every individual institution having to develop the same capabilities independently, we can provide a centralised service. For every transaction passing through the switch, whether it originates from a bank or a mobile money institution, we can assess the risk in real time. This allows us to strengthen the security of the entire payment ecosystem.”
For Africa’s payment landscape, the message from Driss is clear: integration will not descend from a single continental decree, nor will it be solved by front-end apps alone. It will be achieved by sovereign domestic switches that build local resilience, take ownership of their rails, and forge direct, pragmatic alliances across borders.
“One of the beautiful things about Africa is that we are a community,” she reflects. “When I talk about national switches in Nigeria, Angola, Ghana and Rwanda, I am talking about institutions that share similar challenges. We are essentially dealing with the same problems… There is a lot we can learn from one another through benchmarking and sharing experiences.”

articles.title: Hay tantos mapaches sueltos por Alemania que alguien ha tenido una idea radical: empezar a comérselos
articles.text:
En 1934, en los bosques que rodean el lago Edersee, alguien soltó dos parejas de mapaches. No eran buenos tiempos para Alemania, pero mejorar la 'oferta' de los cotos del país, parecía una buena idea.
Spoiler: no lo era.
Sobre todo, porque no estaban solos. Once años después, 25 mapaches escaparon de una granja peletera en la provincia de Brandeburgo. De esos 29 mapaches descienden los casi dos millones de mapaches que hoy viven en el país. Se han convertido en una auténtica plaga, pero ahora algunos alemanes han tenido una idea: comérselos.
¿Comérselos? Efectivamente. En 2025, Steffen Haaßengier, el cocinero del Zum Lindeneck de Weimar, puso el mapache en carta de forma fija: la hamburguesa a 17,50 euros y la pierna con Klöße a 25-30. Un cazador le entrega hasta 20 animales al mes, ya desollados y con el certificado de triquina.
Puede parecer una excentricidad, pero no lo es. El 18 de abril de 2026 el restaurante celebró el que probablemente fue el primer curso alemán dedicado solo a esta carne: hubo unas 70 solicitudes para 20 plazas.
Suena bien, sí. Pero no hace falta decir que un plato no es un plan de control.
El problema en perspectiva. Por poner todas las cifras encima de la mesa, en el año cinegético que fue de abril de 2024 a marzo de 2025, la Federación Alemana de Caza (DJV) registró 284.220 mapaches muertos, entre capturados y abatidos. Es un récord histórico y, aun así, la población no ha bajado.
Y eso sí es inquietante. Porque 284.220 son, aproximadamente, un 16% de la población de mapaches de Alemania. Si la población no está cayendo, es que se repone a un ritmo igual o superior.
Pero... ¡eso es mucha comida! Bueno, no tanto. Según el carnicero de Sajonia-Anhalt Michael Reiß, de cada animal salen entre 1,5 y 2,5 kilos, con más de 25 euros de costes fijos: casi 14 de análisis de triquina, las tasas de inspección y 10 para el cazador. Eso deja el kilo por encima de 10 a 17 euros.
E incluso en el caso de que consiguiéramos usarla, serían apenas 570 toneladas de carne. Solo en cangrejo rojo, Andalucía captura cinco veces más al año.
Sin embargo, la idea es algo distinta. Haaßengier, que es vegetariano en su vida privada, lo planteaba como una forma de aprovechar lo que hay que cazar sí o sí para controlar la población.
Pero la propuesta va un poco más allá: hay muchas especies que son un problema (el mapache, el coipú, el ganso del Nilo y la barnacla canadiense ya se consumen en Alemania y figuran en el Catálogo Español de Especies Exóticas Invasoras), pero no tienen gran espacio entre la opinión pública. Quizás meterlos en nuestros platos sea la manera de romper con eso.

articles.title: Apple says it won't merge macOS and iPadOS, despite years of making them increasingly similar
articles.text:
The takeaway: MacBooks and iPads now use the same chips, extremely similar user interfaces, and the same input devices. Despite their growing similarities over the past several years, Apple refuses to fully merge the two product lines, even as other manufacturers have long since embraced 2-in-1s. That said, recent product launches suggest the Cupertino giant is adopting more trends than it creates.
Apple CEO John Ternus recently stated that the company still has no plans to combine iPadOS and macOS into a single operating system. The operating systems have grown increasingly similar in recent years, but keeping them separate likely helps fatten the company's profits.
The comments came in response to a question during the company's fourth-quarter 2026 earnings call about whether merging Apple's tablet and laptop OSs might reduce costs. Ternus said that while the company remains proud of MacBooks and iPads, it has no plans to fundamentally alter them and would not reveal such plans early.
Ternus' statement echoes comments Apple made last year, after iPadOS 26 introduced Mac-like window and multitasking controls. Craig Federighi, senior vice president of Apple's Software Engineering, said the company didn't want to create a spork by combining iPad and Mac, implying such a product wouldn't be a good tablet or laptop.
Despite claiming that the separation lets iPads focus on being tablets and MacBooks focus on being laptops, the company has made the product lines increasingly similar over the past several years. Macs and iPads now use the same M-series SoCs; the entry-level MacBook Neo uses an iPhone processor; using a mouse and keyboard on an iPad mirrors the laptop experience, and iPadOS's current UI likely laid the groundwork for last week's unveiling of the first touchscreen MacBook.
Meanwhile, 2-in-1s have spent years trying to make Windows work as a tablet and laptop OS, and Google recently started promoting Android laptops. While Microsoft and Google have approached the tablet-laptop synthesis from opposite directions, Apple is arguably the only company with a robust software stack in both areas, putting it in the best position to deliver a satisfying 2-in-1 experience.
However, Apple also likely has the most to lose by merging its tablets and laptops. The iPad App Store, where the company takes a healthy revenue cut, still delivers all iPad software, and Apple has fiercely resisted regulatory pressure to open up its mobile OSes.
Then again, 2-in-1s could one day become the latest tech trend that Apple is fashionably late to adopt. This year alone, the company introduced its first smart home hub, its first foldable smartphone, and its first touchscreen laptop, entering markets Samsung, Google, Microsoft, and others have competed in for years.

articles.title: Windows 11 avec 8 Go de RAM : Microsoft explique sa technique pour rendre votre PC plus réactif
articles.text:
Depuis le déploiement de la dernière mise à jour majeure de Windows 11, les utilisateurs équipé d’un PC à la configuration modeste respirent. L’arrivée de Windows 11 26H2 a en effet permis aux machines équipées de 8 Go de RAM d’obtenir un coup de boost inattendu. Mais ces améliorations soudaines ne sont pas dues au hasard.
Durant plusieurs mois, face à la crise de la pénurie de RAM, Microsoft a retroussé ses manches afin d’optimiser son système d’exploitation. L’objectif principal ? Le rendre plus réactif sur les configurations les moins musclées. La firme de Redmond vient d’ailleurs de dévoiler dans un billet de blog les différentes améliorations qu’elle a appliquées pour réussir ce tour de force.
Pour améliorer les performances de son système d’exploitation, Microsoft a utilisé une approche axée sur trois éléments essentiels : optimiser la gestion de la mémoire, veiller à ce que Windows 11 soit toujours réactif, et réduire la consommation mémoire de ses applications.
Une stratégie a priori payante puisque la firme de Redmond revendique sur les PC équipés de 8 Go, un gain en réactivité de 20 %, et des flux de travail multitâches qui s’exécutent jusqu’à 40 % plus rapidement qu’à l’accoutumée.
Une meilleure gestion de la mémoire
Pour obtenir de tels résultats, Microsoft explique avoir ajusté l’algorithme de compression de sa mémoire. L’entreprise indique par ailleurs qu’elle a relevé les seuils de transfert vers le disque. En opérant ainsi, la firme de Redmond permet à Windows de conserver jusqu’à 2 Go supplémentaires des données actives en mémoire, au lieu de les déplacer vers un stockage plus lent. En conséquence, une appli ou un onglet laissé ouvert est moins susceptible de se recharger une fois que vous revenez dessus.
Outre cet ajustement dans la gestion de la mémoire, Microsoft a revu la priorisation des tâches dans son système d’exploitation. Windows 11 peut désormais les prioriser de manière dynamique, afin d’accorder temporairement le maximum de ressources aux interactions courantes et en mettant momentanément en pause les tâches exécutées en arrière-plan. Avec ce fonctionnement, l’affichage du menu Démarrer, du menu contextuel du clic droit, des Paramètres ou encore de l’Explorateur de fichiers devient plus fluide.
Des applis Microsoft moins gourmandes
Optimiser la gestion de la mémoire dans Windows 11 n’a pas été le seul point d’amélioration sur lequel Microsoft s’est penchée. La firme de Redmond a également veillé à optimiser certaines applications clés du système pour qu’elles soient plus réactives. C’est le cas, par exemple avec Microsoft Edge. Microsoft explique qu’à l’ouverture d’un lien, Windows se connecte directement au processus Edge en arrière-plan, ce qui permet un gain de rapidité au lancement du navigateur de 33 %.
Du côté de Microsoft Teams, Microsoft a choisi d’activer le mode efficacité par défaut sur les PC avec 8 Go de RAM, permettant ainsi au logiciel de se lancer jusqu’à 20 % plus rapidement.
Les widgets quant à eux ne se chargent en mémoire que s’ils sont explicitement ouverts sur les machines équipées de 8 Go de RAM, économisant ainsi environ 200 Mo de RAM. Microsoft a également optimisé l’allocation mémoire dans Word, Excel, PowerPoint et Outlook, ce qui a réduit l’empreinte mémoire de 360 Mo.
Par ailleurs, la firme de Redmond a indiqué être en train de préparer d’autres améliorations à venir au cours des prochains mois. Elle envisage ainsi de mutualiser les moteurs web pour la Recherche et les widgets, ainsi que pour OneDrive et Photos afin d’économiser la mémoire de ces applications.
Microsoft a également prévu d’optimiser l’Explorateur de fichiers, le Bloc-notes, Paint ou encore la recherche Windows en leur faisant adopter WinUI 3, ce qui devrait réduire leur empreinte mémoire et surtout accélérer leur ouverture.
Enfin, l’entreprise de Redmond explique travailler main dans la main avec les fabricants et concepteurs de puces pour réduire la RAM réservée par le matériel pour laisser davantage de mémoire libre pour Windows et les applications que vous utilisez, et avec les développeurs tiers pour les aider à optimiser leurs applications.

articles.title: Binance diz que hackers prepararam roubo bilionário por meses • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Binance diz que hackers prepararam roubo bilionário por meses
Investigação aponta falsas entrevistas de emprego, programas maliciosos e até o uso de ferramenta interna de IA.
A Binance afirma que os responsáveis pelo roubo de US$ 6,34 bilhões (cerca de R$ 34,7 bilhões, em conversão direta) passaram meses preparando a invasão. Segundo uma investigação divulgada pela corretora, a operação começou em junho, com a instalação de um programa malicioso, e avançou em setembro, quando funcionários passaram a ser abordados por falsos recrutadores.
O roubo aconteceu em 29 de outubro e foi considerado o maior da história das criptomoedas. A apuração inicial apontava o computador de um engenheiro como porta de entrada, mas o relatório publicado na terça-feira (03/11) descreve uma operação mais complexa, envolvendo diferentes funcionários e até uma ferramenta interna de inteligência artificial.
Os primeiros sinais da invasão ocorreram em junho, quando um engenheiro responsável pela infraestrutura das carteiras digitais baixou uma versão adulterada do Homebrew, gerenciador de pacotes usado no macOS. Ele procurava uma ferramenta de programação com IA. A equipe de segurança detectou a ameaça, substituiu o computador e renovou as credenciais. Mesmo assim, os criminosos teriam descoberto informações sobre o cargo do funcionário e seus colegas.
Em setembro, outro engenheiro recebeu uma proposta de emprego falsa. Os invasores se passaram por representantes de uma empresa, organizaram entrevistas por vídeo e utilizaram perfis em redes sociais para tornar a abordagem convincente.
Durante uma das conversas, a vítima recebeu uma suposta tarefa de programação. O arquivo continha um malware que substituiu um componente legítimo de uma ferramenta de desenvolvimento, permitindo executar comandos remotamente. Segundo o The Verge, as ferramentas de proteção da Binance não identificaram essa segunda infecção.
Em 20 de outubro, os hackers teriam aproveitado o computador comprometido para acessar uma ferramenta interna de IA da Binance. Segundo a empresa, esse acesso permitiu ampliar o ataque a outros dois funcionários ligados às carteiras digitais.
Os invasores encontraram credenciais com permissão para instalar componentes na infraestrutura da corretora. Em 29 de outubro, utilizaram esse acesso para executar um programa malicioso e iniciar as transferências. A Binance não explicou em detalhes o funcionamento da ferramenta de IA nem como ela foi explorada.
Os criminosos exploraram um recurso do Ethereum chamado EIP-7702, que permite delegar certas operações de uma carteira sem revelar sua chave privada. Com acesso indevido aos serviços de autorização, eles conseguiram criar permissões para movimentar os criptoativos.
A Binance suspendeu os saques após identificar as transações suspeitas, mas a medida não foi suficiente. As autorizações maliciosas já estavam registradas e funcionavam sem depender do sistema convencional de retiradas.
A corretora precisou desenvolver um procedimento específico para cancelar essas permissões. Segundo a empresa, a última transferência não autorizada foi concluída às 20h56 de 29 de outubro, no horário de Brasília.
A Binance afirma que aproximadamente US$ 2,85 bilhões (R$ 15,6 bilhões) em ativos foram congelados ou interceptados com a ajuda de parceiros. A corretora também afirma ter reposto 98% dos ativos afetados até 3 de novembro, utilizando recursos próprios, e promete cobrir integralmente as perdas dos clientes.
O FBI atribuiu o ataque ao grupo TraderTraitor, ligado à Coreia do Norte. A Binance afirma ter substituído equipamentos comprometidos, reconstruído sistemas afetados e reforçado os controles de acesso. A investigação ainda é preliminar e passará por uma revisão independente de especialistas em segurança.
Na segunda-feira (02/11), a Mercado Bitcoin, uma das maiores corretoras brasileiras de ativos digitais, também foi alvo de um ataque hacker. As movimentações suspeitas podem ter envolvido cerca de US$ 40 milhões (aproximadamente R$ 217,7 milhões), mas a empresa afirma que os clientes não tiveram prejuízos.
