articles.title: Could the GTA 6 launch break the Australian internet? We asked NBN Co to find out
articles.text:
Could the GTA 6 launch break the Australian internet? We asked NBN Co to find out
Australia's broadband network is bracing for one of gaming's biggest launches, but NBN Co says it's ready for the challenge
- NBN Co says Australia's broadband network is ready for the expected surge in traffic when GTA VI launches
- A previous major game release pushed NBN traffic to a record 32.91Tbps, around 30% above normal levels
- GTA VI's week-long preload period should help prevent a massive spike in network traffic on launch day
- NBN Co believes GTA VI could set a new record for total download volume across its 7–8-day launch period
Grand Theft Auto VI is shaping up to be one of the biggest video game launches in history, and with millions of gamers expected to download Rockstar's long-awaited sequel, it's fair to wonder whether Australia's internet infrastructure can cope with the demand.
After all, GTA VI is confirmed to require a hefty 212GB download, meaning even a single copy will consume a considerable amount of bandwidth. Multiply that by potentially hundreds of thousands of Australian gamers all wanting to get their hands on the game at once, and it's easy to imagine the strain it could place on the country's broadband network.
But could GTA VI actually break the internet?
We put that question to NBN Co, and its response was reassuring. Not only does the company believe its network is ready for the game's arrival, but it also suggested GTA VI could potentially set a new record for the amount of data downloaded over a single game launch period.
NBN Co says it's ready for GTA VI
Despite the enormous anticipation surrounding GTA VI, NBN Co doesn't appear particularly concerned about the network being overwhelmed when the game launches.
"We've planned for major download events like this, and we're confident the NBN network is ready for the increased demand," an NBN Co spokesperson told us.
The company explained that it works closely with content distributors to model the potential impact of major game releases, allowing it to prepare for periods of particularly heavy demand.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Part of that preparation involves working with distributors to spread downloads over a longer period, rather than allowing everyone to begin downloading at the same time.
This has already changed the way major game launches affect the network. According to NBN Co, traffic now begins building earlier in the day, rather than suddenly surging when gamers return home from work.
Game launches have already pushed NBN traffic to record highs
There's good reason for NBN Co to take major game releases seriously — the company revealed that gaming downloads have been responsible for some of the biggest traffic peaks ever recorded on its network.
In fact, NBN Co told us that “a game download release last year” coincided with a record traffic peak of 32.91 terabits per second (Tbps).
“This was approximately 30% higher than baseline traffic, with almost 8Tbps of additional demand during the busiest hour.”
And while NBN Co didn't identify which game was responsible for that particular peak, it demonstrates just how significantly a major release can affect Australia's internet traffic. With GTA VI arguably being one of the most anticipated games of all time, it's reasonable to expect another substantial increase in demand.
Why preloading could prevent a massive traffic spike
Fortunately, there's one factor working in NBN Co's favour: preloading.
GTA VI preloading is scheduled to begin on November 10 for anyone who has preordered the game from a digital store. For anyone looking to buy the code-in-box variant, preloading is confirmed for November 12, giving players the opportunity to download the game ahead of its official release.
Rather than having millions of players attempting to download more than 200GB of data simultaneously, the preload window allows that demand to be distributed over several days.
"Preloading is good news for gamers and good news for the network," NBN Co told us.
The company explained that the impact of major game launches has become less significant over time, largely because distributors now spread downloads and updates across longer periods. In GTA VI's case, NBN Co expects the week-long preload period to help avoid particularly sharp spikes in network traffic.
However, that doesn't necessarily mean the game won't break any records.
GTA VI could still set a new Australian download record
While NBN Co doesn't necessarily expect GTA VI to produce the biggest single-hour traffic spike in its history, it believes the game's launch could achieve something arguably more impressive.
"While the preloading approach will likely prevent a record-breaking traffic spike during a specific hour or day, we expect to see increased traffic across the preload and release period, which could result in a record-breaking download volume across that 7 – 8-day period," the company said.
In other words, GTA VI might not generate the highest instantaneous demand ever seen on the NBN, but the total amount of data downloaded over its launch period could still be unprecedented.
Indeed, with a 212GB download potentially being repeated across a huge number of Australian households, it's not difficult to see why NBN Co is anticipating a particularly busy week.
How to prepare your internet connection for GTA VI
While NBN Co is confident its network can handle the increased demand, individual households could still encounter slower-than-expected downloads if their home internet setup isn't up to scratch.
The company recommends checking your router's location, ideally positioning it somewhere elevated and central, away from obstacles and sources of interference.
It also suggests checking the age of your router, since older models may struggle to deliver the full speeds available on faster NBN plans. Of course, this isn’t advice aimed solely at prospective GTA players; it’s advice we recommend ourselves, particularly if you have one of the fastest NBN plans.
For larger or multi-storey homes, the best mesh Wi-Fi systems in Australia can help improve wireless coverage, while households still using older copper-based NBN connections may want to check whether they're eligible for a free fibre upgrade.
Finally, NBN Co recommends reviewing your current internet plan to determine whether it still meets your household's needs.
Of course, even the fastest NBN connection won't guarantee maximum download speeds if the game distribution servers are struggling to keep up with demand.
But with GTA VI's launch fast approaching, the message from NBN Co is clear — Australia's broadband network is ready, even if the country's gamers are about to put it through one of its biggest tests yet.

articles.title: Return secures €835 million financing to expand battery storage capacity in Germany | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Amsterdam-based Return, an energy storage startup specialising in large-scale battery systems and energy flexibility services, has secured €835 million in portfolio financing underwritten by Deutsche Bank and Rabobank.
The financing will support the company’s expansion in Germany, where it aims to install at least 1 GW of battery storage capacity annually from 2027 onwards. This follows their 2025 €300 million growth-equity investment.
“As demand for energy flexibility grows, we need to scale not just our battery storage capacity, but also the way we finance it. By bringing together physical infrastructure financing and our virtual flexibility model, we can expand more efficiently and respond to our customers’ evolving needs. This is an important step towards our ambition to become a leading independent provider of energy flexibility in Germany,” says Daniel Witvoet, CFO at Return.
Return’s financing comes amid a series of European investments in battery storage and grid flexibility reported by EU-Startups in 2026.
In Germany, Munich-based Entrix raised €43 million for battery optimisation and flexible energy trading, while encosa secured €25 million to expand commercial and industrial battery storage.
In Return’s home market, Amsterdam-based Ore Energy raised €37.3 million to scale long-duration battery technology, and Utrecht-based Eddy Grid secured €7.5 million for renewable energy asset optimisation.
Together with other comparable announcements across Europe, these rounds represent approximately €158.2 million in EnergyTech financing.
Dominik Thumfart, Head of Infrastructure & Energy Origination, Deutsche Bank, adds: “Battery storage plays a crucial role in Germany’s energy transition, by assisting with optimising the revenue potential of intermittent power generation plants and ensuring grid stability. We are pleased to support Return with a financing structure built to scale and structured to meet the capital expenditure needs of Return’s German BESS project pipeline.”
Founded in 2021 by Willem-Jan Schutte and Daniel Witvoet, Return is headquartered in Amsterdam and operates across several European energy markets. Schutte, the company’s CEO, previously co-founded solar energy company Sunrock, while Witvoet, who serves as CFO, also has a background in renewable energy investment and entrepreneurship.
Return has since expanded its activities across the Netherlands, Belgium, Germany and Spain, focusing on developing, owning and operating large-scale battery storage infrastructure.
With the new financing structure, Return plans to invest between €750 million and €1.2 billion annually in German battery storage projects from 2027, depending on market conditions. The company expects these investments to support increasing demand for energy flexibility as Germany continues to integrate wind and solar power into its electricity system.
The initial framework covers three battery storage projects in Germany with a combined capacity of 117 MW. Under assumptions of four-hour battery duration and two full charging and discharging cycles daily, the facilities could discharge approximately 341,640 MWh annually, equivalent to the yearly electricity consumption of around 100,000 German households.
The investment follows several commercial agreements that have strengthened Return’s position in the German energy market. ENGIE recently expanded its partnership with Return to 400 MW of contracted battery flexibility, while Centrica Energy signed a separate agreement covering 100 MW.
Beyond Germany, Return also works with energy companies including Vattenfall, Essent and Eneco in other European markets.
The German financing builds on a model Return has already implemented in the Netherlands. Earlier in 2026, its Sirius battery storage project reached financial close under a broader financing framework covering multiple storage developments. The new German arrangement extends this approach by connecting financing for physical battery infrastructure with the company’s virtual flexibility services.
Marc Schmitz, Head of Project Finance Europe at Rabobank, says: “Germany needs more flexible capacity as wind and solar generation grows. This facility helps direct investment into large-scale battery storage. Supporting technologies that enable the further growth of renewable energy is a key part of Rabobank’s approach to the German energy transition.
“We are delighted to further strengthen our relationship with Return and support its expansion into Germany. Building on our previous transactions together, we are combining our advisory, underwriting, project finance and hedging expertise to help Return realise its growth ambitions.”
Return currently has an active development portfolio exceeding 8 GW and aims to deliver more than 5 GW of battery storage capacity by 2030. Its expansion into Germany forms part of a broader European strategy focused on addressing the growing need for energy flexibility as renewable electricity generation increases.
The financing represents a step in Return’s plans to scale its Virtual Flexibility Portfolio (VFP), a platform that combines battery storage capacity from multiple facilities into a single virtual portfolio. The approach allows energy companies to access flexible electricity storage capacity without having to manage individual battery assets.

articles.title: Agentic Data Security Firm Sentra Raises $150 Million
articles.text:
Agentic data security company Sentra today announced raising $150 million in a Series C funding round that brings the total raised by the company to over $260 million. The investment round was led by Capital One Ventures.
Founded in 2021 and co-headquartered in New York City and Tel Aviv, Sentra has built an AI-powered, cloud-native platform that provides data security and governance, and AI data readiness.
The solution protects data at rest across cloud, SaaS, data warehouses, knowledge stores, and on-premises file shares, governing both the data and the access agents need.
Sentra finds and classifies data across environments, maps assets reachable by users, AI agents, and service accounts, and enforces least privilege policies while eliminating the high-risk data agents should not find.
The platform flags unusual access to sensitive data, revoking access and blocking the risk through automated remediation. It also provides detailed reports on what the agent could have reached, with business context.
Sentra will use the new funding to accelerate its agentic data security capabilities and provide broad visibility into AI and the data it reaches, continuous least privilege enforcement for all identities, data protection, and rapid containment.
Additionally, it plans to expand its go-to-market organization, grow brand and marketing teams, and expand to new regions.
“Traditional perimeter controls weren’t built for agents moving at machine speed. What organizations can do is make sure the data those agents reach is already secured. Sentra protects data where it lives and controls which identities, human and AI, can reach it, so organizations can deploy AI more quickly while staying in control,” said Sentra co-founder and CEO Yoav Regev.

A powerful rig for serious gaming
There's a CyberPowerPC gaming PC on sale right now with a $300 discount that you won't want to miss. Best Buy has slashed the price on this rig with a 9800X3D, RTX 5070, 32GB DDR5, and a 2TB SSD, bringing it down to just $2,199.

These specs unlock serious performance for 1440p and, thanks to the power of Nvidia DLSS and multi-frame generation, you'll be able to uplift to 4K, too. articles.title: Xbox previews two new ways to control cloud games
articles.text:
I revealed yesterday that the new Xbox Nano controller supports a Wi-Fi connection directly to Xbox Cloud Gaming, and now Microsoft is making it official today. Two new Xbox previews will let players try out using a phone as a controller on smart TVs, as well as cloud connect on the Xbox Nano to connect directly to cloud servers.
Xbox previews two new ways to control cloud games
Xbox Cloud Gaming is getting a phone controller and new direct Wi-Fi connectivity for the Xbox Nano.
“Instead of a Bluetooth connection to your TV, cloud connect uses your Wi-Fi to connect directly to the cloud server running your game,” says the Xbox team. “That can help reduce input latency, so gameplay may feel more responsive.”
Players in the US will be able to preview the new cloud connect option for the Xbox Nano controller starting today. If you’re not in the US you will be able to preview a new phone controller option on smart TVs. The controller is available on the Xbox Cloud Gaming website, allowing people to use the streaming service without a dedicated Bluetooth controller.
Microsoft says “both experiences are still being tested” and that “availability and supported games or devices may be limited” during this beta phase. You’ll need to use the Xbox beta app for Android or the Xbox Accessories app on PC to set up cloud connect on the Nano controller, and the smart TV phone controller just requires a toggle of preview features from the Settings > Account section of Xbox Cloud Gaming.

articles.title: Wie ist dein biologisches Alter? Forscher checken 7 Aspekte deiner Stimme
articles.text:
Was alles in deiner Stimme steckt: Forscher ermitteln das biologische Alter
Es führt kein Weg am Altern vorbei, aber unsere Körper lassen nicht gleich schnell oder in derselben Form nach. Die einen können mit 60 noch zügig ihre Bahnen im Schwimmbad ziehen, die anderen geraten schon bei kürzeren Spaziergängen außer Atem. Auch unsere kognitiven Fähigkeiten, Organe, Muskelkraft und das Immunsystem können entweder relativ gut in Schuss sein oder stärker abnehmen.
Ob wir also langsamer oder schneller altern als unsere Altersgenossen im Durchschnitt – und damit biologisch jünger oder älter sind als unser in Geburtstagen gemessenes chronologisches Alter –, war bisher eher aufwendig und teuer zu bestimmen. Eine ganze Reihe von sogenannten Alternsuhren misst verschiedene Spuren des Alterns. Dafür sind allerdings DNA-Proben, Blut- und Vitalwerte oder gar Gehirnaufnahmen aus bildgebenden Großgeräten nötig.

articles.title: Priyank Kharge asks EV companies to shape Karnataka's growth roadmap
articles.text:
Priyank Kharge asks EV companies to shape Karnataka's growth roadmap
Ahead of the Bengaluru Tech Summit 2026, Priyank Kharge held talks with leaders in the EV industry on specialised skilling, testing infrastructure, and manufacturing support.
Building an electric vehicle ecosystem takes more than putting new vehicles on the road.
It also requires battery research, specialised engineering talent, testing facilities and a manufacturing base that can support the industry as it grows.
As Karnataka looks to strengthen its position in the EV sector, Minister for Home, Electronics, Information Technology and Biotechnology, and E-Governance Priyank Kharge has asked industry players to help shape a roadmap for the state's electric mobility ecosystem.
Ahead of Bengaluru Tech Summit 2026, Kharge held a roundtable with companies and stakeholders from Karnataka's EV industry to understand their priorities, identify areas for collaboration and discuss ways to accelerate the sector's growth.
The meeting brought together representatives from Exponent Energy, Ultraviolette, Simple Energy, Sun Mobility, Moonrider and Multiplex EV, alongside other manufacturers, technology companies, battery and energy solutions providers and startups.
Building the infrastructure behind electric mobility
The discussions covered several areas that could strengthen Karnataka's EV ecosystem, including industry-led research and development, advanced testing and certification facilities, specialised skilling programmes, incubation support and manufacturing infrastructure.
Priyank Kharge emphasised that government support should be shaped by the actual requirements of companies operating across the EV value chain.
“The government is committed to supporting the growth of the EV sector in Karnataka. However, our interventions must be guided by what the industry actually needs,” he said.
He urged companies to come together, identify common priorities and submit a consolidated roadmap to the government. This would help determine which infrastructure and support measures need to be taken forward.
Industry to play a role in training EV talent
Talent development emerged as another key area during the interaction. As the EV industry expands, companies need specialised professionals across battery technology, embedded systems, firmware, power electronics, vehicle diagnostics, manufacturing and after-sales services.
To address this demand, Kharge proposed an industry-backed skilling model in which companies would help design training curricula, certify candidates and provide employment opportunities.
The approach would bring employers closer to the training process, helping align the skills being taught with the requirements of the industry.
Strengthening local manufacturing capabilities
The minister also encouraged companies to explore existing policy incentives available in Karnataka for manufacturing and engineering research and development.
The discussions included opportunities to strengthen local manufacturing capabilities and reduce dependence on imports.
With the EV industry spanning vehicle production, battery systems, electronics, software and energy infrastructure, Karnataka is looking to bring these capabilities together to support innovation and manufacturing within the state.
The roundtable forms part of the state's engagement with industry ahead of Bengaluru Tech Summit 2026, with the proposed roadmap expected to help identify priorities for the next phase of EV ecosystem development.

Points forts
- Autonomie longue durée.
- Nouveau format qui rafraîchit la gamme Fold.
- Écrans très lumineux.
- Charge à 45 W.
Points faibles
- Absence de Flex Mode.
- Pas de téléobjectif.
Le Galaxy Z Fold 8 apporte un souffle nouveau à une gamme Samsung Fold qui commençait sérieusement à s'encroûter. Son format passeport, presque carré, lui confère une ergonomie nouvelle, lui permet de jouer les liseuses, d'être rangé plus facilement dans une poche et presque de se laisser confondre avec un smartphone monobloc traditionnel. Il a bien peu de défauts à son actif : sa batterie au silicium-carbone lui octroie une très bonne endurance, il se charge assez rapidement, il se montre puissant et ses écrans, qui mériteraient sans doute une calibration plus pointue, sont très lumineux et font la chasse aux reflets. Il ne lui manque qu'un volet photo plus généreux, avec un téléobjectif, pour répondre pleinement aux attentes que fait naître son positionnement tarifaire.

articles.text:
El Corte Inglés está celebrando su Adelántate al Black Friday, una campaña centrada en este evento en la que podemos encontrar muchísimas ofertas en todo tipo de dispositivos. Una de las más atractivas ha caído en el LG Smart Monitor Swing, un monitor muy particular que se puede comprar en varias configuraciones:
- LG Smart Monitor Swing con pantalla Full HD por 399 euros.
- LG Smart Monitor Swing con pantalla 4K por 499 euros.
- LG Smart Monitor Swing con pantalla 4K y hasta 144 Hz por 699 euros.
- LG Smart Monitor Swing con pantalla 4K táctil por 849 euros.
Todos ellos tienen una diagonal de 32 pulgadas.
LG Smart Monitor Swing (32 pulgadas) - 4K, 60 Hz
Un monitor para utilizar por toda la casa
El LG Smart Monitor Swing que tiene mejor relación calidad-precio es el que incorpora una pantalla 4K, el modelo que ahora mismo tiene un precio de 499 euros. Es ideal para ver contenido multimedia y también para jugar, siempre teniendo en cuenta que no ofrece una tasa de refresco superior a 60 Hz.
Hay dos particularidades en este monitor: el primero es que viene con el sistema operativo WebOS, el que viene en los televisores de LG. Esto significa que se trata de un monitor "inteligente" que permite descargar un buen surtido de apps, como es el caso de las de streaming.
Lo segundo es que incorpora un soporte de pie. Esto permite varias cosas: no quita espacio en el escritorio en el caso de que queramos utilizarlo en el ordenador y además permite que podamos moverlo entre habitaciones gracias a que el soporte incluye ruedas, algo ideal si queremos estudiar, trabajar, ver contenido o jugar a la consola en diferentes lugares de la casa.

articles.title: IPTV : Warner Bros fait fermer près de 2 000 sites pirates, mais certains réapparaissent aussitôt
articles.text:
Au Chili, Warner Bros. a obtenu le blocage de près de 2 000 URL liées à des services pirates. Une victoire retentissante pour le géant du divertissement ? Pas totalement. En effet, selon un média chilien, certains sites bloqués sont rapidement réapparus sous une autre adresse. Le jeu du chat et de la souris continue donc.
Près de 2000 sites pirates fermés
En janvier 2026, au Chili, Warner Bros. a saisi le 19e tribunal civil de Santiago afin d’obtenir le blocage de sites diffusant des contenus piratés du géant du divertissement. Ce dernier a obtenu gain de cause. Quelques jours plus tard, le régulateur chilien des télécommunications (Subtel) a ordonné à plusieurs opérateurs du pays de bloquer les sites pirates.
Au total, ce sont 1 954 adresses URL de sites pirates qui ont été bloquées, entre juin et octobre 2026. Nous retrouvons notamment des services IPTV illégaux, des plateformes de streaming pirates ou encore des sites miroirs. Le Play Store et l’App Store ont même été notifiés pour retirer l’accès à certaines applications pirates et suspendre les comptes de leurs développeurs.
Un site pirate est fermé : il réapparaît ailleurs
Le géant du divertissement Warner Bros. ressortirait-il totalement vainqueur de cette opération de blocage ? Pas vraiment. Comme bien souvent, lorsqu’un site pirate est fermé, il réapparaît ailleurs sous une nouvelle adresse. Le média chilien BioBioChile assure ainsi avoir retrouvé plusieurs services pirates, ayant pourtant été fermés, toujours accessibles en ligne via d’autres adresses. À ce titre, Rodrigo Ramírez, président de l’Alliance chilienne contre le piratage numérique, explique que « Lorsqu’un domaine ou un lien est bloqué, des répliques, des sites miroirs ou de nouvelles adresses apparaissent rapidement pour contourner les mesures prises ». Une bataille a été gagnée par Warner Bros., mais le jeu du chat et de la souris continue.
Autant dire que nous assistons à la même chose en France avec une bataille qui semble sans fin entre les ayants droit et les services pirates. L’Union européenne mise d’ailleurs sur un mécanisme de blocage dynamique permettant de bloquer un service pirate en 30 minutes maximum, mais la partie est toujours loin d’être gagnée pour les ayants droit qui font régulièrement état de pertes de chiffre d’affaires colossales.

articles.title: CISA flags WordPress RCE flaw as actively exploited in attacks
articles.text:
The US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) warned federal agencies that attackers have started exploiting a recently patched high-severity WordPress vulnerability in the wild.
Tracked as CVE-2026-119977, this high-severity WordPress Core flaw stems from a Time-of-check Time-of-use (TOCTOU) race condition and was reported by Picus Security researcher Umut Bayram.
Successful exploitation can let remote threat actors without privileges execute code on the server in high-complexity attacks due to predictable, web-accessible staging paths used during full-package core upgrades.
"A weakness in the WordPress upgrade process which can lead to remote code execution during the upgrade window," the WordPress security team said on October 28 when it released WordPress 7.1.4 with patches to address this security issue. "Because this is a security release, it is recommended that you update your sites immediately."
CISA confirmed CVE-2026-119977 active exploitation on Tuesday and added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog, ordering Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies to secure their systems by Friday, as mandated by Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04.
"This type of vulnerability is a frequent attack vector for malicious cyber actors and poses significant risks to the federal enterprise," the cybersecurity agency warned.
Although BOD 26-04 targets only US federal agencies, CISA urged all network defenders, including those in the private sector, to prioritize patching this vulnerability to protect their servers.
While CISA didn't provide more details on attackers exploiting CVE-2026-119977 in the wild, WordPress security firm Wordfence says in an advisory update over the weekend that it "blocked 13,095 attacks targeting this vulnerability in the past 24 hours."
In July, the WordPress security team also patched a critical vulnerability chain in WordPress Core (named wp2shell) that can be abused to deploy webshells and take over unpatched servers by exploiting a REST API batch-route confusion vulnerability (CVE-2026-63030) and an SQL injection flaw (CVE-2026-60137).
Public wp2shell exploits were released one day after the patches went live, and attackers began breaching unpatched servers a few days later to deploy persistent webshells and install malicious plugins.
A Chinese-speaking threat actor also weaponized the wp2shell exploit chain in September to steal sensitive data from more than 18,500 records stored in backend databases belonging to small businesses and government organizations.

articles.title: Naruto donne une excellente nouvelle à ses fans
articles.text:
Ce mardi 3 novembre 2026, Lionsgate a donné son feu vert officiel au film Naruto en prises de vues réelles, en développement depuis plus de 10 ans. Le studio s’associe à Sony Pictures, qui cofinance le long-métrage et le distribuera hors d’Amérique du Nord, donc en France. Lionsgate garde la production et la sortie aux États-Unis et au Canada. Le tournage est d’ores et déjà planifié pour démarrer au printemps 2027. C’est ce que l’on peut apprendre via The Hollywood Reporter.
Un capitaine de navire rompu aux blockbusters de super-héros pour Naruto
Le film Naruto est confié à Destin Daniel Cretton, réalisateur de Shang-Chi et la Légende des Dix Anneaux chez Marvel. Il enchaîne après Spider-Man: Brand New Day, en salles depuis fin juillet, qui a rapporté 2,52 milliards de dollars (environ 2,25 milliards d’euros) dans le monde. Il écrira le scénario, réalisera et produira le film via sa société Hisako, avec Arad Productions (Avi et Ari Arad).
Sony possède Crunchyroll, la plateforme de streaming spécialisée dans l’anime, et Destin Daniel Cretton vient de signer un contrat de 3 ans avec Sony Pictures, le studio de Tom Rothman. Adam Fogelson, patron du cinéma chez Lionsgate, met en avant l’expertise de Sony dans le manga et l’anime. Selon TheWrap, plusieurs studios étaient sur les rangs.
Du pain sur la planche pour respecter le phénomène mondial
Le manga de Masashi Kishimoto s’est vendu à plus de 250 millions d’exemplaires, et son adaptation en anime a été diffusée dans plus de 145 pays et territoires, selon Lionsgate et Sony. Dans l’annonce, Destin Daniel Cretton se présente d’abord en fan :
« En tant que fan de longue date de Naruto, j’ai toujours aimé le fait que sous cette action extraordinaire se cache une histoire pleine de cœur, d’humour et d’humanité. Kishimoto-sensei a créé un monde où des héros improbables font des choses extraordinaires. »
Côté casting, Lionsgate n’a pas encore annoncé qui jouera le jeune ninja blond qui abrite le démon renard à neuf queues. Une recherche mondiale a été lancée en juillet pour les rôles de Naruto, Sasuke et Sakura. Un seul nom circule pour l’instant, celui de Charles Melton (Beef, May December). Selon Variety, l’acteur est depuis août en discussions avancées pour jouer Kakashi Hatake, le mentor de l’équipe 7.
Le tournage doit commencer au printemps 2027. Lionsgate et Sony n’ont encore annoncé aucune date de sortie.

articles.title: Airtel Nigeria's data boom hits an operating cost bottleneck
articles.text:
Airtel Nigeria is adding customers, selling more data, and generating higher earnings. Yet a decline in its quarterly operating margin suggests that rising demand is not translating into stronger profitability at the same pace.
The company’s mobile-services Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation, and Amortisation (EBITDA) margin fell from approximately 58.8% in the first quarter of its 2027 financial year to 57.5% in the second. Although its half-year performance remained significantly stronger than a year earlier, the sequential decline points to the growing challenge of managing operating costs while expanding capacity to accommodate rising traffic.
That tension is becoming central to Airtel Nigeria’s growth story. As data consumption accelerates, the operator must balance network investment and rising operating expenses against the need to sustain margins and generate cash. The question is no longer simply how much demand it can capture, but how efficiently it can convert that demand into lasting financial returns.
For Airtel Nigeria, the challenge is to turn Nigeria’s appetite for connectivity into earnings and, ultimately, cash, without allowing the cost of growth to erode profitability.
For the six months ended September 2026, Nigeria’s mobile-services revenue increased 44.6% in reported dollars to $1.008 billion. Underlying EBITDA rose faster, climbing 49.2% to $586 million, while the half-year margin improved to 58.2% from 56.3%.
Those comparisons qualify the quarterly warning. Airtel Nigeria’s earnings are not shrinking, nor has the business lost the benefits of scale. Over the half-year, faster EBITDA growth indicates that rising revenue and cost efficiencies continued to support profitability.
That approach reflects management’s established strategy.
“During the quarter, we accelerated investment to enhance coverage and data capacity while also expanding our fibre network,” Airtel Africa CEO Sunil Taldar said, commenting on the nine-month results for the period ended December 2025.
The latest results show that investment is continuing. But they also illustrate the financial discipline required to ensure that a larger network produces attractive returns.
Currency movements strengthened the reported performance. The weighted-average exchange rate improved from ₦1,553 per dollar to ₦1,360. Excluding currency movements, mobile-services revenue grew 26.6%, and EBITDA increased 30.7%—still substantial, but below the reported dollar increases.
A stronger naira, therefore, helped the financial presentation. It should not be confused with an equivalent improvement in operating efficiency.
Fuel margins pressure and the cash stakes
Energy remains a central challenge. In its September 2026 half-year results, Airtel said fuel prices in Nigeria had doubled since the start of the financial year. Revenue growth and efficiency measures nevertheless supported year-on-year margin improvement. The company did not disclose a separate figure for Nigerian fuel or energy expenditure, leaving the actual increase in its energy bill unquantified.
That exposure remains a risk to profitability. “Looking ahead, margin performance will continue to be influenced by the macroeconomic environment, including its impact on fuel costs,” Airtel Africa CEO Sunil Taldar said in the half-year statement.
Although his warning covered the wider group, the sharp rise in Nigerian fuel prices makes it particularly relevant to the local business.
The tension is straightforward. More customers and higher usage allow an operator to spread infrastructure costs across a larger revenue base. Rising energy expenses can absorb part of that advantage.
Demand remains strong. Airtel Nigeria’s customer base increased 15.1% to 61.7 million, while monthly smartphone data consumption rose from 12.7GB to 16.7GB per customer. Data revenue increased 33.8% in constant currency.
These figures do not establish that each additional gigabyte became more expensive to deliver. They show that rising consumption coincided with lower quarterly margins, making cost control increasingly important.
Meanwhile, Airtel is spending more to sustain that demand. Nigeria’s first-half capital expenditure rose 139.9% to $177 million. Operating free cash flow increased 28.2% to $409 million—healthy growth, but slower than EBITDA as investment absorbed more earnings.
The distinction matters. Airtel Nigeria’s operating free cash flow measure already deducts capital expenditure from EBITDA. It is not, however, the same as cash available for shareholders after taxes, financing obligations and other payments.
The wider group demonstrates that gap. Management reported normalised free cash flow of $280 million, down from $368 million, despite stronger earnings, as cash investment accelerated. These are group figures, not Nigeria-only results, but they show why higher EBITDA does not necessarily translate into higher discretionary cash.
More usage must produce sufficient revenue
Customer spending presents another balancing act. Nigeria’s mobile-services average revenue per user reached $2.80, increasing 28.3% in reported currency and 12.3% in constant currency.
Management nevertheless acknowledged slower data-ARPU momentum. Newly acquired customers initially consume less, while larger bundles reduce revenue per gigabyte for heavier users. Airtel described its pricing approach as “more for more” and said it had not seen evidence of a price war.
Encouraging consumption can strengthen customer relationships, but traffic growth does not necessarily generate proportional revenue growth. Airtel Nigeria must earn enough from that usage to justify additional capacity without weakening its offers.
Its results still support confidence: half-year margins and operating free cash flow improved. The quarterly decline is a warning to monitor, not proof of a failing model. The next test is whether disciplined spending and operating efficiencies can preserve the financial returns that Airtel’s expanding network is intended to deliver.

articles.title: « Apple hardware liberated » : cette distribution Linux arrive sur les Mac M1, M2, M3 et Neo — Frandroid
articles.text:
David Heinemeier Hansson, le créateur de Ruby on Rails, a confirmé dans un message publié sur X que la version 4.5 de sa distribution Omarchy arrivera avec une « compatibilité complète » pour les puces Apple M1, M2 et M3, et pour « Neo ». Tous les Mac à puce Apple sortis entre fin 2020 et fin 2023 pourront donc démarrer sous Linux directement, sans machine virtuelle. DHH résume l’annonce en trois mots, « Apple hardware liberated », le matériel Apple libéré. Il en attribue le mérite à l’équipe Omarchy M, le groupe de développeurs qui s’occupe des Mac.
Comme nous l’expliquions dans notre test, Omarchy est une distribution Linux basée sur Arch et livrée déjà configurée. Elle utilise Hyprland, un gestionnaire qui range les fenêtres en mosaïque et se pilote au clavier. Tous les choix sont ceux de DHH, et le personnage ne fait pas l’unanimité.
Jusqu’ici, le projet visait les PC à processeur Intel ou AMD. Côté Mac, la bidouille marchait plutôt dans l’autre sens, avec macOS 27 installé sur un PC.
Un dual boot par défaut, et des questions sans réponse
À l’installation, DHH promet un dual boot (macOS et Linux sur le même disque, avec le choix au démarrage) si fluide qu’il devient « a no brainer », une évidence. En septembre, Marcelo Alcantara, l’un des développeurs du portage, expliquait déjà dans un message relayé par DHH que l’installeur met le Mac en dual boot par défaut et laisse découper le SSD comme on veut. Par contre, DHH ne dit pas si on peut effacer macOS complètement. Des utilisateurs lui ont pourtant posé la question sous son message.
On ne sait rien non plus de l’autonomie. Un utilisateur a demandé à DHH comment Omarchy se débrouille face à macOS sur batterie, et aucun chiffre n’a été publié. Pour les puces plus récentes, DHH annonce les M4, M5 et M6 comme « on the way », en route, sans donner de date. Pour l’instant, tous les Mac vendus depuis fin 2024 restent donc sur la touche, Mac mini M6 compris.
Les PC portables Snapdragon X et Nvidia N1X aussi
Le site américain Phoronix, qui suit de près l’actualité de Linux, s’est penché sur la première version candidate d’Omarchy 4.5 (une préversion à tester avant la sortie finale). Il y a trouvé un premier support de l’AArch64, l’architecture ARM 64 bits, celle des puces Apple. Jusqu’ici, Omarchy ne tournait que sur des processeurs x86_64, ceux d’Intel et d’AMD. Avec cette version, Omarchy dépasse donc le Mac et arrive sur des PC portables ARM d’autres marques.
Les machines testées sont les Dell XPS 16 et Asus ProArt P14 pour la puce N1X de Nvidia, le RTX Spark, et les Lenovo Yoga Slim 7x et ThinkPad T14s pour les Snapdragon X de Qualcomm. Sur la plupart des PC Snapdragon, Omarchy doit aller chercher les micrologiciels sur la partition Windows, comme les autres distributions Linux. Ce sont les petits programmes dont les composants ont besoin pour fonctionner. Mieux vaut donc garder Windows sur le disque.
Côté Apple, Phoronix précise qu’Omarchy Mac, la version séparée qui faisait tourner la distribution sur les Mac, est maintenant intégrée à Omarchy. Le site rappelle aussi que le noyau Linux officiel gère encore mal les puces M les plus récentes.
Ce qu’il faut vérifier avant d’installer Omarchy 4.5 sur un Mac
La version finale d’Omarchy 4.5 n’a pas encore de date. Ce lundi 2 novembre, le compte officiel du projet a relayé la sortie d’une troisième version candidate, la première avec le nouvel installeur pour les puces Apple.
- Vérifiez la puce de votre Mac dans le menu Pomme, rubrique « À propos de ce Mac ». Seuls les M1, M2, M3 et Neo sont pris en charge.
- Sauvegardez vos données avant de découper le SSD pour le dual boot.
- Sur un PC Snapdragon X, gardez la partition Windows : Omarchy en a besoin pour récupérer les micrologiciels.

articles.title: Los residentes de la zona de Casselton cuestionan la ubicación del centro de datos en tierras agrícolas de primera
articles.text:
El sitio seleccionado para el Harmony Energy Park ha suscitado algunas preocupaciones en la zona de Casselton (Dakota del Norte). En el encuentro con los representantes de la empresa celebrado el 1 de octubre de 2026, varias personas de la zona mostraron su preocupación por utilizar tierras de cultivo. Geronimo Power planea poner un centro de datos en un área al este de Casselton y al norte de Mapleton en el municipio rural de Harmony.
Caryn Weber explica que no se opone a los centros de datos, pero cuestiona la ubicación. “Es preocupante ver cómo se hormigonan tierras agrícolas de primera”, dice en el Bondegard Cafe.
Los temas que preocupaban a los residentes de Dakota del Norte eran los de ruido y los de consumo de agua. También se planteaban los precios de la luz y la reducción de tierras agrícolas. En Casselton, los representantes de Geronimo distribuyeron material explicativo de sus planes y sus razones de construir en Harmony.
La infraestructura prevista para el centro de datos
Una de ellas es que hay infraestructuras de energía y gas existentes y previstas en la zona. En el proyecto prevén un suministro de electricidad inicial de hasta 540 megavatios.
En la zona hay una subestación (Bison) y además están construyendo un parque solar asociado. Además, están previstos sistemas de almacenamiento (con baterías) y una conexión de gas (desde el oeste de Dakota del Norte).
También Samantha Burchill, estudiante de la Universidad Estatal de Dakota del Norte (cuyos padres viven cerca de la zona propuesta), planteó su preocupación por el hecho de que sea en una zona rural. Ella misma ha ido a conocer el centro de datos que está construyendo Applied Digital en la zona cercana a Harwood (al norte de Fargo). Le pareció “muy deprimente”.
El debate en las instituciones
El Instituto Challey de la Universidad Estatal de Dakota del Norte anunció un debate sobre la economía de la IA en el Memorial Union de Fargo. Entre los invitados estaban el responsable estatal de Agricultura, Doug Goehring, y el presidente y consejero delegado de Cass County Electric Coop, Paul Matthys.
Goehring (del Partido Republicano) tiene como rival electoral al demócrata Vern Thompson, que ha hecho de los centros de datos uno de los temas de su campaña.
Al encuentro asistieron más de 200 personas, según un representante de Geronimo. Desde la empresa defienden que quieren responder a las prioridades locales. Esperan crear empleo, recaudación fiscal y dar dinamismo a los negocios de la zona.

articles.title: Render just removed its AI sandbox time limit — and Vercel still has a 24-hour cap
articles.text:
Render just removed its AI sandbox time limit — and Vercel still has a 24-hour cap
Render is taking on Vercel with AI sandboxes that can run indefinitely, along with new tools for managing long-running agent workflows and shared storage.
Announced Wednesday, the launch removes Render’s previous 30-day continuous runtime limit on paid workspace plans. Vercel caps individual sandbox sessions at 24 hours, while Render says its environments can suspend when idle and resume with their files, memory and running processes intact.
Render founder and CEO Anurag Goel, a former Stripe engineer and head of risk, built the platform as an alternative to AWS without the same infrastructure complexity. Now he’s extending that approach to AI agents, combining sandboxes, durable workflows, and shared storage with the applications and databases they depend on.
Not everything is ready yet. Credential brokering will initially be available only to selected customers, private networking for sandboxes is still in development, and Render has yet to settle how its shared storage will handle simultaneous writes to the same file.
Sandboxes that resume mid-task
With this launch, Render sandboxes can stay active through a multi-day codebase migration or while an agent tests an entire application.
The bigger difference comes when a sandbox needs to resume work. Vercel limits uninterrupted sessions to 24 hours, and while persistent sandboxes can restart, their running processes start over.
Render takes a different approach. A sandbox “suspends when it goes idle and wakes on the next command with its files and memory intact, so the agent picks up mid-task instead of rebuilding its state,” the company tells The New Stack.
“suspends when it goes idle and wakes on the next command with its files and memory intact, so the agent picks up mid-task instead of rebuilding its state.”
Credentials that never enter
One of the launch’s security features is credential brokering, which attaches credentials to an agent’s outbound requests as they leave the sandbox so that secrets never enter it.
Pressed on whether that sets Render apart from Vercel, which already offers scoped credentials for agents through its Connect service and has been pushing its own vendors toward short-lived credentials, the company does not claim an edge.
Credential brokering “is not a competitive differentiator” and “is rapidly becoming table stakes,” Render tells The New Stack, calling it “a feature we believe users of Render will appreciate having access to, rather than one users of other platforms will migrate for.”
Render tells The New Stack, it is “turning credential brokering on for small groups of customers first to make sure the experience meets our quality bar” before expanding in the coming weeks, while every developer in the beta gets outbound controls that can “block all traffic from a sandbox or allow only the domains you list.”
The company’s larger argument is that the sandbox matters less than everything around it. Developers choose Render over Vercel, the company contends, because an agent usually has to run inside a larger product and do heavy background work that needs an API staying up and holding its database connections, along with background workers, cron jobs, and the database itself.
Compute flexibility, less complexity
Vercel started with the frontend and serverless functions and is strong there; Render allows, but the company tells The New Stack that Vercel’s “underlying ‘fluid compute’ model is inflexible and inefficient for running the compute-heavy backend workloads that agentic applications depend on,” noting that a single function “tops out at 2 CPUs and 4 GB of RAM,” a ceiling that applies to Vercel Functions rather than its sandboxes.
Render tells The New Stack, it “gives developers the compute flexibility of AWS but takes the complexity off their plate.” Cristian Herrera, CTO of OCMI, which considered Vercel while moving away from AWS, tells Render that “Vercel is a different story,” adding that “if you need to do anything outside of Next.js, you’re fighting the platform.”
“if you need to do anything outside of Next.js, you’re fighting the platform.”
Vercel acknowledged The New Stack’s request for comment but had not provided a statement by publication time.
Workflows that survive crashes
Render’s new Durable Workflows let developers resume long-running jobs after a failure without starting over. Developers can write workflows in Python or TypeScript, with individual tasks running for up to 24 hours. Render “saves the result of every step as it finishes,” the company tells The New Stack. If a process crashes, the workflow can resume on a new machine using those saved results, so “model calls, payments, and database writes that have already succeeded don’t run again.”
A risk remains if a process crashes after a payment goes through but before the result is saved. Render recommends using idempotency keys to prevent duplicate charges or database writes. Shared Filesystems let sandboxes and workflow tasks access the same persistent files, even after the compute that created them shuts down.
Render says the feature is designed for “many agents reading the same repo or dataset, with each one writing its own output.” But handling “concurrent writes to the same file, including locking and conflict resolution, is something we’re still studying,” the company tells The New Stack.
Render says AWS and Vercel are “the two platforms new users most often tell us they’re leaving today, citing complexity and cost as major factors,” the company tells The New Stack. Render doesn’t yet have figures showing how many customers have migrated from Vercel.

articles.title: Docker Urges Isolation and Governance for AI Agent Security
articles.text:
Docker has published a guide to five security risks that arise when AI agents are allowed to browse, run code and call tools with limited human oversight. Writing with product manager Eric Jia, Docker principal product marketing manager Srini Sekaran argues that the autonomy that makes agents useful also makes conventional application security controls insufficient. The company positions isolation and governance, rather than model improvements alone, as the main defences.
The blog post identifies prompt injection, tool misuse and poisoning, excessive autonomy, credential exposure, and data exfiltration as the principal risks. Docker argues that these share a common cause: an agent can select tools at runtime, chain several actions together and often operate with the permissions of the person who started it.
"An agent doesn't just answer a question, it browses, runs code, and calls tools on its own, so a single bad or manipulated instruction can turn into real damage instead of just a wrong answer."
Eric Jia and Srini Sekaran, Docker
Traditional web security often assumes requests arrive at known endpoints and are processed by deterministic code, but agents do not fit that model. A coding agent may read a file, install a dependency, alter configuration, run tests and push a commit after receiving one instruction. Docker says that a compromised or misdirected agent can therefore take a much wider range of actions than a conventional service.
Prompt injection is presented as the defining risk: rather than compromising a system directly, an attacker can place instructions in material an agent is asked to read, such as a web page, code comment, issue or document. Docker cites an incident in which a coding agent followed instructions hidden in repository content and performed actions its user had not requested.
The company is sceptical that prompt injection can be eliminated through instructions to the model, saying that an agent cannot reliably distinguish a legitimate instruction from an injected one. Its preferred response is to limit what a hijacked agent can reach, so that successful manipulation has a smaller effect.
"The agent has no reliable way to tell a legitimate instruction from an injected one, so the defense is to limit what a hijacked agent can reach."
Eric Jia and Srini Sekaran, Docker
Tools are the second area of concern. With agents use connectors, database queries, file operations and code execution to affect external systems, Docker warns that giving an agent more tools than a task requires enlarges the attack surface. It also warns that a tool description can carry hidden instructions that lead an agent to misuse the tool.
This aligns with guidance published by OWASP. In its Agentic AI Threats and Mitigations work, reported by InfoQ in September 2025, OWASP identified tool misuse as a major new threat. It described attackers manipulating agents into abusing authorised tools, potentially gaining unauthorised data access or manipulating systems while remaining within granted permissions. OWASP recommended access verification, behavioural monitoring, operational boundaries and tamper-resistant execution logs.
Docker's third risk is excessive autonomy. The post describes "YOLO mode", where every agent action is approved automatically, as a visible example of broad standing permission. It acknowledges that this mode can be productive, but argues that it should be used inside a boundary that prevents an agent from reaching systems or data it should not touch.
The company gives an example in which a developer asked a coding agent to clean an old repository. The agent generated an rm -rf command with a trailing ~/ and executed it without confirmation, deleting the developer's home directory. Docker also cites an AWS engineer who gave a coding agent a Cost Explorer bug while it ran with operator-level access. The agent chose to delete and rebuild the production environment, resulting in a thirteen-hour regional outage.
Credential handling is closely connected to that problem. Docker says agents should not inherit a developer's personal token, because every action then carries that person's full permissions. It recommends separate, short-lived credentials, injected at runtime and kept out of the conversation. Secrets in prompts, configuration files or image environment variables are also a risk, because injected instructions may be able to read them from the agent's context.
The final risk is data exfiltration. An agent with network access and sensitive information in its context may send that information to an unintended destination. Docker says the risk increases in multi-agent systems, where one agent passes work to another. It recommends allow-listed network egress and treating every handoff between agents as untrusted input.
Those recommendations echo other work covered by InfoQ. Google's GKE security blueprint, reported in July 2026, recommends GKE Sandbox, based on gVisor, for containing agents that execute generated code or call untrusted tools. It also uses Model Armor to inspect prompts and responses for injection attempts and sensitive data exposure. Earlier, Meta open sourced LlamaFirewall, which combines prompt-injection detection, reasoning checks and static analysis of generated code. Google DeepMind's CaMeL research, also covered by InfoQ, takes a different approach by tracking control and data flows around a model.
Docker's answer is Docker Sandboxes and AI Governance. Sandboxes run each agent in a disposable microVM with defined filesystem and network controls. AI Governance is intended to define and enforce which actions, tools and credentials an agent may use. The company says isolation is the highest-impact starting point, with governance providing oversight across a fleet of agents.
Community discussion suggests that isolation alone will not settle the design question. In a thread on r/AI_Agents, a commenter using the name HectaMan wrote that teams should first assess tenancy and risk models. They argued that Docker can be convenient but may still grant excessive authority, noting that it disables around 40 privileged system calls while leaving roughly 500 available. They recommended deny-by-default permissions, least authority, policy enforcement points and controlled information flow.
Another commenter, Groady, said Docker works well for personal agents on a local machine, but questioned a shared kernel when agents execute code on behalf of other people. They suggested microVMs or gVisor-based isolation for that case. The discussion indicates that the useful comparison is not simply container versus no container, but whether the isolation boundary matches the trust boundary of the workload.
Docker's guidance is a useful summary of a problem that is becoming more concrete as coding agents gain write access to repositories, cloud accounts and production systems. Its central claim is persuasive: security teams should assume that agent input may be hostile and design the surrounding system so that a wrong decision cannot become a broad compromise. The harder work is deciding which permissions an agent genuinely needs, how those permissions expire, and who reviews the actions taken under them.

articles.title: España y México, los países que más amenazas reciben por correo electrónico con códigos QR
articles.text:
Los códigos QR se consolidaron como una herramienta de fraude digital durante la primera mitad de 2026. Según el ESET Threat Report H1 2026, España y México figuran entre los tres países con más detecciones de esta modalidad a nivel mundial, solo por detrás de Estados Unidos.
El informe, elaborado por ESET Latinoamérica, revela que estos códigos estuvieron presentes en alrededor del 11% de los correos electrónicos de phishing analizados durante el semestre, lo que ubicó a la amenaza conocida como QRCode/Phishing en el séptimo lugar entre las principales campañas maliciosas distribuidas por correo electrónico.
Por qué España y México concentran las detecciones de phishing con QR
El ESET Threat Report H1 2026 ubicó a Estados Unidos en el primer lugar de detecciones de esta modalidad, con el 19% de los casos registrados a nivel mundial, seguido por España con el 17% y México con el 6%.
Esta distribución geográfica coincide con un fenómeno más amplio: la expansión del uso cotidiano de los códigos QR en pagos, trámites y comunicaciones comerciales, que amplió las oportunidades para que los ciberdelincuentes los utilicen como vehículo de engaño.
En el caso específico de América Latina, los registros de ESET muestran que México lideró los registros regionales asociados a esta modalidad durante el primer semestre de 2026.
La familia QRCode/Phishing figuró entre las amenazas compartidas más extendidas de la región, lo que confirma que esta técnica ya tiene presencia consolidada en el territorio latinoamericano y no se trata de un fenómeno aislado o emergente.
El quishing es una técnica de ingeniería social en la que un atacante oculta una dirección maliciosa dentro de un código QR en lugar de enviarla como un enlace visible. A diferencia del phishing tradicional, la víctima no puede leer ni cuestionar el destino antes de escanear, porque permanece oculto en un patrón de cuadrados blancos y negros hasta el momento mismo de la acción.
Qué es el quishing y cómo actúa el ciberdelincuente
El término “quishing” surge de la combinación de “QR” y “phishing”. El ataque puede producirse en dos escenarios diferenciados. El primero es el digital, donde el código QR llega en el cuerpo de un correo electrónico, en un archivo PDF adjunto, en un mensaje de WhatsApp o SMS, o aparece en un sitio web o perfil de redes sociales.
El segundo escenario es el físico, que incluye códigos impresos en carteles, folletos, papeles colocados en el parabrisas de un vehículo o paquetes. Uno de los casos más frecuentes es el de adhesivos pegados encima de un código QR legítimo, lo que permite al atacante suplantar una fuente confiable sin levantar sospechas inmediatas.
Una vez que la víctima escanea el código, puede ser dirigida a una página falsa de inicio de sesión, a una pantalla de pago, a la descarga de una aplicación maliciosa o a una acción dentro de una aplicación legítima.
Jonathan Ramos, investigador de Seguridad Informática de ESET Latinoamérica, explicó el motivo detrás de esta estrategia: “Al pedirle a la víctima que escanee un código, el ciberdelincuente traslada la interacción desde un entorno relativamente protegido, como la computadora del trabajo, hacia un teléfono móvil que muchas veces no cuenta con las mismas medidas de seguridad”.
El propio ESET Threat Report H1 2026 destaca que los atacantes utilizan códigos QR para desplazar la interacción hacia dispositivos móviles y dificultar una inspección rápida de los enlaces maliciosos. Ese traslado de dispositivo resulta determinante, porque reduce las barreras de seguridad que suelen existir en entornos corporativos.
El caso DocuSign, un ejemplo real de estafa con código QR
Entre los correos electrónicos reales detectados por ESET y presentados en el ESET Threat Report H1 2026 se encuentra un caso que imita una notificación de DocuSign, plataforma de firma electrónica ampliamente utilizada por empresas.
Según los datos regionales de ESET, DocuSign fue una de las marcas más utilizadas por los atacantes en campañas de phishing observadas en América Latina durante el semestre.
El mensaje fraudulento utiliza la identidad visual de la compañía e informa que un documento fue completado para revisión y firma. Incluye un botón amarillo que indica que se debe escanear el código QR para revisar y completar el documento, pero ese botón no dirige a ningún sitio real. La única forma de continuar es apuntar la cámara al código, lo que obliga a la víctima a trasladar la interacción al celular.
El correo contiene muy poco texto, lo que deja pocas señales para sospechar del engaño. La dirección a la que conduce permanece oculta dentro de la imagen, una característica que distingue a esta modalidad del phishing convencional basado en enlaces visibles.
Qué puede hacer el ciberdelincuente tras el escaneo del código
Una vez que la estafa llega al celular, el atacante dispone de varias vías de explotación. La primera es el robo de credenciales y el secuestro de sesiones, mediante páginas falsas de inicio de sesión de bancos, servicios de correo o aplicaciones corporativas adaptadas a pantallas móviles.
La segunda vía corresponde a los pagos fraudulentos. Algunos códigos QR abren pantallas de pago o dirigen a operaciones con datos precargados, lo que reduce las posibilidades de que la víctima detecte irregularidades si no revisa con atención la información antes de confirmar la transacción.
La tercera vía es la instalación de aplicaciones maliciosas. El código QR puede conducir a la descarga de aplicaciones fuera de las tiendas oficiales o a sitios preparados para distribuir software malicioso, sin que la víctima perciba de inmediato el riesgo que corre su dispositivo.
Señales para identificar un código QR sospechoso
ESET comparte una serie de indicios que permiten sospechar de un código QR malicioso. Uno de los más frecuentes es que el código esté pegado encima de otro o presente señales de manipulación física. También resulta sospechoso que llegue sin haber sido solicitado, mediante correo electrónico, mensaje o en un soporte físico inesperado.
Otras señales de alerta incluyen mensajes de urgencia, presión temporal o advertencias alarmistas que acompañan al código, así como una URL mostrada que no coincide con el servicio esperado o que presenta irregularidades evidentes.
Finalmente, deben generar sospecha los códigos que solicitan datos sensibles, como contraseñas, códigos de verificación o información financiera, o que piden instalar una aplicación para continuar con el proceso.
Recomendaciones de ESET para prevenir el quishing
Entre las buenas prácticas que propone ESET se encuentra escanear con cautela y revisar la URL antes de continuar, verificando que la dirección de destino mostrada por el lector corresponda al sitio esperado.
La compañía recomienda además priorizar los canales oficiales para consultar facturas, envíos, beneficios o trámites, ingresando manualmente al sitio web o utilizando la aplicación correspondiente.
Otra medida central consiste en revisar siempre la información antes de confirmar una operación, en particular cuando implica pagos o el ingreso de credenciales.
ESET también aconseja no instalar aplicaciones desde códigos QR desconocidos y descargar software únicamente desde las tiendas oficiales, además de verificar cualquier duda a través de un canal oficial y mantener el celular actualizado y protegido con una solución de seguridad confiable.

articles.title: Six humanoid robots worked a 24-hour shift at a convenience store, but two weren't good enough to keep their jobs
articles.text:
Through the looking glass: If you're wondering which job humanoid robots will take next, or "help the humans with," it could be in your local convenience store. A Chinese robot manufacturer recently launched a livestreamed challenge involving six of its humanoid machines working a 24-hour shift at a store, but not all of them passed their probation.
Agibot's G2 robots took over duties at an operating convenience store in Shanghai's Xuhui district between November 2 and 3. The company called the broadcast "Robots Never Clock Out," which perfectly captures why managers are introducing these robots.
The machines' assignments included stocking shelves, preparing coffee and hot food, greeting customers, and clearing rubbish. The challenge covered four periods: the lunchtime rush, evening crowds, overnight duty, and breakfast preparation. All of which meant there were plenty of opportunities for something to go wrong.
There were also some deliberately awkward tests. According to Machine Heart's report (via Sina), participants asked the robots to distinguish between sugary and sugar-free Coke, placed obstacles in their paths, and shook a container while a machine tried to pick up food. What better way to get robots used to working in a convenience store than to have them encounter difficult customers?
 – AGIBOT (@AGIBOTofficial) November 2, 2026
By the end, the robots had completed 1,730 tasks. These included 683 customer greetings, 369 item retrievals and deliveries, and 147 coffees. However, only four machines passed the assessment. The cleaning robot and one assigned to patrol the shelves fell short. According to ITHome, the latter lacked initiative in inspecting and replenishing goods and failed to keep up with the store's turnover pace. Its on-duty enthusiasm needs to be improved in the future, apparently, which makes it sound even more human.
The cleaning bot encountered a full trash can while on night duty, causing it to deviate from the designated route, run outside the store, and stray from its post. Again, it's a scenario many people might relate to.
Before store owners start calculating how many salaries they could save, there are some fairly important caveats. Although the report describes 24 hours of continuous operation, it doesn't specify whether individual machines needed charging breaks, maintenance, or human assistance during that time.
We also don't know whether the robots matched human workers for speed and cost. A report from January found that humanoid robots were working about half as fast as their human counterparts, but factories were still buying them anyway.
The list of workplaces experimenting with humanoids keeps growing. AGCO plans to introduce Digit robots at its Kansas farm-equipment factory in 2027, complete with the usual assurances that they will help employees rather than replace them.
South Korea has also approved a trial allowing 20 humanoids to share factory workspaces with humans, under an exemption from existing safety-barrier requirements and with additional safeguards. At least making coffee is a more reassuring use for these machines than pummeling a YouTuber in a cage.

articles.title: Xbox Loses Its First Chief Operating Officer Mid-Reset
articles.text:
Wednesday, November 4th 2026
Xbox Loses Its First Chief Operating Officer Mid-Reset
Helen Chiang, Xbox's first-ever chief operating officer, has left Microsoft just three months after taking on the role. The news comes from a short internal memo by Microsoft Gaming CEO Asha Sharma, obtained by The Verge, which simply states that Chiang is leaving the company and thanks her for her years of service. No reason was given, and Xbox's VP of communications, Kari Perez, said the company doesn't discuss individual personnel matters. There's no successor yet either, so Chiang's duties will be split among other Xbox leaders for now, with Sharma promising more details on COO leadership once plans are finalized.
Chiang had been at Microsoft for around 21 years, starting in 2005 and moving to Xbox in 2007, where Sharma credits her with helping build Xbox Live. She later led Mojang and became corporate vice president of the Minecraft franchise in 2020. Sharma created the COO position in July as part of her reset of Xbox, and it came with end-to-end profit and loss responsibility across content, hardware, platform, and services. That same reset includes around 3,200 job cuts by the end of fiscal year 2027, with hundreds of jobs already gone. Losing the executive meant to hold the whole business together this early into the reset probably isn't the kind of stability Xbox was hoping for.
Update Oct 25th: A verified source familiar with the situation has told Eurogamer that Helen Chiang was "terminated for policy violations." This claim has not been independently verified.
Update Nov 3rd: Helen Chiang has since denied being "fired for a policy violation" in a recent LinkedIn post. She goes on to clarify more points about her departure. You can read her full post below.
Helen Chiang, Former Xbox COOClarity is Kindness
There has been some speculation about my abrupt departure from Microsoft, including claims that I was "fired for a policy violation". That's not accurate and while I won't turn this into a play-by-play, silence should not be mistaken for agreement. What has been said about my departure, and what has been left unsaid, has created a picture of me that I hardly recognize. It's important to me to set the record straight.
First, I did not leak confidential company information to the press. I have never communicated with any journalist outside the limited, company-authorized interviews I've done as part of my job. That includes every journalist who reached out this week seeking my side of the story.
Second, I did not leave XBOX to join a competitor. You don't spend two decades somewhere without developing a deep loyalty to the people, teams, and businesses you've helped build. XBOX was never just another stop in my career. My end game was always to keep building here.
Third, I did not engage in discrimination, bullying, harassment, insider trading, embezzlement, or other fraudulent activity. I stand by my record: both the results I delivered and the way I have treated people throughout my career. I won't let speculation define my character or erase that record.
Lastly, I did not leave because I was passed over for a bigger role. Since having children, I've been intentional about how I define ambition and success. I haven't actively sought out bigger roles or increased responsibilities, and the last time I interviewed for a job was in 2011. My reputation and results paved the way for the opportunities that followed. I went where the company believed I was needed and where I could have the greatest impact. I did not ask for my most recent role, either. I was promoted into it in July.
I believe in fairness, accountability, and holding ourselves to the standards we expect of others. Those standards only mean something when they're applied consistently. I have serious concerns about how they were applied in my case, and I believe those concerns deserve to be taken seriously.
I share this because I don't want my departure reduced to an inaccurate story about incompetence, ambition for the next big job, or a Nelson-level scandal. My story is about staying true to your core values, especially when it is hard. That's the legacy I hope to leave behind.
To everyone who has reached out with hugs, love, and support: thank you. So many of you have reminded me of the wonderful times we've shared over the past 20 years and the impact we've had on one another. Some of you I haven't been in touch with for several years, yet you still took the time to check on me. Others are people I've never even met, but you reached out anyway. That speaks volumes about the care and humanity in our industry and the connections that transcend where we work.
This is not how I ever imagined my story here would end. And it is not the whole story.
